excerpt: ProPublica reported that XpresTest received nearly $40m in federal disease-control awards after an investment by a fund associated with Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr.
headline: Ebola Contract Scandal: Eric Trump Slams 'Fake Story' as Spa CEO Admits 'I'm Not Sure We Can Do It'
html_content:
XpresTest's chief executive told ProPublica he was unsure whether the company could carry out a US government assignment in the Democratic Republic of Congo, after its parent company's subsidiary received two federal awards worth nearly $40 million (€36.2 million and £30.2 million).

The awards, for Ebola screening at US airports and infectious-disease work in Congo, followed an investment in XWELL by American Ventures, a fund linked to Donald Trump Jr and Eric Trump. The ProPublica investigation, published on 9 November, examined the company's experience and the timing of the awards.

According to ProPublica, XpresTest, a subsidiary of airport spa operator XWELL, received the awards in 2026 after American Ventures invested in its parent company. The fund was launched by Dominari Holdings, where the president's sons served as advisers.

One award, worth $18.8 million (€17.0 million and £14.2 million), came from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in June for Ebola entry screening at US airports. A separate $20 million (€18.1 million and £15.1 million) State Department award concerned infectious-disease response in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

ProPublica reported that the awards' combined value was seven times the total value of federal contracts XpresTest had previously received.

Eric Trump Disputes Report

Primetimer reported that Eric Trump rejected the account and threatened legal action against ProPublica after Democratic congressman Mike Levin questioned the investment and subsequent awards. His reported response challenged suggestions that he had influenced the contracts.

ProPublica did not establish that either Trump brother directly participated in the procurement decisions. A spokesperson for the brothers told the publication they were passive minority investors in a fund that invested in XWELL and had no involvement in negotiating or obtaining government contracts.

American Ventures invested approximately $30 million (€27.1 million and £22.7 million) in XWELL in February. ProPublica reported that Dominari had previously appointed the brothers as advisers and given them a stake of more than 10 per cent in Dominari.

The reported investment was made by a fund connected to the brothers; the reporting does not show that either man personally invested in XWELL. XWELL's earlier federal work also predates the current administration. Its predecessor, XpresSpa Group, received CDC funding for COVID-19 testing in 2021, during Joe Biden's presidency.

CEO Acknowledges Risks

XWELL chief executive Ezra Ernst told ProPublica that XpresTest secured the awards through competitive bidding. The company had screened travellers for COVID-19 and other pathogens at US airports, but the investigation found it had no prior experience responding to Ebola or providing biosecurity services overseas.

Ernst described the international work as unfamiliar and acknowledged uncertainty about whether the company could complete the assignment in Congo.

'This is a risky contract. I'm not sure we can do it,' he told ProPublica.

The remark concerned the difficulty of carrying out the work; it does not establish that the company failed to meet its contractual obligations. The State Department separately told ProPublica that its award followed a competitive process building on XpresTest's previous screening experience.

Dominari chief executive Anthony Hayes also rejected suggestions of improper influence. He told ProPublica the firm had never seen or heard of either brother using his family name to influence a government contract.

The timing remains central to the investigation: a fund linked to the president's sons invested in XWELL before its subsidiary received two substantial federal awards. However, the reporting cited in the article does not show that either brother intervened in the awards, and the sequence of events alone does not establish wrongdoing.

excerpt: The Chicks displayed profane anti-Trump paper fans during a Los Angeles concert as Democrats swept the 2026 US midterms
headline: Country Music Legends Brought Out Explicit Red Fans To Mock Donald Trump After His Midterm Defeat
html_content:
The Chicks displayed red paper fans bearing a censored insult aimed at President Donald Trump during a concert in Los Angeles on Tuesday, 3 November, as Democrats made sweeping gains in the US midterm elections.

The trio's election-night gesture took place at the Dolby Theatre during their Taking the Long Way 20th-anniversary tour. It also recalled an earlier political backlash that made the band a flashpoint in American country music.

The Chicks Unfold Anti-Trump Paper Fans on Election Night

Natalie Maines, Martie Maguire and Emily Strayer were seated with their instruments when they opened matching hand-held fans reading 'F–k Trump'. The audience cheered as the musicians began fanning themselves.

'Welcome to our blunami night,' Maines told the crowd, referring to the wave of Democratic victories. She then declared, 'Texas is blue. The Senate is blue. The House is blue.'

'This was gonna be a very different night if that wasn't the case,' she added.

The Texas results gave her words particular weight. Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, while James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat. Democrats also captured control of the Texas House of Representatives.

The national picture was still taking shape that night. The Associated Press called Democratic control of the Senate at 11:36pm Eastern on 3 November, followed by the House at 1:24am on 4 November. Trump himself was not on the ballot.

The Chicks Revisit a Protest That Changed Their Careers

The anniversary tour centres on Taking the Long Way, the band's 2006 album recorded after a fierce backlash over Maines' comments about then-President George W. Bush.

At a London concert on 10 March 2003, Maines criticised the impending US-led invasion of Iraq and said she was ashamed that Bush came from Texas. Radio stations dropped the band's songs, and some former fans destroyed their CDs.

'Not Ready to Make Nice', which The Chicks performed again on election night, addressed the fallout. The song won Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the 2007 Grammy Awards.

The old dispute has acquired a new target. At a New York concert in October, Maines updated her Bush-era criticism, saying she was ashamed that the US president came from the United States.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle responded before the November election-night performance, calling her a 'despicable nobody' in a statement to Entertainment Weekly. His remarks were not a response to the paper fans.

The band has also sold T-shirts featuring Maines' revised message. She told The New York Times that the design was its second-biggest seller, behind the tour shirt.

The Chicks Join a Wider Celebrity Reaction to Midterms

The Chicks were hardly alone in celebrating the results. On The View on Wednesday, 4 November, Whoopi Goldberg wore floral overalls to 'give the American people their flowers', crediting voters for the outcome.

Her co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin, a former Trump administration official, called the result a 'total and complete repudiation' of the president's policies. Joy Behar mocked him as 'Lame Donald Duck'.

Elsewhere, John Leguizamo described the election as 'redemption time' in a social media video. Pedro Pascal shared a blue map of Texas, while Stephen King offered a two-word verdict on X, 'Buyers' remorse'.

Even James Woods, who has previously supported Trump, congratulated Democratic winners, although he also criticised Republicans over their defeats.

excerpt: MobLand Season 2, Episode 9 sees Harry rescue Gina from Frankie, while Kat declares "Black Flag" against the Harrigans, signalling an attempt to dismantle their organisation.
headline: What Is Black Flag and Why Did Kat Call It on the Harrigans? 'MobLand' Series 2 Episode 9 Ending Explained
html_content:
MobLand Season 2, Episode 9 delivers a major turning point for the Harrigan family, as Harry Da Souza (Tom Hardy) faces one of his most dangerous confrontations yet and Kat McAllister (Janet McTeer) makes a decisive move against the crime dynasty.

Titled 'Nervous Breakdown', the episode sees Frankie Cooper (Johnny Flynn) kidnap Gina Da Souza (Teddie Allen) to force Harry to answer for the murder of his son, Michael. Although Harry manages to secure her release, the closing moments reveal that the family faces an even greater threat.

Kat declares 'Black Flag' on the Harrigans, announcing that their time in power is over. But what does the phrase mean, and what does it mean for Harry?

What Does Black Flag Mean in 'MobLand'?

The episode opens with Frankie interrupting a diplomatic gathering attended by Kat. Disguised as a waiter, he confronts her and threatens her, prompting Kat to invoke the phrase 'Black Flag'.

She invokes the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which protects the inviolability of embassy premises and restricts unauthorised entry by the receiving state's authorities. Kat characterises Frankie's intrusion as an attack on the nation, warning him that he will not leave without consequences.

However, the phrase takes on a much greater significance in the episode's closing scene. After Frankie contacts Kat during his confrontation with Harry, she delivers a chilling message to the Harrigan fixer.

'As of tonight there is no Harrigans,' she tells him, before explaining that he has a new job and thanking him in advance for what he is about to do.

The episode does not establish 'Black Flag' as the formal name of a specific criminal operation. Instead, Kat uses the phrase as a declaration of war against the Harrigans, signalling that she intends to dismantle their organisation and take control.

Harry's experience as the family's fixer makes him a valuable asset. By offering him a new position, Kat appears to be attempting to secure his services while bringing the Harrigans' existing power structure to an end.

The phrase also carries associations with hostility. Historically, pirate ships used black flags, including variations of the Jolly Roger, to intimidate other vessels and signal that surrender was preferable to resistance. The phrase also evokes the American punk band Black Flag, whose song 'Nervous Breakdown' provides the episode's title.

Nevertheless, the message in the episode is clear: the Harrigans are being targeted.

Does Harry Save Gina From Frankie?

Frankie kidnaps Gina and locks her inside a concealed panic room beneath his London home, a room that previously served as Michael's playroom.

Harry's attempts to move Jan (Joanne Froggatt) and Gina to safety fall apart when Frankie arrives at the family home. Although Harry manages to fight off the armed men who attack him, Gina is captured.

Frankie threatens to have Gina killed during a video call, forcing Harry into a desperate negotiation. Rather than relying on another elaborate scheme, Harry warns Frankie that he could inflict serious damage before his guards could intervene. He then gives him seven seconds to call Joey and order Gina's release. Faced with the threat, Frankie eventually agrees, allowing Gina to escape.

The confrontation demonstrates that Harry is still capable of terrifying his enemies, even when he no longer has complete control of the situation.

What Happens to Conrad and Maeve?

Elsewhere, Conrad Harrigan (Pierce Brosnan) and Maeve (Helen Mirren) attempt to intercept a major drug shipment at Tilbury Docks.

Their plan falls apart when Conrad begins seeing figures from his past and becomes increasingly distressed. Maeve recognises that he is not in a condition to continue, and they abandon the operation.

Meanwhile, Maeve remains determined to remove Harry from the family. She tells Eddie (Anson Boon) that killing him is the final task required to prove himself as a Harrigan.

Kevin (Paddy Considine) also considers taking control of the organisation, adding to the growing divisions within the family.

What Does the Body Found in the Lake Mean?

The episode ends with police recovering a badly decomposed body from a lake at the Harrigan estate. Colin Tattersall is present as the discovery is made, suggesting that the find could be part of a wider plan against the family.

The identity of the body is not confirmed, although the circumstances invite speculation about its connection to the events surrounding Conrad and Frankie.

With Kat declaring the Harrigans finished, Frankie still dangerous and several family members plotting against one another, the season finale now promises a decisive confrontation.

For Harry, the question is no longer simply how to protect the Harrigans. He must decide whether there will be anything left of the family worth protecting.

excerpt: A global Microsoft outage disrupted Outlook, Copilot, Teams-related functions and connected AI tools, reviving Elon Musk's warning that OpenAI could eventually challenge Microsoft directly.
headline: Elon Musk's 'OpenAI Is Going To Eat Microsoft Alive' Remark Returns as Microsoft Battles Global Outage
html_content:
Microsoft's global outage on 12 November disrupted Outlook, Copilot and Microsoft 365 services, including Teams functions that rely on Exchange Online.

As users encountered interruptions, Elon Musk's remark that OpenAI would 'eat Microsoft alive' resurfaced, renewing attention on the companies' partnership and their expanding freedom to compete in artificial intelligence.

The comment followed changes to the Microsoft-OpenAI agreement that give the AI company more flexibility to offer its products through other cloud providers, while preserving significant commercial ties between the two firms.

How Far Did the Microsoft Outage Spread?

The disruption began on 12 November, with Microsoft initially reporting problems affecting Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas. It later warned that users worldwide could experience connectivity issues as the disruption spread across its infrastructure.

The effects extended beyond business email. Because several Microsoft 365 features rely on Exchange Online, mailbox problems could also affect calendars, meeting scheduling and other connected workplace functions.

Downdetector recorded a peak of 138,058 reports of Outlook problems in the United States at around 1pm EST on 12 November, as users struggled to access their inboxes and send or receive emails.

Microsoft said a large number of servers had unexpectedly become unavailable, shifting additional traffic and pressure on to the remaining infrastructure.

'We're working to safely return them to service,' the company said in an update posted on X.

We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. Some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue. We’re focused on…

— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 13, 2026

By early Friday, 13 November, Microsoft reported initial improvements in server stability. Affected services remained disrupted as engineers continued working to restore normal operations. The company also said there was no indication that malicious activity was responsible for the incident.

The disruption also affected AI services connected to Microsoft's systems. OpenAI reported elevated errors affecting its Microsoft 365 connector, warning that new connections could fail and connected tools might not work as expected.

Anthropic also reported that most requests through its Microsoft 365 connector, including mail, calendar and search tools, were failing.

'This issue is caused by a Microsoft 365 service incident,' the company said in its status update.

Why Has Musk's 'Eat Microsoft Alive' Warning Resurfaced?

Musk made the remark on 7 August 2025, after Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella announced that GPT-5 was being made available across Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot, GitHub Copilot and Azure AI Foundry.

'OpenAI is going to eat Microsoft alive,' Musk responded on X.

Nadella replied: 'People have been trying for 50 years and that's the fun of it!'

People have been trying for 50 years and that’s the fun of it! Each day you learn something new, and innovate, partner, and compete. Excited for Grok 4 on Azure and looking forward to Grok 5!

— Satya Nadella (@satyanadella) August 7, 2025

The exchange came as Microsoft was also expanding its work with Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI. On 19 May 2025, Microsoft announced that Grok 3 and Grok 3 Mini were available through Azure AI Foundry.

Is OpenAI Now a Direct Threat to Microsoft?

Musk returned to the competition question in November 2025, after OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman discussed the possibility of replacing traditional office productivity tools, including documents, presentations, email and Slack, with AI agents that could work together and escalate important matters to human users.

'As I was saying, OpenAI will compete directly with Microsoft,' Musk wrote on X on 9 November 2025.

Under an amended agreement announced on 27 April 2026, OpenAI gained the freedom to offer its products through any cloud provider.

Microsoft remained its primary cloud partner, and OpenAI products would continue to launch first on Azure unless Microsoft could not or chose not to support the required capabilities. Microsoft also retained its position as a major shareholder.

The agreement maintained OpenAI's revenue-sharing payments to Microsoft through 2030, subject to a total cap, while ending Microsoft's own revenue-sharing payments to OpenAI.

The outage has brought renewed attention to Musk's comments, but does not establish that his prediction about Microsoft's future is coming true. The revised agreement preserves significant commercial ties between the companies.

excerpt: Russian daredevils Ivan Kuznetsov and Angelina Nikolau remain charged over their Empire State Building stunt, while disputed plea negotiations and deportation concerns cloud their legal future.
headline: Empire State Building Climbers' Lawyer Claims Plea Deal Was Pulled, Warns of Ukraine War Risk
html_content:
A lawyer for Ivan Kuznetsov and Angelina Nikolau says prosecutors withdrew a proposed plea agreement in their Empire State Building climbing case, and has warned that deportation to Russia could put Kuznetsov at risk of being sent to fight in the war in Ukraine.

The couple, who also goes by Angela, appeared in Manhattan Criminal Court on Thursday, 12 November. Their attorney, Noam Biale, said prosecutors had withdrawn a proposed agreement that would have allowed them to plead guilty to lesser offences.

The Manhattan District Attorney's Office disputed his account, saying no formal plea offer had been made.

The couple still face felony charges, possible imprisonment and the prospect of deportation. They have not been convicted of the offences.

Lawyer Raises Concerns About Deportation to Russia

Biale reportedly told reporters that deportation to Russia could have serious consequences for his clients. He warned that Kuznetsov could face conscription into Russia's military and potentially be sent to fight in the war in Ukraine.

That warning describes a possible risk, not a confirmed outcome. The information available does not establish that conscription or deployment would automatically follow deportation.

Biale also raised concerns about Nikolau's potential treatment if she were returned to Russia, saying she could face imprisonment over her artistic expression. This, too, is an allegation about a possible outcome, rather than a confirmed legal consequence.

The lawyer's argument is that the couple's immigration status could shape what happens to them beyond the criminal proceedings in New York. Their future remains uncertain while the case continues.

Conflicting Accounts Over Proposed Plea Agreement

Biale reportedly said prosecutors had been prepared to offer the couple the opportunity to plead guilty to lesser offences. The Manhattan District Attorney's Office, however, said no formal plea offer had been made.

The two accounts leave unclear what was discussed between the defence and prosecutors, and whether any proposed terms were withdrawn before an agreement was reached. Neither account changes the fact that the couple remain charged and have not been convicted.

The case has been adjourned until 28 January 2027, when the pair are expected to return to Manhattan Criminal Court.

They face multiple charges arising from their July stunt, including third-degree burglary, first-degree reckless endangerment and second-degree criminal mischief. The charges remain allegations unless and until proved in court.

The Climb That Led to Their Arrest

The case stems from 1 July 2026, when, according to reports, Kuznetsov and Nikolau climbed the Empire State Building's broadcast antenna without ropes or safety harnesses.

The pair unfurled a banner bearing the message, 'When the power of love beats the love of power, the world knows peace.' Kuznetsov then appeared to propose to Nikolau.

The couple previously featured in the 2024 Netflix documentary Skywalkers: A Love Story, which followed their attempt to scale Malaysia's Merdeka 118 skyscraper.

After their arrest, they defended the climb as artistic expression, saying their intention was to spread a message of love and peace rather than commit a crime. They also acknowledged the risks involved.

Biale said the couple were in the United States on talent visas but did not specify when their immigration authorisation was due to expire. Their status may become a factor as the criminal case proceeds.

The couple are due back in court on 28 January 2027. Their criminal case and immigration future remain unresolved.

excerpt: Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram has praised the second season of BBC drama 'This City Is Ours' while criticising its focus on crime and some Scouse accents.
headline: 'This City Is Ours' Season 2: Liverpool Mayor Calls Actors' Scouse Accents 'A Bit Dodgy'
html_content:
Liverpool City Region Mayor Steve Rotheram has shared his thoughts on the second season of BBC crime drama This City Is Ours, praising its production quality and performances while questioning whether it presents an accurate picture of the city.

Rotheram called the series 'brilliant' and praised its cinematic style and strong acting. However, he said the programme's focus on drugs, organised crime and criminal activity did not reflect the Liverpool he wanted audiences to associate with the city.

He also offered a pointed assessment of the cast's regional performances, saying that some of the Scouse accents were 'a bit dodgy'.

What Did Liverpool Mayor Steve Rotheram Say About 'This City Is Ours'?

Rotheram, who serves as mayor of the Liverpool City Region, said he had recently finished watching the second series of the BBC drama.

Although he praised the programme's overall quality, he expressed reservations about its representation of Liverpool and the people who live there.

He argued that television productions set in the city should do more to showcase the qualities for which its residents are known, particularly their friendliness, humour and welcoming nature.

'We need to get away from the drugs and crime and organised crime and criminal activity to what most people are renowned for, which is the warmth of their welcome, their friendliness, their humour,' he said.

He added that these characteristics were what the Liverpool City Region represented to him.

His comments were not entirely critical, however. Rotheram acknowledged the show's cinematic presentation and praised the standard of its performances, making clear that his concerns were more about the picture of the city being presented than the production itself.

Why Did Rotheram Criticise the Scouse Accents?

One of the mayor's more unexpected observations concerned the Liverpool accents used by some members of the cast. While he did not identify individual performers, Rotheram said he thought some of the accents were 'a bit dodgy'.

The comment touches on a familiar challenge for television productions filmed in Liverpool: capturing the distinctive regional dialect convincingly, particularly when performers come from outside the city.

The show's cast has previously discussed the work involved in getting the accents right. In March 2025, Julie Graham revealed that the actors worked with a voice coach and received guidance from Liverpool-born colleagues and crew members, including the production's sound recordist, who helped them correct individual words when necessary.

The differences between accents across generations and genders can also make the task more complicated. Despite the criticism, the series has attracted praise for its performances and its use of Liverpool locations.

What Is 'This City Is Ours' Season 2 About?

Created by Stephen Butchard, This City Is Ours follows Michael Kavanagh (James Nelson-Joyce), a Liverpool criminal whose attempt to build a future with Diana Williams (Hannah Onslow) is complicated by his involvement in organised crime.

The second season picks up after the events of the first, with Michael and Diana initially enjoying life in Spain. Their plans are disrupted when events pull Michael back into the criminal world.

Meanwhile, a power struggle within the Phelan organisation threatens to destabilise the business. A new threat also emerges in the form of Ozzie Thompson, a gangster from Ronnie Phelan's (Sean Bean) past.

The returning cast includes Jack McMullen as Jamie Phelan and Julie Graham as Elaine Phelan, alongside James Nelson-Joyce, Hannah Onslow and other familiar faces. Shaun Evans joins the new series as Ozzie Thompson, a former associate of Ronnie Phelan who has recently been released from prison. Álvaro Morte also joins as Felipe Guzman, a member of the Colombian cartel.

Does 'This City Is Ours' Give Liverpool a Bad Reputation?

Rotheram's comments come amid wider discussion about how crime dramas influence perceptions of Liverpool.

The series has proved popular, but its focus on criminal organisations has prompted questions about whether television consistently presents the city through the same familiar themes.

The debate also highlights the tension between celebrating Liverpool as a filming location and ensuring that its identity is not reduced to fictional stories about violence and organised crime.

There are clear economic benefits to productions choosing the region. The first series of This City Is Ours generated approximately £9 million for the Liverpool City Region economy. According to the Liverpool Film Office, the production also generated or safeguarded around 300 full-time equivalent jobs and supported 17 trainees entering the film industry.

For Rotheram, the challenge is to encourage more productions that showcase the city's wider character, including its culture, humour and community spirit.

Ultimately, his reaction is a mixed verdict on the BBC drama: he recognises its quality and entertainment value, but believes Liverpool has much more to offer than the criminal world depicted on screen.

excerpt: Rubik's Cube production has resumed in Hungary after more than 40 years, with inventor Ernő Rubik signing the first robot-made puzzle for an auction supporting a local hospital.
headline: First Rubik's Cube Made in Hungary After Over 40 Years To Be Auctioned for Hospital as Puzzle Returns
html_content:
The first Rubik's Cube made in Hungary in more than 40 years has been signed by its inventor and set aside for a charity auction to benefit a local hospital. Ernő Rubik, 82, launched the automated production line at the Jász-Plasztik factory in Jászberény on Tuesday and signed the first puzzle assembled there.

Proceeds from its planned sale will help St Elizabeth Hospital buy medical equipment, according to the local authority. No auction date or estimate of the amount it could raise has been announced.

The reopening brings production back to the country where Rubik invented the puzzle in 1974. Manufacturing moved overseas after demand grew beyond what factories in socialist Hungary could supply.

The return follows a decision by Canadian toy company Spin Master, which owns the Rubik's brand, to resume production in Hungary.

First Rubik's Cube Set Aside for Hospital Auction

Rubik started the new assembly line during Tuesday's inauguration and signed the first completed cube, according to the Jászberény municipal government. Rather than going on sale in a shop, it is earmarked for an auction benefiting the city's St Elizabeth Hospital.

The money raised is intended to pay for medical equipment. The local authority has not announced when the auction will take place or how much the cube might fetch. No proceeds have yet been reported.

'The cube was born here,' Rubik said at the opening. The ceremony marked a return more than 40 years after Hungarian production ended in the early 1980s.

Robots Bring Rubik's Cube Manufacturing Back to Hungary

At Jász-Plasztik, robotic equipment now assembles the cubes and tests them for durability and functionality. Rubik described the automated process as 'very different' from the early days, when the puzzles were assembled by hand.

The plant aims to produce approximately one million cubes a year. That is a manufacturing target, not a figure for output already achieved. The investment has also created 27 jobs, according to Jászberény's municipal government.

Spin Master executive Steve Radewych said the return would bring production closer to important European markets. Calling Rubik's creation 'more than a toy', he described it as 'a global social phenomenon'.

How Rubik's Cube Became a Worldwide Puzzle

Rubik developed the original wooden cube while teaching design in Budapest in 1974. The rotating puzzle, initially called the Magic Cube, began appearing in local shops in 1977. About 5,000 were sold in that initial run.

Demand soon grew beyond Hungary's manufacturing capacity. The puzzle was licensed to a British company and later an American company, with production shifting abroad.

Rubik said 200 million cubes were sold between 1980 and 1983. Total sales have since passed half a billion, with millions still sold each year.

Rubik does not consider himself a speed competitor. He describes the puzzle as a 'transformable sculpture', reflecting how its shifting surfaces combine design and engineering. For him, its appeal extends beyond how quickly someone can solve it.

The new production line brings modern manufacturing technology to an invention that became a worldwide success after leaving Hungary. Its robotic assembly and quality checks are intended to supply international markets from the country where the puzzle originated.

The first cube produced on the line, however, will not enter the retail market. Bearing its inventor's signature, it is destined for a charity auction to help buy equipment for St Elizabeth Hospital. The auction has been announced, but its date and potential proceeds remain unknown.

excerpt: Jimmy Kimmel criticised Donald Trump's latest posts about Democrats, Senate rules and migrant caravans, arguing that the president was repeating familiar political talking points.
headline: 'It's Sad': Jimmy Kimmel Says 'He's Lost His Mojo' After Donald Trump Posts About Democrats and Migrants
html_content:
Jimmy Kimmel said Donald Trump had 'lost his mojo' after the president posted a series of messages about Democrats, the Senate and migrant caravans. Speaking on ABC's Jimmy Kimmel Live! on Thursday, 12 November, the comedian said Trump's political warnings sounded familiar.

Kimmel told viewers that Trump had begun posting at 5.50am Eastern time, starting with a complaint that Democrats repeatedly called his administration corrupt. The president accused his opponents of using the allegation to distract from what he described as wrongdoing in Democratic-led states.

Kimmel responded with mock disbelief, pretending nobody would make such an accusation. Rather than challenge each claim in the posts, he made their familiar language the focus of his response.

Kimmel Turns Trump's Senate Complaint on McConnell

Trump's posts also renewed his demand to end the Senate filibuster, a procedural rule that can require 60 votes to advance most legislation. He argued that Republicans had failed to pass election legislation and that the chamber had become a place where proposals went to die.

Kimmel picked up on that complaint. Feigning agreement, he suggested sending Republican Senator Mitch McConnell home to Kentucky instead. McConnell remains a senator but is no longer the chamber's Republican leader. John Thune holds that post.

The joke did not address Trump's argument about Senate rules. It shifted attention to McConnell, one of the party's best-known figures. In the monologue, Kimmel treated each grievance as part of a political argument he believed audiences had heard before.

Trump's Migrant Warning Meets Mexico's Account

Trump also warned that large caravans were moving through Mexico and threatened to double tariffs on the country unless its government stopped them. His message followed Republican defeats in the midterm elections, which he linked to renewed warnings about migration.

Reuters reported that about 1,500 people had set off from Tapachula in southern Mexico on Tuesday. Their initial destination was Mexico City, where they hoped to seek assistance, although many ultimately wanted to reach the United States. The report described movement within Mexico, rather than a group already approaching the US border.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Thursday that no migrant caravan had reached the US border since Trump returned to office in January 2025.

She also described a group in Chiapas that had largely dispersed. Her comments challenged the impression of an imminent mass arrival at the border, while acknowledging that migrants were travelling within Mexico.

Kimmel's response focused on what he saw as repetition in Trump's messaging. He grouped the references to caravans, Democrats and ballrooms together, and said the president was repeating himself rather than finding a new message. He also described Trump's performance as pathetic.

Kimmel then compared Trump to former American football quarterback Joe Namath advertising hearing aids. Namath has appeared in advertisements for hearing-aid products, making the reference a comparison to a familiar advertising role.

'It's sad,' Kimmel said.

The judgement was Kimmel's, rather than an assessment of Trump's political influence. His monologue centred on the contrast between the president's continued online posts and the comedian's view that the message had become repetitive.

The segment addressed Trump's comments on the Senate and migration, but did not examine the detail behind each of the president's claims.

excerpt: The Princess of Wales sent a Welsh-language message to BBC Radio 2 presenter Owain Wyn Evans during his charity cycling challenge, drawing praise for her pronunciation.
headline: 'Oh My Gosh!': BBC Host Praises Kate Middleton's 'Perfect' Welsh During Epic 'Royal Surprise'
html_content:
The Princess of Wales sent a Welsh-language message to BBC Radio 2 presenter Owain Wyn Evans on Friday, 13 November 2026, prompting him to exclaim 'Oh my gosh!' as he neared the finish of a charity cycling challenge. Evans later praised her pronunciation as 'perfect'.

The recording was played during Sara Cox's breakfast programme as the Welsh broadcaster tackled the final stage of a five-day ride for BBC Children in Need. His journey covered nearly 400 miles through Scotland, Northern Ireland, England and Wales, with Cardiff as the finishing point.

Cox teased a royal surprise before revealing that Catherine had sent encouragement in Evans's native language. He responded with a startled 'Oh my gosh!' before listening to the message.

A Royal Message in Welsh

Catherine opened with the Welsh greeting 'Bore da Owain' and introduced herself by her first name. She went on to praise Evans's progress, urge him to keep going and wish him well for the remainder of the ride.

The message was brief, but the choice of language gave it a personal touch. Rather than sending a conventional English greeting, the Princess addressed the Welsh-speaking presenter in the language he grew up with.

Asked by Cox what Catherine had said, Evans translated the encouragement for listeners. He appeared surprised by the unexpected message and repeatedly expressed his astonishment at the royal intervention.

Cox then asked about Catherine's pronunciation. Evans offered an emphatic verdict: 'Yeah, it was perfect! She's doing great!'

His praise reflected his assessment of the recording, rather than evidence that Catherine speaks Welsh fluently. The Princess delivered the message directly to Evans as he approached the end of the ride.

Evans thanked Catherine while continuing his journey through Wales. By Friday morning, the cycling effort had raised £2.9 million for BBC Children in Need, according to the Press Association.

The fundraising appeal supports projects providing practical help, safe spaces and opportunities for children experiencing hardship throughout the UK.

William and Kate's Welsh Lessons

The broadcast also recalled the royal couple's efforts to learn Welsh, a language associated with the title they have held since 2022.

During a visit to St Thomas's Church in Swansea that year, Prince William spoke about practising Welsh. The church supports local families through services including a food bank and a baby supply initiative.

The Rev Steven Bunting later recalled the Prince discussing expressions he had been learning. They included 'paned', a word used for a cup of tea, and 'bara brith', the traditional Welsh tea loaf.

During a visit to Powys in March 2026, William and Catherine met a group of Welsh learners at the Gallery Café. The Princess jokingly asked whether the group intended to test their Welsh.

When a participant praised William's progress, Catherine responded warmly, describing her husband as very smart. The exchange showed the couple discussing their language learning with people in Wales.

Friday's recording offered another public example of the couple's interest in Welsh. For Evans, it came as he neared the end of a five-day fundraising ride that had taken him across four nations.

The ride was BBC Radio 2's longest-distance fundraising challenge for Children in Need. The charity supports children and young people facing disadvantages across the United Kingdom.

excerpt: The US Senate has requested testimony from former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as lawmakers investigate suspected espionage allegations and chip export controls.
headline: US Senate Summons Former Nvidia Chief Jensen Huang and Commerce Chief Over China Security Concerns
html_content:
The US Senate has sought testimony from former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over suspected Chinese espionage and the handling of sensitive chip exports.

Senator Tim Scott sent both men letters on 12 November requesting testimony before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang was asked to appear voluntarily on 3 December, with the panel warning it could issue a subpoena to compel his attendance, the BBC reported on 13 November.

Lutnick has also been asked to testify on 10 December as questions mount over his department's approach to Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chip exports to China.

Huang Faces Questions From Both Chambers

The Senate request concerns reports of a personal relationship between Huang and a woman suspected by US intelligence officials of spying for China. His resignation from Nvidia has not ended congressional demands for an account of the relationship and its potential national security implications.

Three House of Representatives committees have separately requested a closed-door interview with Huang on 1 December, according to the BBC.

The committees oversee intelligence, foreign affairs and China-related issues. Their request would bring Huang before House lawmakers two days before his proposed Senate appearance.

Reuters reported that the House committee chairs had also warned of subpoenas if Huang and Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, failed to attend their respective interviews. Teter was asked to appear on 2 December.

Lutnick Scrutinised Over China Chip Restrictions

Lutnick faces scrutiny over claims that he delayed efforts to strengthen restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China.

The BBC reported that unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration had briefed US media about the allegations.

A Commerce Department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had 'proactively' agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.

The pressure extends beyond Congress. Reuters reported on 12 November that senior White House officials were discussing whether Lutnick should be removed, citing two people familiar with the situation.

Nvidia Appoints Interim Chief, Hires US Law Firm To Investigate Huang

Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim chief executive on 12 November after Huang resigned. The leadership change comes while the company's independent directors pursue their own investigation into the allegations surrounding its former chief.

They have retained Joon H. Kim, a former acting US attorney for the Southern District of New York, and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead the inquiry.

In a statement dated 10 November, the independent directors confirmed the appointment for an investigation.

The BBC reported that Kim previously worked as a government lawyer handling fraud and other criminal matters. The broadcaster also reported a separate investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

Nvidia Says No Evidence of Compromised Secrets

Nvidia's board has said it has 'no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,' while pledging to examine all available information.

The BBC, citing The New York Times, reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent senior Washington officials a memo earlier this year warning about Huang's close relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China.

Beijing has rejected allegations that Huang was targeted. China's foreign ministry said the claims were 'intended to smear and malign China'.

Reuters also reported that US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on 12 November that the Justice Department had not reached a conclusion on whether the woman was a spy.

excerpt: Rich Logis, founder of Leaving MAGA, says Republican losses and growing doubts among some former supporters may weaken Donald Trump's movement but will not necessarily end it.
headline: 'Maga Is Going To Survive' Warns Insider Despite Ex-Trump Devotees Exposing 'A Series of Lies and Falsehoods'
html_content:
Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections on 3 November, raising questions about Donald Trump's influence over his party. But Rich Logis, founder of Leaving MAGA and a former Trump supporter, warned that the result does not mean the movement is finished.

Speaking to Raw Story, Logis described hearing from people reconsidering their political loyalties. One person, according to his account, called MAGA a movement built on 'a series of lies and falsehoods'.

Logis believes the movement can survive even if its electoral appeal has weakened. His warning comes as Republicans debate how to recover from their losses while Trump remains president.

Leaving MAGA Offers a Place for Doubters

Logis founded Leaving MAGA to provide a community for people questioning their support for Trump and the political identity built around him. The organisation gives people opportunities to speak with others who have experienced similar doubts.

Some participants have described damaged relationships, disputes within families and the difficulty of reconsidering beliefs they once defended publicly. Those accounts suggest that changing political allegiances can involve more than deciding which candidate to support.

Logis told Raw Story that the organisation had 40 members and that its website attracted 660,000 unique visitors between January and early November 2026, compared with 542,000 during 2025.

The figures are attributed to Logis and have not been independently audited. Website visits also cannot establish how many visitors abandoned MAGA, changed their votes or were unique individuals across the periods compared.

The organisation has also sought publicity beyond its website. Logis said it placed more than 50 billboards across 29 states, including an advertisement in New York's Times Square, to reach supporters privately questioning the movement.

Independent reporting earlier this year documented the group's billboard campaign and its effort to reassure sceptical supporters that they were not alone. The article does not establish how many people saw the adverts or whether they prompted anyone to leave the movement.

A Republican Setback Is Not MAGA's End

Logis believes enquiries increased around the election, although more conversations with his organisation would not, by themselves, demonstrate a broader shift among Republican voters.

He also raised the possibility that some disillusioned supporters backed Democrats. That remains an interpretation, not a finding established by voting data. Election returns cannot identify an individual voter's past political loyalties.

The distinction matters for Democrats, who must decide whether their midterm gains represent a lasting realignment or a more temporary rejection of the governing party. The results alone do not show whether former Trump supporters changed their votes, stayed home or continued to back Republicans.

Logis has argued that former MAGA supporters should be met with patience rather than contempt. In his view, Democrats hoping to build alliances before the 2028 presidential election cannot assume that abandoning Trump means embracing every Democratic position.

His message also challenges predictions of an imminent collapse. MAGA has become entwined with Republican politics over the past decade, and its supporters do not all share the same reasons for remaining loyal.

For Logis, Republican infighting and electoral losses may create openings for people who want to leave. They do not, however, erase the sense of belonging that has sustained the movement. Nor do they show that the organisation's advertising caused any particular change in the election results.

His central warning is that an election defeat may weaken MAGA, but it does not settle what comes next.

excerpt: Eleanor Donaldson has been placed on the sex offenders' register for five years and given a three-year supervision order after a trial of the facts at Newry Crown Court
headline: Jeffrey Donaldson's Wife Eleanor Placed on Sex Offenders' Register for Five Years After Court Hearing
html_content:
Eleanor Donaldson, wife of jailed former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Jeffrey Donaldson, was placed on the sex offenders' register for five years at Newry Crown Court on Friday, 13 November 2026. The order followed a jury's findings in a trial of the facts, which did not result in criminal convictions.

Judge Paul Ramsey also imposed a three-year supervision and treatment order. In June, jurors found that the 60-year-old had carried out the acts alleged in five charges, including four involving aiding and abetting her husband's child sexual abuse.

Donaldson was found medically unfit to stand trial. The jury's findings did not amount to criminal convictions, a distinction that governs the court's options.

Eleanor Donaldson's Supervision Order and Appeal

According to Press Association reporting, Ramsey considered evidence from medical experts, a social worker and probation officials before imposing the order.

Under the three-year order, Donaldson will be supervised by a social worker from the Craigavon Community Mental Health Team. She must attend appointments, undergo treatment and allow home visits. Separately, police administer the sex offender notification requirements that will apply for five years.

Donaldson, from Dromore, County Down, appeared briefly by video link alongside her solicitor. After Ramsey explained the conditions, she nodded and confirmed that she understood. Lawyers represented her during the earlier trial, which she did not attend.

The fifth allegation concerned child cruelty. A trial of the facts determines whether alleged acts occurred when a defendant cannot participate in a conventional trial. It cannot result in a guilty verdict or a prison sentence.

Her legal team applied for permission to appeal the findings, as confirmed in September by the Northern Ireland Courts and Tribunals Service. Her husband is separately appealing his convictions.

Jeffrey Donaldson's Convictions and Sentence

Jeffrey Donaldson, 63, was convicted at Newry Crown Court on 22 June of 18 sexual offences against two women who were children when the abuse occurred. The convictions comprised one count of rape, 13 of indecent assault and four of gross indecency.

The Public Prosecution Service for Northern Ireland said the offending took place from 1985 to 1991 and from 1999 to 2008. Both complainants, whose identities are legally protected, gave evidence during his trial and attended Friday's hearing, according to Press Association.

On 15 October, Ramsey sentenced him to 15 years' imprisonment. Under the remission rules applicable to his offences, he is expected to serve seven and a half years in custody, with the remainder on licence. He continues to deny the offences.

Following sentencing, Police Service of Northern Ireland Detective Chief Inspector Leah Crothers said he had 'robbed them both of their childhood and innocence'.

Independent Review of Trial of the Facts Law

On 20 October, Justice Minister Naomi Long and Health Minister Robbie Butler appointed former Lord Justice of Appeal Sir John Gillen to review Northern Ireland's law and procedures on unfitness to plead and trials of the facts.

The review will consider public protection, victims' interests and whether conventional trials should become possible if defendants regain fitness to plead. An interim report is due by February 2027, with final findings expected in spring 2027.

excerpt: Pope Leo XIV met six survivors of abuse linked to Catholic clergy and institutions in Lima, Peru, hearing their experiences and discussing healing without announcing new reforms.
headline: Pope Leo XIV Meets Six Church Abuse Survivors in Peru Hours Before Emotional Return to His Former Diocese
html_content:
Pope Leo XIV met six survivors of abuse involving Catholic clergy and Church institutions in Lima on Thursday, 12 November. The private meeting lasted just over an hour and came hours before his planned return to Chiclayo, the Peruvian diocese he once led.

The Vatican said Leo listened individually to each survivor at the Apostolic Nunciature. One participant, Camila Bustamante, called it 'an important milestone', while cautioning that survivors rarely achieve closure.

Leo arrived in Peru on Wednesday after visits to Uruguay and Argentina. The 71-year-old pontiff served as a missionary and bishop in the country for about two decades before becoming pope in May 2025.

Pope Leo Listens to Six Survivors in Lima

The Holy See Press Office said the meeting began shortly after 4.30pm local time. After a greeting in the nunciature chapel, Leo heard individual accounts of suffering and discussed how the Church could respond more effectively to abuse.

The discussions covered listening to survivors, establishing the truth, supporting healing and creating safer environments. The Vatican said some participants had previously belonged to groups linked to the Sodalitium of Christian Life, but did not say all six had such connections.

The Peru-based Catholic organisation was suppressed in 2025 with Pope Francis' approval, after an investigation into allegations of sexual, physical and psychological abuse.

Leo thanked the survivors and expressed solidarity with others he could not meet, the Vatican said. Bustamante said the pope appeared 'very committed' to helping victims, but stressed that being heard does not necessarily bring closure.

The Vatican's account described the themes of the discussion, but did not set out specific steps arising from it.

Pope Leo's Earlier Argentina Meeting Draws Criticism

Thursday's encounter was Leo's second meeting with survivors during his South American tour. He had spoken with five survivors in Buenos Aires on Monday, 9 November.

The international group Ending Clergy Abuse criticised the earlier meeting for excluding others, including survivors of abuse at an institution for deaf children in Argentina. The criticism concerned Buenos Aires, not Lima.

The Vatican did not explain how participants in Argentina had been selected. It generally avoids discussing such arrangements to protect survivors' privacy.

Its account of Thursday's discussion announced no new reforms or timetable for implementing changes.

Pope Leo Prepares for an Emotional Chiclayo Return

Leo is due in Chiclayo on Friday, 13 November, for a homecoming in the city where he served as bishop before moving to Rome in 2023. Church organisers have said as many as one million people could attend an outdoor Mass near the city, although that remains a projection.

Leo mentioned Chiclayo in Spanish during his first address as pope in May 2025. Residents also remember his work during the pandemic and floods.

Rocio Zena, who said he helped after she lost her home in the 2023 floods, declared, 'Chiclayo is a party.'

In Lima, Leo attended public events, including a youth gathering attended by an estimated 60,000 people. In Chiclayo, he is also scheduled to meet clergy and visit a Catholic university where he previously served as chancellor.

Bustamante welcomed the encounter while emphasising the challenges survivors still face. 'Victims are accustomed to persevering, even when things become difficult,' she said.

excerpt: Greg Sargent and Holly Berkley Fletcher criticised Donald Trump's remarks about his eternal soul and debated whether they reflected political frustration or personal concerns.
headline: 'He Is Amoral': Pundits Slam Donald Trump for Giving Evangelicals 'The Middle Finger' After Defeat
html_content:
President Donald Trump's remarks about his eternal soul drew criticism from pundits Greg Sargent and Holly Berkley Fletcher during Thursday's Daily Blast podcast, with Sargent suggesting he was giving evangelical supporters 'the middle finger' after what he described as an electoral repudiation.

The discussion followed Trump's conversation with 60 Minutes about his soul. Sargent, of The New Republic, questioned the political timing of those remarks, while Berkley Fletcher, who writes about right-wing Christianity on Substack, examined their implications for white evangelical supporters.

Why Trump's Remarks Concerned the Pundits

Sargent described it as 'a little remarkable for him to talk this way after such a dramatic national repudiation of him.'

Berkley Fletcher argued that a politically astute leader would be trying to reinforce his remaining support. She characterised Trump's base as largely white evangelical Christian and argued that his comments would do little to strengthen that relationship.

'And this is certainly not the way to do it,' Fletcher stated. Her criticism focused on the tension she perceived between Trump's statements and evangelical beliefs about loving enemies, repentance and forgiveness. She argued that such moments leave supporters struggling to reconcile their religious commitments with his behaviour.

'Whenever he puts them on the spot by countering explicitly a really foundational evangelical Christian belief like loving your enemies or repenting or forgiving, these types of things, it really puts them in a very tough spot and sort of sends them scrambling,' Fletcher stated.

Election Frustration Shapes Sargent's Trump Theory

Sargent linked his interpretation to what he described as the 2026 election failures. He argued that Trump knew evangelical supporters had not turned out in the numbers he needed, despite his appeals for them to vote.

'I think Trump is essentially giving his evangelical supporters the middle finger in some sense,' Sargent stated.

In Sargent's reading, Trump's comments might express frustration with those supporters and indifference towards their beliefs about Heaven. That was his interpretation of Trump's motives, rather than an established explanation for the remarks.

Berkley Fletcher questioned whether Trump was calculating enough to act with that intention. Although she believed he would be upset with evangelical supporters, she offered a different explanation for his comments about his soul.

How Berkley Fletcher Interpreted Trump's Beliefs

'He usually tells us what he's thinking,' she explained.

Berkley Fletcher suggested Trump had long worried about the eternal destination of his soul and sometimes revealed that concern. She also argued that he lashes out when upset, while remaining uncertain about Sargent's theory of a deliberate political rebuke.

The disagreement concerned his possible motives. On his relationship with religion, the commentators expressed similar opinions. Sargent stated that he did not believe Trump had a religious bone in his body, and Berkley Fletcher described him as 'without belief of any kind.'

'I think he's amoral. I think he believes in his own narcissism and I think he's been using religion this entire time. They're a very easy mark for a conman,' she stated.

Berkley Fletcher argued that evangelical Christians' deeply held beliefs could be exploited by using familiar language and by supporting particular issues. She concluded, 'He's been using them the whole time. They've been a very cheap date, and he's taken advantage.'

excerpt: William, 17, was found alive after six days alone in Victoria's bushland, having survived on crisps and creek water before being rescued and treated for dehydration
headline: Who Is William, and Why Did He Go Missing? The Teen Who Left Camp To Collect Gear and Got Lost for Days
html_content:
A 17-year-old boy named William has been reunited with his family after surviving six days alone in dense Australian bushland, where he survived cold nights, warm daytime temperatures and a severe shortage of food. His disappearance prompted a major search involving police, specialist rescue teams, and volunteers before a helicopter crew finally located him alive on 12 November.

William, whose full identity was not initially released by police, had been on a weekend camping trip with his stepbrother near Walhalla East in Victoria, approximately 180 kilometres east of Melbourne. He disappeared on 6 November after leaving the campsite to retrieve additional equipment, unaware that the short journey would leave him stranded in unfamiliar and difficult terrain.

Who Is William?

William, also known as Will, is a 17-year-old from Victoria's Latrobe Valley region. His mother, Elizabeth Barkley, had dropped him off for what was reportedly his first independent camping trip.

The teenager, who has been publicly reported to have autism, was camping with his stepbrother in the Walhalla East area.

How Did William Disappear?

Police said William walked a short distance towards the original drop-off point to collect additional camping supplies. However, he failed to return, prompting his stepbrother to go looking for him. When the search proved unsuccessful, authorities were alerted.

William was last seen at approximately 4 p.m. on 6 November near Stoney Creek Road, between Cowwarr and Walhalla. He had reportedly left his mobile phone, food and drinking water at the campsite, leaving him without essential supplies as he became increasingly separated from the familiar surroundings.

According to his mother, William initially missed a turn while attempting to return to the campsite. He reportedly sheltered beneath bushes before setting off again the following day to find his way back. During his attempts to navigate the bushland, he lost his footing and slid down a steep embankment, leaving him unable to get back up.

'He didn't see there was a bit of a gap in a cliff, and he slid down and got stuck there,' Elizabeth, William's mother, told The Sydney Morning Herald. 'He couldn't move because his legs were sore.'

How William Survived Six Days Alone

William endured several nights outdoors with limited protection against the elements. Reports said he used towels and a pillow to keep himself warm, while a packet of chicken-flavoured crisps provided some food during his ordeal.

He also drank water from a nearby creek. After falling down the steep embankment, he remained near the waterway for approximately two days, unable to navigate the surrounding terrain.

How Was William Finally Found?

More than 100 emergency personnel and volunteers participated in the search, with police deploying specialist units, dog teams, divers and helicopters to cover the challenging landscape.

On 12 November, a police helicopter crew searching the Cowwarr area spotted a fishing tacklebox in bushland approximately two kilometres east of Stoney Creek. Using the aircraft's equipment to examine the area, officers located William lying nearby in a creek bed.

William was reunited with his mother before being taken to Latrobe Regional Hospital for treatment and monitoring. Although police initially described him as being in good spirits and generally good health, his condition subsequently required closer medical attention.

According to ABC News, he was transferred to intensive care overnight after his blood pressure dropped because of dehydration. He was later scheduled to be transferred to The Alfred in Melbourne for further testing and specialist assessment.

'Flight officers winched down and retrieved Will before bringing him back to the command post to reunite with his mum,' police said. 'Amazingly, William is in good spirits and for the most part, in good health,' they added, per DW Australia.

Barkley expressed overwhelming relief at seeing her son alive. 'I'm just over the moon he's alive,' Elizabeth said. 'He just stayed in one spot and waited to be rescued.' She also joked that he would not be allowed to go camping again without her. 'He's never leaving the house again,' Elizabeth told reporters. 'He's grounded for life.'

excerpt: British surgeon Goher Rahbour has described toxic fumes and extensive damage after an Israeli strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital, where six people were reportedly killed and 52 injured.
headline: British Surgeon Tells of Horror as Israeli Strike Kills Gaza Doctor He Operated With Hours Earlier
html_content:
A doctor killed in an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital had been operating beside British surgeon Dr Goher Rahbour just hours earlier, Gaza's Health Ministry said.

Rahbour was inside the hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, when an airstrike shook the building shortly after midnight on Thursday, 12 November. He described choking fumes and damage to the surgical department.

Volunteering at Nasser with the organisation IDEALS, Rahbour said he had worked with Dr Rizq Abu Shaira until about 8pm. 'I was operating with him up until about 8:00 PM,' he told The Independent.

Remembering his colleague, Rahbour described him as 'A very gentle soul'.

The strike killed six people and injured 52, according to Gaza's Health Ministry and medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), respectively. The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas commander and other militants allegedly operating from the hospital complex. It did not publicly provide evidence for the claims.

British Surgeon Describes Moments After Israeli Strike

Rahbour was on the fourth floor of the surgical department when the strike occurred, according to his account. The building shook. 'Initially there was a lot of toxic choking fumes,' he said, adding that staff put on face masks and moved towards the recovery area.

The area was severely damaged. Concrete and dust covered surgical facilities, leaving six operating theatres unusable, Rahbour said.

Gaza's Health Ministry said the attack struck the second floor of the surgical wing. Images from inside showed damage to wards and operating rooms, equipment and debris scattered across hospital beds.

Abu Shaira, a general surgeon, was among those killed, alongside a 13-year-old boy and at least one other patient, health officials said.

MSF said two injured doctors and another patient needed surgery and were treated by its team in a separate building. Its statement on 12 November said the emergency, radiology, laboratory and operating departments were out of service.

Nasser Hospital Loses Vital Surgical Capacity

Nasser is a major referral hospital for southern Gaza, serving an estimated 1.3 million people, according to MSF. Staff were already struggling with medical shortages.

Hospital director Ahmed al-Farra said operations and other services had been suspended. Nearby facilities lacked the resources to carry out the specialised procedures provided at Nasser, he said, leaving patients who needed them with uncertain options.

A strike on the hospital complex in August 2025 killed 22 people, including five journalists, according to reporting at the time.

Rahbour also described conditions outside the hospital, saying recent torrential rain and flooding had affected 70,000 tents in Gaza. Earlier that week, he had operated on a pregnant woman with a gunshot wound.

Israel's Military Claims and Hospital Warning Disputed

The Israeli military said Hamas had established a presence inside Nasser and that a commander had used it as a headquarters. Hamas denied the allegation. The commander named by Israel was not among those reported killed; the available accounts did not establish his whereabouts or condition.

MSF said its staff had previously reported armed men in parts of the hospital complex in January, but said the incidents did not occur in areas where it worked. The organisation later resumed core medical activities following security improvements. Its latest statement called for greater protection for healthcare workers and patients.

Al-Farra said there had been no warning immediately before Thursday's strike. Israel said it had issued warnings on several occasions, including recently, that military activity at the hospital must stop. The accounts do not establish whether any earlier warning specified the time or location of this strike.

Hospitals and medical personnel have special protection under international humanitarian law. That protection can cease under strict conditions if a hospital is used for acts harmful to the enemy outside its medical duties, subject to warning requirements. The available accounts do not establish whether those conditions were met in this case.

'No one's safe here,' Al-Farra said. Rahbour, who had operated beside Abu Shaira the previous evening, questioned the killing of doctors and damage to medical services. 'What is the motive? Why are you killing doctors and medical staff?' he asked.

excerpt: A series of posts by Donald Trump on Iran, domestic politics, Mexico and Nvidia prompted renewed online calls for the 25th Amendment, while the White House defended him.
headline: Is Donald Trump 'Unhinged'? Social Media Users Call for the 25th Amendment After Truth Social Spree
html_content:
President Donald Trump's early Thursday posting spree on Truth Social has sparked renewed social media calls invoking the 25th Amendment after he abruptly redirected Vice-President JD Vance away from diplomatic negotiations with Tehran.

According to reports, the 80-year-old president published eight separate posts within a six-hour window on Thursday, 12 November 2026, declaring that the United States no longer needed an agreement with Iran whilst addressing domestic crime, Republican legislative strategy, Mexican tariffs, and executive succession at Nvidia.

The sudden diplomatic pivot drew immediate commentary on X, where online critics and journalist Ray Locker invoked the constitutional provision governing presidential incapacity.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle forcefully rejected the criticism, accusing media critics at The Daily Beast of spreading baseless conspiracy theories whilst defending Trump's sharpness, work ethic, and excellent health.

Iran Shift Drives Truth Social Reaction

Trump wrote that he had asked Vance to focus his 'complete and total attention' on alleged corruption and crime in cities and states run by Democrats across the US. Vance had previously been assigned to lead talks with Tehran.

Trump wrote, 'We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.' He also claimed that the US had Iran's money and 'their Strait'.

The change of emphasis drew criticism on X. 'Trump can't make up his mind,' one user wrote. 'Maybe 25th Amendment looming.'

Another user posted, 'Tr*mp is totally unhinged. 25th Amendment.' An anti-Trump profile wrote, '🚨25th amendment for Grandpa Crazy needed right now.'

Journalist Ray Locker also invoked the constitutional provision, writing, 'Every day from now on will be a deeper journey into 25th Amendment territory.' These statements expressed the authors' opinions about Trump's fitness for office and their calls for action.

White House Defends Trump After Truth Social Spree

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle responded to the criticism by attacking the Daily Beast. He accused the publication of promoting 'baseless conspiracy theories about President Trump' and employed insulting terms about its staff.

Ingle defended Trump's health and performance, citing his 'sharpness, unmatched energy, relentless work ethic and historic accessibility'. He contrasted those descriptions with his allegation that Democrats and the media had concealed Joe Biden's mental and physical decline during the previous administration.

Ingle added, 'The President is working nonstop to solve problems and deliver on his promises, and he remains in excellent health.'

The assertions about Trump's health and accusations concerning the previous administration formed part of Ingle's defence. His response challenged criticism of the president as the posts addressed several subjects, from the vice president's assignment to the conduct of Republican lawmakers.

Other Truth Social Posts Target Both Parties

Five of Trump's eight posts centred on Democrats. He accused the party of 'MASSIVE BLUE STATE CORRUPTION' without providing evidence and described himself as its 'exact opposite'.

Trump also criticised Republican lawmakers for failing to pass the SAVE America Act and terminate the filibuster. He wrote that this would 'go down as being one of the greatest mistakes in the Political History of America. So sad!!!'

In another post, Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless it curbed what he claimed was an 'invasion' by Mexican immigrants. He wrote that Gina Hinojosa, whom he described as Texas's new governor, Border Patrol and ICE had been informed.

Trump also claimed that Jensen Huang had resigned as Nvidia chief executive and proposed Apple's Tim Cook as his replacement. He wrote, 'A Legend replaces a Legend!'

excerpt: A viral video appears to show a dog stopping a woman shortly before a man emerges from a dark alley, prompting claims that the animal sensed danger. The circumstances remain unverified.
headline: 'Animals Can Smell Danger': Dog Blocks Woman's Path Before Man Emerges From Dark Alley
html_content:
A dog may have prevented a woman from walking into a potentially dangerous encounter after a viral video showed the animal blocking her path moments before a man emerged from a dark alley. The footage, recorded on 12 February 2026 and shared on X, has attracted at least 2.5 million views, with many viewers convinced the dog saved the woman's life by recognising a potential threat before she did.

The clip captures an unsettling sequence that has prompted fresh discussion about animal instincts and the relationship between dogs and humans. Although the footage does not establish what the man's intentions were, the timing of the dog's intervention has led viewers to question whether the animal sensed something was wrong.

Dog Blocks Woman's Path Before Man Emerges

The video begins with a woman walking along what appears to be a relatively quiet street. A dog is lying beside the pathway, seemingly resting as pedestrians pass.

Then something changes.

As the woman approaches, the dog suddenly gets up and positions itself directly in her path. Rather than moving aside, the animal appears determined to stop her from continuing in the same direction.

The dog runs a few metres ahead of the woman before stopping while staring at her. She appears to notice the dog's behaviour and, instead of ignoring the warning, quickly changes direction and runs away.

Moments later, a man emerges from a dark alley ahead of where she had been walking.

切记！动物拦路，调头就跑！这个小姐姐太机灵了！ pic.twitter.com/nhs4U4h1yq

— 吉祥富 (@HGDA777) November 13, 2026

That brief sequence has become the central talking point surrounding the footage. The dog appears to have intervened before the man became visible, giving the woman an opportunity to leave the area.

However, the video does not establish whether the man was pursuing her, whether he intended to approach her or whether his appearance was connected to the dog's behaviour. There is also no confirmed information about the man's identity or the circumstances surrounding the recording.

Dog Saves Woman as Viewers Praise Its Instincts

The footage has generated an enthusiastic response on X, with viewers praising the animal for apparently recognising a situation that the woman had not yet noticed.

One commenter, reacting to the apparent warning, wrote, 'Animals can smell danger.' 'Animal instincts are always Sharp,' another added.

动物能闻到危险的气息

— 龙泉毅 (@JOJO85871961) November 13, 2026

A third viewer was even more convinced about the dog's role, declaring, 'That dog saved her life.'

That dog saved her life

— ThatDUDE201 (@ThatDUDE201) November 13, 2026

Other reactions explored the possibility that the animal had recognised something unusual about the approaching situation. One commenter recalled the saying, 'If an animal blocks your path, run.'

动物拦路就跑这个说法

— Zach (@zach_l_J) November 13, 2026

Another user suggested that dogs could detect adrenaline and changes in human behaviour. They also shared an anecdote about surveillance footage allegedly showing a dog confronting a stranger later identified as a human trafficker. However, that separate account was not independently verified and should not be treated as evidence about the incident in the viral video.

Several other commenters praised the woman for paying attention rather than dismissing the animal's behaviour. One described her decision as sensible, arguing that animals share the planet with humans and can display empathy towards them.

The broader reaction centred on two things. Viewers admired the dog's apparent awareness, while others highlighted the importance of paying attention to unusual animal behaviour.

IBTimes UK cannot independently verify the circumstances surrounding the recording or the man's intentions. The claims about the apparent danger should therefore be treated with caution.
