excerpt: An unnamed prison employee has alleged that convicted murderer Chris Watts formed close relationships with younger inmates, gave them gifts and exchanged lengthy letters
headline: 'Younger Guys Flock to Chris': Prison Source Alleges Watts Gives Male Inmates Gifts and Attention for Sex
html_content:
Chris Watts, the convicted killer serving five consecutive life sentences for murdering his pregnant wife and two young daughters, has reportedly formed close relationships with younger male inmates, according to an unnamed prison employee who alleges that he gives them gifts and personal attention.

The allegations were reported by the Daily Mail on 11 November, which cited an unnamed employee at Dodge Correctional Institution in Wisconsin, where Watts is serving five consecutive life sentences for murdering his pregnant wife, Shanann, and their two young daughters in 2018.

The employee alleged that Watts, 41, had recently been separated from another male inmate after correctional officers became suspicious of their relationship. The source also claimed that several younger prisoners seek out Watts' company, with some competing for his attention and receiving items purchased through his prison commissary account.

Prison Employee Describes Watts' Relationships

According to the employee, many of the prisoners drawn to Watts are men in their twenties who appear eager to gain his approval. The source alleged that Watts gives them gifts and spends considerable time with them, creating close attachments that sometimes appear to go beyond ordinary friendships.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, the employee said the younger male prisoners are attracted to Watts and 'follow him around, want to talk to him, want his attention.' 'Younger guys flock to Chris,' he said. 'He's really got a hold over them and they'll usually do whatever he wants.'

A former inmate also claimed that Watts writes lengthy letters to younger prisoners with whom he has developed close connections, sometimes after spending much of the day in their company. Some prisoners have reportedly developed romantic feelings for him, while the source suggested that Watts reciprocates their interest.

'Chris will see them all day and then at night write a long letter and hand it to them the next day. It really does make them feel special,' he told the news publication. 'There is some thinking among guards that these relationships are too intimate.'

The employee also suggested that some interactions between Watts and younger inmates may have crossed into physical territory. However, the source did not provide independently verifiable evidence establishing that sexual encounters had taken place.

Earlier Prison Incident Raised Questions

The latest allegations follow a 2020 disciplinary incident involving another prisoner, Dylan Tallman. According to records cited by the Daily Mail, officers discovered Watts' underwear, petroleum jelly, baby oil and other personal belongings inside Tallman's cell.

The two men had occupied neighbouring cells and reportedly communicated through an electrical outlet in the wall, which they nicknamed the 'holy outlet'. They also worked on Christian devotional writing together and described themselves as close friends. Tallman, however, denied that their relationship had become sexual. He was released in 2021 and subsequently lost contact with Watts, according to the report.

A former prisoner also described how inmates attempting sexual encounters sometimes take advantage of areas where surveillance cameras cannot clearly capture their activities. However, this account does not establish that Watts participated in any particular encounter or confirm the allegations made against him.

'Chris will see them all day and then at night write a long letter and hand it to them the next day. It really does make them feel special,' he told the news publication. 'There is some thinking among guards that these relationships are too intimate.' The employee also suggested that some interactions between Watts and younger inmates may have crossed into physical territory. However, the source did not provide independently verifiable evidence establishing that sexual encounters had taken place. Earlier Prison Incident Raised Questions The latest allegations follow a 2020 disciplinary incident involving another prisoner, Dylan Tallman. According to records cited by the Daily Mail, officers discovered Watts' underwear, petroleum jelly, baby oil and other personal belongings inside Tallman's cell. The two men had occupied neighbouring cells and reportedly communicated through an electrical outlet in the wall, which they nicknamed the 'holy outlet'. They also worked on Christian devotional writing together and described themselves as close friends. Tallman, however, denied that their relationship had become sexual. He was released in 2021 and subsequently lost contact with Watts, according to the report. A former prisoner also described how inmates attempting sexual encounters sometimes take advantage of areas where surveillance cameras cannot clearly capture their activities. However, this account does not establish that Watts participated in any particular encounter or confirm the allegations made against him.

excerpt: Commercial pilot Steve Frazer says he filmed unexplained lights during flights over Europe, including near Brussels, while acknowledging that their identity and apparent movement remain unconfirmed.
headline: 'Didn't Make Any Sense': UK Commercial Pilot Films Unexplained Baffling UFO Orbs Invading European Airspace
html_content:
UK commercial pilot Steve Frazer has spoken out after filming unexplained glowing UFO orbs above Europe, including during an October flight near Brussels, Belgium, where the lights' erratic movements defied conventional aviation explanations.

The 48-year-old captain from Cheshire, England, who brings 27 years of commercial cockpit experience, revealed that he has encountered similar mysterious lights across six or seven separate flights since 2022.

According to reporting by BroBible, citing the Daily Express, Frazer initially assumed the luminous shapes near the Belgian capital were from a distant military refuelling aircraft, but their baffling speed and persistent distance from him challenged his judgement.

Although the veteran aviator captured video footage showing bright orbs darting across the sky before abruptly vanishing, neither the recording nor his cockpit observations establish the objects' physical identity.

Near Brussels, UFO Orbs Defied His Expectations

The objects' erratic trajectory and apparent velocity quickly forced him to reconsider the conventional explanation.

'I just thought it was a military refuelling aircraft, but the way it was moving and [its] speed, it didn't make any sense,' Frazer stated. 'We were going towards them for seemingly ages and never got to them.'

According to BroBible, Frazer described bright orbs moving across the sky before suddenly vanishing. It also describes a video he recorded as showing several bright lights moving before disappearing. That description does not establish their identity.

His experience in the cockpit informed his reaction, but his description remains a personal observation rather than a confirmed explanation of the lights.

'I've been flying 27 years commercially, and it doesn't fit with anything I've seen previously,' he stated.

The Apparent Distance of UFO Orbs Puzzled Frazer

A particular feature of the sightings was the impression that the lights remained distant despite the aircraft travelling towards them. Frazer's description does not include a measured distance or speed, leaving those aspects of the encounter uncertain.

He considered whether satellites could explain what he witnessed, including those belonging to Elon Musk's Starlink network. His comments drew a distinction between the lights' movement and that of the satellites he had previously observed.

'I know what satellites normally look like; I've seen plenty of Starlinks and things like that,' he explained. 'They don't fit with that movement.'

The comparison reflects Frazer's assessment. BroBible does not provide technical analysis that establishes or excludes satellites as an explanation for the footage.

Another Pilot Saw Similar UFO Orbs, Says Frazer

Frazer also stated that another pilot saw similar lights while returning from Lithuania. BroBible does not identify that pilot, date the journey or provide enough detail to establish the relationship between the observations.

'We saw them in the same space and roughly the same direction, but it was ever so strange,' he stated.

BroBible separately describes a reported encounter involving a British Airways jet over England and a reported sighting photographed by two pilots over Ohio at 41,000 feet. The article does not date either incident or establish a connection with Frazer's observations. These remain separate claims rather than corroboration of what he witnessed.

Frazer did not claim that aliens were responsible for the lights over Belgium. His description was narrower, referring to something he could not recognise rather than identifying its origin.

'Technically, in a sense, it's an unidentified object that seems to be flying,' he stated.

excerpt: Lori and Jensen Huang jointly control about 800 million Nvidia shares through trusts and companies, bringing renewed focus on their financial arrangements after Jensen's resignation.
headline: Lori Huang's Role in Jensen Huang's $140 Billion Nvidia Fortune Revealed After CEO Exit
html_content:
Lori Huang's role in the Nvidia fortune shared with her husband, Jensen Huang, has come into sharper focus following his resignation as chief executive of the chipmaker. Hundreds of millions of Nvidia shares are held through trusts and limited liability companies in which Lori and Jensen have shared control, according to Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings.

The allegations surrounding her husband's conduct have brought renewed attention to the family's financial arrangements. Those ownership structures could also have implications for the family's stake following Jensen's departure from the company's leadership.

Lori Huang and Jensen Huang Share Control of Nvidia Wealth

Lori and Jensen have shared beneficial ownership of about 800 million Nvidia shares, worth roughly $135 billion (£102 billion), according to the filings described in the supplied CNBC report. Jensen separately holds about 70 million shares valued at approximately $12 billion (£9.1 billion). These figures are estimates based on share prices and should not be treated as fixed valuations.

The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Living Trust holds approximately 530 million shares, with the couple serving as co-trustees. They also jointly oversee the Huang 2012 Irrevocable Trust, which holds 31.4 million shares, and the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust, with approximately 109 million shares.

A further approximately 74 million shares are held through limited liability companies whose sole member is the living trust. The filings state that 'Each of Mr. Huang and his wife may be deemed to have shared beneficial ownership of, and to exercise shared voting and investment power over' the shares.

Lori is also president of the Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation. The philanthropic organisation holds Nvidia shares and reported assets of approximately $9 billion (£6.8 billion) in 2024, according to its tax filings. The SEC filing states that the couple may be deemed to share voting and investment power over the foundation's shares, but neither has a personal financial interest in them.

Living trusts can help couples avoid probate and manage assets after one spouse dies. Established in 1995, the Huangs' trust may be revocable, although its precise terms are not publicly available.

A revocable trust can generally be amended, and shares may be divided or sold, subject to applicable restrictions. Kathleen Martone, a partner at Varnum LLP, likened the arrangement to 'a joint checking account'.

Irrevocable trusts are harder to change. The 2012 trust may be an intentionally defective grantor trust, a structure that can move assets outside an estate while leaving the grantor responsible for income tax. The remainder trust may benefit the couple's children, although its precise terms have not been confirmed.

Leslie Evans, a partner at Withers, said a division of shares could involve restrictions. Jensen might retain the stock while Lori received other assets or an equalisation payment. The outcome would depend on the trust documents and applicable law, rather than simply on the couple's relationship.

Jensen Huang's Resignation Puts Lori's Financial Position in the Spotlight

The scrutiny of the family's wealth comes after Nvidia confirmed on 12 November that Jensen had resigned as president, chief executive and a member of the board, effective immediately. The company appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive while beginning its search for a permanent successor.

The departure followed mounting scrutiny of Huang after allegations of extramarital relationships emerged. The latest involved Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice-president of healthcare, who was reported to have had a relationship with Huang while reporting directly to him.

The claim was attributed to The New York Times, which cited five people who had worked at Nvidia. Neither Powell nor Nvidia had immediately responded to requests for comment.

Huang had previously acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a statement published by Nvidia on 8 November. The admission and subsequent allegations have drawn attention to Lori, although she has not been accused of wrongdoing. They have also given the family's shareholding structure renewed relevance.

excerpt: Elon Musk said hiring Jensen Huang would be an honour after a public appeal on X, but no job offer or employment discussions have been announced.
headline: Elon Musk Eyes Jensen Huang After Nvidia CEO Resigns Amid Alleged Chinese Spy Affair Controversy
html_content:
Elon Musk expressed openness to hiring Jensen Huang in an exchange on X before Nvidia announced its co-founder's resignation as president, chief executive and board member.

The Tesla billionaire did not identify a role or indicate that employment discussions were taking place.

His response followed a public appeal from the financial news account ZeroHedge to recruit Huang.

Nvidia subsequently confirmed Huang's immediate departure and appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive while it searches for a permanent replacement.

Musk Responds to Jensen Huang Hiring Suggestion

'Elon please hire Jensen,' ZeroHedge wrote on X. Musk replied, 'That would be an honor.'

The brief exchange offered no details about which of Musk's businesses might employ Huang. No formal job offer or employment discussions have been announced, and neither executive has announced plans to work together.

Musk's response came before Nvidia confirmed the resignation, rather than after the company's announcement. It expressed willingness to consider the suggestion without outlining a recruitment process, a prospective position or any arrangement between the two executives.

Bloomberg stated that Musk and Huang have known each other for at least a decade. Musk has previously praised the Nvidia co-founder, placing his response within a longstanding professional relationship.

In a separate post on X, Musk wrote, 'Old friends are the best friends. Jensen rocks.'

Nvidia Announces Jensen Huang's Departure

Nvidia confirmed that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and a member of its board with immediate effect. Its board acknowledged his contributions to the company, which he co-founded in 1993 and led for more than three decades.

During that period, Huang developed Nvidia into a major supplier of the computing hardware behind artificial intelligence. His experience spans chip technology, artificial intelligence infrastructure and large-scale computing, all areas relevant to Musk's expanding technology interests.

Kress's appointment provides interim leadership as Nvidia searches for a permanent chief executive. The company's announced succession arrangements do not identify a future role for Huang at any of Musk's businesses.

For Huang, the departure marks the end of more than three decades leading the company he helped establish. He has not publicly indicated what he intends to do next.

That would be an honor

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 12, 2026

Technology Links Jensen Huang and Musk

Nvidia supplies graphics processing units that Tesla employs to train artificial intelligence models for its self-driving technology. The chipmaker's technology has also supported Tesla's driver-assistance systems, although the automaker continues developing its own chips.

Musk has expressed his intention to continue purchasing Nvidia hardware. That commercial relationship connects the two executives through the computational demands of Tesla's development work, as well as Musk's broader investment in artificial intelligence.

Tesla is developing autonomous driving technology and humanoid robots. Musk's artificial intelligence ventures also require substantial computing power, giving Nvidia's hardware a role in the technology supporting those ambitions.

Huang's expertise could be relevant to businesses pursuing those projects. However, the possibility of closer collaboration remains unresolved, with Musk's public comment providing no indication of responsibilities, terms or a timetable.

Nvidia's search for a permanent chief executive continues under Kress's interim leadership. Neither Musk nor Huang has announced an agreement for Huang to join one of Musk's companies.

excerpt: Trump directs JD Vance to focus on alleged corruption in Minnesota, California, and Illinois, raising questions over future US-Iran negotiations with Tehran.
headline: Trump Redirects JD Vance From Iran Diplomacy to Investigating Democratic States After VP Blames War for GOP Defeat
html_content:
Donald Trump has redirected Vice President JD Vance from Iran diplomacy to investigating alleged corruption in Democrat-led states, days after Vance blamed the war for the Republican Party's midterm defeat. The move shifts Vance's immediate focus from negotiations with Tehran to Trump's domestic political priorities, while raising questions about the future of US diplomatic efforts.

In Truth Social posts on Thursday, 12 November, Trump said Washington no longer needed a diplomatic agreement with Iran and named Minnesota, California, and Illinois as states requiring scrutiny. The directive marks a change in Vance's responsibilities after months of leading US negotiating delegations seeking a ceasefire and renewed nuclear talks with Tehran.

Trump Says US No Longer Needs an Iran Deal

'We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,' Trump wrote on Truth Social. He also claimed the US had secured substantial financial and strategic advantages from the conflict, referring to hundreds of billions of dollars and control of the Strait of Hormuz. These claims have not been independently established.

Earlier in the week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly told G7 counterparts in Paris that Trump had considered resuming military action or pursuing another agreement with Tehran. The administration instead opted to focus on isolating the Iranian regime. Vance had previously been involved in diplomatic efforts, including considering direct discussions with senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei. Trump's latest instruction shifts his immediate priorities away from those negotiations. Oil prices rose and stocks declined following the president's comments, as markets reacted to uncertainty over the conflict.

Vance Blamed Iran War for Republican Election Defeat

The timing of the announcement follows Vance's unusually blunt assessment of the Republican Party's midterm losses, which cost it control of Congress. 'The reason we lost is the war,' Vance wrote on X last week, linking the electoral setback to the Iran conflict and its impact on the cost of living.

He also questioned whether the consequences of the military campaign had justified its political cost, particularly the loss of the Senate for the next six years. 'But everyone knows why we lost,' he added. Trump has continued to defend the military campaign, maintaining that it was necessary and that he would not have handled the situation differently.

One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was…

— JD Vance (@JDVance) November 4, 2026

Vance to Focus on Alleged Fraud in Democrat-Led States

Vance will now focus on his existing role as chairman of Trump's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, established through an executive order earlier this year. Trump named Minnesota, California, and Illinois in his announcement.

'I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the US,' he wrote. The president alleged that billions of dollars were being stolen every month and claimed that tackling the misconduct could help balance the federal budget. These remain allegations, not established findings.

Democratic Investigations Add to Political Tensions

The announcement comes amid tensions over investigations planned by congressional Democrats. Incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman Robert Garcia recently warned administration officials and corporate executives to prepare for scrutiny over Trump's business dealings and immigration enforcement.

Trump accused Democratic leaders of using investigations into his administration to distract from alleged misconduct in their own jurisdictions. He also criticised Republican senators for failing to pass the Save America Act, describing the setback as damaging to the party's midterm performance.

What Happens to US-Iran Relations Now?

Trump's directive leaves questions about who will lead any future negotiations with Tehran. Rubio's reported remarks suggest the administration is prioritising the isolation of the Iranian regime, but the announcement does not establish that all diplomatic channels have closed. For Vance, the move marks a shift from his prominent role in Iran diplomacy to a domestic anti-fraud agenda, following his public criticism of a conflict he identified as a major reason for the party's election defeat.

excerpt: Jemima Goldsmith says she contacted police during an alleged violent incident involving Russell Brand in 2014, after which officers confirmed attending her Oxfordshire home following a complaint.
headline: Russell Brand's Ex Reveals She Called Police To Have Him Removed From Her Home After Alleged Violent Incident
html_content:
Jemima Goldsmith has revealed that she called police to remove former partner Russell Brand from her Oxfordshire home following an alleged violent confrontation in 2014.

The television producer shared the disclosure on X on Monday, 9 November 2026, hours after the 51-year-old comedian was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison at Southwark Crown Court for rape and sexual assault.

Thames Valley Police subsequently confirmed that officers attended an Oxfordshire address on 25 July 2014 after a woman reported her partner had assaulted her, ensuring he left the property at her request without making any arrests.

Goldsmith, who dated Brand for roughly a year, stated she endured violence, coercive control, and abuse during their relationship, explaining that she avoided pressing charges or speaking out earlier to shield her teenage children from intense media scrutiny.

Praising the courage of the four women whose trial testimony secured Brand's conviction for offences committed between 2004 and 2009, Goldsmith confirmed she has neither seen nor spoken to him since 2014.

Police Confirmed They Attended Goldsmith's Home

Thames Valley Police confirmed that officers were dispatched to an address in Oxfordshire on 25 July 2014, after a woman reported that her partner had assaulted her.

The force said officers spoke with the complainant, considered her concerns and offered assistance before ensuring her partner departed the property at her request.

No arrests were made in connection with the incident, according to police. The force's confirmation provides independent corroboration that officers attended following an assault complaint and arranged for Brand to leave, although it does not establish that an assault took place or that he committed a criminal offence during the encounter.

Goldsmith Explained Why She Did Not Pursue Charges

In the statement, Goldsmith said she decided against pursuing charges or discussing the experience publicly to shield her children from the intense scrutiny that could follow.

She also confirmed that she had not seen or spoken to Brand since their relationship ended in 2014.

'I have had my own personal experience of his violence, coercive control and abuse. I had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident,' Goldsmith said in her social media post.

I am going to describe some painful and personal things in relation to Russell Brand because I have been put in a position now where I feel that I have no choice other than to do so, given the misleading reports and speculation around the facts of a harassment injunction that was…

— Jemima Goldsmith (@Jemima_Khan) November 9, 2026

'I have neither seen nor spoken to Brand since that period in 2014. Whilst my pain in relation to this, pales in comparison to what the women have testified in court have suffered, this was a difficult period in my life which has had a lasting impact,' she added.

The television producer also expressed support for the women who testified against Brand, praising their decision to come forward. 'I am in awe of the courageous women who came forward at Brand's trial, told their stories, testified and ensured justice was done,' she said.

Brand Sentenced to More Than 10 Years in Prison

Goldsmith's disclosure came after Brand received a 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence at Southwark Crown Court on 9 November.

He was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women, following a trial in which prosecutors presented evidence of offences committed between 2004 and 2009.

Brand had denied the charges and maintained that he had never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity. However, the jury found him guilty of the four offences, while clearing him of two additional rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Meanwhile, the Metropolitan Police confirmed that detectives are actively examining additional information concerning Brand following his conviction.

excerpt: Bitcoin falls below $69,000 after $1.47 billion in crypto liquidations as Peter Schiff declares a long-term bear market and warns of further losses.
headline: Peter Schiff Says Bitcoin Is In a 'Long-Term' Bear Market as Prices Crash After $1.4B of Crypto Liquidations
html_content:
Bitcoin has plunged below $69,000 after nearly $1.4 billion in leveraged crypto positions were wiped out, prompting gold bull Peter Schiff to state that the world's largest cryptocurrency has entered a long-term bear market, with further losses potentially ahead.

In a recent X post, Schiff challenged Bitcoin holders to explain why the cryptocurrency was trading below its 2021 record high, despite nearly five years of adoption, institutional investment, and growing mainstream acceptance.

'Bitcoin is in a long-term bear market. The long-term trend is down,' he wrote, warning investors not to confuse past price gains with evidence of a lasting recovery.

The sell-off has given fresh ammunition to one of Bitcoin's most outspoken critics. Bitcoin fell as low as 7% over 24 hours to $68,408 per token.

BTC Liquidations Mount as Critical Support Breaks

The market downturn triggered a substantial wave of forced selling as leveraged traders betting on higher prices were caught on the wrong side of the move.

CoinGlass data showed $1.47 billion in cryptocurrency liquidations over 24 hours, including $1.31 billion in long positions. More than 175,000 traders were liquidated.

Bitcoin was not alone in the market downturn. Ethereum fell approximately 6% to $1,921, while BNB and XRP also suffered losses.

Quantitative trader KillaXBT identified the $69,000 region, corresponding to Bitcoin's November 2021 bull-market high, as a crucial technical level. The trader warned that failure to find support there could open the door to fresh lows.

Why Schiff Believes Bitcoin's Economics Are Broken

Schiff's argument goes beyond technical charts. The economist has repeatedly questioned Bitcoin's underlying value, arguing that unlike gold, it produces no earnings, dividends, or cash flow.

He believes Bitcoin's recent demand has become increasingly dependent on financial products, exchange-traded funds, and corporate treasury buyers rather than people seeking to use it as money.

In recent remarks reported by a media outlet, Schiff argued that much of the capital entering Bitcoin could prove temporary. If ETF investors and companies holding Bitcoin begin withdrawing their money, he believes selling pressure could accelerate.

He has also challenged the argument that Bitcoin can endure several years of weakness before recovering, suggesting the current market structure makes this downturn fundamentally different. His preferred alternative remains gold, which he considers a tangible asset with monetary value rather than a speculative digital instrument.

Michael Saylor and Schiff's BTC Feud Intensifies

The latest warning also revives Schiff's long-running disagreement with Strategy chairman Michael Saylor, one of Bitcoin's most prominent corporate advocates. Schiff has repeatedly questioned Saylor's aggressive BTC accumulation strategy, particularly the company's buying and selling decisions.

In September, Schiff highlighted Strategy's sale of 6,948 Bitcoin between late May and early August for approximately $431.8 million, before criticising Saylor for subsequently buying Bitcoin back at prices above $80,000.

Schiff predicted that Strategy could eventually sell again at lower prices, questioning the sustainability of its approach. He also dismissed Saylor's bullish interpretation of the stalled Clarity Act, arguing that the executive would have portrayed either legislative outcome as positive for Bitcoin.

For Saylor, Bitcoin remains a long-term strategic asset rather than a short-term trading opportunity, but Schiff's warning comes at an uncomfortable moment for crypto bulls as leveraged investors face substantial losses.

Remember, investments are subject to market risks, and past performance does not guarantee future returns.

excerpt: Donald Trump's repeated leg tapping during a Veterans Day ceremony attracted attention after commentator David Pakman suggested it might be a physical therapy cue.
headline: Donald Trump's Leg Tapping Might Be a Physical Therapy Technique, Commentator Suggests
html_content:
Donald Trump's leg tapping at a Veterans Day memorial service at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia could be a physical therapy technique, commentator David Pakman has suggested.

The president's vocal critic described his theory as speculation and acknowledged that he did not know what explained the movement.

The appearance renewed questions about Trump's mental and physical well-being during his second term in the White House.

Official reports from his physician state that he is in good health, while Pakman's comments focused on a movement he claimed to have noticed repeatedly over the past year.

At Arlington, Trump's Leg Tapping Drew Attention

Trump laid a wreath at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and delivered an address during the occasion honouring veterans of the United States Armed Forces. Viewers noticed him repeatedly tapping his right leg as he walked.

On his YouTube channel, Pakman described what he considered a recurring movement in different locations. He suggested one possible explanation was tactile cueing, a technique involving physical touch or tapping to assist someone in performing a movement.

Pakman qualified his remarks by stating that 'we have no medical transparency on this guy, other than he's the healthiest president ever'. That was his criticism of the information available about Trump's health, rather than a medical assessment of the president.

Could Leg Tapping Be a Therapy Cue?

Tactile cueing uses touch, pressure, tapping or objects to guide a patient's movement, improve body awareness and prompt proper muscle activation.

Explaining his theory, Pakman stated, 'This is a real technique for people in physical therapy, including in neurological rehab. Sometimes if a person has trouble, coordinating a certain movement or a certain movement, they are told to use a physical touch or a tap, which is like an extra sensory input which will help you perform that movement.'

He described cueing as preparation for a movement that someone finds difficult, offering examples from neurological rehabilitation. His question was whether Trump might be tapping his leg to remind himself to prepare for a more difficult movement.

'For example, you might use a cueing technique if you have Parkinson's, or certain neurological injuries, or movement disorders, in order to prepare yourself for a certain movement that's more difficult.'

Those examples were part of Pakman's explanation of cueing. They did not establish a connection between Trump's tapping and any particular illness. There is no suggestion that Trump has Parkinson's or another neurological condition.

Pakman's central qualification was explicit. 'This is a real rehab concept. We don't know that's what Trump is doing.'

Other Questions Surround Trump's Leg Tapping

Pakman also noted the White House's acknowledgement that Trump has chronic venous insufficiency. The condition prevents leg veins from properly returning blood to the heart, causing blood to pool in the lower limbs.

It can cause swelling and is more common in older people. Pakman did not think it explained the tapping, although he questioned whether there might be a relationship between the condition and the movement.

He also mentioned other people's suggestions about stiffness, an orthopaedic problem or leg braces. These were additional theories raised in his commentary, rather than established explanations for what viewers observed at Arlington.

excerpt: Sarah Kellen told Congress FBI agents left St Thomas airport without questioning her after Jeffrey Epstein intervened, as lawmakers call for witnesses to be reinterviewed.
headline: Epstein Report Reveals FBI Agents Left Without Questioning Two Women After He Personally Intervened
html_content:
A former assistant to Jeffrey Epstein has told Congress that two FBI agents left St. Thomas Airport in 2007 without questioning her or another woman after the financier intervened, according to her testimony. The encounter also shaped how she understood the allegations against him: she said she believed his account because investigators had never asked for hers.

Sarah Kellen recounted the incident during a 21 May 2026 interview with the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. She said an airport handler told her FBI agents wanted to speak to her and another woman. Epstein told them to wait, then approached the agents himself. About 10 minutes later, he returned and said: 'Okay, let's go.' The group boarded the plane.

Kellen Says Investigators Never Heard Her Account

Kellen told lawmakers that Epstein portrayed himself as the victim of women seeking his money. Because law enforcement had not questioned her, she said she had little information beyond his explanation.

'Nobody questioned me, nobody approached me, so I only had his narrative,' she testified.

She also said she did not know she had been named as a potential co-conspirator in the 2007 non-prosecution agreement between Epstein and federal prosecutors until it became public. The agreement extended federal protection to four women named as potential co-conspirators, including Kellen. She said she had not been consulted before it was signed.

The report does not establish what Epstein said to the agents, why they left, or whether they intended to conduct formal interviews. The airport account is presented through Kellen's testimony, not an independent finding about the agents' actions or motives.

Congressional Report Calls for Witnesses to Be Reinterviewed

The Republican-led House committee released its 137-page report on 10 November after a 15-month investigation into the handling of the Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell cases. It argues that federal investigators and prosecutors repeatedly failed to pursue evidence and witnesses that could have strengthened the case against Epstein.

The report criticises the 2007 agreement, which allowed Epstein to avoid federal prosecution in Florida in exchange for pleading guilty to state charges. In 2008, he pleaded guilty in Florida state court to soliciting prostitution from a minor. He received an 18-month sentence and was released after serving about 13 months.

The committee recommends that the Justice Department interview or reinterview key witnesses, investigate allegations involving Epstein's associates, and give survivors access to their personal records. It identifies longtime assistant Lesley Groff as a witness who should be questioned further.

A Separate Airport Incident Involved a Target Letter

The report also describes a separate episode at Teterboro Airport in New Jersey. Investigators planned to serve a target letter on another woman they regarded as an alleged co-conspirator, but Epstein diverted his aircraft to the US Virgin Islands, preventing delivery.

The committee does not identify this as the same incident Kellen described at St. Thomas. The accounts concern different women and separate investigative actions.

The report's recommendations put renewed attention on people who may hold information about Epstein's operations. Kellen's account illustrates one consequence of the earlier investigative gaps: without being interviewed, she said, she accepted Epstein's version of events. The committee says further interviews are needed to pursue outstanding leads and address failures that left survivors without adequate protection.

excerpt: In 2027, 401(k) limits and IRA thresholds rise, a new Saver's Match offers up to $1,000, and Social Security benefits increase by 3.6%.
headline: Millions of Americans Face Five Major Retirement Changes in 2027 as the IRS Raises 401(k) Limits
html_content:
Millions of Americans will see major retirement changes in 2027, including higher 401(k) limits, a federal savings match worth up to $1,000 and a 3.6% Social Security increase. These developments could affect workers, older savers, and retirees.

The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) announced new contribution limits on 12 November 2026, while the Social Security Administration (SSA) confirmed its annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA).

1. The 401(k) Contribution Limit Rises to $25,500

Workers can contribute up to $25,500 to their 401(k) accounts in 2027, compared with $24,500 in 2026. The limit also applies to 403(b) plans, governmental 457 plans, and the federal Thrift Savings Plan. Employees aged 50 and older can contribute an additional $8,500, bringing their total to $34,000. The SIMPLE retirement account limit will increase from $17,000 to $17,500, while certain eligible plans will have a $19,100 limit.

2. More Taxpayers Could Qualify for IRA Benefits

The annual IRA contribution limit will remain $7,500, with an additional $1,100 allowance for people aged 50 and older. However, higher income thresholds could make more taxpayers eligible for traditional IRA deductions or Roth IRA contributions.

The traditional IRA deduction phase-out range will rise to $83,000-$93,000 for eligible single taxpayers and $133,000-$153,000 for married couples filing jointly. Roth IRA income limits will increase to $158,000-$173,000 for single taxpayers and heads of household, and $250,000-$260,000 for married couples filing jointly.

3. Workers Aged 60 to 63 Can Save Up to $37,250

Eligible workers aged 60 to 63 during 2027 can make enhanced catch-up contributions of up to $11,750 to qualifying workplace plans, up from $11,250 in 2026. Combined with the standard $25,500 allowance, their potential annual contribution reaches $37,250. This replaces the ordinary $8,500 catch-up allowance for this age group rather than adding to it. Eligibility depends on the workplace plan.

4. A New Federal Retirement Savings Match Begins

The federal Saver's Match programme will begin in 2027, replacing the Saver's Credit for qualifying retirement plan and IRA contributions. Eligible savers can receive a federal contribution worth up to 50% of qualifying savings, capped at $1,000 annually on contributions of up to $2,000.

The full match applies to modified adjusted gross incomes of up to $20,500 for single taxpayers, $30,750 for heads of household, and $41,000 for married couples filing jointly. It gradually decreases and becomes unavailable at $35,500, $53,250, and $71,000, respectively. Applicants must be at least 18, meet US tax-residency requirements, not be qualifying students, and not be claimed as dependants.

The match goes directly into an eligible retirement account, even if the recipient owes no federal income tax. Claims will be made through 2027 tax returns filed in 2028. The Saver's Credit will remain available for qualifying ABLE account contributions.

5. Social Security Payments Increase by 3.6%

The SSA has confirmed a 3.6% COLA beginning in January 2027, affecting nearly 72 million beneficiaries. It is the largest annual increase since 2023. The average retired worker's monthly benefit will rise from $2,095 to approximately $2,170, adding $75. For retired couples receiving benefits, the average payment will increase from $3,238 to approximately $3,355.

However, individual increases vary, and Medicare Part B premiums and other deductions can reduce the additional amount received. The 2027 Part B premium has not yet been officially announced.

What the Changes Mean for Retirement Planning

Americans should review their retirement contributions, check eligibility for the new federal match, and consider enhanced catch-up allowances. Retirees should also account for healthcare costs when assessing higher Social Security payments. Understanding these changes could help households make better-informed retirement decisions.

excerpt: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang is set to forfeit $108 million in unvested pay after resigning as CEO, while falling shares cut his fortune by nearly $11 billion.
headline: Jensen Huang Forfeits $108M—Could His Billion-Dollar Fortune Take Another Hit?
html_content:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang is set to forfeit approximately $108 million in unvested equity compensation following his resignation as chief executive, according to Bloomberg. The forfeited awards represent only a fraction of his multibillion-dollar fortune, raising questions about whether other developments could affect his remaining wealth.

Huang, 63, stepped down following reports of multiple extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whose suspected links to Chinese intelligence have been the subject of US scrutiny. However, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had not reached a conclusion on whether she was acting as a Chinese spy. Jensen Huang's departure coincided with a sharp decline in Nvidia's share price, wiping billions of dollars from his estimated net worth.

Huang's Net Worth Falls Nearly $11B as Nvidia Shares Slide

Nvidia shares have reportedly fallen nearly 13% this week, according to the New York Post, reducing the estimated value of Jensen Huang's holdings. As per Forbes, his estimated net worth dropped from approximately $154 billion to $143.3 billion by Thursday, a decline of nearly $11 billion. The downturn placed him 13th on the publication's global wealth rankings, behind Walmart heir Jim Walton and his family.

Still, Huang remains one of Nvidia's largest shareholders, holding a stake exceeding 3.5% in the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Bloomberg reported that the forfeited awards account for less than 0.1% of Huang's estimated net worth.

Nvidia Faces Questions Over Huang's Exit and Possible Testimony

Crisis communications expert Patrick Riccards suggested Nvidia's leadership would prefer to avoid further confrontation with its former chief executive. 'I think Nvidia just needed to be done with this,' Riccards told the New York Post. 'They're not fools. They realise that all of them are very wealthy because of him, and they don't want him to be an enemy,' he added.

Nvidia could also face further congressional scrutiny, with its interim chief executive potentially called to testify. Riccards suggested Huang could also appear before lawmakers, saying the company's board of directors 'has to be very wary of what he's gonna say.'

How a Divorce Could Affect Huang's Wealth

A hypothetical divorce from his wife of more than 40 years, Lori Huang, could also have significant financial implications, although there is no confirmed indication that the couple plans to separate. As per the New York Post, securities filings show that approximately 740 million Nvidia shares are held through family trusts and limited liability companies.

Legal experts cited by the outlet also discussed the possibility of a multibillion-dollar settlement if the couple were to divorce. Huang will also lose the cash compensation associated with his former executive role, which reportedly amounted to approximately $7.5 million annually over the past two years.

A Potential Share Sale Could Unsettle Investors

Instead of seeking to force Huang to give up his shares, Nvidia may be more concerned about the potential market reaction if he decides to sell, including whether such a move could prompt other shareholders to follow suit, Riccards said. 'I'm sure he's (Huang) sitting down with financial planners now to determine how much of his stock he should keep and how much he should drop,' he said.

'Once they find out that he's dumping shares, it's gonna devastate this company's financial picture,' he added. There is no confirmed indication that Huang intends to sell his holdings.

excerpt: University of Maryland student Maria Flores Garcia has described missing classes and difficult conditions while detained with her mother at an ICE facility in Louisiana.
headline: ICE Detains University of Maryland Student on Full-Tuition Scholarship With No Criminal Record, Lawyers Say
html_content:
A 19-year-old University of Maryland student who graduated as her high school's valedictorian and earned a full-tuition scholarship is being held in ICE detention after accompanying her mother to an immigration appointment in Baltimore.

Maria Flores Garcia, who hopes to become an emergency-room doctor, has no criminal record, according to her lawyers. She is now missing classes while detained alongside her mother in Louisiana.

'I keep thinking, "Oh, I should be doing this in my math class, or going to my class,"' she told WUSA9.

Flores Garcia arrived in the United States from El Salvador aged nine. She graduated as Parkdale High School's valedictorian in May 2026 before enrolling at university to study public health.

ICE Detains University of Maryland Student During Immigration Check-In

Flores Garcia accompanied her mother, Mirna Aracely Garcia Cabrera, to a scheduled immigration appointment in Baltimore on 5 November.

Her boyfriend, Cesar Saavedra, said officers asked whether she wanted to leave or remain with her mother. She chose to stay, and both women were detained before being transferred to Louisiana.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said the pair entered the United States unlawfully in 2016 and were apprehended in Texas's Rio Grande Valley. According to DHS, an immigration judge issued a final removal order on 23 February 2021.

'She will remain in ICE custody pending her removal from the United States,' a department spokesperson said.

However, the women's lawyers say the same ruling granted them protection against deportation to El Salvador under the Convention Against Torture. Murray Osorio PLLC said that protection remains in force and has not been terminated.

Their lawyer, Justice Haynes, said ICE intended to deport both women to Mexico, where neither holds legal status. He warned they could subsequently be deported to El Salvador.

Although protection against removal to El Salvador does not automatically prevent deportation elsewhere, the lawyers argue that the proposed transfer raises serious concerns about their safety and legal rights. Neither woman has a criminal record, according to their legal team.

University of Maryland Student Describes Life Inside ICE Detention

Flores Garcia described difficult conditions at the Louisiana facility, including coughing among detainees and unpleasant surroundings. 'It's just a big room. You can hear the people coughing. It smells in here,' she said.

Speaking to CBS News Baltimore, she acknowledged struggling emotionally while trying to remain positive. 'There's obviously times where I break down because it's devastating being here, knowing that my life outside is on pause,' she said.

Her detention has drawn criticism from Maryland Governor Wes Moore, who called for her return home. 'ICE isn't rounding up "the worst of the worst." This is just pure cruelty for cruelty's sake,' Moore wrote on 11 November.

Democratic Representative Steny Hoyer also urged President Donald Trump to secure Flores Garcia's release. University of Maryland students have organised support for her, while the university said it was providing assistance where possible.

Haynes has called for both women to be released and allowed to challenge the proposed removal to Mexico. For Flores Garcia, the detention has interrupted her education and plans to pursue a career in medicine.

excerpt: Mark Cuban proposes a 44% top tax rate, a $20 minimum wage, and wider Social Security taxes to cut the US deficit, but offers no detailed plan.
headline: Mark Cuban's Budget Deficit Playbook: 44% Top Tax Rate, $20 Minimum Wage, and Social Security Tax on Earnings Up to $5M
html_content:
Billionaire investor Mark Cuban has proposed raising the top federal income tax rate to 44%, introducing a $20 minimum wage at large companies, and extending Social Security taxes to earnings of up to $5 million as part of an ambitious plan to reduce America's budget deficit and rein in government spending.

Note that he proposed the wage hike for companies exceeding an unspecified sales or EBITDA threshold, while urging for increasing the stock buyback tax to 4% for public companies that do not pay employees at least $25 an hour.

In a 7th November X post, the Cost Plus Drugs co-founder outlined a series of tax increases, corporate penalties, and federal spending cuts, arguing that the US needs practical economic policies rather than partisan slogans to tackle its mounting fiscal challenges.

'Actually, it means that we have run out of time believing Ideology is a Strategy,' Cuban wrote. 'We have to take steps that are not based on slogans.' His proposals could have implications for high-income earners, major employers, public companies, and investors.

Cuban Wants Wealthier Americans to Pay More

Cuban wants the highest federal income tax bracket raised from 37% to 44% on earned income. The increase would target people at the top of the income ladder rather than impose a universal tax increase on workers.

He also called for higher corporate income tax rates and an alternative minimum tax, but did not specify the proposed corporate rate or explain how the additional tax would work alongside existing rules.

For investors and business owners, the distinction matters: higher corporate taxes could affect after-tax earnings, investment decisions, and company valuations, depending on how the changes were designed.

One of Cuban's most consequential proposals would extend Social Security payroll taxation to annual earnings between $1 million and $5 million. Currently, the tax stops at the first $192,300 of earnings in 2027.

Extending the taxable threshold could increase contributions from very high earners and provide additional revenue for the programme.

Cuban also wants every federal agency to reduce spending by 1% annually for five consecutive years, creating a cumulative five-year push to limit government expenditure.

Healthcare Reform Also Makes the List

Cuban urged lawmakers to pass the Break Up Big Medicine Act, which seeks to restrict common ownership between certain healthcare providers, insurers, pharmacy benefit managers, and medical wholesalers.

The proposal reflects his longstanding criticism of healthcare industry consolidation and opaque pricing practices. He had recently criticised CVS Health's planned breakup, arguing that the healthcare giant's decision to split into two publicly traded companies would do little to make medicines or healthcare more affordable for ordinary Americans.

Cuban had also warned lawmakers and consumers not to mistake the corporate restructuring for meaningful healthcare reform, saying the move was largely beneficial to shareholders rather than patients.

Concluding his more recent X post, Cuban argued that the midterm elections should be viewed as a rejection of how Washington operates rather than a straightforward victory for either political party. 'We need to be honest. Transparent. And stop pushing ideology,' he noted.

Cuban's plan offers a glimpse of the tax and regulatory changes that could become part of America's fiscal debate, but he did not provide revenue estimates, an implementation timetable, or a detailed legislative framework, leaving the actual deficit-reduction impact uncertain.

excerpt: Israel's defence spending is expected to approach 8% of GDP in 2026, squeezing public services and investment as debt and fiscal pressures rise.
headline: Israel's Renewed War with Iran Adds to Fiscal Strain as Defense Spending Nears 8% of GDP
html_content:
Israel's renewed confrontation with Iran is sharpening a budgetary dilemma that could outlast the fighting: how to maintain military readiness without allowing public services and investment to deteriorate. Defence expenditure is expected to approach 8% of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026, almost twice its 2022 share, according to the Israel Democracy Institute (IDI).

The IDI estimates total defence spending at approximately 175 billion shekels in the 2026 budget, including the Ministry of Defence, other security-related expenditure, and a reserve for wartime needs. Defence is expected to account for about a quarter of state spending, compared with 16% in 2022.

Defence Spending Is Reshaping Civilian Priorities

Israel's civilian spending was already low by international standards before the war. The IDI estimates that civilian expenditure, excluding interest payments, is around 10 percentage points of GDP below the median for advanced OECD economies, equivalent to a funding gap of approximately 220 billion shekels in 2026.

The institute expects real civilian expenditure per person to fall by 3.3% between the 2025 and 2026 budgets. Excluding exceptional and reconstruction-related items, the decline is about 6%. Infrastructure, education, welfare, higher education, and employment programmes are among the areas facing reductions.

The consequences could extend beyond the current budget cycle. Reduced investment in transport, skills, and public services risks weakening productivity and limiting the economy's ability to generate future tax revenue. This could make it harder to finance a permanently higher security burden.

Debt Forecasts Depend on a Fragile Security Outlook

Israel's public debt rose from 60.5% of GDP before the war to 68.5% in 2025, according to the IDI. The Bank of Israel's October 2026 forecast projects a budget deficit of 4.4% of GDP in 2026 and 4.6% in 2027, with public debt reaching about 68% of GDP at the end of 2026.

The central bank's baseline assumes fighting remains at low intensity and defence spending does not exceed the reserve allocated in the state budget. It warns that further military expenditure without offsetting adjustments would widen the deficit and could add to inflationary pressure.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) highlights the longer-term risk. Its July 2026 assessment projects public debt could reach 74% of GDP by 2031 without further fiscal adjustment. It expects heightened geopolitical tensions to keep defence spending elevated while civilian expenditure faces increasing pressure.

Israel Faces a Choice Over How to Finance Security

The IMF recommends gradual fiscal consolidation, prioritising revenue measures because civilian services and infrastructure are already relatively underfunded compared with advanced-economy peers. The IDI similarly argues that the government should review spending priorities, broaden the tax base, and protect investment that supports growth.

For policymakers, the challenge is how to distribute the cost. Higher taxes, reduced civilian allocations, and additional borrowing each carry economic and political consequences.

The Bank of Israel's forecast offers a route towards a more stable deficit, but depends on contained security conditions and defence spending staying within the budget provision. Renewed escalation could force the government to reconsider its plans.

For households, the consequences may emerge through strained public services, delayed infrastructure projects, and reduced support programmes.

Israel's security spending is becoming a test of whether it can sustain military preparedness without weakening the economic foundations needed to pay for it.

excerpt: Lahore TikToker Noman Hassan was arrested after a 19-year-old worker died in a tigress attack. Police allege it was initially reported as a dog attack.
headline: TikTok Influencer Arrested After Tiger Kills 19-Year-Old During Video Shoot; Police Investigate Alleged Cover-Up
html_content:
A TikTok influencer has been arrested in Lahore after a tigress mauled a 19-year-old farm worker to death during a video shoot. Police are investigating claims that his death was passed off as a dog attack.

Lahore police announced on Thursday 12 November that they had detained TikToker Noman Hassan and the farm's owner, Fayyaz, alias Faizi. Police said Hassan kept two of his own lions at the property.

The victim, Talha Munir, worked there as a caretaker. His father and brother were also employed at the farm, local media reported.

According to police, Hassan took the tigress out of its cage at about 5 p.m. on Wednesday, 11 November and asked Talha to appear in his video. The animal turned on the teenager, leaving deep wounds to his neck and back.

Police said Hassan drove him to a private hospital, where he died during treatment.

Lahore Tiger Attack: How the Dog Story Unravelled

The hospital was told Talha had been bitten by a dog, police said, without naming who gave that account. His parents were told the same and were initially reluctant to register a case, local media reported.

Investigators later obtained a recorded conversation between the farm owner and Talha's father, Munir Ahmed, that exposed the tigress attack. When officers reached the farm, its CCTV cameras and digital video recorder were missing, according to local reports.

'An attempt was made to pass off the tigress attack as a dog attack to conceal the truth,' Lahore Police said in a statement on X. Some Pakistani outlets have reported that the animal was a lioness.

The case was registered on the father's complaint under sections 289 and 322 of the Pakistan Penal Code and the Punjab Wildlife Act. Section 289 covers negligence with animals. Section 322 covers unintentionally causing a death through an unlawful act and carries liability for diyat, or compensation, to the victim's heirs.

Local media reported that an unnamed third suspect was later detained.

Lahore's Deputy Inspector General of Operations, Faisal Kamran, said the farm's licence had expired in 2025. Authorities have sealed the farmhouse, handed the tigress to the Punjab Wildlife Department, and seized 33 lions from the site.

Wildlife Department Gives a Conflicting Account

The Punjab Wildlife Department has described the attack differently, saying Talha was attacked while feeding the animal inside its cage, in breach of safety rules.

It added that the farm's carnivore section had been sealed since January 2026, although staff were still allowed in to care for the animals.

Police maintain the tigress was taken out for the TikTok video.

A tigress taken out of its cage for a TikTok video killed Talha, a 19-year-old farm worker, in Lahore, Pakistan.

TikToker Noman Hassan had asked him to join the shoot.

It was first passed off as a dog attack. Noman and the farm owner, Fayyaz, are under arrest. Daily Pakistan… pic.twitter.com/TssxTlF5Z8

— Angry Saffron (@AngrySaffron) November 13, 2026

Punjab Tightened Big Cat Rules After Earlier Attacks

In January 2025, a man was badly hurt by a lion while filming a TikTok video at another breeding farm in Lahore. That month, Punjab's cabinet brought lions, tigers, cheetahs, pumas, and jaguars under the Wildlife Act 1974, requiring licences and banning their promotion on social media.

Two eight-year-olds were hurt in separate lion attacks in the city in January 2026. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz then ordered that permission to keep big cats be revoked, the Punjab government said.

Talha's body was sent for a post-mortem examination. Police said they are still examining the tigress's ownership permit, safety arrangements at the farm, and possible negligence.

excerpt: Avril Lavigne has announced the birth of her first child, a daughter, sharing photographs on Instagram while keeping the baby's name and father private.
headline: Who Did Avril Lavigne Have a Baby With? Question Swirls as Singer Reveals 'Mini Princess' in New Post
html_content:
Avril Lavigne has surprised fans by announcing the arrival of her first child, a baby girl, after more than a year away from Instagram. While the news has been met with excitement, the 42-year-old singer has left one question unanswered: who is the baby's father?

'Our Mini F****** Princess has arrived 🎀👑🍼,' Lavigne wrote on Friday, 13 November, sharing photographs of her newborn daughter.

The announcement came without an earlier public pregnancy announcement. Lavigne's last Instagram post was in October 2025, when she shared photographs from the When We Were Young Festival, where she performed with Simple Plan.

Her return was met with congratulations from fans, many of whom were delighted that her first post in over a year was to introduce her daughter. Others expressed surprise that she had managed to keep the news private for so long.

The photographs show Lavigne cradling her daughter and an unidentified man holding the baby's hand. Another image features three pairs of black-and-white checkered Vans trainers arranged on a skateboard, apparently representing the family and nodding to her 'Sk8er Boi' image.

View this post on Instagram

Who Is the Father of Avril Lavigne's Baby?

Although a man appears in the photographs, Lavigne has not identified him or confirmed her current relationship status.

Her decision to keep the pregnancy out of the public eye has also prompted speculation among social media users, with some questioning whether the singer welcomed her daughter through surrogacy. However, Lavigne has not discussed the circumstances of the birth, and there is no verified information supporting those claims.

Their romance was short-lived. They split in June 2023, briefly reunited the following month and reportedly separated again later that year.

Before Tyga, Lavigne was engaged to musician Mod Sun, but the pair called off their engagement in February 2023. She was also previously married to Sum 41 frontman Deryck Whibley from 2006 to 2010 and Nickelback frontman Chad Kroeger from 2013 until their separation in 2015.

None of her former relationships has been publicly connected to the birth of her daughter.

Although Lavigne's announcement caught fans off guard, the singer had previously spoken about wanting children. In an interview with E! News published in November 2013, she said she hoped to have one or two children eventually, although she wanted to focus on music and touring first.

'I want one or two [kids], but not right now,' she said. 'Like, in the future. Eventually.'

At the time, Lavigne was 29 and married to Kroeger, who said the couple needed to find a time when they were both home before starting a family. More than a decade later, the singer has shared the arrival of her daughter, marking a new chapter in her life.

Lavigne has yet to reveal the baby's name or date of birth, but her unexpected return to Instagram has given fans plenty to celebrate.

excerpt: New York finance writer Charlotte Cowles revealed how scammers posing as CIA agents tricked her into handing over $50,000 in a shoebox.
headline: How a NY Finance Writer Was Tricked by Fake CIA Agents Into Handing Over $50,000 in a Shoebox
html_content:
New York finance writer Charlotte Cowles handed $50,000 (£37,790) in cash to scammers posing as federal agents, placing her savings inside a floral shoebox before passing it through the window of a waiting SUV outside her Brooklyn apartment on Halloween 2023.

In a first-person essay published by The Cut on 15 February 2024, Cowles described how hours of threats and fabricated criminal allegations persuaded her to surrender money she had accumulated over several years.

The ordeal began with a supposed Amazon customer-service call about suspicious purchases. Within hours, Cowles believed she faced arrest, financial ruin and possible danger to her family. The personal-finance columnist, who regularly advised readers about money, later struggled to understand why she had obeyed the callers.

How Fake CIA Agents Frightened Charlotte Cowles Into Withdrawing $50K

At approximately 12.30pm on 31 October, a woman claiming to work for Amazon contacted Cowles about $8,000 (£6,046) in electronics purchases. Cowles checked her account and found nothing unusual. The caller insisted the transactions involved separate business accounts opened using her identity.

She then transferred Cowles to a supposed Federal Trade Commission investigator who identified himself as Calvin Mitchell. The man knew her address, date of birth and the last four digits of her Social Security number.

He claimed 22 bank accounts had been opened in her name and linked to overseas transfers exceeding $3 million (£2.27 million). The allegations became increasingly frightening. Cowles was told she was implicated in drug trafficking, money laundering and criminal investigations in Texas and Maryland.

Another caller, identifying himself as a CIA investigator named Michael Sarano, claimed her home was under surveillance. He warned her against contacting police, lawyers or family members, suggesting that doing so could endanger her husband and two-year-old son.

When Cowles questioned his credentials, a call appeared to come from the FTC's official number. She suspected spoofing but continued listening. The caller then claimed federal investigators needed to freeze her assets and issue a new Social Security number.

To protect her money, he instructed Cowles to withdraw $50,000 (£37,790) and hand it to someone he described as an undercover CIA agent.

Charlotte Cowles Hands $50K in Shoebox to Supposed CIA Courier

Cowles went to her bank, where a teller counted out $50,000 (£37,790) in $100 notes and handed her a warning about scams. Despite growing doubts, she returned home with the cash. She placed it inside a floral shoebox, taped it shut and labelled it with details supplied by the caller. At 6.06pm, a white Mercedes SUV arrived outside her building.

Following instructions, Cowles placed the box through the rear window without speaking to the driver, whose identity was not established. The caller subsequently sent an image of a purported Treasury cheque promising reimbursement.

But the promised government appointment never materialised. Later that evening, Cowles realised she had been deceived. She told her husband and contacted police, who visited her apartment around 10.30pm.

In her account for The Cut, Cowles described the shame, anxiety and financial uncertainty that followed. She reported the incident to authorities, froze her credit and sought therapy.

Psychologist Saul Kassin, whom Cowles interviewed, explained how prolonged questioning and incremental demands can alter a person's sense of reality. The fraud cost Cowles savings accumulated over several years, including money inherited from her grandfather.

Her February 2024 account did not report recovering the stolen $50,000 (£37,790).

excerpt: Nvidia has appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO after Jensen Huang's resignation, amid reported tensions over AI financing risks and an independent company investigation.
headline: Jensen Huang Once Called Colette Kress a 'Deer in the Headlights'. Now She's Nvidia's Interim CEO
html_content:
Jensen Huang reportedly called Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress a 'deer in the headlights' during a tense meeting in August. Three months later, she is running the company he co-founded. Kress, 59, was appointed interim CEO following Huang's resignation on 11 November 2026, a leadership change Nvidia announced the following day.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang questioned Kress's ability to contribute to strategic decisions as Nvidia faced mounting financial commitments tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The executive he reportedly criticised now faces responsibility for overseeing those same challenges while Nvidia searches for a permanent chief executive.

The transition follows reports concerning Huang's extramarital relationships and allegations of foreign intelligence targeting. Nvidia has launched an independent investigation but says it has no reason to believe company secrets were compromised. The company has not publicly attributed Huang's resignation to those reports.

Why Jensen Huang Reportedly Questioned Colette Kress

During an August meeting, Huang interrupted Kress's presentation and described her as a 'deer in the headlights', according to a person familiar with his comments. The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang also called her a 'reporting CFO', questioning her ability to help develop strategy and make decisions.

The criticism came as Nvidia considered billions of dollars in financial guarantees for companies seeking to purchase its artificial intelligence chips. Some arrangements involved Huang's son-in-law, Nico Caprez, who reportedly pursued financing agreements with emerging cloud providers and data centre developers.

The proposed deals were intended to turn smaller companies into long-term Nvidia customers. However, Huang had begun questioning whether the financing strategy exposed the company to excessive risk, according to people familiar with the discussions.

He reportedly warned executives that major cloud providers were exploring alternative chips to reduce their dependence on Nvidia. Meanwhile, substantial commitments to purchase chip wafers and memory were creating additional financial pressure.

Huang described those obligations as an 'avalanche', according to the newspaper. The reported exchange highlights tensions over Nvidia's financial strategy between Huang and the executive now overseeing its leadership transition.

Colette Kress Takes Over Nvidia Following Jensen Huang's Resignation

Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation on 11 November and appointed Kress interim CEO, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Kress has served as Nvidia's chief financial officer since September 2013 and will retain that position while the board searches for a permanent chief executive.

Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft. The company also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first board chairman.

Despite Huang's reported criticism, Nvidia's official announcement expressed confidence in Kress's leadership. 'Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth,' Jones said, citing her understanding of the company's operations and finances.

Kress pledged to build on Huang's legacy while maintaining Nvidia's focus on accelerated computing and artificial intelligence. Her immediate responsibilities include overseeing the company's financial commitments during a period of intense scrutiny.

Nvidia is scheduled to report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, 17 November. The figures cover the quarter ending 25 October, before Kress assumed leadership. The accompanying earnings call will offer investors an early opportunity to assess Nvidia's direction following Huang's departure.

For Kress, the challenge is particularly significant. The finance chief once reportedly criticised for her approach to strategic decisions must now oversee Nvidia's financial commitments and guide the company through its first leadership transition since its founding in 1993.

excerpt: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on 13 November 2026 after air traffic control communications problems, halting departures while officials investigated the disruption and its duration.
headline: Why Is There a Nationwide Ground Stop Today? What We Know About Flights Halted Across the US
html_content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop across the United States on Friday, 13 November 2026, after serious communications problems disrupted air traffic control operations.

The order prevented flights from taking off across the country, raising concerns about widespread delays, cancellations and missed connections.

The disruption began in Chicago before the FAA expanded the restrictions nationwide.

According to Reuters, the agency cited 'extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety' when announcing the ground stop.

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the communications problems were affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

Officials have yet to confirm what caused the problems or when flights can resume normal operations.

Why Did the FAA Order a Nationwide Ground Stop?

The nationwide ground stop followed an earlier disruption in Chicago, where communications problems had already affected air traffic operations.

As the problems spread, the FAA ordered departing aircraft to remain on the ground.

'All departing traffic should remain groundstopped until further notice,' the agency said.

The decision was made to keep flights from taking off while officials investigated the communications issues.

However, aircraft already in the air were not required to land immediately.

Reuters reported that those flights could continue to their destinations, while aircraft waiting to depart had to remain grounded.

International flights were also affected, although the FAA said incoming international services would be handled on a case-by-case basis.

The agency has not explained how those arrangements will affect individual airports or routes.

It also remains unclear whether the communications problems were caused by equipment failure, a technical malfunction or another issue.

How Will the Nationwide Ground Stop Affect US Flights?

For travellers, the biggest concern is the disruption to scheduled departures and connecting flights.

Flights waiting to take off could face significant delays until air traffic controllers give airlines permission to resume departures.

Passengers with connecting flights may also face problems if their incoming aircraft are delayed at other airports.

Even after the ground stop is lifted, airlines may need time to get aircraft back into position, adjust schedules and accommodate affected passengers.

The longer the restrictions last, the greater the potential disruption to flights across the country.

Passengers are advised to check their flight status directly with their airline before heading to the airport.

They can also visit the FAA's National Airspace System Status website for the latest updates.

When Was the Last Nationwide Ground Stop in the US?

Friday's ground stop is an extremely rare event in US aviation.

According to Reuters, it is only the second nationwide suspension of departures since the terrorist attacks of 11 September 2001.

The previous ground stop happened in January 2023, when a malfunction in the FAA's Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) system temporarily halted domestic departures.

That disruption lasted less than two hours, although flight delays continued after operations resumed.

The latest incident has also raised fresh concerns about the FAA's ageing infrastructure.

Reuters reported that Congress approved $12.5 billion (£9.45 billion) in 2025 to upgrade the agency's communications systems.

On Friday, the FAA and White House requested another $30.1 billion (£22.74 billion) to address other aviation infrastructure problems.

However, officials have not linked those funding needs to the latest communications failure.

For now, two questions remain: What caused the nationwide communications problems, and when will flights return to normal?
