excerpt: A Starbucks customer's TikTok has raised questions about the amount of short rib in the chain's new grilled cheese sandwich, although experiences reported by other diners vary.
headline: Customer Opens $9 Starbucks Short Rib Grilled Cheese to Find Meat Covering One Quarter of the Bread
html_content:
A Starbucks customer has drawn attention to the chain's new Braised Short Rib Grilled Cheese after posting a video showing a small piece of meat covering roughly a quarter of one slice of bread. TikTok user Ashley, who posts as @liftwithlipp, questioned whether the sandwich matched its name and price.

https://www.tiktok.com/player/v1/7704692407282978062?embed_from=oembed&music_info=1&description=1&autoplay=1&muted=1

Her clip shows the sandwich taken apart on a napkin. On-screen text reads: 'When I am already at my limit but Starbucks thinks this qualifies as a braised short rib grilled cheese.' She tagged the company and asked: 'Where is the rest of the short rib?'

The video raises a question about how much filling customers should expect.

Starbucks' Holiday Sandwich Has No Published Meat Portion

Starbucks introduced the sandwich on 5 November as part of its 2026 holiday menu. It describes the item as grilled cheese elevated with braised short rib, savoury caramelised onion jam and Dijon, alongside Cheddar, Parmesan and mozzarella on sourdough.

The announcement lists the ingredients but does not state how much short rib each sandwich should contain. Customers have no published meat-portion benchmark against which to compare what they receive.

Price varies by location. Tasting Table reviewer Dani Zoeller paid $8.25 (about £6) on launch day. A separate Tasting Table article put the price at roughly $8–$10 (about £6–£8) after tax, with some New York locations charging more than $9 (about £7).

Zoeller initially thought the bread looked hard and the filling appeared sparse, but said the short rib, cheese and bread worked well together once she tasted it. She enjoyed the flavour, although the bread was too hard for her liking. Her review contrasts with Ashley's video but does not establish how consistent portions are between stores.

Nutrition Figures Do Not Settle the Portion Debate

Starbucks' published nutrition information lists the sandwich as a 640-calorie serving with 26 grams of protein. Those figures describe the whole product; they do not disclose how much of it is short rib rather than bread, cheese or other ingredients.

The nutrition panel cannot establish whether Ashley's portion fell below the company's standard.

Customers Report Different Experiences

Reactions to Ashley's video were mixed. Some viewers said their sandwiches had more filling, while others shared her disappointment. One commenter questioned whether the sandwiches arrived at stores prepackaged.

A Reddit discussion also included a customer photograph and criticism of the amount of meat. Other commenters said they enjoyed the item, showing that online experiences have not been uniform.

BroBible previously reported on a separate TikTok complaint by Binkbadd, who said her Starbucks Bacon, Gouda and Egg Sandwich contained only three small pieces of bacon. She received a refund and was later given another sandwich. Her video attracted more than 100,000 views.

Starbucks Has Not Responded to Ashley's Complaint

BroBible reported that it contacted Ashley through TikTok and Starbucks by email, but its article did not include a response. IBTimes UK has not independently verified the sandwich's portion specifications.

Ashley's video documents one disappointing order, while other customers and a reviewer describe different experiences. Starbucks' nutrition information does not show how much short rib customers should expect. A company response on portion standards would help clarify whether the video shows an isolated preparation issue or a wider consistency concern.

excerpt: Stephen King posted about aliens during the 13 November FAA ground stop, while the agency attributed the US disruption to a telecommunications outage.
headline: Stephen King Claims 'The Aliens Have Landed' During FAA Ground Stop as Sean Duffy Blames Old System
html_content:
Stephen King posted an alien-themed message on X during a nationwide FAA ground stop in the United States on 13 November 2026. The Federal Aviation Administration attributed the disruption to a telecommunications outage.

The restriction was reportedly lifted after a few hours. The agency had described a 'temporary telecommunications outage', while Sean Duffy stated on X that communications problems were affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers and that FAA technicians were working on the issue.

Stephen King Posts About Aliens During FAA Outage

King's message suggested that extraterrestrials had arrived and that their presence was being concealed to prevent public panic. His post provided no evidence supporting those suggestions.

'The aliens have landed. That's the REAL reason for the ground stop. They don't want to start a worldwide panic. They are blind but can hear like a motherf**ker,' King wrote.

His wording did not establish whether he intended the remarks literally. The message nevertheless placed an alien explanation alongside an incident for which the FAA had identified a telecommunications problem.

Other X users also posted about extraterrestrials. 'The alien mothership is here,' one wrote.

Another framed the possibility as a hypothetical scenario rather than an established event.

'Can you imagine if it was actually the great disclosure event that's been rumored lol,' the user wrote.

Some posts connected the aviation disruption with reports of a Microsoft outage. Others suggested that it could be a distraction or linked to a fabricated cyberattack. None of those posts provided evidence establishing what caused the ground stop.

'First Microsoft now this ... 👀😳 I've retired my conspiracy theorist ways.. well most of them, but them ways and my prepper ways too about to come right back,' another user wrote.

The excerpts reflected speculation about the disruption. They did not establish a connection between the reported outages or provide support for claims of extraterrestrial involvement.

Official FAA Outage Account Differs From Stephen King's Post

Duffy and Markwayne Mullin addressed the incident at a White House news conference. Mullin stated that the FAA outage was unrelated to Microsoft's global outage and rejected suggestions that a cyberattack was responsible.

His remarks concerned those specific explanations. The account of the news conference did not establish that officials had addressed King's alien-themed post.

Duffy attributed the ground stop to 'old legacy equipment' and an 'incredibly old air traffic control system'. He reportedly called for Congress to provide $50 billion to improve the system.

That explanation focused on ageing infrastructure, while the FAA's announcement identified the immediate problem as a telecommunications outage. Neither statement provided support for the alien speculation circulating on X.

Beyond Stephen King's Post, SMART's Role Is Disputed

A separate report cited an unnamed source who attributed the outage to SMART, described as an AI-supported FAA air traffic system. Duffy stated at Friday's White House news conference that SMART was not responsible for the ground stop.

The allegation about SMART's role rested on the report's unnamed source and was not presented as a confirmed finding. The reported timing of SMART's introduction alone does not establish that the system caused the outage.

The report described SMART as a platform combining information about flight paths, schedules, weather and other factors in one place. It described the system as anticipating airspace constraints and other potential problems. The same report stated that SMART had been introduced three days before the disruption.

excerpt: Alaina Kunes' father reportedly received a voicemail threatening his daughter after Ring footage of alleged racist gestures at Ole Miss circulated online.
headline: Alaina Kunes' Father Receives Voicemail Allegedly Threatening to Hang Her After Viral Ole Miss Clip
html_content:
Alaina Kunes' father reportedly received a voicemail allegedly threatening to hang his daughter after Ring footage of alleged racist gestures outside Black Ole Miss students' apartment circulated online.

Kunes issued a public apology after the footage prompted allegations that she and another white classmate made monkey noises and racist gestures outside an apartment occupied by three Black students. Her spokesperson stated that Kunes and her family had faced harassment and threats of violence during the week.

Alaina Kunes' Father Reportedly Receives Threatening Message

A woman reportedly left the voicemail for Scott Kunes, allegedly threatening his daughter and warning against her returning to the university.

The caller allegedly stated, 'Scott, I'm going to hang your daughter. I'm going to hang the b**** when I find her.'

In the quoted voicemail, the caller claimed to live in Mississippi and attend Ole Miss. That claimed connection remains unverified.

'I live in Mississippi, by the way, and I go to Ole Miss, so you best not send your daughter back to that school. That's your best bet right now. Cause Monday morning...'

Kunes' spokesperson also expressed concern about hostility towards the Black students and fundraising campaigns the family described as fake.

'At the same time, they are deeply troubled by fake fundraising campaigns circulating online about this incident, as well as the vitriol directed at Jakiyra, Victoria and Kaiyden,' the statement read.

'Alaina hopes that the hate and hostility will cease and that the Ole Miss community can begin to heal and move forward in unity and peace,' the spokesperson added.

Alaina Kunes Apologises for Her Actions

Kunes stated in her public apology that she was 'unaware of their race' when she performed the gestures. She nevertheless described her actions as harmful and sought forgiveness from the women and the university community.

'To the women I offended, and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize. I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful. I pray they will forgive me,' she stated.

Her apology also addressed the effect on the women who lived in the apartment.

'I can never truly understand the pain I have caused them and it was never my intention. These girls deserve to feel seen and understood and what I did is not a reflection of who I am trying to become.'

The footage circulated after Tasha Bolton shared a recording from her daughter's Ring camera on Facebook. Bolton identified her daughter as a University of Mississippi freshman with two Black roommates and stated that the women in the footage lived upstairs from them.

University Condemns Conduct in Alaina Kunes Footage

'My daughter sent me this video from her Ring camera at her apartment,' Bolton wrote.

She called for accountability and an explanation of how university administrators would address the incident.

'The video has been shared with university administration, and we want answers. Specifically, what steps will be taken to address this behavior and ensure accountability?'

In a statement quoted in the reporting, the University of Mississippi condemned the conduct.

'The behavior depicted in this video is deeply troubling, hurtful, and unacceptable.'

The university added, 'We condemn the behavior as it does not reflect our university's values or the kind of community we strive to be every day. Racism and actions that disparage people because of an aspect of their identity have no place in our campus community.'

excerpt: A New Jersey Bigfoot sighting left a couple convinced they saw an eight-foot figure, but investigators found no conclusive evidence.
headline: New Jersey Bigfoot Sighting: Couple Say Eight-Foot Figure Crossed Road, 'We Know What We Saw'
html_content:
A couple reported a New Jersey Bigfoot sighting after seeing what they described as an eight-foot, black-furred figure on a rural road. They said it crossed Route 542 in Burlington County during a rainy night drive on Sunday, 11 October 2026. The figure's identity remains unverified.

Keyara Klawitter submitted her account to the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization (BFRO). She was travelling with her husband, Jason, while their children slept in the back seat. The case received renewed news coverage on 12 November, but the report contains no photograph of the figure.

New Jersey Bigfoot Sighting Lasted Only Seconds

Klawitter said the car's high beams caught a large figure stepping from the right-hand side of Route 542 near Loveland Lane. She braked as it crossed in front of them.

She described a bulky frame, jet-black fur that appeared soaked, unusually long arms and what resembled human hands. The figure walked with a slight hunch, she said, yet moved so quickly that it seemed to be 'gliding' across the road.

Klawitter asked Jason whether he could see it too. According to her account, he confirmed that he had. Neither witness saw its face, investigators later recorded.

The exact time is unclear. Klawitter placed the encounter at around 10 p.m., while BFRO investigator Jacob Korbel wrote that it happened at 10.30 p.m. A subsequent reconstruction suggested the couple saw the figure for only four or five seconds.

After driving away, Klawitter telephoned her mother. She said she knew little about Bigfoot or Sasquatch beforehand, but remained convinced by what she had witnessed.

'We know what we saw,' she wrote. Her certainty does not independently establish the figure's identity.

Investigators Examine the New Jersey Bigfoot Sighting

Korbel and another BFRO investigator, identified as Mike, arranged to meet the couple at the roadside about a week later. The witnesses showed them where the figure had appeared and disappeared into the woods.

Investigators found a well-used wildlife trail on either side of the road, along with broken branches and indistinct ground impressions. Korbel said none could confidently be connected to the reported encounter.

He suggested heavy rain might have washed away any tracks left that night. That explanation remains speculative, and no identifiable footprint or other physical trace linked to the figure was presented.

Using a nearby telephone pole as a reference, investigators estimated the reported height at between seven-and-a-half and eight feet. The estimate relied on the witnesses' recollections, not a direct measurement.

Korbel and his colleague considered the witnesses credible. He described their reaction as 'a very normal, human reaction' and said they appeared uneasy during the visit, repeatedly looking towards the woods.

The BFRO categorised the report as 'Class A', which under its own rules means it considers the circumstances less open to misidentification. The classification is not independent scientific verification of Bigfoot.

The organisation's New Jersey database lists 80 reports, including 17 in Burlington County. These are recorded accounts, not proof of a previously unidentified species.

Korbel also wrote that the couple contacted New Jersey State Park Police and the state's Department of Environmental Protection after returning home. He said the environmental agency referred them to the BFRO, but the published report contains no statements from either agency confirming those exchanges.

After driving away, Klawitter telephoned her mother. She said she knew little about Bigfoot or Sasquatch beforehand, but remained convinced by what she had witnessed. 'We know what we saw,' she wrote. Her certainty does not independently establish the figure's identity. The witnesses showed them where the figure had appeared and disappeared into the woods. Investigators found a well-used wildlife trail on either side of the road, along with broken branches and indistinct ground impressions. Korbel said none could confidently be connected to the reported encounter. He suggested heavy rain might have washed away any tracks left that night. That explanation remains speculative, and no identifiable footprint or other physical trace linked to the figure was presented. Using a nearby telephone pole as a reference, investigators estimated the reported height at between seven-and-a-half and eight feet. The estimate relied on the witnesses' recollections, not a direct measurement. A section of Route 542 in Burlington County, New Jersey. A couple reported seeing an unidentified figure along the road on 11 October 2026steve baxter/Wikimedia Commons Public domain Korbel and his colleague considered the witnesses credible. He described their reaction as 'a very normal, human reaction' and said they appeared uneasy during the visit, repeatedly looking towards the woods. The BFRO categorised the report as 'Class A', which under its own rules means it considers the circumstances less open to misidentification. The classification is not independent scientific verification of Bigfoot. The organisation's New Jersey database lists 80 reports, including 17 in Burlington County. These are recorded accounts, not proof of a previously unidentified species. Korbel also wrote that the couple contacted New Jersey State Park Police and the state's Department of Environmental Protection after returning home. He said the environmental agency referred them to the BFRO, but the published report contains no statements from either agency confirming those exchanges.

excerpt: The FAA ground stop halted US departures on Friday after communications failures, with 3,374 flights cancelled by early Saturday.
headline: Why Did the FAA Issue a Nationwide Ground Stop on Friday and How Many Flights Were Cancelled Saturday?
html_content:
An FAA ground stop halted departures across the United States on Friday, 13 November, after communications failures affected air traffic control systems. By 6 a.m. Eastern Time on Saturday, FlightAware had recorded 3,374 flight cancellations and 1,008 delays involving US airports. Although the restriction ended Friday evening, airlines were still recovering from the disruption.

Friday's toll reached 9,132 cancellations and 7,030 delays, according to figures published early Saturday. Those totals cover flights within, into or out of the United States. They do not show how many disruptions resulted solely from the nationwide ground stop.

Why Did the FAA Issue a Nationwide Ground Stop?

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the technical instability began at 3:36 p.m. Eastern Time. At approximately 3:54 p.m., the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide advisory instructing departing aircraft to remain grounded for safety reasons.

The FAA cited intermittent telecommunications outages affecting radar and communications at air traffic control centres. Aircraft already airborne continued under established safety procedures, while inbound international flights were handled individually.

Duffy blamed overloaded routers and switches within an ageing network, saying they had produced inconsistent information for controllers. Newer equipment had remained operational, he said, urging Congress to provide more money for modernisation. His explanation was preliminary rather than the outcome of a completed investigation.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said investigators had found no evidence of a cyberattack. However, he cautioned that officials had not ruled out every possible cause.

The FAA reopened US airspace at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time, more than four hours after the ground stop began. Officials said the affected systems had been tested before departures resumed. Duffy warned that reopening airspace would not immediately put aircraft and flight crews back where airlines needed them.

The shutdown was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a separate failure affected the FAA's pilot-notification system. Concerns about ageing infrastructure predated Friday's outage. In a 2024 review, the US Government Accountability Office reported that the FAA had classified 51 of its 138 air traffic control systems as unsustainable.

How Many Flights Were Cancelled Saturday After the FAA Ground Stop?

Saturday's 3,374 cancellations were an early count, not a final tally. Aircraft diversions complicated the recovery. Aviation analytics firm Cirium recorded 827 diversions by 7:05 p.m. Friday, including 670 aircraft returning to their departure airports and 157 landing elsewhere.

Cirium estimated that about 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to depart US airports after 4 p.m. Friday. That was the volume of planned travel, not a count of passengers left stranded.

The effects reached weekend sport. The University of Oklahoma confirmed its football game against Ole Miss had been moved from Saturday to Sunday after the visiting team's flight was disrupted. Oklahoma's athletics director criticised the decision, citing the effect on supporters who had arranged travel and accommodation.

Duffy encouraged college teams using charter aircraft to contact the FAA about their flight arrangements. The agency's Saturday operations plan also listed possible airport-specific restrictions.

For affected passengers, the US Transportation Department says a cancelled flight generally entitles travellers to a refund if they decline alternative transport and do not travel. That right applies regardless of the reason for cancellation. Other assistance, including meals or hotels, depends on airline policies and circumstances.

excerpt: Sam Hartman is the next Bachelor star. Explore his NFL practice-squad status, college football records, family and the health scare he overcame.
headline: 10 Photos of Sam Hartman: Inside 'The Bachelor' Star's Personal Details, Family Background and Football Career
html_content:
Sam Hartman, 27, was named the next star of ABC's The Bachelor on Friday, 13 November 2026, during an appearance on Good Morning America.

The Washington Commanders practice-squad quarterback will lead the dating show's 30th season, premiering on 21 March 2027. Despite throwing 134 college touchdown passes, he has yet to make an NFL regular-season appearance.

View this post on Instagram

The announcement introduces Hartman to a wider television audience after a six-year college football career, a serious medical setback and his move to Washington in 2024.

'I'm excited but also very nervous,' Hartman admitted during his Good Morning America interview.

View this post on Instagram

He also joked about the prospect of dating 30 women, acknowledging that even maintaining a conversation with one potential partner could prove difficult.

Sam Hartman's Football Career and 2022 Health Scare

Born in Charlotte, North Carolina, Hartman played at Wake Forest University from 2018 to 2022 before transferring to Notre Dame for his final college season in 2023.

View this post on Instagram

According to Notre Dame's official records, he finished his college career with 15,656 passing yards and 134 touchdown passes, an Atlantic Coast Conference record.

His college achievements did not immediately translate into NFL appearances. Hartman joined the Washington Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024 and remains on their practice squad.

View this post on Instagram

Although he has participated in preseason games, he has not appeared in an NFL regular-season contest.

His football journey also included a frightening medical episode.

View this post on Instagram

In August 2022, Hartman was diagnosed with Paget-Schroetter syndrome, a rare condition involving blood clots in a vein near the collarbone.

The Atlantic Coast Conference reported that he underwent treatment to remove a clot, followed by surgery to relieve pressure on the affected vein.

Hartman missed only one game before returning that season. He subsequently received the ACC's Brian Piccolo Award, which recognises courage among conference football players.

View this post on Instagram

Sam Hartman's Family Background and Bachelor Announcement Reaction

Hartman's family has influenced the qualities he hopes to find in a partner.

His father is a surgeon, while his mother is a nurse. Hartman said their dedication to helping others shaped his appreciation for compassion and caregiving.

He also wants someone ambitious and competitive, particularly a partner whose personal goals motivate him to pursue his own.

View this post on Instagram

However, accepting The Bachelor was not an immediate decision.

Hartman initially hesitated before discussing the opportunity with Jesse Palmer, the programme's host and a former NFL quarterback. Palmer previously starred in the show's fifth season in 2004.

The conversation helped Hartman reconsider. His parents also encouraged him to remain himself, enjoy the experience and trust his instincts.

View this post on Instagram

His casting drew supportive reactions from former franchise contestants.

According to Bachelor Nation's official website, Tyler Cameron celebrated the announcement on Instagram, while former Bachelor star Ben Higgins wrote, 'So far I really like this decision.'

View this post on Instagram

Hartman previously appeared in the football documentary series QB1: Beyond the Lights, although his upcoming television role will place his personal relationships at the centre of attention.

Season 30 of The Bachelor premieres on Sunday, 21 March 2027, at 8 p.m. Eastern Time on ABC, with next-day streaming on Hulu in the United States

excerpt: A Mariah Carey walking video from Brazil has divided fans over her cautious steps, as new photographs show the singer later greeting supporters in flats.
headline: Fans Debate Whether Mariah Carey 'Looks Like She's in Pain' or Just Wore Wrong Boots in Brazil Rain
html_content:
A Mariah Carey walking video from Brazil prompted debate on Friday, 13 November 2026, after fans noticed her cautious steps while greeting supporters.

Later photographs from São Paulo showed the singer wearing flat shoes, adding another detail to questions about her earlier high-heeled boots.

Some viewers wondered whether Carey was uncomfortable as she walked while holding a woman's arm. Others suggested her footwear or the walking surface might explain her movements. Neither explanation has been confirmed.

The singer is in Brazil ahead of her Christmas Time concerts, scheduled for 17 November in São Paulo and 21 November in Rio de Janeiro.

Mariah Carey Fans Debate Heels and Cautious Steps

In an Instagram clip circulating online, Carey wore a gold minidress and knee-high, high-heeled boots. She held the arm of a woman accompanying her as she approached waiting supporters.

A post shared by instagram

Carey smiled and interacted with fans, but her careful movements attracted attention.

Some Instagram users questioned whether the singer was experiencing discomfort, while others expressed concern about her wellbeing.

The reactions reflected viewers' interpretations rather than evidence of a medical problem. The recording does not establish why Carey accepted assistance or whether she was in pain.

A second video circulated on X, prompting further discussion about the conditions underfoot.

THIS VIDEO OF MARIAH CAREY IS TRENDING AS EVERYONE NOTICED 😳 pic.twitter.com/ZPQBHnVdNM

— Truth Seeker (@_TruthZone_) November 13, 2026

One commenter suggested that what appeared to be tile or cut stone might be uneven or slippery beneath narrow heels. Another argued that Carey was walking downhill in the rain and trying to avoid falling.

Rain was reported in São Paulo during her visit, although the precise conditions when the clips were filmed remain unverified.

The debate also reached Reddit, where commenters offered differing interpretations.

'She does look like she is struggling to me, but it could be any number of things,' one participant wrote.

Others pointed to Carey's longstanding preference for elaborate outfits and high heels, questioning whether her cautious steps necessarily indicated a health concern.

New Photos Show Mariah Carey Wearing Flats

Photographs published on Friday showed Carey greeting fans outside a São Paulo hotel in a black minidress, tights and flat Gucci loafers.

She signed autographs and waved to photographers during the appearance.

The footwear change offered a fresh detail following the earlier discussion. However, it did not establish that the boots had caused her cautious movements or that she had experienced discomfort.

In its initial report, Page Six said it had contacted Carey's representative for comment. No response was included in that report.

Earlier Mariah Carey Performance Raised Similar Questions

The Brazil footage recalled discussions surrounding Carey's Celebration of Mimi residency in Las Vegas.

In February 2025, fan footage circulated showing her moving slowly during a performance of 'Fantasy' at Dolby Live at Park MGM.

Carey continued singing and smiling as dancers performed nearby. Some viewers described her movements as stiff, while others defended the singer against criticism of her limited choreography.

The earlier recording offered no verified explanation for her movements, just as the Brazil clips do not establish a medical cause.

Carey's next scheduled appearance is her São Paulo concert on Tuesday, 17 November, followed by another performance in Rio de Janeiro on Saturday, 21 November.

excerpt: Katie Price and Lee Andrews remain separated, but she says she has cut 'toxic people' from her life while planning to see him in Dubai.
headline: Katie Price Claims Lee Andrews 'Scammed Her Heart', Thought Husband Had £50M Before Finding £2.22
html_content:
Katie Price has revealed plans to see estranged husband Lee Andrews in Dubai, despite their September separation. The 48-year-old discussed the meeting on Thursday, 12 November, before an interview emerged in which she described removing 'toxic people' from her life.

The former glamour model married Andrews in Dubai in January 2026. Their relationship later became embroiled in disputed claims about his cryptocurrency holdings, which he denied misrepresenting.

Price discussed her plans on the 12 November episode of The Katie Price Show, which she co-hosts with her sister Sophie. She confirmed she intended to see Andrews during a visit involving cosmetic treatments, but did not announce a reconciliation.

Katie Price and Lee Andrews Dispute £2.22 Crypto Claim

Price confirmed their separation in September, months after their wedding. During an appearance on ITV's Good Morning Britain on 16 September, she described feeling emotionally deceived by Andrews.

Reports suggested that a cryptocurrency wallet associated with Andrews contained approximately £2.22, despite claims of substantial wealth.

Andrews disputed the allegations. In a voice message played on the programme, he said Price had checked the wrong wallet and claimed another contained 50 million USDT, a cryptocurrency designed to track the US dollar.

Neither the reported £2.22 balance nor Andrews' claimed holdings has been independently verified. The figures do not establish his overall financial position.

Andrews maintained that he had not misled Price and offered to undergo a lie-detector test.

Price insisted Andrews had not taken money from her. Instead, she said she felt she had fallen in love with someone who had presented himself differently from the man she came to know.

'I love him, but who is he?' she asked during the ITV interview.

The disagreement also involved an engagement ring. Price said Andrews had described it as worth £72,000, but an insurance valuation placed it at £5,000. That account was not independently verified.

Katie Price Credits Sophie With Supporting Her Independence

In a joint interview with The Times published on Friday, 13 November, Price described reassessing her personal relationships after years of emotional difficulties.

She said she had been working through past trauma and distancing herself from people she believed were harmful. However, she did not identify those individuals or directly connect her remarks to Andrews.

Price also described feeling more independent, saying she no longer had managers or a man controlling her decisions.

'I've got rid of all the toxic people,' she said, describing the changes as a source of freedom.

Her sister Sophie has remained an important source of support. Price credited her with helping during difficult periods, even when she ignored advice.

Sophie has reportedly stopped involving herself in her sister's romantic decisions. Price, who previously married Peter Andre, Alex Reid and Kieran Hayler, maintained that four marriages had not changed her determination to choose her partners.

'My family aren't marrying them,' she said.

Price also discussed undergoing relationship therapy and becoming clearer about what she wants from future relationships.

Her latest podcast remarks nevertheless introduce another question. She has confirmed plans to see Andrews in Dubai, but neither has publicly established whether the planned meeting signals another change in their relationship.

excerpt: Ashley Judd recalls Naomi Judd's 'Trump' surgery joke and explains why the name written on her thigh concerned her ahead of a 2020 operation.
headline: Ashley Judd Says Late Mum Naomi Wrote 'Trump' on Her Inner Thigh Before 2020 Surgery at Hospital
html_content:
Ashley Judd says her late mother, Naomi Judd, wrote 'Trump' on her inner thigh before a minor bladder operation at a Tennessee hospital in 2020. Recalling the incident on her new podcast, the actress explained why she challenged what she understood to be an attempt at humour.

The story emerged in the first full episode of A Table Prepared, released on Thursday, 12 November 2026. Naomi had once worked as a nurse at the hospital and knew the surgeon who would operate on her, according to Ashley.

Before the procedure, Naomi used a Sharpie normally reserved for signing autographs to write Donald Trump's surname on her skin. Ashley said her mother hoped to relieve the awkwardness of a situation she found deeply uncomfortable.

Ashley, however, worried about the people other than the surgeon who might see the inscription in the operating theatre.

Ashley Judd Recalls Her Mother's Discomfort Before Surgery

Naomi had known the doctor since she was a nurse in her 30s, Ashley explained. The prospect of being examined by someone familiar from her working life made the operation especially difficult for her.

'She was nervous and she was ashamed,' Ashley said, describing her mother's feelings about being in such a physically and socially vulnerable position.

Ashley understood the gesture as a joke designed to ease that embarrassment. Her account did not establish that Naomi meant the word 'Trump' as an endorsement of the politician, who was president when the operation reportedly took place.

Ashley referred to the hospital by its former name, Williamson County Hospital. Williamson Health's official history says it became Williamson Medical Center in 1986, when the facility moved to a new site in Franklin.

The 2020 procedure remains part of Ashley's recollection. No hospital records have been presented to independently confirm the circumstances, and Ashley did not accuse the surgeon or the hospital of wrongdoing.

Why Ashley Judd Questioned the Message Hospital Staff Might See

'What if you were a nurse in that O.R.?' Ashley recalled asking her mother. She also raised the possibility of an orderly encountering the writing while assisting with the operation.

Ashley asked Naomi to think about workers of colour or those whose immigration status might influence how they understood the message. These were hypothetical concerns, not descriptions of employees known to have been present.

She also questioned how her mother's fame might affect the encounter. Naomi was a widely recognised country singer who had previously worked at the hospital. Ashley argued that the words could be received differently by staff who did not share her status.

The disagreement was therefore about more than whether the surgeon would laugh. Ashley wanted her mother to consider everyone whose job might bring them into contact with the writing.

There is no evidence in the published account that staff saw the inscription, complained or were affected by it. Nor did Ashley suggest that the operation was disrupted.

Ashley co-hosts A Table Prepared with Anglican priest Dan Scott. According to the podcast's producer, the series explores family relationships, compassion and disagreements over deeply held beliefs.

Naomi, who performed with her daughter Wynonna as The Judds, died on 30 April 2022, aged 76. Ashley is now revisiting a private disagreement years after her mother's death.

Despite her objections at the time, Ashley said she eventually let the matter go.

Ashley wanted her mother to consider everyone whose job might bring them into contact with the writing. There is no evidence in the published account that staff saw the inscription, complained or were affected by it. Nor did Ashley suggest that the operation was disrupted. Ashley co-hosts A Table Prepared with Anglican priest Dan Scott. According to the podcast's producer, the series explores family relationships, compassion and disagreements over deeply held beliefs. Naomi, who performed with her daughter Wynonna as The Judds, died on 30 April 2022, aged 76. Ashley is now revisiting a private disagreement years after her mother's death. Despite her objections at the time, Ashley said she eventually let the matter go.

excerpt: Trump's BBC defamation lawsuit can proceed after a Florida judge dismissed a separate claim, with a disputed deposition deadline approaching.
headline: Judge Refuses To Toss Trump's $10B BBC Suit While Network Says He Skipped Deposition for Campaigning
html_content:
President Donald Trump's BBC defamation lawsuit can proceed in Florida after a federal judge rejected the broadcaster's dismissal bid on Tuesday, 10 November 2026. However, the judge dismissed a separate consumer-law claim, leaving Trump with a partial victory.

The case concerns a BBC Panorama documentary, Trump: A Second Chance?, broadcast on 28 October 2024. Trump estimates his damages at approximately $10 billion, but the court has made no award. The broadcaster apologised for its editing of his speech and denies that it defamed him.

A separate dispute over Trump's testimony is also unresolved. He faces an 11 December deadline to answer questions under oath after cancelling a deposition scheduled for October.

Why Trump's BBC Defamation Lawsuit Can Proceed

US District Judge Jeffrey T. Kuntz concluded that Trump's allegations were sufficient to survive the BBC's request for dismissal. His 10 November order did not determine whether the broadcaster committed defamation or caused the damage Trump alleges.

The documentary joined separate passages from Trump's speech on 6 January 2021, before his supporters attacked the US Capitol. Remarks about walking towards the Capitol were combined with words spoken nearly 55 minutes later, including 'fight like hell'.

The disputed segment omitted Trump's instruction that supporters should make their voices heard 'peacefully and patriotically'. The editing made the remarks appear to form one continuous statement.

BBC chair Samir Shah acknowledged the problem in correspondence with MPs on 10 November 2025. He apologised for an 'error of judgement', accepting that the edit suggested a direct call for violent action. The BBC subsequently apologised to Trump but maintained that the mistake did not amount to defamation.

Kuntz found that Trump's allegations plausibly met the US legal requirement of 'actual malice'. To succeed, Trump must prove the BBC published a false statement knowing it was false or with reckless disregard for the truth.

That finding concerned the adequacy of Trump's allegations, not proof of wrongdoing. The judge also dismissed his claim under Florida's Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, ruling that the documentary was editorial rather than commercial speech.

Trump called the decision a 'Huge Victory' on Truth Social. The BBC said it was surprised but respected the ruling and remained confident in its position. Its response to the surviving claim is due by 1 December.

Deposition Dispute Adds Pressure to Trump's BBC Defamation Lawsuit

US Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett ordered Trump to attend a deposition by 11 December after his lawyers cancelled questioning scheduled for 16 October. They cited 'matters of national importance'.

BBC lawyer Charles Tobin argued that Trump had prioritised political campaigning over his deposition. The president attended a rally in Dalton, Georgia, that day, although the rally alone does not establish why he cancelled.

Trump's lawyers disputed the suggestion that he was avoiding questioning. They proposed a new window from 11 to 22 January 2027, beyond the existing December deadline.

Lett warned that failure to comply could bring sanctions, potentially including dismissal of the lawsuit, unless the discovery timetable is extended.

The BBC also disputes whether the documentary reached American audiences. Trump's lawyers acknowledged gaps in evidence concerning some proposed US distribution routes. However, Kuntz found sufficient alleged links to Florida for the case to remain there.

A July court order allowed the BBC to seek financial records from Trump's trust. The documents could bear on the reputational and economic losses he says the broadcast caused.

excerpt: Reports put Natalie Harp's annual salary at $150,000 and describe access to Trump's private dining room amid criticism of his inner circle.
headline: Trump Aide Natalie Harp Reportedly Earns $150,000 and Allegedly Uses POTUS' Dining Room
html_content:
Natalie Harp reportedly earns $150,000 (£113,350.35) a year as Donald Trump's executive assistant and allegedly works from his private White House dining room, amid criticism of his inner circle following Susie Wiles' reported departure as chief of staff in November.

The scrutiny follows remarks attributed to an unnamed senior administration official about personal loyalties and rivalries in the West Wing. Columnist Maureen Callahan examined Trump's relationships with female advisers in an opinion piece, questioning whether admiration for the president carried greater weight than political experience.

Natalie Harp's Reported Access Extends to Trump's Dining Room

Harp, 35, is a former One America News Network host who frequently accompanies Trump during public appearances and official trips. Her reported annual salary relates to her position as an executive assistant.

White House staffers have reportedly nicknamed her the 'Human Printer' because she regularly provides Trump with printed articles and favourable news coverage. Reports also describe her as a gatekeeper who influences which information reaches the president.

Trump has allegedly allowed Harp to work in his private dining room near the Oval Office and watch television with him. That reported arrangement places her close to the president beyond the public appearances at which she is regularly seen.

Her proximity to Trump has reportedly frustrated other administration staff members, some of whom have questioned the extent of her influence. The criticism centres on access to the president and the role of personal loyalty within his advisory circle.

Natalie Harp Features in Criticism of Trump's Inner Circle

The unnamed official quoted in the reporting described the West Wing as a 'lunch table' and warned against a 'mean-girl machine' more interested in controlling access than building a lasting legacy.

The remarks were attributed to an unnamed official. They do not establish Harp's responsibilities or performance, nor do they constitute a documented assessment of the administration's hiring decisions.

Callahan separately questioned whether Trump prioritised personal loyalty and admiration over political experience. Her account contrasted the advisers closest to him with Wiles, whose political experience had supported his return to the White House.

The columnist also suggested Harp had effectively replaced conservative activist Laura Loomer as one of Trump's most devoted supporters. Loomer had considerable access to Trump during the 2024 campaign and reportedly influenced his views about the loyalty of certain administration figures.

Callahan cited Katie Zacharia's five-day tenure as White House press secretary as another example of instability within the advisory circle. These comparisons formed part of her commentary, rather than established findings that personal admiration outweighed professional qualifications.

Wiles' Departure Provides Context for Natalie Harp Scrutiny

Wiles, 69, reportedly resigned as White House chief of staff earlier in November after playing a major role in Trump's return to office. Her departure followed Republican losses in the 3 November midterm elections, although Trump maintained that the leadership change was unrelated to the results.

On 6 November, Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Wiles.

Callahan presented Wiles' departure as part of her wider criticism of the influence of younger female advisers around Trump. Her comparison focused on the distinction she drew between political experience and personal admiration for the president.

Karoline Leavitt previously defended Harp amid questions about her access to the president. She confirmed that the aide had obtained security clearance and described her as a loyal and hardworking member of the administration.

excerpt: Thomas Markle Sr. reportedly faces a maximum 20-year sentence if convicted of possessing child pornography following a Florida arrest.
headline: Prosecutors Confirm Thomas Markle Sr., 82, Faces Up to 20 Years in Prison if Convicted on Charge
html_content:
Thomas Markle Sr., 82, reportedly faces one count of possessing child pornography following his arrest in Florida on 6 November 2026. According to the report, prosecutors identified a maximum possible sentence of 20 years if he is convicted.

The reported arrest followed an investigation that began after his son, Thomas Markle Jr., alerted authorities to material allegedly discovered at his father's former home in the Philippines. Federal investigators subsequently searched two storage units connected to the elder Markle near Los Angeles, according to the account.

Authorities reportedly stressed that the maximum sentence would not be automatic following a conviction. The potential penalty does not establish what sentence, if any, Markle might receive.

Thomas Markle Sr.'s Reported Charge Follows Searches

Investigators allegedly recovered approximately 80 items containing suspected child sexual abuse material from the two storage units.

The reported discoveries included slides, photographic negatives and books believed to contain illegal images.

The account describes an investigation that progressed from examining suspected material to bringing a criminal charge. The allegations concerning the material and its possession remain subject to the court process.

Meghan Markle's Estrangement From Thomas Markle Sr.

Meghan Markle has reportedly remained estranged from her father since preparations for her 2018 wedding to Prince Harry. The allegations have brought renewed attention to that relationship and her decision to prevent contact between her father and her children.

The report attributes comments to Meghan describing her as 'deeply distressed' by the allegations and stating that her thoughts 'are with any children who may have been harmed.'

Meghan and Harry share Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5. A person described in the report as a friend of Meghan outlined the emotional strain surrounding the allegations.

'Meghan has been left deeply shaken by everything that has emerged, and the possibility of her father facing such a lengthy prison sentence has only added to an already incredibly distressing situation. As a mother of two young children, the nature of these allegations is particularly difficult for her to comprehend.

Her overriding concern is for any children who may have suffered, and the whole situation has brought enormous emotional strain. It's an extremely painful chapter for someone who has already endured years of turmoil surrounding her relationship with her father.'

Thomas Markle Sr. Allegations Prompt Reported Appeal

Meghan and Harry are understood to have received updates about the investigation while on holiday with their children during the school break, according to the report.

In a statement attributed to Meghan, she addressed criticism of her decision to prevent her father from having contact with his grandchildren.

'I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.'

The statement also included the words, 'I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.'

Her reported statement also included an appeal for the protection of children.

'Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.'

excerpt: Cole Tomas Allen, accused of attempting to assassinate Donald Trump, now faces a terrorism charge over an alleged shooting at a Secret Service checkpoint in Washington.
headline: Cole Allen Charged With Terrorism, But How Did He Get So Close to Trump With Weapons at White House Dinner?
html_content:
Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old California man accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump, faces a new terrorism charge following a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in Washington.

Federal prosecutors announced the additional count on Friday, 13 November, more than six months after the incident at the Washington Hilton.

The charge follows an April shooting at a Secret Service screening checkpoint while Trump was attending the dinner. Prosecutors allege Allen carried a shotgun through a magnetometer and fired at an officer before being arrested. The crucial unanswered question is how close he actually came to the president.

How Cole Allen Reached the Dinner Security Checkpoint

According to the Justice Department's April account, Allen travelled by train from California, changing services in Chicago before arriving in Washington on 24 April. He had booked a room at the Washington Hilton on 6 April and checked in the day before the event.

On 25 April, shortly after 8.30pm, prosecutors say Allen approached a Secret Service checkpoint on the hotel's Terrace Level. He allegedly sprinted through a magnetometer carrying a Mossberg Maverick 88 12-gauge pump-action shotgun.

The department says he ran towards stairs leading to the ballroom where Trump was present. As he did so, he allegedly fired the shotgun, striking a Secret Service officer once in the chest.

The officer, who was wearing a ballistic vest, fired five shots in response, according to prosecutors. Allen fell, was restrained and arrested. Authorities said he sustained a minor knee injury but was not struck by gunfire.

Prosecutors said investigators recovered the shotgun and a .38-calibre pistol, alongside ammunition, two knives, four daggers, holsters and other equipment. They have not established that Allen entered the ballroom or specified how far he was from Trump.

Those details narrow the security question considerably. The alleged breach took place at a screening checkpoint, rather than inside the room where the president was attending the dinner.

🚨 A federal grand jury just added a terrorism charge against Cole Tomas Allen, the man accused of trying to assassinate President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.

He now faces 5 counts, and his trial is set for Sept 2027.

Justice must be served.

Lock him up… pic.twitter.com/0J6GOzHkpx

— Mila Joy (@Milajoy) November 13, 2026

Cole Allen's New Terrorism Charge and the Evidence Cited

A five-count superseding indictment announced on 13 November adds one count of committing an act of terrorism while armed under District of Columbia law. Prosecutors linked that allegation to the attempted first-degree murder of Trump.

Allen previously faced four charges, including attempted presidential assassination, assault on a federal officer with a deadly weapon, transporting a firearm across state lines with the intent to commit a felony and discharging a firearm during a crime of violence. The Justice Department says he faces a maximum possible penalty of life imprisonment if convicted.

In May, US Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro said prosecutors had evidence Allen intended to assassinate Trump. FBI Director Kash Patel also alleged that Allen travelled to Washington to target the president and administration officials. Those assertions remain allegations to be tested in court.

The Justice Department's April statement described an email allegedly sent by Allen to family members and a former employer shortly before the shooting. Investigators obtained a copy from a recipient, prosecutors said. The message included an apology for the trouble he expected to cause.

The FBI Washington Field Office is investigating the case. The November announcement did not identify any changes to security arrangements after the shooting, and Allen is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

excerpt: A Jesus statue was smashed at a Vilnius shrine, prompting a police investigation, an appeal from clergy and warnings about altered images
headline: Golden Jesus Christ Statue Allegedly Stolen and Smashed by Suspected 'Drunk British Tourists' in Vilnius
html_content:
Lithuanian police are investigating after a gold-coloured Jesus statue was removed from a cross and smashed at a Vilnius shrine on Wednesday 11 November 2026. CCTV footage shows one man holding the sculpture while another appears to photograph him.

The incident occurred at about 9pm in the inner courtyard of the Shrine of Divine Mercy on Dominikonų Street. Police opened a pre-trial investigation into a suspected public order offence, and the church appealed for help identifying the man.

By Friday 13 November, investigators were still seeking his identity. Meanwhile, manipulated images circulating online had added misleading claims to an incident already attracting attention.

CCTV Captures the Moments Before Jesus Statue Breaks

Footage circulated by the church shows a man carrying the figure towards another man sitting on a bench. He holds it up while his companion appears to take a photograph. The statue then falls and breaks into pieces, and both men leave.

The men can be heard speaking English, according to Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT. That does not establish their nationality or whether they were visiting Lithuania. Police have not confirmed claims that they were British tourists or intoxicated.

The shrine's vice-rector, Elijas Anatolijus Markauskas, told local journalists that he believed the man handling the sculpture appeared intoxicated. That remains his assessment, not an official finding. Nor have investigators publicly established whether the damage was deliberate.

Markauskas said the statue was made of plastic rather than precious metal. Yet its modest material did not make it unimportant to the congregation. The figure had been blessed, and people regularly prayed beside it.

The priest said the church bought the sculpture approximately eight years ago for €1,000. He estimated that replacing it might cost about €2,000. Police, however, have not announced a final assessment of the financial loss.

Church Appeals for Help as Altered Jesus Statue Images Spread

Markauskas shared footage of the incident and asked people who recognised the man to contact police. His appeal particularly addressed Old Town residents and staff at nearby accommodation businesses, who might have information useful to investigators.

The church also expressed grief at the damage and appealed for prayer and forgiveness. Its response reflected the shrine's religious significance. The church houses the original Divine Mercy painting associated with St Faustina Kowalska, a focus of devotion for pilgrims.

A separate problem emerged online. On 13 November, Lithuanian fact-checkers at 15min reported that images promoted as clearer pictures of the suspected perpetrator had been altered using artificial intelligence. The changes affected facial features, making the images unreliable for identification.

The report warned that presenting AI-generated details as improvements to blurry CCTV could fuel false assumptions about a person's background. The altered pictures should not be treated as authentic evidence of anyone's identity.

Vilnius police said an unidentified person had removed the sculpture from its wooden cross and broken it. The investigation is proceeding under Article 284 of Lithuania's Criminal Code, concerning public order violations. Police have not announced a theft charge.

On 13 November, officers said they were still trying to identify the suspected perpetrator. Markauskas said he hoped the church could install a replacement before Advent, while its appeal for information remained open.

excerpt: A pastor cheating allegation has drawn attention on TikTok after a woman recalled a childhood encounter involving a church piano and a younger woman
headline: Woman Says She Was 8 When Church Piano Noise Led to 50-Year-Old Pastor: 'We Book It Out of the Room'
html_content:
A pastor cheating allegation has attracted attention on TikTok after a woman claimed she discovered a minister with a younger woman at her church when she was eight.

Creator @828deev described the alleged encounter in a video posted on Tuesday, 10 November 2026, saying a loud piano noise led her and a friend to investigate.

She claimed she later saw the pastor hurriedly pulling up his trousers. However, neither the encounter nor the alleged infidelity has been independently verified.

The account concerns a childhood experience rather than a recent incident. The creator has not identified the church, the pastor or the woman allegedly involved.

How a Church Piano Noise Led to the Alleged Encounter

According to @828deev, she and a friend were attending a children's Bible class when a youth pastor sent them to collect sweets. The treats were stored in a fridge near the church auditorium's stage. Children participating in the activity were supposed to earn them by reciting a prayer.

The errand took an unexpected turn when the girls heard a loud noise coming from the piano. Although frightened, they approached to find out what had happened.

The creator claimed they discovered a pastor sitting on the piano bench beside a considerably younger woman. She estimated that the minister was around 50, while the woman appeared to be in her 20s.

She also believed the younger woman attended the church, although neither her identity nor her relationship with the pastor has been established.

Recalling their immediate reaction, the creator said, 'We book it out of the room and then like we close the door hella hard.'

The girls hurried away with the sweets, but the creator claimed she glanced back through a window in the door. She said she saw the pastor pulling up his trousers, leading her to suspect he had been unfaithful to his wife.

Her account does not establish what happened before the girls entered the room.

When they returned to class, the youth pastor reportedly asked whether everything was all right. Both girls said they were fine and continued their lesson without mentioning the encounter.

Pastor Cheating Allegation Draws Reactions and Unanswered Questions

The creator said she believed the pastor never discovered who had entered the room. She also recalled that she and her friend devised 'the most insane [...] plan ever' afterwards.

However, she did not reveal what the plan involved, indicating that she intended to continue the story in another video.

Comments reproduced in contemporaneous reporting showed viewers sharing their own experiences involving church leaders. One recalled an alleged affair involving a pastor at another church. Another expressed sympathy, writing, 'I am sorry you went through this.'

Those reactions do not independently corroborate the creator's allegations.

Questions surrounding adultery among religious leaders have previously been examined by Lifeway Research.

https://www.tiktok.com/player/v1/7706415883408706846?embed_from=oembed&music_info=1&description=1&autoplay=1&muted=1

Its survey of 1,000 US Protestant pastors, conducted in 2019 and published in August 2020, found that 27% supported permanent withdrawal from public ministry for pastors who committed adultery. Another 31% were unsure how long they should withdraw, while 2% believed no withdrawal was necessary.

The findings reflect opinions about hypothetical misconduct, not evidence concerning this particular allegation.

The identities of those allegedly involved remain undisclosed, and the available reporting provides no independent corroboration of the claimed affair. What happened after the girls returned to class also remains unclear.

excerpt: Rajendra Barautiya died in Madhya Pradesh after a cheese-dough ball filled with gunpowder exploded in his mouth, while police investigate the device's origin and the neighbour's intent.
headline: 'It Exploded in His Mouth': Indian Man, 35, Dies After Eating Crude Bomb Disguised as Sweet Dessert
html_content:
Rajendra Barautiya, 35, died on Tuesday in Madhya Pradesh's Dindori district after a crude bomb disguised as a sweet dessert exploded in his mouth, police said.

Barautiya had finished dinner with his family and was sitting beside a bonfire outside his home when a neighbour handed him what appeared to be a rasgulla, according to India Today. The popular sweet is made from cottage cheese.

What appeared to be a traditional dessert was instead a ball of cheese dough filled with gunpowder. Police said the explosive detonated when Barautiya put it in his mouth. He suffered severe injuries and was taken to hospital, where he was pronounced dead, according to the coverage.

A Crude Bomb Presented as a Sweet

Police officer Rekha Singh described the fatal explosion in comments to AFP. Her statement identified the device as a type some people in the area use to kill wild boars.

'The bomb, used by some tribal people in the area to kill wild boars, was offered to this man,' Singh told AFP. 'It exploded in his mouth.'

The device's resemblance to a rasgulla forms part of the description of how it was offered to Barautiya. The cheese dough concealed gunpowder, rather than forming an ordinary dessert. The explosive was described as a method employed by villagers against wild boars in Dindori district.

That description does not establish why this particular device was handed to Barautiya. Police were examining both how it had been obtained and the reason it was offered to him.

Questions Surround the Crude Bomb's Origin

A homicide case against the neighbour, identified as Ram Bhagat Barotiya, and another man was pending, according to the coverage. Officials were investigating how the neighbour had obtained the crude bomb and why he offered it to Barautiya.

The existence of the pending case does not resolve the question of intent. Singh explicitly left open whether Barautiya's death followed an attempt to kill him or a malicious prank.

The sequence described by India Today places the encounter after a family meal, with Barautiya sitting outdoors beside the bonfire. It identifies the neighbour as the person who handed him the apparent sweet. It does not, by itself, establish that the neighbour intended the fatal outcome.

Barautiya's injuries and subsequent death were described separately from the investigation into motive. Police described the explosion, while Singh's comments left the purpose behind offering the device unresolved.

Police Examine Intent Behind the Crude Bomb

Singh outlined the uncertainty when discussing the investigation. 'We do not know whether the intention was to kill him or whether it was a malicious prank. That will be determined during the investigation,' Singh stated.

Her comments describe two possibilities under examination, rather than a conclusion about either. Singh's statement did not identify either possibility as the established explanation for the explosion. Her comments placed the question of intent within the investigation into Barautiya's death.

Officials were also investigating how the crude bomb had been obtained. Alongside that inquiry, the question Singh identified remained why an explosive device employed against wild boars had been offered to Barautiya as something to eat.

excerpt: Jean Guerrero, author of Hatemonger, told Wired that criminalising migrants can weaken collective worker organising, while questioning Stephen Miller's immigration and foreign policy outlook.
headline: Biographer Jean Guerrero Labels Stephen Miller a 'Class Supremacist' Who Wants a 'Servant Class'
html_content:
Stephen Miller's biographer Jean Guerrero has criticised the administration's approach to immigration, arguing in comments to Wired that criminalising migrants weakens workers' ability to organise together and demand better conditions.

Guerrero examined the White House official in Hatemonger, published in 2020. In that book, she described Miller as a 'key player' in delivering Donald Trump's America First agenda. Her interview returned to his political outlook and explained how her interpretation had developed since Trump's first administration.

Guerrero Questions Stephen Miller's Immigration Approach

Guerrero's criticism centred on the relationship between immigration policy and workers' collective position. She argued that attention to the administration's treatment of immigrants could obscure the consequences for their ability to join other workers.

'By focusing all the attention on the war on immigrants, it distracts us from understanding that when you have one sector of the population that is being criminalized and forced to stay in the shadows, then they cannot link arms with other workers to demand to live with dignity,' Guerrero stated.

Her argument concerned the effects she believed those circumstances had on organising. She connected the position of immigrants with the wider working population through their shared ability to demand dignity.

That emphasis on class formed part of her reassessment of Miller. Guerrero explained that she had returned to her earlier work while considering the administration's approach to immigration and foreign policy.

How Foreign Policy Shaped Her Stephen Miller Assessment

Guerrero referred to Venezuela and the elections in Honduras when outlining questions that had contributed to her thinking. She questioned the relationship between the administration's actions abroad and its position on migration.

'I came to this conclusion because when I first saw what the administration was doing on the foreign policy front, I was confused,' she stated.

'Why would they be interfering in Venezuela or the elections in Honduras, when we know those are the exact types of actions that cause instability and migration?'

Her question linked her criticism of foreign intervention to the consequences she believed it had for migration and immigration policy.

She also cited an exchange with Jake Tapper in which, according to Guerrero, Miller described international affairs in terms of strength, force and power.

Guerrero quoted Miller as telling Tapper, 'You can talk all you want about international niceties and everything else. But we live in a world, in the real world, Jake, that is governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power,' and explained that his remarks prompted her to reread sections of her book.

White House Highlights Stephen Miller's Policy Work

The White House defended Miller by emphasising his contribution to Trump's agenda. Its statement credited him with work across policing, deregulation, energy, drug cartels and border security.

Those descriptions represented the White House's assessment of his record. The response focused on the administration's policy priorities and Miller's role in advancing them.

'Stephen Miller has been a key player in delivering on President Trump's America First agenda, including spearheading the administration's crime crackdown, including in DC and Memphis, record-setting deregulation, unleashing American energy, dismantling drug cartels, and securing our border'

excerpt: Andrew Neil has warned that Donald Trump's economic policies could create serious risks, citing rapid money-supply growth, a large deficit and limited options during a potential AI downturn.
headline: Andrew Neil Warns Donald Trump's Economic Policies 'Will End in Tears' Amid Stagflation Concerns
html_content:
Andrew Neil has warned that Donald Trump's economic policies will 'end in tears', arguing that monetary and fiscal policy are both running too hot late in the economic cycle.

The presenter of The Andrew Neil Report discussed his concerns with Gerard Baker on Friday's Times Radio podcast. Baker is a columnist at The Times and editor-at-large at The Wall Street Journal.

Trump had been touting a roaring economy. Neil's comments addressed the outlook for monetary and fiscal policy and the risks he anticipated. Neil focused on the money supply, the deficit and the scope for responding if an AI boom were to collapse, while Baker warned against expectations of a steady political transition following the election.

Why Andrew Neil Warns About Economic Policy

Neil argued that the timing of the policy approach was central to his concerns. He described monetary and fiscal policy as both running 'hot hot, hot' in the late stages of the economic cycle.

'You don't run hot on both [of these] at the end of an economic cycle. You're supposed to run both after we've hit an economic recession, then you run things hot.'

He cited growth in America's broad money, describing it as 'now rising by 7 percent'. Broad money is the sum of liquid financial instruments held by money-holding sectors and serves as a measure of an economy's money supply.

Neil also pointed to the deficit. 'Plus, the deficit is at least 6.5 percent, probably headed for 7 percent of GDP,' he stated.

His warning connected the money supply increase with the scale of the deficit. He argued that running both monetary and fiscal policy hot at this stage of the economic cycle would have consequences.

Budget Bargaining Adds to Andrew Neil's Concerns

During his 2024 campaign, Trump pledged to eliminate the national debt within one term without cutting 'one penny' from Social Security or Medicare. His proposed approach relied on economic growth, crypto and tariffs.

Neil argued that divided government following the election could worsen spending pressures through the bargaining required to pass a budget.

He outlined hypothetical exchanges in which additional defence spending would be paired with more health spending, or funding for a border wall with more welfare spending. In his view, both sides would secure increases and the deficit would deteriorate further.

Neil linked that prospect to his broader warning about economic policy, stating that 'something big is coming, regardless of AI'.

AI Downturn Raises Andrew Neil's Stagflation Fears

Neil also described a potential AI bust as a 'nightmare scenario'. He warned of limited room for an economic response, citing high interest rates, continuing high inflation and a fiscal position he described as 'completely out of control'.

His reference to stagflation was a warning about a risk. It did not establish that the scenario had materialised.

Baker separately challenged expectations that the election would bring a steady transition towards Trump's retirement. He cautioned that anyone anticipating that outcome was 'going to be in for a bit of a shock'.

'Fasten your seatbelts on the political front and on the economic front. It's going to be wild.'

excerpt: A purported GTA 6 map appeared online after a folded version was displayed at Selfridges in Manchester, alongside reports on launch plans, pre-loading and technical features.
headline: Purported GTA 6 Map Circulates Online as Rockstar Games Confirms 30FPS Frame Rate and 210GB File Size
html_content:
A purported GTA 6 map circulated online after a folded map from the game's Collector's Box was displayed at Selfridges in Manchester, according to Indy100, whose coverage also described a 30fps frame rate and an approximate 210GB storage requirement.

The publication linked the image to preparations for a scheduled 19 November release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Its live coverage described pre-loading arrangements, allowing players who pre-ordered the Standard or Ultimate Edition to download the game ahead of launch.

How the GTA 6 Map Circulated Online

Indy100 described a folded physical map on display at the Manchester department store. Someone then appeared to have posted the full map on social media before apparently deleting their entire profile, the publication wrote.

The connection between the display and the circulating image rests on that coverage. The image should therefore be treated as a purported map, with its authenticity unresolved in Indy100's description.

Alongside the map discussion, Indy100 described another social media post attracting attention. An Instagram video from onlyindade appeared to depict a Vice City street, non-player characters and vehicles, including a police vehicle.

According to the publication, Rockstar Games reposted the video to its official Instagram Story. Indy100 characterised that action as apparent confirmation of the footage, rather than quoting an explicit statement authenticating it.

Launch Details Accompany the GTA 6 Map Coverage

Rockstar's promotional message encouraged players to pre-order and pre-load, and stated that code-in-box versions were available for collection from retailers worldwide. The company also wrote in a comment, 'See you in Leonida next week!'

That relative reference belongs to the promotional post. Indy100 identified 19 November as the launch date without specifying a release year, so the timing cannot be placed definitively from its coverage alone.

The publication described PlayStation 5 pre-loading as beginning at midnight on 10 November in local time zones. For Xbox Series X/S, it listed a simultaneous start at 12am GMT on 10 November.

It also distinguished the launch arrangements. PlayStation 5 players were given midnight on 19 November in their local time zones, while Xbox Series X/S players were given a universal release time of 12am GMT.

Take-Two Interactive chief executive Strauss Zelnick confirmed during an earnings call that development was complete and the game had gone gold, according to Indy100. The publication explained that this meant the final consumer version was ready.

Performance Features Beyond the GTA 6 Map

Indy100 attributed confirmation of a 30fps frame rate to Rockstar Games. However, the approximate 210GB storage figure appeared in the publication's narrative, rather than in the Rockstar statement it quoted.

That statement outlined improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows available only on PlayStation 5 Pro. It also described DualSense haptic feedback adjustable through accessibility settings, improved spatial audio and faster load times on PlayStation 5.

Rockstar's statement also outlined availability through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One consoles, employing Xbox Series S graphics settings. It specified support for Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.

The company cautioned, 'And as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay.'

excerpt: Clinical and forensic psychologist John Paul Garrison questioned an apparent shift in Donald Trump's speech during a Veterans Day address, but said the clip did not establish a medical condition.
headline: Forensic Psychologist Breaks Down Why Donald Trump Was 'Constantly Swaying' During Veterans Day Speech
html_content:
Clinical and forensic psychologist John Paul Garrison has questioned changes in President Donald Trump's speech delivery during his Veterans Day address at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia on Wednesday 11 November 2026.

Garrison suggested that an abrupt shift in the president's voice merited scrutiny, although his comments did not establish any medical condition.

Trump was speaking at a ceremony honouring American military veterans. His address followed tributes to those who served, including remarks from Vice President JD Vance.

The president praised veterans and their families while discussing his administration's military policies.

Garrison subsequently analysed a clip from the address in a video on his YouTube channel. His comments were reported on Saturday 14 November, with attention focused on the pace and clarity of Trump's speech.

What Psychologist John Paul Garrison Questioned About Trump's Speech

Garrison questioned whether Trump understood everything he was saying. 'I really don't think he understands what he's saying,' he remarked, according to the published account of his analysis.

The psychologist also highlighted what he perceived as a sudden change in delivery near the end of the clip. He compared the transition to a switch being flipped, then replayed the passage to discuss the difference in Trump's voice.

'The way that he sounded shifted so dramatically,' Garrison said. 'It does make me wonder if that was the end of some kind of neurological event.'

His wording was a question about a possible explanation, not a medical finding. The available report does not establish that Trump experienced a neurological episode, or that changes in his voice resulted from illness.

Donald Trump's Veterans Day Remarks and the Medical Record

The White House's account of the ceremony focused on Trump's tribute to American service personnel. In the published transcript, the president praised veterans' sacrifices and promised continued support for those who served.

'While I'm president of the United States, we will always fulfill our duty to them,' Trump said.

The ceremony took place at Arlington National Cemetery, where Trump addressed veterans and military families. Vance introduced him after also paying tribute to those who had served.

Questions about the president's health require particular care. In a medical report released in May 2026, presidential physician Sean P. Barbabella described Trump as being in excellent health and reported normal neurological function.

The physician also reported a perfect score on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, a screening test of cognitive abilities. That result reflects the assessment administered at the time, not an independent evaluation of the November footage.

Garrison's comments likewise cannot establish Trump's health status. They remain one psychologist's interpretation of a recording, rather than evidence that a neurological event took place during the Veterans Day speech.
