Trump was speaking at a ceremony honouring American military veterans. His address followed tributes to those who served, including remarks from Vice President JD Vance. The president praised veterans and their families while discussing his administration's military policies. Garrison subsequently analysed a clip from the address in a video on his YouTube channel. His comments were reported on Saturday 14 November, with attention focused on the pace and clarity of Trump's speech. 'I really don't think he understands what he's saying,' he remarked, according to the published account of his analysis. The psychologist also highlighted what he perceived as a sudden change in delivery near the end of the clip. He compared the transition to a switch being flipped, then replayed the passage to discuss the difference in Trump's voice. 'The way that he sounded shifted so dramatically,' Garrison said. Barbabella described Trump as being in excellent health and reported normal neurological function. excerpt: Steve Camp, the Grammy-nominated Christian singer and pastor, has died aged 71 after a battle with heart failure, his family announced, following decades of music and ministry.
headline: How Did Steve Camp Die? Christian Singer Who Warned of 'Lukewarm Laodicean Sleep' Passes Away at 71
html_content:
[Christian singer and pastor] Steve Camp died on Wednesday 11 November 2026, aged 71, after a battle with heart failure, his family announced. The Grammy-nominated musician spent more than five decades combining Christian music, preaching and ministry.

The news came through a family statement expressing grief while reflecting on the Christian faith that shaped Camp's life.

'It is with heavy hearts, yet great hope in Christ, that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, and grandfather, Steve Camp,' the family wrote.

Beyond his recordings, Camp became an outspoken critic of commercial influences on contemporary Christian music. He argued that biblical teaching should take precedence over popularity and financial success.

How Did Steve Camp Die? Family Confirms Battle With Heart Failure

Camp's family confirmed that he died following a battle with heart failure. They did not disclose further medical circumstances or specify where his death occurred.

'On Wednesday, November 11, 2026, after a battle with heart failure, the Lord called Steve Home,' the statement said.

His relatives reflected on his commitment to Christian evangelism, describing a career extending well beyond music.

'For over 50 years, Steve dedicated his life to proclaiming the Gospel through music, preaching, and life on life ministry,' they wrote.

The family identified Acts 20:24 and 2 Corinthians 4:5 as two Bible passages that influenced Camp's ministry.

The passages emphasise perseverance in preaching the Gospel and proclaiming Jesus Christ rather than oneself.

Those principles also shaped his criticism of the Christian music industry's commercial direction.

His family expressed their belief that Camp had completed his earthly ministry.

'Though our hearts are broken, we rejoice in knowing that Steve has finished his race,' they said.

The family thanked supporters for their prayers and encouragement during their bereavement.

Steve Camp's 'Lukewarm Laodicean Sleep' Warning Reflected His Call for Reform

Camp began his musical career in 1975 and released his debut album, Sayin' It with Love, three years later.

According to the Gospel Music Association, he released 22 albums, achieved 15 No. 1 songs and recorded more than 40 Top 10 hits.

His recording of 'Love's Not a Feeling' with Michele Pillar earned a Grammy nomination in 1985.

Despite his commercial achievements, Camp questioned whether Christian artists were compromising their message to appeal to wider audiences.

In 1997, he published 107 theses calling for reform in Christian music and publishing, drawing inspiration from Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses.

His criticism extended beyond recording companies to concerns about complacency within evangelical churches.

In a 31 October 2005 blog post, he warned against a 'lukewarm Laodicean sleep,' urging Christians to pursue spiritual renewal.

Camp subsequently devoted greater attention to pastoral work, becoming an associate pastor at Grace Community Church in 1998.

He was ordained senior pastor of The Cross in 2009, according to his official biography.

His involvement in music nevertheless continued.

On 18 October 2024, Camp released Neighbors in an Age of Rage, returning to full-length studio recording more than two decades after his previous project.

excerpt: State Department budget proposals would shift $888m towards a US-focused health innovation fund while eliminating country-level allocations for eight nations and redirecting most approved family planning aid.
headline: Leaked State Department Budget Shows $888M Moving to US Firms While Eight Nations Lose All Health Aid
html_content:
The Trump administration plans to direct $888 million (£672.2 million) into a US-focused global health innovation fund while reducing country-level allocations for eight nations to zero. The proposals emerged after internal State Department budget documents were made public on Saturday 14 November 2026.

The preliminary fiscal year 2026 report, sent to Congress in May, also outlines plans to withhold or redirect nearly all international family planning funding approved by lawmakers.

An analysis by Public Citizen, Partners In Health and PAI calculated a $1.66 billion (£1.26 billion) reduction in planned country-level health assistance compared with FY 2024.

The documents describe proposed allocations, not completed payments to private companies.

Eight Countries Face Zero Planned Health Allocations

Of 79 countries examined, 69 face lower planned health allocations than in 2024, according to the three organisations.

Eight have their allocations reduced to zero within the report's country-level Global Health Programs comparison.

They are Afghanistan, the Central African Republic, Gambia, South Africa, Somalia, Sudan, Timor-Leste and Yemen.

South Africa faces the largest reduction, at $437.1 million (£330.9 million). Tanzania and Zimbabwe follow with decreases of $137.4 million (£104 million) and $126.1 million (£95.5 million) respectively.

The changes extend to international family planning programmes.

Congress approved $607.5 million (£459.9 million) for family planning and reproductive health assistance, but the administration plans to withhold or redirect approximately $605 million (£458.5 million).

The preliminary report lists $523.95 million (£396.7 million) as 'To Be Programmed,' leaving its eventual allocation uncertain.

Another $32.5 million (£24.6 million) previously designated for the United Nations Population Fund is earmarked for alternative uses.

On 25 September, Secretary of State Marco Rubio authorised the potential redirection of up to $125 million (£94.6 million) in foreign assistance towards energy security.

The accompanying memorandum identified $48.498 million (£36.7 million) previously allocated for family planning.

Rubio cited urgent energy needs arising from supply disruptions and rising costs, particularly those attributed to Russia, China and Iran.

Advocacy groups argue the proposed changes undermine congressional spending decisions. The legality of these specific reallocations has not been established by a court.

US-Focused Innovation Fund Faces Oversight Questions

The proposed innovation fund represents a substantial increase from the $60 million (£45.4 million) set aside in FY 2025.

Its planned allocation has risen to $888 million (£672.2 million), supporting American companies working on health-related technologies.

However, the documents do not identify which businesses would receive the funding.

Public Citizen and its partners questioned how recipients would be selected and whether the government would use competitive procedures.

They warned that directing more money towards commercial innovation while cutting country-level programmes could weaken healthcare services in lower-income nations.

The State Department defended its approach when contacted by CNN.

A spokesman said the administration was reviewing foreign assistance to address critical needs within its appropriated budget and legal authority.

The department also said it was exploring American innovations to save lives more cost-effectively while working with Congress.

Representative Lois Frankel, a Florida Democrat serving on the House Appropriations Committee, criticised the family planning reductions.

She described the administration's refusal to spend congressionally appropriated funding as 'shameful and dangerous.'

The State Department did not answer CNN's specific question about how contracts would be awarded through the innovation fund.

excerpt: Elon Musk says he will sign a petition seeking Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO after the co-founder resigned amid reports of infidelity and national security concerns.
headline: Elon Musk Joins Petition To Reinstate Jensen Huang as Ally Says He Did Something 'Incredibly Dumb'
html_content:
Elon Musk has backed a petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as NVIDIA's chief executive, saying he would sign it following the co-founder's resignation. Musk made the pledge on X on Friday, 13 November, one day after NVIDIA announced Huang's immediate departure.

Earlier, Musk had agreed with Huang supporter Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia Capital, who said Huang had done something 'incredibly dumb' but called him 'irreplaceable' for America's AI leadership.

Huang's resignation followed reports of extramarital relationships and national security concerns involving a woman some US intelligence officials reportedly suspect of having links to Chinese intelligence. The allegations have not been independently substantiated.

Huang acknowledged infidelity in a message to NVIDIA employees on 8 November. He apologised to his family and colleagues but did not identify the person involved. NVIDIA's board had announced an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

The board confirmed Huang's resignation on 12 November and appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. It is searching for a permanent successor. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones, a longtime director and former Synopsys chief executive, as its first chair.

WIRED reported on 12 November that an internal employee suggestion-box post calling for staff views on Huang had attracted more than 1,600 comments. Most supported bringing him back, according to the publication's review of internal correspondence. The post was submitted by a longtime engineer before Huang resigned, and comments continued after his departure.

Elon Musk Backs Calls To Reinstate Jensen Huang

Musk's post came in response to X user @yunta_tsai, who urged NVIDIA employees who wanted Huang back to take collective action. The user argued that skilled chip engineers would be hard to replace.

'Engineers should take their destiny into their own hands if they love the company. They shape and deliver the company mission, not the boards,' the user wrote.

Musk replied: 'A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too.' His post did not identify the petition, its organiser or the number of signatures. The Washington Post reported that it was unclear which petition he meant. It remains unclear whether the petition Musk referenced is connected to the internal employee campaign.

A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 13, 2026

On 12 November, Musk had responded to an @zerohedge post suggesting that he hire Huang. 'That would be an honor,' he replied. Musk did not make a formal offer.

That would be an honor

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 12, 2026

Why Jensen Huang's Supporters Say He Matters

Maguire posted his defence of Huang on 8 November, four days before the resignation. He wrote that Huang had done something 'incredibly dumb' and that it was 'bad for America,' but added that he believed there had been no bad intention.

'Two mistakes don't make a right, and I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership,' Maguire wrote. Musk replied: 'I agree.'

Maguire did not dispute the admitted infidelity. Instead, he emphasised Huang's importance to US artificial intelligence leadership while acknowledging his mistakes.

NVIDIA has not announced plans to reverse Huang's resignation. Its public statement confirmed Kress's interim appointment and the search for a permanent chief executive. Musk's support and employee comments have not resulted in any announced change to the board's decision.

excerpt: Marjorie Taylor Greene accused the Trump administration of exploiting a major aviation disruption to seek $50bn for air traffic control upgrades.
headline: Former Trump Ally Marjorie Taylor Greene Calls $50B FAA Outage Funding Appeal 'Like a Shakedown for More Money'
html_content:
Marjorie Taylor Greene has accused President Donald Trump's administration of using an aviation emergency to press Congress for more money. The former Republican congresswoman called the $50 billion (£37.82 billion) air traffic control modernisation request 'literally like a shakedown for more money' in posts on X on Saturday, 14 November.

Greene alleged officials were lying about Friday's disruption and claimed it was a cyberattack. She provided no evidence. Federal officials said they had found no indication of an attack, but the investigation was continuing.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, 13 November, after telecommunications outages affected air traffic control communications and radar systems. The stop lasted more than four hours and was lifted at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time.

At a White House briefing, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said outdated switches and routers had become overloaded. The Department of Transportation said more than 3,500 aircraft were in the air when the ground stop began. More than 10,000 flights were disrupted, and FlightAware recorded more than 4,100 cancellations on Saturday.

This press conference is unreal bullshit. It’s literally like a shakedown for more money.

Basically they are saying,

Hey guys, relax it’s just our “old antiquated systems and old hardware” that went down causing a communication crisis that forced FAA to ground all airplanes in…

— Former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene🇺🇸 (@FmrRepMTG) November 14, 2026

Greene rejected that explanation. 'Plus they are lying. Of course it was a cyber attack,' she wrote. 'F---ing liars. But build the big ballroom and more weapons that's the only funding they really care about.'

Raw Story reported Greene's comments in posts responding to the briefing. Her cyberattack claim remains unsubstantiated, and the official cause is still under investigation.

Greene Accuses Officials of Using Crisis to Secure Funding

Greene focused on the cost of modernising the air traffic control system. Duffy called the situation an emergency and asked Congress for $50 billion. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said a complete overhaul was estimated to cost about the same amount.

'This press conference is unreal bulls---. It's literally like a shakedown for more money,' Greene wrote. She argued that Americans were being asked to pay more despite already paying taxes.

Mullin said there was no evidence pointing to a cyberattack, but officials were still investigating.

Greene contrasted the aviation request with Trump's call for another $350 billion for the military. Trump made that call in a Truth Social post on 12 November. Greene linked the spending to weapons and the war with Iran.

December Funding Deadline Adds Political Pressure

Congress faces an 11 December deadline for stopgap federal funding. The continuing resolution Trump signed on 2 September funds federal agencies through that date.

Greene accused Duffy and Mullin, both former members of Congress, of using 'a crisis like public blackmail' to win funding. No evidence presented at the briefing showed officials had deliberately caused the outage or misrepresented its cause.

Greene criticised Trump for not addressing the disruption while travellers faced delays. She said he had instead posted about Hollywood and tax incentives. Her comments follow her resignation from the House on 5 January 2026.

Georgia's 14th District elected Clay Fuller as her successor in a 7 April runoff, where he defeated Democrat Shawn Harris. Greene's criticism comes from a former lawmaker who was once a prominent Trump ally.

The outage renewed concerns about ageing air traffic control infrastructure, while the $50 billion overhaul became a political flashpoint. The cause remains under investigation, and Congress has yet to decide whether to provide the funding.

excerpt: US flight schedules are expected to recover by Sunday evening after a nationwide FAA ground stop caused thousands of cancellations, while officials warned further outages remain possible.
headline: FAA Ground Stop Update: Schedule Recovery Set for Sunday as Sean Duffy Warns 'You Will Have More of These'
html_content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) expects US flight schedules to recover by Sunday evening after a nationwide ground stop on Friday, 13 November.

But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has warned that further outages could occur as the country replaces ageing air traffic control equipment.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford gave the recovery forecast on Saturday, while cautioning that flight delays and cancellations would continue.

Officials said new technology installed during a modernisation project had overloaded older systems, causing intermittent communications and radar gaps.

The shutdown lasted more than four hours before departures resumed on Friday evening. It was the country's first nationwide ground stop since January 2023 and its second since the 11 September 2001 attacks.

Flight Disruptions Continue Across the US and UK

Saturday brought another round of disruption as airlines sought to reposition aircraft and crews. FlightAware recorded more than 4,100 cancellations, while aviation data provider Cirium reported more than 3,200.

The figures reflected different tracking services rather than a single agreed total.

Andrew Charlton, managing director of Aviation Advocacy, estimated that Friday's stoppage affected about a quarter of the 45,000 flights operating daily in the United States.

He explained that an aircraft delayed on one route could miss several subsequent journeys, spreading the disruption across the network.

The effects reached Britain. Several flights between London's Heathrow Airport and the United States were listed as delayed or cancelled on Saturday.

Tim Johnson, consumer director at the UK Civil Aviation Authority, warned that airlines might need additional time to rebook travellers and restore services, even though American departures had resumed.

The disruption also derailed personal plans. Emily Brown told the Associated Press that she and her 14-year-old daughter waited over four hours at a Dallas airport before abandoning their flight to Columbus, Ohio.

Her daughter had saved money for the ticket and planned to surprise a friend.

Sports teams were affected too. Mississippi's college football game against Oklahoma was moved from Saturday to Sunday after travel arrangements were disrupted.

Duffy Warns of Further Outages During Modernisation

Duffy said the trouble emerged while a contractor replaced old copper wiring with fibre-optic technology.

Investigators were examining whether a faulty router or contractor error caused the overload. Those possibilities had not been established as the final cause.

The transportation secretary acknowledged that officials had not expected such a serious outage. He warned, 'But, you will have more of these.'

Congress approved $12.5 billion ( £9.46 billion) for air traffic control modernisation in 2025.

Duffy and the White House are seeking another $30 billion ( £22.70 billion), while the FAA continues replacing outdated wiring and radio equipment.

Duffy said the incident was unrelated to a new FAA artificial intelligence system intended to anticipate aviation problems.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said more than 3,000 aircraft already in the air when flights were grounded had landed safely. He maintained that passengers had not been endangered.

Earlier equipment failures disrupted flights around Newark and across the northeastern United States. Friday's outage, however, stretched nationwide, leaving investigators to establish precisely why an equipment upgrade interrupted the network.

But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has warned that further outages could occur as the country replaces ageing air traffic control equipment. Officials said new technology installed during a modernisation project had overloaded older systems, causing intermittent communications and radar gaps. The shutdown lasted more than four hours before departures resumed on Friday evening. It was the country's first nationwide ground stop since January 2023 and its second since the 11 September 2001 attacks. Flight Disruptions Continue Across the US and UK Saturday brought another round of disruption as airlines sought to reposition aircraft and crews. FlightAware recorded more than 4,100 cancellations, while aviation data provider Cirium reported more than 3,200. The figures reflected different tracking services rather than a single agreed total. Andrew Charlton, managing director of Aviation Advocacy, estimated that Friday's stoppage affected about a quarter of the 45,000 flights operating daily in the United States. He explained that an aircraft delayed on one route could miss several subsequent journeys, spreading the disruption across the network. The effects reached Britain. Several flights between London's Heathrow Airport and the United States were listed as delayed or cancelled on Saturday. Tim Johnson, consumer director at the UK Civil Aviation Authority, warned that airlines might need additional time to rebook travellers and restore services, even though American departures had resumed. The disruption also derailed personal plans. Emily Brown told the Associated Press that she and her 14-year-old daughter waited over four hours at a Dallas airport before abandoning their flight to Columbus, Ohio. Her daughter had saved money for the ticket and planned to surprise a friend. Sports teams were affected too. Mississippi's college football game against Oklahoma was moved from Saturday to Sunday after travel arrangements were disrupted. Duffy Warns of Further Outages During Modernisation Duffy said the trouble emerged while a contractor replaced old copper wiring with fibre-optic technology. Investigators were examining whether a faulty router or contractor error caused the overload. Those possibilities had not been established as the final cause. The transportation secretary acknowledged that officials had not expected such a serious outage. He warned, 'But, you will have more of these.' Congress approved $12.5 billion ( £9.46 billion) for air traffic control modernisation in 2025. Duffy and the White House are seeking another $30 billion ( £22.70 billion), while the FAA continues replacing outdated wiring and radio equipment. Duffy said the incident was unrelated to a new FAA artificial intelligence system intended to anticipate aviation problems. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said more than 3,000 aircraft already in the air when flights were grounded had landed safely. He maintained that passengers had not been endangered. Earlier equipment failures disrupted flights around Newark and across the northeastern United States. Friday's outage, however, stretched nationwide, leaving investigators to establish precisely why an equipment upgrade interrupted the network.

excerpt: A disruption during routine FAA telecommunications maintenance may have triggered a four-hour US ground stop, affecting radar and communications and causing thousands of flight cancellations.
headline: What Caused the US FAA Ground Stop and How Did a Copper-To-Fibre Switch Disrupt Flight Radar Feeds?
html_content:
A contractor's work replacing copper telecommunications lines with fibre may have triggered the US Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) ground stop on Friday, 13 November. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said investigators were examining whether contractor error or a faulty router disrupted communications and radar feeds. The exact fault has not been confirmed.

The ground stop was lifted after more than four hours, but the disruption carried on into Saturday, 14 November. FlightAware data showed 3,374 US flights cancelled by early Saturday morning.

Duffy said the problem began during routine maintenance at a remote FAA site. He named L3Harris Technologies, the FAA's long-time telecommunications contractor and the operator of its network, as the company carrying out the work.

How the Contractor's Network Upgrade May Have Triggered the Outage

According to Duffy, a router involved in the copper-to-fibre switch started flooding other routers across the air traffic control network. 'We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,' he said.

The network carries radar data and voice communications between FAA facilities, allowing controllers to monitor aircraft and communicate with pilots. As the connection attempts overwhelmed the network, controllers experienced inconsistent radar data and difficulties communicating with aircraft. A senior government official later told NBC News the system behind the outage had been identified and taken offline.

Investigators are examining whether the incident resulted from 'user error or installer error' or faulty equipment, Duffy said.

The FAA has been replacing old copper lines with fibre, 5G wireless and low-Earth-orbit satellite links. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told lawmakers in September that over 64 per cent of the copper-based network had been replaced by 1 September. Duffy put the figure at 69 per cent on Saturday.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials had found no sign of an attack but were not ruling one out. 'There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way,' he said.

Duffy said officials did not believe a foreign nation had attacked the network.

Flight Disruptions Spread Across the US and Canada

Controllers first noticed the inconsistent radar and communications data at 3.36pm Eastern time on Friday, according to Duffy. The FAA issued the ground stop at 3.54pm and lifted it at 8.15pm. About 3,500 aircraft were airborne, and officials said all of them landed safely.

The effects reached beyond US airports. Canadian Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said Canada's air traffic systems were operating normally but warned that travel to the US could be disrupted. He said Canada had offered the FAA its 'full assistance', including room for US-bound aircraft.

Toronto Pearson said flights to and from the US would keep facing disruptions and cancellations even after the ground stop ended. Air Canada cancelled all its US flights for the rest of Friday evening and said the impact would continue into Saturday. Passengers were told to check with their airlines.

Bedford said he expected US air travel to return to normal by the end of Sunday, 15 November. Duffy was more cautious, saying delays and cancellations would continue as carriers 'reposition aircraft/crews where they are needed most'.

The harder questions are still open. Investigators have yet to explain how one router produced enough traffic to unsettle control centres across the country. Until investigators establish the precise cause, contractor error and faulty equipment remain possible explanations rather than confirmed findings.

excerpt: Shakira joins Abdul El-Sayed's 'Shakira Law' joke on Instagram, adding a playful twist to the senator-elect's response to campaign attacks.
headline: Shakira Backs Abdul El-Sayed's Viral 'Shakira Law' Pun: 'Finally, a Law My Hips Can Agree With!'
html_content:
Colombian singer Shakira has joined Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's 'Shakira Law' joke on Instagram, asking whether Congress could pass the fictional measure. Her comment drew attention on Thursday, 12 November, after his victory in the US Senate election.

'Finally, a law my hips can agree with! Habibi, think you can get it through Congress?' she wrote beneath a video shared by El-Sayed's team. The remark referenced her hit song 'Hips Don't Lie' and a campaign joke directed at claims about his Muslim faith.

El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's 3 November election. He is due to become the first Muslim US senator when he takes office in January 2027.

View this post on Instagram

How Abdul El-Sayed Revived the Shakira Law Joke

The joke predated his election victory. It originated during the campaign, with a video posted to El-Sayed's TikTok account on 14 October.

In the clip, he rejected claims that he wanted to impose Sharia law, the religious and ethical framework associated with Islam. He then introduced a fictional alternative named after Shakira, saying its only commandment was that hips should not lie.

He illustrated the punchline with a small hip movement. That brief gesture made the response easy to share, but the accusation behind it was serious.

El-Sayed faced attacks from political opponents questioning his faith and loyalty. Claims that he intended to impose Sharia law were unsubstantiated. His joke rejected the allegation rather than announcing any policy.

The wordplay was already familiar online. According to meme archive Know Your Meme, examples of 'Shakira Law' appeared as early as 2013, long before El-Sayed's Senate campaign.

In 2018, then congresswoman-elect Ilhan Omar used the same pun after an Instagram commenter accused her of wanting to enforce 'Shakira Law'. She, too, answered with a reference to 'Hips Don't Lie'.

Shakira Law Draws Fresh Attention After Michigan's Election

Shakira's intervention gave that older internet joke a new audience. Her question about Congress was playful, and nothing in the exchange suggests she endorsed El-Sayed's party, policies or campaign.

The political context was nevertheless difficult to miss. According to the Associated Press, President Donald Trump and other Republicans sought to associate El-Sayed with terrorist organisations during the campaign, despite there being no evidence of such ties.

El-Sayed's victory put those attacks in the spotlight again. He had won an open Senate seat in a closely watched race, making his October video relevant to a different conversation about representation in Washington.

In his victory speech, El-Sayed accused Republicans of targeting his name and faith instead of addressing voters' financial concerns. That was a markedly different setting from his light-hearted response in October.

Instagram users responded to the joke's delivery as well as Shakira's reply. One wrote, 'That's such a dad joke.' Another said, 'Abdul is becoming a rockstar!'

Other reactions praised his handling of questions from the press, sometimes separating appreciation for the humour from support for his politics. Some users instead extended the joke with references to Shakira's songs.

El-Sayed's campaign, meanwhile, centred on policies including universal healthcare and reducing outside money in elections. Those issues, rather than the fictional 'Shakira Law', are among the questions awaiting him in the Senate

excerpt: Egypt have dismissed manager Hossam Hassan after their historic 2026 World Cup run, with the federation citing concerns over the team's image and stability.
headline: Hossam Hassan Sacking Explained: Quick Facts About the Egypt Coach's Exit, Media Ban and Replacement
html_content:
Egypt's national football team dismissed Hossam Hassan on 7 November 2026, ending his tenure less than two months after extending his contract until 2030.

The decision followed controversy surrounding his private life, a nationwide media ban and questions about his management of the squad.

The Egyptian Football Association (EFA) also parted ways with Hassan's brother and assistant, Ibrahim Hassan.

It appointed Ali Maher as his successor, bringing an abrupt end to a coaching spell that included Egypt's historic progress at the 2026 World Cup.

The federation cited recent events affecting the team's image and stability. However, it did not explicitly identify Hassan's personal disputes as the sole reason for his dismissal.

Why Was Hossam Hassan Sacked After Egypt's World Cup Success?

Hassan's departure followed months of unwanted publicity surrounding his family life. In August, a confrontation reportedly occurred between Howaida Al-Gharbawi and Dina Mustafa, also known as Dan Adam, at a hotel café on Egypt's North Coast.

According to reports, the argument became physical and required police intervention. Hassan reportedly attempted to separate those involved before collapsing and receiving medical attention.

Footage purportedly showing the confrontation subsequently circulated online. The dispute also involved complaints alleging forgery and bigamy, although those allegations were denied.

🇪🇬 La Federación Egipcia de Fútbol anunció en sus redes el fin de ciclo de Hossam Hassan, que estuvo involucrado en un problema matrimonial hace unos meses

✍️ "Luego de analizar todas las circunstancias y… pic.twitter.com/bHRp66ZBXc

— Diario Olé (@DiarioOle) November 9, 2026

The controversy intensified on 4 November when Egypt's Supreme Council for Media Regulation barred Hassan from appearing across television and other media platforms.

The restriction came just three days before his dismissal.

Despite the controversy, Hassan had delivered notable sporting achievements since becoming Egypt's manager in March 2024.

He guided Egypt to the semi-finals of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations before leading the country into the 2026 World Cup knockout stages.

Egypt secured their first World Cup victory in 92 years against New Zealand before suffering a 3-2 defeat against Argentina in the last 16.

Those performances earned Hassan a contract extension in September. Yet his achievements could not prevent the federation from reconsidering his position.

His international record stood at 21 victories, 10 draws and seven defeats across 38 matches.

Salah Tensions and Ali Maher's Appointment

Hassan also faced scrutiny over his relationship with Egypt captain Mohamed Salah.

During September's goalless draw against Angola, the manager substituted Salah in the 60th minute. The forward subsequently missed the South Sudan fixture, with the EFA citing concerns about artificial playing surfaces.

Federation president Hany Abo Rida later travelled to Turkey to meet Salah, apparently seeking to address tensions.

Meanwhile, Hassan received a three-match FIFA suspension after publicly criticising refereeing decisions following Egypt's World Cup defeat against Argentina.

His replacement, Ali Maher, 52, brings extensive experience from Egyptian club football.

A former Al Ahly and Egypt striker, Maher has managed Smouha, ENPPI, Al Masry and Future FC. His most recent appointment was at Ceramica Cleopatra.

There, he won the 2024-25 Egyptian League Cup and developed a reputation for attacking, possession-oriented football.

Maher's appointment was announced on 7 November, with Egypt scheduled to face Malawi on 13 and 17 November in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

The immediate challenge is taking charge of a national side whose previous manager departed despite securing the country's most successful World Cup campaign.

excerpt: Rick Frazier, a longtime Trump supporter who attended more than 100 rallies, says he has rejected the president over foreign policy, Epstein-related records and perceived political cronyism.
headline: Former Trump Superfan Who Attended Over 100 Rallies Calls Donald Trump 'King of the Swamp' and Exits MAGA
html_content:
Rick Frazier, an Ohio voter who attended more than 100 Donald Trump rallies, has turned against the president after a decade of devoted support. In an interview published by The Washington Post on Friday, 13 November 2026, he called Trump the 'king of swamp'.

The change marks a sharp reversal for Frazier, 70, a founding member of the Front Row Joes, whose members travelled across America to attend Trump's rallies.

Frazier now questions the president's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related records, the war with Iran and his relationships with wealthy political donors.

The disappointment runs deeper than ordinary party disagreement. Frazier once believed Trump would challenge the political establishment rather than become part of it.

What Led Rick Frazier To Turn Against Trump?

Frazier began supporting Trump during his first presidential campaign in 2015, drawn to his promise to 'drain the swamp'.

He became a familiar face at rallies, sometimes waiting outside venues to secure a front-row seat.

But his enthusiasm gradually faded as Trump pursued policies Frazier believed contradicted his original campaign promises.

'He promoted himself as a no-war president. That didn't work out,' Frazier told Politico, referring to the administration's military involvement in Iran.

The president's handling of Epstein-related records also troubled him. Frazier had expected greater transparency about the disgraced financier's crimes.

He questioned Trump's growing association with wealthy political figures and the continued influence of Washington lobbyists.

'There's more lobbyists involved now, and the swamp has gotten bigger,' Frazier told CNN.

Another grievance was Trump's pardon of former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández on 1 December 2025.

Hernández had been convicted in the United States of drug-trafficking-related offences.

The decision was particularly painful for Frazier, whose daughter died from a drug overdose in 2023.

Trump and First Lady Melania Trump had previously sent him a condolence letter following her death.

Frazier also disliked Trump's attacks on Republican Representative Thomas Massie, who supported releasing Epstein-related records.

His final Trump rally was in Kentucky, where the president criticised Massie from the stage.

Former Trump Superfan Rick Frazier Backs Democrats in Ohio Midterms

Frazier's political shift became evident during the 3 November midterm elections.

He voted for Republican Representative Jim Jordan but crossed party lines to support Democrats Amy Acton and Sherrod Brown.

Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio's gubernatorial election, while Brown unseated Republican Senator Jon Husted.

Frazier told The Washington Post that he wanted to return to choosing candidates individually rather than following party loyalties.

'I was independently swinging wherever the best guy was running,' he said.

Another former Front Row Joe, Trisha Hope, has also publicly rejected Trump.

Hope, who attended 42 rallies, became disillusioned after Trump dismissed questions about Epstein during a July 2025 Cabinet meeting.

She described the moment to Politico as 'a dagger in my heart'.

Still, Frazier estimated that approximately 95% of the Front Row Joes remained loyal to Trump.

A White House spokesperson directed The Washington Post to Trump's comments suggesting MAGA could survive beyond his presidency.

Frazier has not rejected every Republican leader. He told the newspaper he still viewed Vice President JD Vance favourably.

excerpt: Fans have speculated about tension between Dua Lipa and SZA after Coachella announced its 2027 lineup, but neither artist has confirmed a dispute and no public evidence proves a feud.
headline: Netizens Convinced Dua Lipa Is Upset With SZA Over Coachella 2027 Lineup Despite Zero Proof
html_content:
Fans are speculating that Dua Lipa is unhappy with SZA after the Coachella 2027 lineup announcement. However, no public evidence shows that Lipa is upset. The theory rests on SZA's apparent early reveal, Lipa's caption and an anonymous blind item.

Coachella confirmed Lipa, SZA and Tame Impala among its leading acts, with Daddy Yankee in a special fourth-headliner slot. Lipa will headline Fridays, Tame Impala Saturdays and SZA Sundays. The festival runs at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California, on 9–11 April and 16–18 April 2027, according to the official Coachella website.

SZA appeared to disclose her booking before the announcement. The Tab reported that she shared a message on a private Instagram account three days earlier. It read: 'I said yes to the big show. I'm not gonna rush my album no matter what this time. It's gonna be perfect. See u f**kers in the desert.'

A music news account, @femalernb, later shared the post. One commenter objected to SZA being a headliner, writing: 'No cap .. can do without her being a headliner.' SZA replied: 'You can literally go see the other two headliners. I assume u must listen to lots of tame and dua lipa lol. But you chose to publicly bring down the ONLY BLACK woman headliner this year... as a black man. Super wack of u honestly. I'm still headlining. Enjoy.'

The commenter said they did not listen to the other acts and did not consider the three headliners the best choices. SZA later edited the same comment, replacing her original reply with: 'Could literally just not go.' Lipa was not involved in the exchange.

The Tab, which reported the theory on 12 November, said it had contacted Lipa, SZA and Coachella for comment. It did not report receiving a response. Neither artist has publicly confirmed a dispute.

Why Fans Suspect Dua Lipa Is Upset With SZA

The speculation partly centres on Lipa's Instagram post. She shared the lineup poster with the caption: 'I guess i'll see you in the desert @coachella !!!!!' Some users read 'I guess' as a sign that the announcement surprised her, though the caption does not say so.

View this post on Instagram

An anonymous post from the celebrity gossip account Enty Lawyer added to the speculation. Dated 11 November 2026, it referred to an unnamed 'desert headliner' who allegedly blamed another headliner for an early reveal. It did not identify anyone or provide evidence.

A blind item invites readers to guess identities behind an anonymous description. Its claims are difficult to verify.

What Coachella's Announcement History Shows

Another online claim suggested the lineup was intended for January, possibly to coincide with a new Lipa album. No reliable evidence establishes a planned January announcement or a connection to her music schedule. Lipa has not announced a release date for a fourth studio album.

excerpt: Russell Brand is serving a 10-year, six-month sentence after being convicted of rape and sexual assault, as police investigate two further allegations and six women make fresh claims.
headline: Russell Brand Prison Sentence Explained: Inside His Ten-Year Sentence and the Eight New Sexual Assault Claims
html_content:
Russell Brand is serving a 10-year, six-month prison sentence after being convicted of rape and sexual assault in London. His sentencing on 9 November 2026 was followed by fresh reporting involving six women, alongside two further rape allegations under police investigation.

The developments followed a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court, where a jury convicted Brand on 5 November of offences against four women.

The comedian and actor, 51, denied wrongdoing throughout proceedings. He was also acquitted of two rape charges and one attempted indecent assault charge.

The additional allegations have not resulted in further convictions, and another trial has not been confirmed.

Russell Brand Receives 10-Year Sentence for Rape and Sexual Assault

Mr Justice Joel Bennathan sentenced Brand to nine years for rape and imposed separate sentences for three sexual assaults committed between 2004 and 2009.

The sexual assault sentences run concurrently with one another but consecutively to the rape sentence, bringing the total to 10 years and six months.

In his sentencing remarks, Bennathan described Brand as a 'sexual predator' and criticised his disregard for women's right to refuse sexual contact.

The judge said Brand's fame had allowed him to act with a sense of entitlement towards women.

Brand must serve two-thirds of his prison term before release on licence. He will remain subject to sex offender notification requirements indefinitely.

Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts praised the women whose evidence secured the convictions.

'They did not know each other, and each has carried what happened to them for almost two decades,' he said.

The Metropolitan Police also encouraged anyone with further information about alleged sexual offences to contact investigators.

Six More Women Make Allegations Against Russell Brand

On 12 November, The Times and The Sunday Times published accounts from six additional women alleging sexual misconduct involving Brand between 2005 and 2015.

The newspapers said they had delayed publication to avoid prejudicing his criminal trial.

One woman, identified as Vicky, alleged that Brand continued having sex with her after she repeatedly asked him to stop because she was hurting.

Another woman claimed Brand had sex with her without consent and subsequently apologised.

A separate accuser described an alleged assault involving unwanted physical contact and digital penetration.

These accounts concern allegations that have not been established in criminal proceedings.

The newspapers said their investigation included supporting material and interviews with people familiar with the women's experiences.

Brand did not provide a response to the new allegations before the investigation was published, according to the newspapers.

Separately, police have investigated two further rape allegations, including one involving a woman who was 16 at the time of the alleged incident.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed that additional people had contacted investigators during and after Brand's trial.

Detectives said they were assessing the information to determine whether it indicated further criminal offences.

Material concerning additional allegations has also been referred for prosecutorial consideration.

Brand has previously maintained that his sexual relationships were consensual, although the jury rejected his defence concerning the four offences for which he was convicted.

As of 14 November, prosecutors had not publicly confirmed additional charges or a second trial.

excerpt: Former Pentagon investigator Sean Kirkpatrick suggested a kite with streamers could explain an unusual Anchorage video, while stressing that the footage cannot conclusively identify the object.
headline: Pentagon's Former UFO Chief Offers 'Kite With Streamers' Theory for Mysterious Jellyfish Object Video
html_content:
Former Pentagon UFO investigator Sean Kirkpatrick has suggested a kite with streamers could explain a mysterious 'jellyfish UFO' filmed in Anchorage, Alaska, on 15 June 2026.

His assessment, reported on Saturday, 14 November, offers a possible explanation for footage that has attracted attention online.

Sara Jane Osborn recorded the object while photographing a rainbow. The video shows a dark shape apparently hovering against a mountainside, with strands moving beneath it.

The sighting drew particular interest because it was described as being in the direction of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson.

Kirkpatrick, the former director of the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, cautioned that the recording alone could not establish what was in the sky.

Sean Kirkpatrick Says Jellyfish UFO Could Be a Kite

'The motion is similar to a kite with streamers, particularly the waves,' Kirkpatrick told Fox News Digital.

The object appears to shift from one side of the frame to the other as its dangling strands rise and fall. That movement prompted his comparison, although neither the recording nor his comments establish that a kite was present.

Kirkpatrick was particularly wary of treating compressed footage circulating online as reliable evidence. He said it could not reveal the object's size, altitude, distance or true movement.

He also questioned whether a video available online could be authenticated without examining better evidence.

The weather provides one point of reference. Weather Underground observations cited by Fox News recorded westerly winds of 16 mph at 9.55pm on 15 June. Winds from the west-southwest were measured at 15 mph at 10.55pm, around the reported 10.15pm sighting.

Wind alone cannot establish an explanation. The footage does not conclusively show the object's position or distance, making its apparent path difficult to assess.

Separately, Alaska News reported that the filming location appeared to be in East Anchorage, looking towards the Chugach Mountains.

Its analysis placed Russian Jack Springs Park, a location associated with kite flying, along the possible viewing direction. That finding does not identify the object.

'UFO EXPERTS' say 'GIANT JELLYFISH UFO' FILMED in June was 'some sort of a KITE or BALLOON' pic.twitter.com/TT1NXjjIby

— RTVisual (@RT_Visual_on_X) November 14, 2026

Witness Disputes Kite Theory as Military Base Responds

Osborn's own reaction was markedly different from Kirkpatrick's cautious suggestion. In the recording, she compares the object to an alien and expresses discomfort.

Moments later, she adds, 'It's moving very weirdly.'

In earlier reporting, Osborn said she had considered whether the object was a kite. She maintained that its movements did not resemble one and said she and her husband searched a nearby park without finding anyone flying a kite.

Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson's 673d Air Base Wing Public Affairs office told Fox News Digital that officials were aware of the video but had no additional information.

The statement did not establish whether military personnel detected the object, whether it entered restricted airspace or whether activity at the installation was connected to the sighting.

Kirkpatrick said further checks could include nearby events, weather patterns and footage taken from another angle. For now, the apparent jellyfish remains unidentified in the publicly available evidence.

excerpt: Megyn Kelly accused Dakota Johnson of arranging paparazzi photographs outside a gym, but the claim remains unsubstantiated and Johnson or her representatives did not respond.
headline: 'Would You Look at What She's Wearing?': Megyn Kelly Accuses Dakota Johnson of Staging Gym Paparazzi Photos
html_content:
Megyn Kelly has accused Dakota Johnson of arranging paparazzi photographs outside a gym, but offered no evidence that the actress was involved. On the Friday, 13 November 2026, episode of her talk show, Kelly questioned Johnson's comments about wanting to keep her movements private.

The criticism followed photographs of Johnson leaving a workout and an interview in Vogue's October 2026 issue. Kelly argued that the sighting suggested Johnson was seeking attention, despite saying she preferred to keep her whereabouts private.

Megyn Kelly Questions Dakota Johnson's Gym Pictures

Discussing photographs she said she had seen online, Kelly asserted there was little possibility the encounter had happened without Johnson's involvement. The allegation was presented as Kelly's opinion, rather than a finding supported by details about the photographer or circumstances.

Kelly drew particular attention to Johnson's clothes, asking, 'Would you look at what she's wearing?' She described a mauve outfit, sheer tights, a crop top and sunglasses, comparing the look to aerobics fashion from the 1980s.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The Megyn Kelly Show (@megynkellyshow)

OK! Magazine described Johnson as wearing dark leggings, a white T-shirt and sunglasses. It is not clear whether that description and Kelly's remarks referred to the same set of photographs.

Neither account establishes that Johnson contacted a photographer, knew cameras would be waiting or deliberately arranged the sighting. The photographs alone cannot determine how the encounter happened.

Dakota Johnson's Privacy Comments Revisited

Kelly's criticism also focused on an interview with Vogue, published online on 18 September as part of its October 2026 cover coverage. Johnson discussed the difficulty of maintaining a private life while working in an industry that attracts constant scrutiny.

She told the magazine she was 'obsessed with people not knowing' her whereabouts or activities. Her comments concerned a broader preference for privacy, not a specific promise never to appear in public photographs.

Kelly nevertheless interpreted the gym images as evidence that Johnson welcomed attention under certain circumstances. She suggested the actress's presentation was carefully curated and accused her of wanting publicity while defending her privacy.

There is no independent evidence supporting that interpretation of the photographs. Johnson's choice of clothing, her visibility in a public place and her comments to a magazine do not show that she arranged a paparazzi encounter.

There was no response from Johnson or her representatives included in the OK! Magazine account. Without further evidence, Kelly's accusation should be understood as commentary rather than a verified description of events.

Recent Sightings Fuel Interest in Johnson's Personal Life

The coverage comes amid continuing speculation about Johnson and musician Machine Gun Kelly, also known as MGK. People reported that the two dined with friends at the Tower Bar & Restaurant inside Los Angeles' Sunset Tower Hotel on Wednesday, 11 November.

An eyewitness quoted by the magazine said they appeared affectionate during the meal. Other reports have cited unnamed sources describing their connection, but those accounts do not amount to confirmation from either person.

Vogue has also reported that the pair have been photographed together on several occasions, while noting that they have not publicly defined their relationship.

For now, the verified story is Kelly's criticism of Johnson, not proof that Johnson staged photographs.

excerpt: A claim that Prince William may exclude Prince Harry from a future coronation has renewed scrutiny of their strained relationship, though no ceremony date or invitation decision has been announced.
headline: Prince William Reportedly Does Not Want Harry at His Coronation as Royal Expert Warns of Lasting Rift
html_content:
Prince William reportedly does not want Prince Harry at his future coronation, according to a claim discussed by veteran royal photographer Arthur Edwards on the Express podcast Royals Unscripted.

The remarks, reported on Saturday, 14 November 2026, have renewed questions about whether the estranged brothers could reconcile before William becomes king.

The Prince of Wales is first in line to succeed King Charles III. However, there is no announced date for his eventual coronation, and neither brother has publicly confirmed any decision about Harry's attendance.

A Coronation Claim, Not a Confirmed Decision

During the Express podcast, royal editor Emily Ferguson questioned Edwards about Cup of Tea, Arthur?, My Extraordinary 50 Years Photographing the Royal Family, published by HarperCollins on 5 November.

Ferguson described a passage in the book as suggesting that William 'doesn't want his own brother at the Coronation.' She also portrayed the brothers as so estranged that even meeting in the same room could be difficult.

Her comments were an account of what Edwards had written, not a quotation from William. The published exchange offered no direct confirmation that the Prince of Wales intends to exclude Harry from a future ceremony.

Prince Harry ‘not trusted’ by Prince William as brutal reason behind royal rift revealed 👑🥊 #RoyalUpdate #Harry #William pic.twitter.com/NAg5oVy0ZW

— Daily Express (@Daily_Express) November 12, 2026

Edwards has covered the Royal Family for five decades, photographing royal tours, weddings and landmark occasions. Yet that experience did not lead him to claim certainty about the cause of the brothers' disagreement.

He acknowledged that he did not know what had started the row. Reflecting on its possible seriousness, he suggested that 'maybe there's no forgiveness there.'

The photographer's remarks raise questions about reconciliation, but they do not establish William's present intentions. Nor do they amount to evidence that invitations to a coronation, which has no announced date, have been considered.

Harry's Memoir Put Family Disputes in Public View

The discussion also returned to tensions involving Harry's wife, Meghan Markle. Edwards did not identify a particular dispute over Meghan as the confirmed reason for the brothers' estrangement.

Their disagreements became especially public following the release of Harry's memoir, Spare, in January 2023. In it, Harry alleged that William physically confronted him during an argument at Nottingham Cottage in London in 2019.

According to Harry's account, William criticised Meghan, and the exchange escalated until his brother grabbed his collar and knocked him to the floor. Harry also alleged that William had described Meghan as difficult, rude and abrasive.

Those allegations remain Harry's account of the confrontation, rather than independently established findings. They help explain why the relationship attracts scrutiny, but they cannot establish whether William wants Harry at his coronation.

Harry attended King Charles III's coronation at Westminster Abbey on 6 May 2023, despite the public dispute. His presence at his father's ceremony does not determine what would happen at William's.

The Royal Family's published succession order places Harry fifth, behind William and William's children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis. If William becomes monarch and the order remains unchanged, George would become heir apparent and Harry would move to fourth.

For now, the reported exclusion remains a claim discussed on a podcast. There has been no public invitation decision, and whether the brothers could eventually share that occasion is unresolved.

excerpt: Donald Trump says Washington no longer needs an agreement with Iran, as sanctions, frozen assets and military pressure continue while Tehran demands conditions for nuclear negotiations.
headline: Trump Says 'We've Got Their Money' and Calls Strikes 'Quite Unlikely' After Republicans Lose Midterm Majority
html_content:
'We don't need a deal with Iran,' Donald Trump said, arguing that Washington already had leverage because billions of dollars in Iranian assets were frozen overseas. In a Truth Social post on Thursday, 12 November, the US president added: 'We've got their money.' He also said fresh strikes on Iran seemed 'quite unlikely', more than a week after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress.

The post came more than eight months into the US-Israeli war with Iran. Qatar is still mediating between Washington and Tehran. Trump met Qatar's Prime Minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, this week and said Gulf Arab allies preferred the 'status quo' of economic pressure. He added that the US remained 'locked and loaded', but that new strikes on Iran seemed 'quite unlikely'.

That marks a shift from the swift strikes Trump threatened before the US midterm elections. In the 3 November vote, Republicans lost control of both the House and the Senate. Vice-President JD Vance blamed the losses on the war and on US relations with Israel.

Netanyahu Faces a Coalition Challenge

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also faces a coalition challenge. In Israel's 27 October election, Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot won 48, and Arab-led parties won 19. Neither bloc reached the 61 seats needed for a majority. President Isaac Herzog has since given Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, after 67 lawmakers backed him.

Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, warned on 9 November that the region faces a long period of uncertainty. He said neither a decisive resolution nor a stable regional order could be taken for granted.

Economic Pressure Has Not Ended the Standoff

Iran has demanded that vessels get its permission to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. US escorts have helped oil tankers use a route near Oman, but pre-war exports of liquefied natural gas, fertiliser and aluminium have not recovered.

The International Monetary Fund's October projections show three Gulf economies shrinking this year. Kuwait's economy is forecast to contract by 16.7 per cent, Qatar's by 15.6 per cent and Bahrain's by 11.3 per cent.

On 13 November, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it had destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. It called this retaliation for an attack on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran. The US military said it intercepted two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain, reporting no injuries or damage. Iran's claim that it destroyed the radar has not been independently verified.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said military action was not needed at present because sanctions were working. US Central Command says the naval blockade has cut Iran off from at least $25 billion (£18.89 billion) in revenue.

Iran has set seven conditions before direct nuclear talks. They include lifting sanctions, ending the blockade, releasing frozen assets and a ceasefire on all fronts, including Lebanon and Gaza. 'These seven items are on the table. Take it or leave it,' Tehran municipality spokesperson Hamidreza Gholamzade told NPR. Rubio called the conditions 'absurd.'

Iran has also rejected proposals to move its enriched uranium abroad. 'We will not remove even a shred of enriched nuclear material from Iran,' Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on state television on 11 November.

For now, Washington appears set to keep up economic pressure while holding military options in reserve.

He added that the US remained 'locked and loaded', but that new strikes on Iran seemed 'quite unlikely'. That marks a shift from the swift strikes Trump threatened before the US midterm elections. In the 3 November vote, Republicans lost control of both the House and the Senate. Vice-President JD Vance blamed the losses on the war and on US relations with Israel. Netanyahu Faces a Coalition Challenge Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also faces a coalition challenge. In Israel's 27 October election, Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot won 48, and Arab-led parties won 19. Neither bloc reached the 61 seats needed for a majority. President Isaac Herzog has since given Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, after 67 lawmakers backed him. Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, warned on 9 November that the region faces a long period of uncertainty. He said neither a decisive resolution nor a stable regional order could be taken for granted. Economic Pressure Has Not Ended the Standoff Iran has demanded that vessels get its permission to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. US escorts have helped oil tankers use a route near Oman, but pre-war exports of liquefied natural gas, fertiliser and aluminium have not recovered. The International Monetary Fund's October projections show three Gulf economies shrinking this year. Kuwait's economy is forecast to contract by 16.7 per cent, Qatar's by 15.6 per cent and Bahrain's by 11.3 per cent. On 13 November, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it had destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. It called this retaliation for an attack on a telecommunications tower in southern Iran. The US military said it intercepted two Iranian drones heading towards Bahrain, reporting no injuries or damage. Iran's claim that it destroyed the radar has not been independently verified. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said military action was not needed at present because sanctions were working. US Central Command says the naval blockade has cut Iran off from at least $25 billion (£18.89 billion) in revenue. Iran has set seven conditions before direct nuclear talks. They include lifting sanctions, ending the blockade, releasing frozen assets and a ceasefire on all fronts, including Lebanon and Gaza. 'These seven items are on the table. Take it or leave it,' Tehran municipality spokesperson Hamidreza Gholamzade told NPR. Rubio called the conditions 'absurd.' Iran has also rejected proposals to move its enriched uranium abroad. 'We will not remove even a shred of enriched nuclear material from Iran,' Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said on state television on 11 November. For now, Washington appears set to keep up economic pressure while holding military options in reserve.

excerpt: DNA testing has identified the remains of Maine soldier Willard C. Orr, who died during the Pearl Harbor attack, allowing his family to bring him home for burial nearly 85 years later.
headline: DNA Finally Identifies Pearl Harbor Soldier Killed at 21, Bringing Him Home to Family Nearly 85 Years Later
html_content:
DNA testing has identified the remains of a US soldier killed at 21 during the attack on Pearl Harbor, allowing his family to bring him back to Maine nearly 85 years later.

Private First Class Willard C. Orr, known to relatives as Carleton, was the only Bangor resident to die in the 7 December 1941 attack, according to the family account. For decades, his relatives had no remains to bury. They received official notification that he was missing in action, along with his military medals.

Relatives and community members gathered for a memorial service on Saturday at Brookings-Smith Funeral Home. After the service, a procession continued to Maple Grove Cemetery, where Orr is expected to be laid to rest in the family plot.

DNA Testing Identifies Orr After Decades

According to a report from WABI5, the US Army contacted Orr's relatives approximately five years ago to request DNA samples as part of efforts to identify missing service members from the attack.

The identification process took several years before the family received confirmation that the remains recovered in Hawaii belonged to Orr. Relatives were informed late last year or early this year that a confirmed match had been established and arrangements could be made to bring him back to Maine.

His nephew, Thomas Orr, explained that the family had waited a long time for the opportunity to bring his uncle home.

He described the occasion as both a difficult reminder of the young soldier's death and a moment of happiness because the family could finally give him a proper burial.

Orr's remains were transported from Hawaii to Maine, where a procession followed the memorial service and continued to Maple Grove Cemetery. He is expected to be laid to rest in the family plot.

From Maine To Hawaii Before Pearl Harbor

During the memorial, Thomas shared details of his uncle's military journey and the memories passed down through the family.

Orr enlisted in the United States Army Air Corps in December 1940. He was initially assigned to Mitchell Field on Long Island before being transferred to Hickam Field in Hawaii in March 1941.

He was stationed there when Japanese forces launched their surprise attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941. Following his death, he was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart in recognition of his sacrifice.

For years, however, his relatives had no physical remains to bury. His family received a missing-in-action notification and some of his military medals, leaving his final resting place unknown.

His great-nephew, Timothy Sargent, said he only learned about Orr's connection to Pearl Harbor after joining the military. His grandfather casually mentioned having a brother who had died during the attack, a revelation that made a lasting impression on him.

Sargent, who has served in the military for approximately 24 years, said the homecoming was an opportunity to recognise a relative whose sacrifice had remained part of the family's history.

Family Gathers for Orr's Homecoming

Relatives travelled from different parts of the United States, including Indianapolis, to attend the ceremony and honour Orr's memory.

For Sargent, the return was particularly meaningful because previous generations had lived without knowing where their loved one was buried. Having his remains identified after so many decades gave the family an opportunity to provide the farewell they had never been able to hold.

Bangor had also maintained a public connection to Orr's sacrifice. In 2021, the city named the Willard C. Orr Pedestrian Bridge in downtown Bangor in his honour.

His return to Maine adds to that remembrance. Nearly 85 years after the attack that took his life, Orr has returned to his hometown and is expected to be laid to rest alongside his family.

excerpt: An undated analysis says Tesla and SpaceX recovered most of a combined $420 billion decline, while warning that regulation, ambitious projects and valuations create risks for Musk's companies.
headline: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX Lost Over $420B in Two Days After US Midterms as Probe Fears Mount
html_content:
Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX recovered most of a combined $420 billion (£317.4 billion) decline following a US midterm election, according to an undated investment analysis warning that political and regulatory pressures could affect both businesses. The election year and the dates of the decline and recovery are not identified.

The analysis places both companies around their pre-election levels at the time of writing, while arguing that their valuations depend heavily on ambitious projects. For Tesla, those include robotaxis and humanoid robots. For SpaceX, it highlights space travel and plans to expand computing capacity for artificial intelligence services.

Political Uncertainty Surrounds Musk's AI Plans

The analysis links the election outcome to possible restrictions on data-centre expansion. It states that voters elected officials who campaigned to limit such development, although it does not name those officials or identify specific measures.

Tesla requires substantial computing capacity to train the artificial intelligence models behind its Full Self-Driving software and Optimus humanoid robot, the analysis explains. Restrictions could therefore complicate those ambitions, but the article describes a potential obstacle rather than an enacted policy.

The author presents Optimus and robotaxis as important reasons for Tesla's high earnings multiple, contrasting those ambitions with what the analysis describes as mixed performance from its core electric-vehicle business. Its investment argument centres on the potential of these projects and the risks that could affect their development.

Cybercab Scrutiny Adds to Musk's Regulatory Exposure

Tesla's Cybercab is another possible point of regulatory pressure. The analysis states that the vehicle attracted scrutiny when it hit the road and suggests it could face another investigation.

It does not identify the regulators, specify the earlier scrutiny or establish that a further inquiry has begun. Its argument is that additional intervention could affect expectations for a venture it considers important to Tesla's prospects.

SpaceX also faces possible constraints, according to the analysis. It describes plans for greater computing capacity to meet demand for artificial intelligence services. The author argues that restrictions on data-centre expansion could interfere with those plans, without establishing that such restrictions have been imposed.

The author further suggests that federal contracts could be vulnerable if lawmakers conclude that the US government depends too heavily on SpaceX. That is a prediction about possible future revenue, rather than evidence of an announced contract reduction.

Valuations Shape the Investment Case for Musk's Companies

A possible Tesla and SpaceX merger adds another uncertainty. The analysis states that both boards formed special committees to assess a combination, while stressing that there is no guarantee they will proceed. It predicts regulatory resistance if they do.

The article assigns forward earnings multiples of 48.4 to SpaceX and 159.5 to Tesla, without specifying a valuation date or the underlying calculations. Those figures represent the analysis's stated valuations rather than verified current trading measures.

Its positive investment case includes Starship, which it describes as designed for full reusability and potentially lower launch costs. Tesla's robotaxi service could become more profitable with sufficient scale and utilisation, while Optimus offers another possible opportunity.

Nevertheless, the author considers the share prices discussed in the analysis too demanding given the risks and the success already anticipated from those projects. The author would reconsider after a decline of perhaps 20% or more from those unspecified price levels.

excerpt: As Ever website traffic fell 9% year on year in October, but an unnamed source claims sales rose as Meghan Markle promotes her holiday range.
headline: Meghan Markle's As Ever Website Traffic Falls 9% as Source Claims Sales Rose
html_content:
Meghan Markle's As Ever website traffic fell by about 9% in October 2026 compared with a year earlier, according to Similarweb estimates analysed by Newsweek. The US lifestyle retailer recorded approximately 179,000 visits, down from 197,000, as it prepared for the holiday shopping season.

An unnamed source familiar with As Ever told Newsweek that sales nevertheless increased year on year. The company has not released figures that would independently verify the claim.

As Ever Website Traffic Falls Despite October Rebound

The difference between October 2025 and October 2026 amounted to roughly 18,000 visits, or 9.1%. These are estimates of website visits, not counts of unique customers, completed orders or revenue.

October also brought a recovery from September 2026, when visits were estimated at 141,000. The increase to 179,000 was almost 27%, although traffic remained below January's estimated 268,000 visits. July had brought a low of approximately 127,000.

An As Ever spokesperson previously described variations in website activity to Newsweek as the 'normal ebb and flow of a consumer brand'.

'Product drops and PR create predictable spikes in engagement, so I wouldn't read too much into a single period,' the representative said.

Those remarks preceded the latest October figures. Without published order totals, revenue or profit figures, the traffic estimates cannot establish whether As Ever's financial performance has improved or deteriorated.

Sales Claim Does Not Establish Meghan Markle's Revenue

The anonymous source's account offers a different measure of the business, but it remains unverified. Fewer visits can coincide with more orders if a greater proportion of visitors buy something. As Ever has not disclosed the conversion figures needed to assess that possibility.

The comparison also spans two stages of a young retailer. As Ever's first products sold out rapidly after its April 2025 launch, and inventory was reportedly more consistent by August that year.

Newsweek reported that October 2025 was only the second full month with products consistently available, following repeated stock shortages. That complicates comparisons with the earliest months after launch.

Meghan Markle's Holiday Push Follows Netflix Separation

Netflix and As Ever announced the end of their business partnership on 6 March 2026. Netflix said Meghan's transition to running the brand independently had 'always' been intended. The announcement did not attribute the decision to website traffic or sales performance.

In a 17 June 2025 interview on Emma Grede's Aspire podcast, Meghan discussed Netflix's support and described the arrangement as 'doubling down in the growth of me as an entrepreneur'. She also raised the prospect of expanding overseas.

Newsweek reported that As Ever had sought trademark protection in Britain, Canada and Australia. Applications do not confirm launch dates. The brand's shipping policy currently allows US deliveries but says international shipping is unavailable.

Similarweb estimated that nearly 60% of October visits came from US IP addresses and almost 20% from Britain. Canada accounted for approximately 6% and Australia 4%. The locations indicate online interest, not purchases.

As Ever is now promoting gift baskets, chocolates and a 2026 Advent calendar developed with Los Angeles chocolatier Compartés. Its holiday collection is available online, but the company has disclosed no sales totals for those products.
