excerpt: Marine veteran Brandon Quinnelly adopted Ares after the rescue dog's appearance reminded him of Achilles, his late service companion who helped him cope with PTSD for 14 years.
headline: Marine Veteran Finds New Companion in Shelter Dog That Looks Remarkably Like His Late Service Dog
html_content:
A Marine veteran has adopted a shelter dog whose photograph reminded him of his late service dog, Achilles, who helped him cope with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) during their 14 years together.

Brandon Quinnelly spent 14 years with Achilles. After the dog died, Quinnelly began looking for another companion.

His search led him to Ares, a shelter dog whose photograph reminded him of Achilles. Quinnelly contacted the rescue centre and arranged to meet him.

Ares Recovers After Shelter Staff Step In

Before finding his new home, Ares had to overcome a difficult start. According to a report from People, the dog was brought to Shawnee Animal Services in Oklahoma in a severely distressed state.

Shelter personnel found him barely responsive, with an unusually high body temperature and numerous fleas. He also had visible injuries to his face and considerable swelling around one of his front legs.

Staff members began treating him immediately. Their initial efforts included cleaning him, administering flea treatment and providing the care needed to stabilise his condition. His temperature subsequently returned to normal, the swelling began to ease and he started eating again.

However, the shelter recognised that he required more extensive veterinary attention. It therefore contacted Best Friends Animal Society, which helped arrange further treatment at its Pet Resource Center in Bentonville, Arkansas.

The effort involved a lengthy journey. Shawnee's sole animal services officer reportedly took a day off to drive Ares on the seven-hour round trip so he could receive the additional care.

After treatment and recovery, Ares began showing a much more affectionate side. He developed a habit of extending his paw towards people, seemingly asking them to give him attention.

A Photograph Brings Achilles to Mind

Meanwhile, Quinnelly was trying to find another dog following Achilles' death. The veteran had served six deployments with the Marines and was medically retired in 2010 because of chronic PTSD.

He knew that having another companion could help him through the loss. While browsing the Best Friends Animal Society website, he came across Ares' photograph and was struck by how closely the rescue dog resembled Achilles.

Speaking about the similarities, Quinnelly told the organisation: 'The similarities between Ares and Achilles are uncanny.'

He also described the profound impact his former service dog had on his life, saying: 'Achilles saved my life more times than I can count.'

Quinnelly contacted the rescue centre and arranged to meet Ares. Their first meeting went well, and he chose to take the dog home that same day.

The adoption gave Ares a permanent home after his recovery while offering Quinnelly the chance to build a new bond following the loss of his longtime companion.

Training Begins as Ares Settles In

Ares has already become comfortable in his new surroundings. The 68-pound dog is particularly fond of being close to Quinnelly and has made a habit of climbing onto his owner's bed.

Quinnelly joked that the dog had effectively taken ownership of the house, explaining that Ares now expects to sit beside him whenever he is in bed, often settling directly on his feet or legs.

The relationship may eventually involve more than companionship. Quinnelly started working with Ares on training the day after bringing him home, with the hope that he could eventually serve as his PTSD assistance dog.

There is still work ahead before Ares can take on that responsibility. He will need to learn to recognise signs that his owner is experiencing difficulties and respond appropriately.

Nevertheless, Quinnelly is encouraged by the dog's early progress.

'He's catching on pretty quick,' he told People, while acknowledging that the training process would take time.

For now, Ares is adjusting to his new life while the pair continue developing their connection. After losing a dog who stood beside him for 14 years, Quinnelly has found another companion with an unexpectedly familiar face.

excerpt: An unidentified man was arrested in France after allegedly stealing and destroying a Saint Nicholas bone fragment from a Lorraine basilica, according to reports.
headline: Man Arrested in France Reportedly Burned Saint Nicholas Bone Relic He Called a 'Symbol of Fetishism'
html_content:
An unidentified man was arrested in France on 2 November after allegedly stealing and destroying a Saint Nicholas bone relic from the Basilica of Saint Nicolas-de-Port in Lorraine during Halloween weekend, according to Catholix.

The relic was a 2-centimetre bone fragment displayed beneath a statue of the saint in the church's chapel. Its destruction prompted a parish statement describing the loss as an attack on the faith and devotion of generations of pilgrims.

Destruction Of The Saint Nicholas Bone Relic

The man allegedly smashed glass to take the relic from its patronal altar. The parish stated that he subsequently burned and crushed it.

Catholix wrote that the suspect admitted the act and expressed a 'desire to destroy' the relic, which he regarded as a 'symbol of fetishism'.

The parish's statement emphasised the religious significance of the object alongside its historical value. For the church, the loss concerned both the relic itself and its place in the religious life of pilgrims.

'Beyond the patrimonial value of this object, it is above all a profound attack on our history, our faith and the devotion of generations of pilgrims that touches us today,' the statement from the 15th-century Catholic church read.

Authorities had not publicly identified the suspect. Catholix stated that he was expected to face trial in December. The year of the arrest and anticipated trial remains unspecified.

Lorraine's Connection To The Saint Nicholas Bone Relic

'Saint Nicholas is the patron saint of Lorraine,' stated Luc Binsinger, mayor of Saint-Nicolas-de-Port. The town celebrates his feast day on 6 December.

'Saint Nicholas is where the heart of Lorraine beats every December 6th. As soon as someone attacks it, it creates a particular emotion and a kind of inner revolt for each and every one of us,' Binsinger stated, according to FranceInfo.

His comments linked devotion to the saint with Lorraine's annual December celebrations. The parish's response, meanwhile, emphasised the connection between the basilica's history, its faith and generations of pilgrims.

The destroyed fragment was classed as a minor relic. The basilica's principal relics, including a larger bone fragment attributed to a finger of Father Christmas, remained in its treasury.

Thousands of Catholics were expected at the basilica's annual torchlight procession on 5 and 6 December. This was an expectation for the celebrations, rather than a confirmed attendance figure.

Separate Fires And The Saint Nicholas Bone Relic Case

FranceInfo also described fires at the basilica. On 4 February, vandals lit two small fires inside the building, blackening a statue of the Virgin Mary. The year of those fires is also unspecified.

Saint Nicholas was a fourth-century Catholic bishop of Myra, a Lycian city in what is now south-west Turkey. He was known for generosity and secret gift-giving and participated in the Council of Nicaea.

The Marians of the Immaculate Conception link the Christmas stocking tradition to a story about his generosity towards a poor family.

According to the organisation, Nicholas secretly dropped three bags of gold coins through the family's window to prevent a father from selling his daughters into prostitution. The bags landed in the family's stockings, inspiring the Christmas tradition.

For the church, the loss concerned both the relic itself and its place in the religious life of pilgrims. 'Beyond the patrimonial value of this object, it is above all a profound attack on our history, our faith and the devotion of generations of pilgrims that touches us today,' the statement from the 15th-century Catholic church read. Authorities had not publicly identified the suspect. Catholix stated that he was expected to face trial in December. The year of the arrest and anticipated trial remains unspecified. Lorraine's Connection To The Saint Nicholas Bone Relic 'Saint Nicholas is the patron saint of Lorraine,' stated Luc Binsinger, mayor of Saint-Nicolas-de-Port. The town celebrates his feast day on 6 December. 'Saint Nicholas is where the heart of Lorraine beats every December 6th. As soon as someone attacks it, it creates a particular emotion and a kind of inner revolt for each and every one of us,' Binsinger stated, according to FranceInfo. His comments linked devotion to the saint with Lorraine's annual December celebrations. The parish's response, meanwhile, emphasised the connection between the basilica's history, its faith and generations of pilgrims. The destroyed fragment was classed as a minor relic. The basilica's principal relics, including a larger bone fragment attributed to a finger of Father Christmas, remained in its treasury. Thousands of Catholics were expected at the basilica's annual torchlight procession on 5 and 6 December. This was an expectation for the celebrations, rather than a confirmed attendance figure. Separate Fires And The Saint Nicholas Bone Relic Case FranceInfo also described fires at the basilica. On 4 February, vandals lit two small fires inside the building, blackening a statue of the Virgin Mary. The year of those fires is also unspecified. Saint Nicholas was a fourth-century Catholic bishop of Myra, a Lycian city in what is now south-west Turkey. He was known for generosity and secret gift-giving and participated in the Council of Nicaea. The Marians of the Immaculate Conception link the Christmas stocking tradition to a story about his generosity towards a poor family. According to the organisation, Nicholas secretly dropped three bags of gold coins through the family's window to prevent a father from selling his daughters into prostitution. The bags landed in the family's stockings, inspiring the Christmas tradition.

excerpt: Donald Trump's announcement that US military aid to Israel would end has been followed by reports of continued funding, leaving the alliance and future payments unresolved.
headline: Did Trump Abandon Netanyahu? What His Israel Military Aid Announcement Means for Their Alliance
html_content:
US President Donald Trump's announcement on 3 November that military aid to Israel would end this year raised questions about his alliance with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

But subsequent reports suggest funding may continue, making an immediate break increasingly uncertain.

Speaking on Fox & Friends, Trump said Israel no longer needed roughly $4 billion (approximately €3.63 billion and £3 billion) in annual support. He claimed he and Netanyahu had agreed months earlier to stop the payments, although no final bilateral agreement was publicly confirmed.

The existing US-Israel arrangement provides $3.8 billion (approximately €3.45 billion and £2.9 billion) annually, $3.3 billion (approximately €2.99 billion and £2.5 billion) for military purchases and $500 million (approximately €453.58 million and £378 million) for missile-defence cooperation.

It runs until September 2028, with Congress responsible for appropriating funds.

Netanyahu Signals a Gradual Exit, Not an Immediate Cutoff

Netanyahu's office initially sought to play down suggestions of a rupture. On 6 November, it said a move 'from aid to partnership shows the strength and sophistication of our relationship'.

Its position became clearer on 11 November. The office said Israel planned to phase out US military assistance gradually, echoing Netanyahu's earlier remarks about reducing dependence over time rather than abruptly ending support.

U.S. military aid to Israel has always been a cross-the-aisle agreement. Israel has used it both to defend itself and to confront enemies who threaten America and the West.

Today, Israel has a strong and stable economy. The move by PM Netanyahu and President Trump from aid to… pic.twitter.com/ssEaavMc0F

— Prime Minister of Israel (@IsraeliPM) November 6, 2026

Others were less reassured. Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on 5 November that Trump's announcement 'hit me like a bolt out of the blue.'

The dispute also unfolded during Israel's post-election negotiations. On 8 November, Herzog tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after parties representing 67 of the Knesset's 120 seats recommended him.

That endorsement was not a coalition deal, Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.

Talks Point to Military Funding Beyond 2026

On 9 November, Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth reported that negotiators were discussing continued direct military financing for five years after the current agreement expires in 2028.

The proposal would preserve roughly $3.3 billion (approximately €2.99 billion and £2.5 billion) a year until 2033, totalling $16.5 billion (approximately €14.97 billion and £12.5 billion), rather than $33 billion (approximately €29.94 billion and £24.9 billion) over a decade. Separate US funding for joint missile-defence programmes could increase. None of those terms has been finalised.

On 13 November, The Times of Israel reported, citing three US and Israeli officials, that the Trump administration expected security assistance to continue beyond 2026. Officials also pointed to existing American defence contracts and the costs of cancelling them.

That money has supported purchases of American-made aircraft, ammunition and other equipment. An abrupt interruption could therefore disrupt procurement plans already agreed with US suppliers, not simply future payments between governments.

Congress remains crucial. The memorandum of understanding is not itself an appropriation, and lawmakers can decide how much money to provide.

Domestic Politics Complicate Trump's Decision

Trump made his announcement before the 3 November midterm results. In an 8 November 60 Minutes interview, he blamed Republican losses partly on the Iran war, petrol prices and 'a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel'. He also asserted that Israel 'would not exist except for Donald Trump'.

A March Pew Research Center survey found 60 per cent of Americans viewed Israel unfavourably. An October Chicago Council poll found 56 per cent supported reducing or ending US military aid.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race despite independent spending against him by United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super PAC; James Talarico won in Texas.

The evidence points to political strain, not a severed alliance. Washington and Jerusalem remain engaged over future funding, but the scale, timetable and congressional support are unresolved.

excerpt: Trump demanded a DOJ investigation of Democrats, but Attorney General Todd Blanche says no criminal inquiry into lawmakers' oversight remarks is open.
headline: Donald Trump Orders DOJ to Investigate Democrats and Threatens Jail as House Oversight Prepares Probes
html_content:
President Donald Trump called for a Justice Department investigation of Democratic lawmakers and suggested they should be jailed after the 3 November 2026 midterm elections. But Attorney General Todd Blanche said on 12 November that no criminal inquiry into lawmakers' oversight remarks was under way. Democrats are preparing to control both chambers of Congress in January.

The dispute began with Trump's 7 November Truth Social post accusing Democrats of threatening administration officials and Republican donors with punishment. 'The imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS,' he wrote, saying he was ordering the Department of Justice (DOJ) to investigate. He provided no evidence that the lawmakers had committed extortion.

Blanche's subsequent clarification drew a distinction between political confrontation and criminal conduct. 'There's no ongoing investigations, criminal investigations, into words that incoming senators or congressmen have said,' he told reporters. He said criticism of Trump was lawful and acknowledged that he had not determined Democrats had crossed a criminal threshold.

The attorney general nevertheless argued that threats could become criminal in certain circumstances. He did not rule out future investigations if conduct crossed that threshold.

Donald Trump's White House Warns Incoming Oversight Chairman

The White House had already delivered a formal warning to Representative Robert Garcia, the senior Democrat on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee. In a three-page letter dated 9 November, presidential counsel William O. Scharf argued that congressional investigations must serve a legitimate legislative purpose.

Scharf said efforts to intimidate executive officials 'may cross the line into blatant criminality'. He also suggested that unlawful subpoenas designed to deprive citizens of their rights could warrant investigation. The letter did not identify a criminal charge against Garcia or establish that his proposed inquiries were unlawful.

Garcia, who is expected to chair the committee in January, has told Trump officials to 'lawyer up'. In a statement on 11 November, he rejected Scharf's warning and defended Congress's constitutional authority.

'We are a co-equal branch of government,' Garcia said, adding that Democrats would not be deterred by threats from the administration. His response cited Article I of the Constitution as the basis for congressional oversight.

Congress can seek records and question officials to support legislation, but those powers have limits. Courts can hear challenges to subpoenas, and a disputed demand for documents is not automatically a criminal offence.

Donald Trump Faces Democratic Probes and a Legislative Standoff

Garcia has identified immigration enforcement and the Justice Department's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related records among his oversight priorities. On 10 November, he criticised a Republican report on the Epstein investigation and called for public hearings. These are proposed inquiries, not findings that Trump or his associates committed offences.

Senator Richard Blumenthal separately renewed document requests on 5 November concerning donations to Trump's White House ballroom project and immigration enforcement. His letters sought information rather than announcing criminal charges.

White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said Trump was willing to work across party lines, but accused Democrats of planning 'sham investigations'. Her remarks reflected an administration preparing for sustained scrutiny as well as legislative opposition.

Reuters reported on 1 November that Stephen Miller and budget director Russ Vought had helped draft possible executive measures on immigration, tariffs and spending. Miller was appointed White House chief of staff on 6 November. Such measures would remain subject to legal limits and possible court challenges.

excerpt: Trump Media faces a 30 November deadline to repay up to $1bn in convertible debt, with falling shares and Bitcoin prices increasing pressure on its finances.
headline: Donald Trump's Media Company Races 30 November $1B Debt Deadline as Stock Nears All-Time Low
html_content:
Trump Media & Technology faces a 30 November deadline to repay up to $1 billion (£751 million) in convertible debt as its stock hovers near an all-time low, according to Benzinga. Falling Bitcoin prices have also reduced the value of the media company's cryptocurrency holdings, adding pressure ahead of the potential repayment.

The company sold the debt last year to finance its Bitcoin accumulation. Lenders aimed to convert their notes into shares at $34.72 (£26.24), but the subsequent stock decline has left that conversion price well above the shares' trading level described by Benzinga.

Why Trump Media Faces a 30 November Debt Deadline

A redemption of up to $1 billion would strain the finances of President Donald Trump's media company. Benzinga stated that Trump Media has ruled out selling shares to repay the debt, potentially requiring it to part with some of its cryptocurrency holdings.

That leaves the company facing pressure from both sides of its investment strategy. Its shares have fallen, making conversion less attractive to lenders, while the company's Bitcoin holdings have also lost value.

Benzinga put Trump Media's holdings at 15,649 coins, valued at $1 billion. The article does not establish whether the company will redeem the full amount of debt or how much cryptocurrency it might sell.

Falling Bitcoin Values Add Pressure to Trump Media

Bitcoin declined from an October peak of $87,300 to $66,000 (£65,973.93 to £49,877.20), according to Benzinga. Its analysis warned that further losses were possible as US Treasury yields rise and the Crypto Fear and Greed Index falls.

Those price movements complicate the repayment picture. Selling cryptocurrency could provide funds, but it would also reduce the company's holdings following the decline in Bitcoin's price from its October peak.

The dates require caution. Benzinga's article does not identify the year of the 30 November deadline or the October Bitcoin peak. Its reference to debt sold last year also lacks a publication date against which readers can place that transaction.

Political and Product Risks For Trump Media

Benzinga also identified potential political scrutiny. It stated that Democrats had retaken the House of Representatives and the Senate and predicted that they were likely to investigate the company.

One issue it highlighted was Trump Media's decision to launch a service giving high-frequency traders earlier access to Trump's posts than other users receive. The article does not confirm that an investigation has begun or include a response addressing that possibility.

There are pressures on the company's core product, too. SimilarWeb data cited by Benzinga indicated that website traffic fell 22% in October compared with the preceding month.

Benzinga suggested that advertising traffic could continue declining, particularly given a fall in Trump's approval rating. It provided neither an approval-rating figure nor evidence establishing that declining approval caused the website traffic reduction.

Technical Signals Weigh on Trump Media Stock

Benzinga's technical analysis described DJT shares as being in a steep sell-off near their all-time low. The stock had fallen below $6.80 (£5.14), identified as its June low, and below the 50-day exponential moving average and the Supertrend indicator.

The analysis identified a risk of further losses towards $3 (£2.27) as the debt deadline approached. That level was presented as a possible downside target, rather than an established outcome or a confirmed future share price.

excerpt: A Southwest flight concert featuring Hoobastank, Simple Plan and The Used narrowly escaped the FAA ground stop before Vans Warped Tour in Orlando.
headline: Passengers Stuck During Nationwide FAA Grounding Got 'A Free Hoobastank Show' With Simple Plan and the Used
html_content:
A Southwest flight concert featuring Hoobastank, Simple Plan, The Used and LØLØ took place on Friday, 13 November, after the aircraft left Los Angeles for Orlando ahead of a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop.

The musicians were travelling to Florida for Vans Warped Tour's Orlando shows on 14 and 15 November. Their plane was already airborne when the FAA halted departures across the United States, leaving other travellers facing widespread cancellations and delays.

The performances were part of Southwest Airlines' 'Live at 35' programme, rather than a concert hastily arranged because of the disruption. The airline launched the series in 2011 to bring live music into aircraft cabins.

Hoobastank and Simple Plan Bring Southwest Flight Concert to Life

Footage shared on social media showed Hoobastank frontman Doug Robb walking through the aisle singing 'The Reason', accompanied by guitarist Dan Estrin. Passengers held up their phones and joined the singalong as Robb also performed 'Crawling in the Dark'.

The Used's Bert McCracken performed 'All That I've Got' and 'The Taste of Ink', while Simple Plan singer Pierre Bouvier played acoustic versions of 'Perfect' and 'I'm Just a Kid'. LØLØ added her song 'hot girls in hell' to the airborne line-up.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Southwest Airlines (@southwestair)

Passenger Tori Kravitz shared footage of Simple Plan's performance and described it as a childhood dream come true. Before boarding, travellers on the special Warped Tour flight had also encountered karaoke, meet-and-greets and festival-themed gifts.

LØLØ later said passengers who had Wi-Fi discovered the ground stop while the aircraft was at 35,000 feet. They were worried, she explained, but Bouvier's performance helped lift the mood.

'Every plane was grounded today, but the emo gods made sure this one flew,' she wrote on Instagram. Her description reflected the scale of the disruption, rather than a literal grounding of aircraft already in flight.

Robb subsequently described the atmosphere to Rocksound as 'a tube of happy people'. The cabin performances offered an unusual festival preview during a nationwide aviation shutdown.

FAA Ground Stop Disrupts Vans Warped Tour Travel Plans

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said instability affecting US air traffic control radar and communications began at 3.36 p.m. Eastern on Friday. The FAA subsequently ordered a nationwide ground stop as a safety precaution.

The restriction was lifted at 8.15 p.m. Eastern. Duffy warned that airlines would still need time to reposition aircraft and arrange available crews, prolonging disruption after departures resumed.

On Saturday, 14 November, Duffy said investigators were examining whether an installation error or defective router caused the telecommunications problem during equipment replacement work. Officials had not established a definitive cause.

The effects extended to Orlando's Vans Warped Tour. Festival founder Kevin Lyman warned that some bands might be unable to appear and said musicians were changing flights or driving long distances.

'Some bands have jumped in vans and [are] driving from as far away as Chicago and Houston,' Lyman said in a video update.

Organisers planned to move some Saturday performances to Sunday and lengthen other sets. The exact number of acts ultimately affected was not confirmed in Lyman's update.

excerpt: María del Carmen García's sentence was reduced after she set fire to Antonio Cosme, the man convicted of assaulting her daughter, who later died from his burns.
headline: Mother Had 9.5-Year Sentence Cut to 5.5 Years and Paid Damages After Burning Daughter's Convicted Rapist
html_content:
María del Carmen García had her prison sentence reduced from nine and a half years to 5.5 years in 2010 after setting alight the man convicted of raping her daughter. Antonio Cosme died 10 days after the attack, which followed an encounter during his temporary release in June 2005.

García's daughter Verónica was 13 when the assault occurred in Benejúzar, in Spain's Valencian Community, in 1998. Cosme received a nine-year prison sentence in December 2000. García was later ordered to compensate his family as part of her own sentence.

A Mother Learns of Her Daughter's Assault

Verónica had been sent to collect bread and regularly stopped to visit a stray dog along the route. On that occasion, the animal did not appear when she called.

Cosme, a local bricklayer described as 62, threatened her with a knife before the assault. According to Gema Peñalosa's book Fuego, he subsequently threatened to kill Verónica if she told her mother.

Verónica returned home and immediately disclosed the assault. According to the Express US, García took a knife to confront Cosme at his home. He denied the accusation, claiming he had just woken up.

Neighbours accompanied García home. Some locals sided with Cosme, suggesting that the family wanted financial gain or questioning whether someone his age could have committed the offence.

Medical Evidence and the Mother's Move

Medical findings established the presence of semen and documented injuries consistent with sexual assault. The family moved elsewhere in the town because remaining in the neighbourhood had become untenable.

DNA testing identified Cosme as a match 12 months later. His trial began in October 2000, and he received his sentence that December. He maintained his innocence, but his appeal was denied.

In June 2005, García was waiting for a bus when a car pulled up, and Cosme stepped out. His temporary release had been authorised without her knowledge. 'Good morning, ma'am. How is your daughter?' he asked her.

Fear for Her Daughter Preceded the Mother's Attack

García feared that Cosme might carry out his earlier threat against Verónica. She went to a nearby petrol station seeking a jerry can, but none was large enough. She then returned home for a one-and-a-half-litre bottle and matches.

After filling the bottle with petrol at the station, she went to the bar where Cosme was having breakfast. 'Do you remember me?' she asked him. 'So you won't forget me!'

She poured the petrol and ignited it. Cosme suffered burns over 60% of his body and died 10 days later.

The Mother's Sentence Was Cut in 2010

García was admitted to the psychiatric wing of Fontcalent penitentiary hospital. At her 2009 trial, she testified, 'I didn't want to kill him; I wanted to scare him so that he would leave and never come near my family again.'

She received a nine-and-a-half-year sentence, was placed under a restraining order and was ordered to pay compensation to Cosme's family. Her sentence was reduced in 2010.

In November 2017, García was permitted to serve the remainder from home, initially returning to prison nightly before later being fitted with a tag. She was granted parole and released in August 2018.

Antonio Cosme died 10 days after the attack, which followed an encounter during his temporary release in June 2005. García's daughter Verónica was 13 when the assault occurred in Benejúzar, in Spain's Valencian Community, in 1998. Cosme received a nine-year prison sentence in December 2000. García was later ordered to compensate his family as part of her own sentence. A Mother Learns of Her Daughter's Assault Verónica had been sent to collect bread and regularly stopped to visit a stray dog along the route. On that occasion, the animal did not appear when she called. Cosme, a local bricklayer described as 62, threatened her with a knife before the assault. According to Gema Peñalosa's book Fuego, he subsequently threatened to kill Verónica if she told her mother. Verónica returned home and immediately disclosed the assault. According to the Express US, García took a knife to confront Cosme at his home. He denied the accusation, claiming he had just woken up. Neighbours accompanied García home. Some locals sided with Cosme, suggesting that the family wanted financial gain or questioning whether someone his age could have committed the offence. Medical Evidence and the Mother's Move Medical findings established the presence of semen and documented injuries consistent with sexual assault. The family moved elsewhere in the town because remaining in the neighbourhood had become untenable. DNA testing identified Cosme as a match 12 months later. His trial began in October 2000, and he received his sentence that December. He maintained his innocence, but his appeal was denied. In June 2005, García was waiting for a bus when a car pulled up, and Cosme stepped out. His temporary release had been authorised without her knowledge. 'Good morning, ma'am. How is your daughter?' he asked her. Fear for Her Daughter Preceded the Mother's Attack García feared that Cosme might carry out his earlier threat against Verónica. She went to a nearby petrol station seeking a jerry can, but none was large enough. She then returned home for a one-and-a-half-litre bottle and matches. After filling the bottle with petrol at the station, she went to the bar where Cosme was having breakfast. 'Do you remember me?' she asked him. 'So you won't forget me!' She poured the petrol and ignited it. Cosme suffered burns over 60% of his body and died 10 days later. The Mother's Sentence Was Cut in 2010 García was admitted to the psychiatric wing of Fontcalent penitentiary hospital. At her 2009 trial, she testified, 'I didn't want to kill him; I wanted to scare him so that he would leave and never come near my family again.' She received a nine-and-a-half-year sentence, was placed under a restraining order and was ordered to pay compensation to Cosme's family. Her sentence was reduced in 2010. In November 2017, García was permitted to serve the remainder from home, initially returning to prison nightly before later being fitted with a tag. She was granted parole and released in August 2018.

excerpt: Royal author Christopher Andersen claims Prince William and Prince Harry are unlikely to reconcile, but reports of contact attempts and the brothers' private positions remain unconfirmed.
headline: Prince William Reportedly Shuts the Door on Prince Harry as Royal Author Claims Reconciliation Isn't an Option
html_content:
Prince William is unlikely to reconcile with Prince Harry, royal author Christopher Andersen has claimed, describing the brothers as men who have learned to live separately despite Harry's stated openness to repairing relations with his family.

Andersen's assessment follows what Soap Opera Spy describes as repeated attempts by Harry to contact William, with little indication that his older brother is ready to respond. Those alleged approaches are not supported by named sources or correspondence in the publication's coverage.

Why Prince William Remains Central To Reconciliation Claims

Andersen, author of Kate!, told Fox News Digital that neither brother believes he owes the other an apology. His remarks offer an interpretation of their positions, rather than a statement from either prince confirming what they would require before resuming contact.

'Harry has never believed he has anything to apologise for,' Andersen told the publication.

He also described William as believing he had nothing to apologise for. 'Reconciliation is not in the cards.'

The distinction matters because the assertion that William has closed the door on Harry rests on commentary about his intentions. Soap Opera Spy does not quote William directly or include a statement from his representatives confirming that reconciliation is impossible.

According to Andersen, William regards Harry as having betrayed both the royal family and the institution of the monarchy. The author also characterised Harry's return to the UK after Megxit as aggravating that sense of grievance. William's own explanation of his position does not appear in the coverage.

Harry's Overture And Prince William's Reported Silence

Soap Opera Spy refers to a GQ Magazine interview in which Harry expressed openness to reconciling with his family. It does not provide the interview date or reproduce his remarks, leaving the timing and precise wording of that position unclear.

The publication also attributes claims of Harry's increasing frustration to unnamed insiders. It describes William as remaining silent in response to his brother's efforts, but offers no direct confirmation from either man about those exchanges.

Those allegations should therefore be distinguished from Andersen's public comments. Neither establishes what the brothers may have discussed privately, whether a recent approach received a response or what conditions either might attach to reconciliation.

Soap Opera Spy also states that Harry and his family moved to the UK in August and that the move had been expected to ease tensions. It identifies neither the year nor who advanced that prediction. The reference cannot establish a current development without that missing chronology.

The Events Behind Andersen's Prince William Assessment

Andersen cited major family events and illnesses when explaining his pessimism about the brothers repairing their relationship.

'These are two extraordinarily strong and stubborn men who have, sadly, learned over the past few years that they can live without each other,' he told Fox News Digital.

He pointed to Queen Elizabeth II's death, their father's coronation and the cancer battles involving the king and the Princess of Wales as occasions that, in his assessment, had failed to reunite them.

'If the death of their grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, their father's coronation and the cancer battles of both the king and the Princess of Wales didn't bring them together, it's very hard to imagine what would.'

excerpt: Rick Frazier, a longtime Trump supporter, says he voted Democrat in Ohio after questioning the Iran war and Trump's pardon of a former Honduran president.
headline: Ohio Man Who Attended Over 100 Trump Rallies Voted Democratic for Senate After Honduras Drug Pardon and War
html_content:
Rick Frazier, an Ohio Donald Trump supporter who attended more than 100 rallies, says he voted Democratic for US Senate on 3 November 2026. He also backed a Democrat for governor, citing grievances over the Iran war and Trump's pardon of a former Honduran president.

The reported split-ticket vote marked a remarkable change for Frazier, 70, who spent a decade travelling to Trump events. In a 13 November interview with The Washington Post, he described the president as 'the king of swamp'.

Why Rick Frazier Turned Against Donald Trump

Frazier was a founding member of the Front Row Joes, who travelled nationwide to secure places near the stage at Trump rallies. He was drawn to Trump's 2015 promises to challenge Washington's establishment, tighten border security and fight drug trafficking.

The anti-drug message mattered personally. Frazier's daughter died of an overdose in 2023, and Trump sent a condolence letter. The Washington Post reported seeing that letter framed in Frazier's Ohio home, alongside photographs of the two men.

Trump's pardon of former Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández became a particular grievance. A US court sentenced Hernández to 45 years in June 2024 for conspiring to import cocaine and related firearms offences. Trump granted him a full pardon on 1 December 2025, and he was released that day.

'See, that got me all upset,' Frazier told The Washington Post. His daughter's death and Hernández's criminal case are separate matters.

Frazier also criticised Trump's response to demands for additional government files relating to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. He disliked hearing the president mock the term 'affordability' at a rally.

The war with Iran had already shaken his loyalty. Speaking to Politico on 28 September, Frazier said Trump had presented himself as an opponent of war. At the time, he was considering skipping November's election altogether.

Ohio Election Reveals a Split With Trump, Not Every Republican

He eventually voted, supporting Republican Representative Jim Jordan for Congress but Democrats in both statewide contests, according to his account. Individual ballot choices are private, so his description cannot be independently verified.

Democrat Sherrod Brown defeated incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while Democrat Amy Acton beat Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in the governor's race. Neither Democrat has yet taken office.

Frazier said his final Trump rally was in Kentucky, where the president criticised Republican Representative Thomas Massie. Frazier admired Massie, who opposed the Iran war and pushed for greater disclosure of Epstein-related records.

His break with Trump did not extend to every Republican. Frazier said he still liked Vice President JD Vance, who blamed the party's midterm defeats on the Iran war on 4 November.

Another former rally regular, Trisha Hope, raised similar objections in a September interview with Politico. Their experiences do not establish a broader collapse in Trump's support. On Reddit, some commenters questioned why Frazier had taken so long to change his mind.

A White House spokesperson pointed The Washington Post to Trump's comments that the MAGA movement could continue without him. Trump separately argued that Republicans would have performed better had he appeared on the ballot.

Frazier now wants to judge candidates individually. 'I was independently swinging wherever the best guy was running,' he said.

excerpt: Sam Hartman's agent joked about shouting NFL offers over The Bachelor mansion gate, but his contract status may make the plan unnecessary.
headline: Sam Hartman's Agent Jokes He Will Yell NFL Contract Offers Over the Bachelor Mansion Gate During Free Agency
html_content:
Washington Commanders practice-squad quarterback Sam Hartman's agent joked on Friday, 13 November 2026, that he could shout NFL offers over The Bachelor mansion gate. His remark raised questions about juggling television filming and football, although a subsequent contract clarification changed the picture.

The joke followed ABC's announcement that Hartman, 27, would lead the dating show's 30th season. It is scheduled to premiere on Sunday, 21 March 2027, but production dates have not been publicly confirmed.

Brian McLaughlin, one of Hartman's agents, told ESPN reporter Kalyn Kahler that producers were working around Washington's schedule. Hartman had discussed the programme with the Commanders, he said, and the team understood.

Why Sam Hartman's NFL Contract Changes the Joke

Hartman joined Washington in 2024 after going undrafted and is currently on its practice squad. His football commitments could extend beyond the regular season if the Commanders reach the playoffs, although no filming clash has been established.

The NFL's 2027 free agency signing period begins on 11 March. Teams may start negotiating with prospective unrestricted free agents on 9 March, raising questions about how Hartman would hear from his representatives if filming were under way.

Asked whether the quarterback would be able to use his phone during production, McLaughlin offered an unusual solution.

'I plan on standing outside the mansion and yelling offers to him over the gate,' he told Kahler.

He added another suggestion, also joking. 'I'll call the [Bachelor] Mansion landline, worst case scenario.'

However, Kahler corrected the free agency premise on 14 November. She clarified that Hartman was expected to be an exclusive-rights free agent rather than an unrestricted free agent.

That distinction matters. Under NFL rules, a player in that category cannot negotiate with rival clubs if his current team makes the required one-year, minimum-salary offer.

Washington's decision would therefore determine whether Hartman could receive competing offers at all.

Neither McLaughlin nor ABC has confirmed whether Hartman will have access to his phone during filming. The March premiere also does not establish that production will overlap with free agency.

Why Sam Hartman Said Yes to The Bachelor

Hartman initially had little interest in accepting ABC's invitation. During a 13 November interview on Good Morning America, he explained that his first reaction was 'No way.'

A conversation with host Jesse Palmer helped change his mind. Palmer led The Bachelor in 2004 while pursuing his own NFL career, giving him experience of both professional football and reality television.

Hartman said Palmer helped him understand what the programme involved. The possibility of finding a future partner eventually persuaded him to reconsider.

Still, the quarterback acknowledged his nerves about meeting so many prospective romantic partners.

'I'm excited but also very nervous,' he said.

His casting drew enthusiastic responses from familiar franchise personalities. Former Bachelorette contestant Tyler Cameron welcomed the announcement during the 13 November episode of Bachelor Happy Hour.

Cameron expressed surprise that producers had recruited an NFL player during football season. He praised Hartman's established career and described him as 'Prince Charming'.

Other former contestants were equally supportive. Joey Graziadei posted 'And we're back' on Instagram, while Ben Higgins wrote, 'So far I really like this decision,' according to Bachelor Nation's account of the reactions.

The NFL and Commanders also promoted Hartman's casting on social media, bringing the announcement to football audiences beyond the show's usual following.

excerpt: Online support is growing for proposed UK age-of-consent reforms that could restrict sexual relationships between adults and 16- and 17-year-olds amid renewed safeguarding concerns.
headline: Netizens Praise Proposed UK Consent Law Reform to Stop Older Men Targeting Teens
html_content:
Under current UK law, people aged 16 can consent to sex, but ministers are reportedly considering tighter rules on relationships between adults and 16- and 17-year-olds. The possibility has prompted support on social media, where users say a change could offer teenagers greater protection from significantly older adults.

The issue attracted attention after Politics UK shared the development on X on November 15. The post had received more than 1.4 million views at the time shown in a screenshot cited in the article, and prompted hundreds of replies about the current law and possible reform.

Many commenters backed the idea of a legal safeguard, arguing that the current age of consent should not, by itself, settle concerns about relationships involving teenagers and much older adults. Discussions also spread to Reddit, where users debated whether existing rules adequately protect young people from exploitation and unequal power dynamics.

🚨 NEW: The Government has confirmed it's considering introducing a "staggered" age of consent

It would make relationships between adults and 16 and 17-year-olds illegal

— Politics UK (@PolitlcsUK) November 15, 2026

Online Support Focuses on Age Gaps and Safeguards

Several X users expressed support for the proposed reform, with some questioning why adults should be legally permitted to pursue relationships with 16-year-olds.

One commenter argued that the law should not be used to justify relationships between middle-aged men and teenagers simply because they meet the current legal age requirement. Another described relationships between adults and 16-year-olds as disturbing, while a separate user suggested that the law should better reflect concerns about exploitation.

The Reddit discussion showed similar support. One participant said they had emailed their Member of Parliament about the issue, explaining that young people at school could be vulnerable when approached by significantly older individuals. The commenter argued that teenagers may lack the protection and support needed to recognise or challenge exploitative situations.

Other Reddit users discussed whether a change should include restrictions based on the age difference between partners. Some suggested that relationships involving people close in age should be treated differently from those involving teenagers and substantially older adults.

The reactions reflect concerns about the potential imbalance of power in relationships involving young people, rather than simply the age at which someone can legally consent.

What Is Known About the Proposed Reform

According to The Independent, the renewed debate follows calls for a staggered age-of-consent system after allegations involving entertainers, including Russell Brand and David Walliams.

The proposal was publicly advocated by Mia Latter, now 37, who said she had a relationship with Brand when she was 16 and he was 30. She previously appeared anonymously as 'Alice' in a 2023 investigation by The Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches, before waiving her right to anonymity.

The Independent reported that Latter called for adults to be prohibited from having sexual relationships with 16- and 17-year-olds. The report also attributed support for further consideration of the proposal to Louise Haigh and Pat McFadden. No final decision had been announced.

The debate has also intensified following allegations against comedian David Walliams involving girls as young as 15. Walliams denies wrongdoing. The allegations have prompted further discussion about how institutions protect young people and respond to allegations of abuse.

Under current UK law, the age of consent is 16. Adults can therefore legally have sexual relationships with 16- and 17-year-olds, subject to other offences and safeguarding restrictions. The proposed reform would introduce additional age-related limits, but remains under consideration and has not become law. The reports cited here do not clearly set out the proposal's precise scope.

excerpt: Olympic figure skating star Alysa Liu was covered in green slime after winning Favorite Female Sports Star at the 2026 Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards, prompting mixed online reactions.
headline: Olympic Skater Alysa Liu Drenched in Green Slime to Close Kids' Choice Awards
html_content:
Olympic figure skater Alysa Liu was drenched from head to toe in Nickelodeon's signature green slime at the 2026 Kids' Choice Awards, in a moment that quickly spread online.

A video shared by Pop Crave on X on 15 November showed the 21-year-old standing onstage as bright green slime poured over her head and soaked her clothes, leaving her almost completely covered.

The ceremony's sports award was presented to Liu before the slime segment. Liu had just received the Favorite Female Sports Star award. She attended the ceremony wearing a Golden State Warriors jersey honouring basketball star Stephen Curry, and kept it on during the sliming. The moment prompted jokes and nostalgic reactions from social media users, as well as questions about Nickelodeon's long-running tradition.

Alysia Liu gets slimed at the Kids’ Choice Awards. pic.twitter.com/cC34AZODkV

— Pop Crave (@PopCrave) November 15, 2026

Liu's Slime Moment Draws Mixed Reactions

The Pop Crave post had attracted more than 413,000 views by the time the screenshot was taken, with users commenting on the award-show moment.

Some commenters welcomed the sliming as a throwback to an earlier era of the Kids' Choice Awards. One X user described being slimed at the ceremony as a dream from the early 2000s, while another praised Liu's appearance and said it was a fitting end to an enjoyable night.

Others questioned whether the tradition still belonged at a modern awards show. One commenter asked whether being slimed was still a thing in 2026, while another joked that Liu had trained for years on the ice but could not avoid a bucket of green goo.

Some reactions also referred to controversies involving Nickelodeon. One commenter said the network should reconsider the tradition in light of its history. That was the user's view; the post itself did not provide further details.

The clip was shared online after the ceremony, alongside discussion of Liu's award and the slime tradition.

How Nickelodeon Slime Became a Pop Culture Tradition

The green substance has been closely associated with Nickelodeon for decades, becoming one of the entertainment network's most recognisable features.

According to a report from VICE, the tradition can be traced back to the Canadian children's television programme You Can't Do That on Television, which premiered on Nickelodeon in 1979. A sketch involving a bucket of slop being dumped over a young performer reportedly helped inspire the network's now-famous slime concept.

The substance's recipe also changed over the years. VICE reported that an early version reportedly contained gelatin, food colouring and oatmeal, while a mixture used on Double Dare included vanilla pudding, oatmeal, applesauce and green food colouring.

VICE's account describes more than one mixture used over the years. An early version contained gelatin, food colouring and oatmeal, while the recipe used on Double Dare included vanilla pudding and applesauce as well as oatmeal and green food colouring.

The sliming tradition eventually became a major feature of the Kids' Choice Awards, with celebrities and performers regularly getting covered in the bright green mixture during the show bringing the tradition from children's television into the annual awards show.

For Liu, the experience added an unexpected twist to an evening in which she was recognised for her achievements in sport. Her award win and slime-covered appearance gave fans two reasons to celebrate, while the viral clip brought Nickelodeon's signature spectacle back into the online conversation.

A sketch involving a bucket of slop being dumped over a young performer reportedly helped inspire the network's now-famous slime concept. The substance's recipe also changed over the years. VICE reported that an early version reportedly contained gelatin, food colouring and oatmeal, while a mixture used on Double Dare included vanilla pudding, oatmeal, applesauce and green food colouring. VICE's account describes more than one mixture used over the years. An early version contained gelatin, food colouring and oatmeal, while the recipe used on Double Dare included vanilla pudding and applesauce as well as oatmeal and green food colouring. The sliming tradition eventually became a major feature of the Kids' Choice Awards, with celebrities and performers regularly getting covered in the bright green mixture during the show bringing the tradition from children's television into the annual awards show. For Liu, the experience added an unexpected twist to an evening in which she was recognised for her achievements in sport. Her award win and slime-covered appearance gave fans two reasons to celebrate, while the viral clip brought Nickelodeon's signature spectacle back into the online conversation.

excerpt: Mia Latter has publicly revealed her identity after alleging Russell Brand raped her when she was 16. The Metropolitan Police says its investigation remains ongoing.
headline: Who Is Mia Latter? Russell Brand Accuser Claims He Told Her 'I Just Wanted To See Your Mascara Run'
html_content:
Mia Latter, who alleges Russell Brand raped her after meeting her in London in 2006, publicly revealed her identity on 14 November 2026. The Metropolitan Police confirmed that the investigation into her allegation remains ongoing.

Previously known as 'Alice' in a 2023 investigation by The Sunday Times, The Times and Channel 4's Dispatches, Latter was 16 when she met Brand, then 30.

Brand, 51, was convicted on 5 November of one rape and three sexual assaults involving four other women. He received a 10-year-and-six-month prison sentence on 9 November. Latter's allegation was not among the charges.

Who Is Mia Latter, Previously Known as 'Alice'?

Latter, now 37, told The Sunday Times that Brand approached her in Leicester Square while she was returning from shopping. The then-MTV presenter asked about her purchases before taking her telephone number.

She said she disclosed her age during subsequent messages, expecting him to lose interest. Instead, he invited her to dinner the following day.

Latter alleges Brand initiated sexual contact at his flat despite her attempts to resist. Their relationship continued for approximately three months, during which she claims he instructed her to conceal it from school friends.

She said people in Brand's entourage knew about their relationship and that he sometimes referred to her as 'the child'. She also alleged that cars collected her during school hours despite her parents' objections.

Towards the relationship's end, Latter alleges Brand orally raped her at his home. She said she struggled, cried and eventually struck him in the stomach to make him stop.

According to Latter, Brand then told her, 'I just wanted to see your mascara run.'

Her allegation has not been established in court. Brand denied the allegations raised in the original 2023 investigation. People contacted his lawyer on 14 November but received no immediate response.

Latter said the relationship affected her education and mental health. She left school without completing her A-levels and later experienced depression.

Why Is Mia Latter's Allegation Still Under Police Investigation?

Latter said she was devastated when her allegation was excluded from Brand's recent trial.

She claims prosecutors believed his earlier public discussions of her allegations could complicate proceedings. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has not publicly confirmed that explanation.

According to ITV News, Latter has decided not to continue participating in the criminal process.

However, the Metropolitan Police confirmed that detectives opened an investigation in January 2026. Officers sought prosecutorial advice and were told additional information was required before a charging decision.

'This investigation remains ongoing,' a police spokesperson said.

The CPS separately told People that it would continue assisting investigators to progress cases promptly.

Latter is now supporting Close the Consent Gap, which campaigns for stronger protections for 16- and 17-year-olds.

Its proposal would restrict sexual activity involving adults aged 20 or older and teenagers aged 16 or 17 where the age difference exceeds three years.

The general age of consent in Britain remains 16, with additional protections involving certain positions of trust. The campaign's proposed restrictions have not become law.

The proposal would leave the general age of consent at 16, but introduce an additional limit based on the age gap when one person is 16 or 17 and the other is at least 20. It is a campaign proposal, not current law, and would require legislation before it could take effect.

excerpt: Online rumours about Donald Trump's whereabouts intensified during a nationwide FAA ground stop, but official schedules and available findings provide no evidence he disappeared or entered a bunker.
headline: Missing Donald Trump Sparks Wild 'Bunker' Theories After Vanishing for 72 Hours Amid FAA Ground Stop
html_content:
'Missing Donald Trump' rumours circulated online after the US president went without a public appearance in Washington following Wednesday's Veterans Day ceremony. Speculation intensified during the nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop on Friday, 13 November, although no evidence has emerged that he disappeared or entered a bunker.

For context, the White House schedule shows Trump attended the ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery on 11 November. He recorded two interviews behind closed doors on Thursday and had private policy meetings scheduled on Friday. Reporters received a 'travel/photo lid' on Saturday, signalling no further public appearances were expected.

On Sunday, 15 November, Trump offered his own account on Truth Social.

'I am in the White House having meetings on many subjects.'

His statement did not independently establish his location.

How Alex Jones Amplified the Claims

Broadcaster Alex Jones fuelled the speculation on Saturday, claiming Donald Trump was 'holed up in the White House' while supposed cyberattacks disrupted American systems.

Jones's website claimed unidentified Pentagon sources had placed the president in the White House Situation Room. Neither the sources nor the alleged cyberattack have been independently verified. The Situation Room claim also provides no evidence of a bunker evacuation.

Trump's absence from public events did not mean he was absent from official business. CBS News reported that government officials briefed him within 30 minutes of the FAA ground stop, while he was attending an economic policy meeting.

The president subsequently met Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to the network's reporting.

Administration officials addressed travellers publicly on Friday.

What Officials Say About the FAA Ground Stop

The FAA halted departures nationwide when intermittent telecommunications outages affected radar information and communications used by air traffic controllers. Duffy said technical instability emerged at approximately 3.36pm Eastern Time.

Aircraft already in the air were allowed to land, and some emergency flights continued. Officials reopened the airspace at 8.15pm, permitting departures to resume gradually. Airlines faced further cancellations and delays as crews and aircraft were repositioned.

At Saturday's briefing, Duffy said investigators were examining maintenance involving contractor L3Harris Technologies. The work involved replacing ageing copper telecommunications lines with fibre-optic connections. A router apparently overwhelmed the network with connection attempts.

Officials had not established whether the problem resulted from equipment failure or installation error.

In a 14 November statement, L3Harris confirmed it was assisting the FAA investigation and took the disruption's impact on travellers and airlines seriously.

Mullin said authorities had found no evidence of a cyberattack, although investigators had not announced a final cause. Jones's theory therefore remains unsupported by the available findings.

Donald Trump also used Truth Social on Sunday to urge Congress to fund a wider upgrade of air traffic control systems.

'If Congress approves the desperately needed money for Air Traffic Control, we can get it built quickly and efficiently,' he wrote.

He blamed the Biden administration for the ageing system, but that political criticism did not establish responsibility for Friday's technical failure. Duffy said investigators were still examining the affected equipment.

excerpt: A former model identified as Simona alleges Jeffrey Epstein raped her about 200 times after she was recruited through modelling connections, according to a BBC investigation into his network.
headline: 'We Were Slaves': Jeffrey Epstein Survivor Claims He Raped Her 200 Times as Models Break Silence on Abuse
html_content:
A former model has alleged that Jeffrey Epstein raped her approximately 200 times over two years after meeting him in New York. Her testimony featured in a November 2026 BBC investigation examining how connections within the modelling industry allegedly helped the financier recruit and exploit young women.

The woman, identified as Simona to protect her identity, was 20 when she met Epstein. Originally from Eastern Europe, she believed his industry contacts could help launch her career.

Instead, she alleged that promises of professional opportunities drew her into years of sexual abuse and control.

'We were there for the purposes of serving Epstein. Slaves, who also have been raped,' she told the BBC.

Jeffrey Epstein Survivor Describes Abuse Behind Modelling Career Promises

The BBC's documentary, The Model Trap: Exposing Jeffrey Epstein's Network, investigated Epstein's relationships with modelling agencies and scouts after his 2008 conviction for sex offences.

Simona said Epstein introduced her to Faith Kates, then a senior executive at Next Management, suggesting the meeting could advance her career.

She alleged that Kates recommended plastic surgery during their meeting.

Kates's lawyers denied the allegation, saying she had never made such a recommendation and had been misled by Epstein.

Simona subsequently became Epstein's assistant, a position she says exposed her to repeated sexual abuse.

Another woman, identified as Anka, described meeting Epstein through model scout Daniel Siad in Paris.

Anka alleged that Epstein controlled women through their housing, finances and immigration arrangements. She also described pressure on assistants to introduce other women to him.

Her account suggests that promised employment could become another means of maintaining control over women who lacked support networks.

The BBC investigation examined how those arrangements allegedly continued long after Epstein became a convicted sex offender.

Jeffrey Epstein's Modelling Network Faces Scrutiny Over Recruitment Practices

BBC Eye examined more than three million pages of US Justice Department records and interviewed more than 100 models from 14 countries.

The documents revealed Epstein's financial dealings with modelling agencies, including a $1 million (£756,600) payment to MC2 Model Management in 2005.

The investigation also examined correspondence involving scouts who introduced aspiring models to Epstein.

Roza Gilles, originally from Uzbekistan, said MC2 arranged two photoshoots at Epstein's Palm Beach property when she was 18.

Gilles alleged that Epstein subsequently employed her as an assistant and sexually abused her repeatedly over three years.

She said her agency failed to protect her despite sending her to a convicted sex offender's property.

MC2's former US president, Jeff Fuller, previously denied knowing Gilles was being sent to Epstein's home or experiencing abuse.

Former model agent Ramsey Elkholy, whose correspondence with Epstein featured in the investigation, denied knowingly facilitating abuse.

He said he had relied on Epstein's account of his earlier criminal case.

Lawyer Sigrid McCawley, who represents Epstein survivors, described the recruitment arrangements as a sophisticated operation involving modelling-industry contacts.

The allegations have also brought renewed attention to efforts to hold people who knowingly benefited from trafficking accountable.

New York State Senator Zellnor Myrie has sponsored legislation that would expand potential criminal liability and provide civil remedies relating to trafficking ventures.

The proposal passed the state Senate in June 2026 but had not become law in the legislative record reviewed.

Gilles, who previously appeared anonymously in court records, questioned why her agency arranged work at Epstein's home while he was serving a sentence for a sex offence involving a minor.

excerpt: A man in his 30s died after being struck by an ambulance on the A19 near Sunderland. Police are investigating and appealing for witness and dashcam footage.
headline: Man in His 30s Dies After Being Hit by Ambulance on A19 in 'Hugely Tragic' Incident, Officials Say
html_content:
A man in his 30s died after being struck by an ambulance on the A19 near Sunderland early on Sunday, 15 November 2026. Northumbria Police said the ambulance was carrying a patient and travelling northbound without its blue lights activated when the collision occurred shortly after 2am.

The incident happened between the A1018 and A690 junctions. Emergency services attended, but the pedestrian died at the scene despite efforts to save him. His next of kin have been informed and are receiving support from police.

The incident prompted officers to close the A19 in both directions for several hours while emergency crews responded and initial enquiries were carried out. The road subsequently reopened. Investigators have not publicly established how the collision occurred.

Ambulance Crew Was Transporting Patient Before A19 Collision

The North East Ambulance Service (NEAS) confirmed that one of its crews was taking a patient and the patient's partner to a nearby hospital. Police said nobody travelling in the ambulance was injured.

The driver, a man in his 40s, remained at the scene to assist officers with their enquiries. Police have not announced any charges or made a public finding of fault.

Following the collision, NEAS dispatched additional resources to the scene. The patient and their partner were transferred to another ambulance and taken to hospital for further treatment, the service said.

Paramedics also attended to the pedestrian, who died despite the efforts of the crews who responded. The ambulance service confirmed his death at the scene.

'This is a hugely tragic incident for all involved,' an NEAS spokesperson said in a statement issued on Sunday. The service expressed its condolences to the man's loved ones and said it would cooperate with the police investigation.

Police confirmed that the ambulance was not using blue lights when the collision occurred. However, this does not establish how the crash happened or whether anyone was responsible. No explanation has been confirmed for the pedestrian's presence on the carriageway.

Northumbria Police Appeal for A19 Dashcam Footage

Northumbria Police's Roads Policing Unit is investigating and has asked anyone who witnessed the collision to come forward. Officers are particularly interested in CCTV or dashcam footage showing the collision or events immediately before the impact.

Sgt Ben Rutherford said the force's thoughts were with the family and loved ones of the man who died. He said officers would continue to support them during an extremely difficult time.

Rutherford said investigators had already conducted enquiries but wanted to hear from anyone who might be able to help. Information that initially seems insignificant may still assist officers in establishing the sequence of events.

Such information 'could prove key to our investigation and help provide answers for the man's loved ones', he said. The appeal includes motorists with recordings they have not yet reviewed.

Anyone with relevant information can contact Northumbria Police through its website's live chat or reporting forms, or by sending the force a direct message on social media. Witnesses should quote reference NP-20261115-0086.

The investigation remains focused on establishing the circumstances of the collision, while police continue to seek accounts and footage from the early hours of Sunday.

excerpt: A woman reportedly used her own money to bring Costco food to stranded families at San Jose airport during the FAA ground stop.
headline: San Jose Woman Rushed to Costco to Buy Food for Stranded Travellers After Nationwide FAA Ground Stop
html_content:
Precius Dixon said she bought food at Costco with her own money and took it to families stranded at San José Mineta International Airport (SJC) following a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop on 13 November, according to a video circulating on social media. In the footage, Dixon says she does not work at the airport and decided to help after thinking about mothers and babies affected by the disruption.

The video circulated as thousands of US passengers faced cancellations, delays and overnight waits after a telecommunications problem disrupted air traffic control systems. The FAA reported 12,462 cancellations on Friday, including 9,082 by major airlines. It said not all were directly caused by the ground stop.

What Dixon Said About Helping Families

'I do NOT work at the airport,' Dixon said in the video. She described hearing about the disruption and deciding to go to Costco, a warehouse club retailer, to buy food for passengers waiting at the airport.

'I'm like, I'm sure there's moms up there, what about their babies? So I went to Costco and did what I could. That's it. Do what I could,' she said. The video does not independently establish how much she spent, what food she bought or how many people received it. Her identity and the details of the distribution remain based on the circulating footage.

Precious Dixon does not work at the airport. She heard families were stranded by the FAA ground stop, thought about the moms and babies, and went to Costco to feed them. Ordinary people doing extraordinary things. 🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/uqQ0lJMQbO

— Grassroots Army (@GrassrootArmy) November 15, 2026

FAA Ground Stop Halted US Departures

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop at about 3.30pm Eastern Time (ET) on 13 November after legacy equipment became unstable when data flooded its telecommunications network. The agency said the network was receiving about 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Instability affected 17 of its 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers and spread into several Terminal Radar Approach Controls.

The FAA's initial investigation identified a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas, as possible sources of the excess data. L3Harris, the agency's network service provider, had been carrying out work at the Arkansas site, including deploying a new router. However, investigators have not established whether the equipment or the installation work caused the failure.

The ground stop was lifted at 8.15pm ET. The agency said approximately 3,500 aircraft landed safely during the disruption and that all passengers aboard those flights arrived safely. It added that there was no indication of a cyberattack or malicious outside actor.

Bay Area Airports Faced Further Delays

San José Mineta International Airport, San Francisco International Airport and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport were among the Bay Area airports affected. ABC7 News reported that passengers at SJC remained aboard aircraft for hours before being allowed to deplane and collect their baggage. At the time of its report, nearly two dozen flights in and out of San José had been cancelled.

The disruption also stranded a family travelling from India for a wedding in the South Bay, NBC Bay Area reported. The groom eventually managed to fly out on Saturday afternoon and make it to the wedding, but relatives and other guests remained unable to travel. The wedding had been expected to draw more than 100 people, but only about 20 to 30 attended, the report said.

Airlines Continued Recovery Through Weekend

The ground stop ended on Friday night, but airlines spent the weekend dealing with cancellations, delays and aircraft and crews out of position. The FAA described the recovery as slow and steady. More than 6,600 flights were cancelled on Saturday out of about 41,000 scheduled, according to FlightAware data cited by the Associated Press. The figure reflected cancellations recorded at the time, rather than a final tally.

The FAA said it disabled the functionality of the originating routers and the same function on about 60 similar routers as a precaution. The agency and L3Harris continued investigating the telecommunications failure, with the root cause still undetermined.
