Ordinary people doing extraordinary things. 🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/uqQ0lJMQbO — Grassroots Army (@GrassrootArmy) November 15, 2026 FAA Ground Stop Halted US Departures The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop at about 3.30pm Eastern Time (ET) on 13 November after legacy equipment became unstable when data flooded its telecommunications network. The agency said the network was receiving about 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Instability affected 17 of its 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers and spread into several Terminal Radar Approach Controls. The FAA's initial investigation identified a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas, as possible sources of the excess data. L3Harris, the agency's network service provider, had been carrying out work at the Arkansas site, including deploying a new router. However, investigators have not established whether the equipment or the installation work caused the failure. The ground stop was lifted at 8.15pm ET. The agency said approximately 3,500 aircraft landed safely during the disruption and that all passengers aboard those flights arrived safely. It added that there was no indication of a cyberattack or malicious outside actor. Bay Area Airports Faced Further Delays San José Mineta International Airport, San Francisco International Airport and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport were among the Bay Area airports affected. ABC7 News reported that passengers at SJC remained aboard aircraft for hours before being allowed to deplane and collect their baggage. At the time of its report, nearly two dozen flights in and out of San José had been cancelled. The disruption also stranded a family travelling from India for a wedding in the South Bay, NBC Bay Area reported. The groom eventually managed to fly out on Saturday afternoon and make it to the wedding, but relatives and other guests remained unable to travel. The wedding had been expected to draw more than 100 people, but only about 20 to 30 attended, the report said. Airlines Continued Recovery Through Weekend The ground stop ended on Friday night, but airlines spent the weekend dealing with cancellations, delays and aircraft and crews out of position. The FAA described the recovery as slow and steady. More than 6,600 flights were cancelled on Saturday out of about 41,000 scheduled, according to FlightAware data cited by the Associated Press. The figure reflected cancellations recorded at the time, rather than a final tally. The FAA said it disabled the functionality of the originating routers and the same function on about 60 similar routers as a precaution. The agency and L3Harris continued investigating the telecommunications failure, with the root cause still undetermined.

excerpt: Florida pastor Randon Lee Carroll received life without parole and 15 years after pleading no contest to sexual battery and recording sexual acts involving a child.
headline: Florida Pastor Sentenced to Life for Sexually Abusing Teenage Boy After Claiming He Was 'Lured'
html_content:
A Florida pastor who sexually battered a teenage boy under his custodial authority and videotaped some of the acts has been sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole, plus 15 years.

Randon Lee Carroll, 41, of Ponce de Leon, was sentenced on 10 November 2026 by Circuit Judge Russell Roberts in Holmes County. Carroll pleaded no contest to sexual battery of a victim over 12 but under 18 while under his custodial authority. He also pleaded no contest to sexual performance by a child for videotaping some of the sexual acts.

The Charges and Open Plea

Carroll had been scheduled to stand trial in October 2026 on multiple charges before entering an open no-contest plea. Unlike a negotiated agreement, an open plea leaves the decision on sentencing to the judge after hearing from the prosecution and defence.

Holmes County Chief Prosecutor Cook had offered no plea deal other than life in prison. Roberts imposed life without parole for sexual battery and 15 years for sexual performance by a child. The sentencing announcement did not specify whether the 15-year term would run concurrently with or consecutively to the life sentence.

Investigation and Confession

The sexual battery took place on 16 May 2026 at Carroll's home. The victim was a teenage boy under Carroll's custodial authority. Carroll videotaped some of the sexual acts, leading to the separate sexual-performance charge.

Holmes County Sheriff's Office Capt. Bill Pate testified that he observed the victim's forensic interview at a Children's Advocacy Center, where trained professionals conduct interviews with children involved in abuse investigations. Pate then interviewed Carroll at his home on 19 May 2026.

Carroll admitted committing the sexual acts, telling Pate: 'I have a problem. I shouldn't have done it.' The details Carroll provided matched the victim's account. State Attorney Larry Basford later credited the confession with helping bring the case to a quick resolution and thanked the Holmes County Sheriff's Office for its investigation.

Prosecutor Sought Maximum Sentence

At the sentencing hearing, Cook presented the state's case, cross-examined defence witnesses and asked Roberts to impose the maximum sentence. Cook said Carroll continued to shift blame, citing his testimony that he 'fell for it' and was 'lured'. The prosecutor said those claims were contrary to the evidence.

'I think this is the worst possible act that can be committed against a child, your Honour, and the State requests that he die in prison,' Cook told Roberts. He added: 'This is as bad as it gets.'

Roberts said he had considered all the evidence before imposing the sentences. The life term was for the sexual battery charge, while the 15-year term related to the recording of sexual acts involving a child. The announcement did not clarify whether the terms would be served at the same time or one after the other.

Victim's Mother Describes Impact

The victim's mother submitted a written impact statement describing the family's strong religious beliefs and questioning how a pastor could preach while sexually abusing a child. 'It takes a wicked person to do that,' she wrote. 'There's no way this is of God. This is pure evil.'

Cook said he hoped the sentence would bring justice to the victim and his family. He also praised Pate's work, describing the investigation as 'terrific' and saying Carroll had been 'permanently removed' from the community.

excerpt: Newly released body-camera footage captures University of Georgia student Kristin Sargent speaking to emergency responders after surviving an estimated 65 to 70-foot fall from an Athens apartment.
headline: Georgia Student Survives Eight-Storey Fall While Singing Miley Cyrus's 'The Climb' as Her First Words Emerge
html_content:
A University of Georgia student who survived an eight-storey fall from her Athens apartment window told emergency responders that nobody had hurt her, newly released police body camera footage shows. Kristin Sargent, 21, is heard telling emergency medical technicians, 'No one did anything bad to me.' The footage is the first time her own words from that night have been made public.

Sargent, a University of Georgia senior, fell from the eighth floor of the Rambler Athens apartment building on 26 September. The incident happened during the Georgia-Oklahoma football weekend. Investigators estimated that she fell approximately 65 to 70 feet before reaching the pool deck below.

A roommate told police that the group had been dancing and singing Miley Cyrus's 2009 song 'The Climb' shortly before Sargent fell backwards through an open window screen. The roommate said the glass was raised while the screen remained in place. Security camera footage captured Sargent falling, with the screen following her.

Police, firefighters and emergency medical crews were called to the building at approximately 7:37pm, according to the incident report.

Body Camera Captures the Aftermath of the Fall

The footage, recorded by Athens-Clarke County Police, was obtained by Local 12 and reported by Atlanta News First. It shows officers speaking with friends at the scene.

A responding officer described Sargent as having an open femur fracture and blood coming from a wound in her chest. She was conscious and able to speak when first responders arrived. The footage records her telling emergency personnel that nobody had done anything bad to her.

One friend told an officer, 'I thought I was coming down here to see her dead.' Another said, 'I would die if I fell from that. She's just a beast.' The friend added that the group believed Sargent would survive if anyone could.

The roommate also said Sargent had been at a bar during the Georgia-Oklahoma game. Several friends were staying at her five-person apartment that weekend.

Investigators found evidence that Sargent struck a cushioned metal bench near the pool. An incident report described blood on its cushion and a broken armrest. It is not clear how the bench affected her injuries.

What Is Known About Sargent's Condition

A hospital administrator later described Sargent as 'drunk', according to the footage. An officer suggested her condition may have affected whether she braced herself during the fall.

An early police incident report said evidence gathered at the scene suggested the fall was accidental. It also stated that the investigation remained ongoing at the time. Police have not said anyone else was involved.

Sargent's father, Richard Sargent, previously told WSB-TV that his daughter had suffered several broken bones. He said she was recovering better than many had expected.

Atlanta News First reported on 14 November that it had contacted Sargent, her father and her four roommates for an update. The outlet said it received no response. Her current condition has not been confirmed.

The body camera footage provides a closer account of the moments after the fall. The roommate's account, security camera footage and the early police report offer details about the circumstances. Sargent's own words to responders, spoken while she lay injured on the pool deck, also form part of the public record. However, police have not announced a final finding on the circumstances of the fall.

excerpt: A 19-year-old farm worker died after a captive tiger attacked him during a TikTok shoot at a Lahore farmhouse, prompting arrests and questions over safety and wildlife permits.
headline: Teenager Mauled to Death by Tiger While Helping TikTok Influencer Film Dangerous Stunt in Pakistan
html_content:
A 19-year-old farm worker was mauled to death by a captive tiger during a TikTok video shoot in Lahore, Pakistan, last week, according to police. The influencer and farmhouse owner were arrested following the attack but were granted bail on Saturday, 14 November 2026.

The victim, identified as Talha, worked at a private farmhouse in the Kahna area, where TikTok influencer Nauman Hassan had reportedly arrived to film content involving a big cat.

Police said the animal became uncontrollable during the recording and attacked the teenager, leaving him critically injured.

Investigators subsequently uncovered what they described as an attempt to disguise the incident as a dog attack.

Lahore TikTok Video Shoot Ends in Fatal Tiger Attack

Talha was taken to a private hospital following the attack but died during treatment, according to Lahore police.

A complaint reportedly alleged that Hassan had asked the teenager to remove the animal from its enclosure for filming.

That allegation has not been established by a court.

There were initially conflicting accounts of the animal involved. Some reports described a tigress, while Lahore police identified it as a lioness.

The Punjab Wildlife Department confiscated the animal following the incident.

Investigators also examined allegations that the circumstances of Talha's injuries had been deliberately concealed.

Police said the incident had initially been described as a dog attack before investigators established that the injuries resulted from a captive big cat.

The available police reporting did not establish who was responsible for the alleged concealment.

Lahore's Deputy Inspector General of Operations, Faisal Kamran, condemned the circumstances surrounding Talha's death.

He said making TikTok videos could not take precedence over protecting human life.

Kamran also promised an investigation into possible negligence and any effort to conceal the truth.

Police examined whether the farmhouse had the necessary wildlife permit and adequate safety arrangements for keeping the animal.

No final finding concerning those requirements was reported.

A 19-year-old farm worker was mauled to death by a lioness at a farmhouse in the Kahna area, prompting police to arrest the property owner and a TikToker who was reportedly visiting the premises to record a video. The victim, Talha, suffered fatal injuries when the lioness attacked him during the visit of TikToker Nauman. The victim was rushed to a private hospital but succumbed to his injuries. Kahna police arrested the farmhouse owner, Fayyaz and the TikToker. The Punjab Wildlife Department took the lioness into custody, while the victim’s body was shifted to a morgue for post-mortem examination.

Posted by Express Tribune on Friday, November 13, 2026

TikTok Influencer and Farm Owner Granted Bail After Family Forgives Suspects

Police arrested Hassan and farmhouse owner Fayaz Ahmad in connection with the fatal attack.

Both appeared before Magistrate Qaiser Riaz at Lahore's Model Town courts on Saturday, 14 November.

According to Pakistani newspaper Dawn, Talha's legal heirs appeared at the hearing and submitted affidavits saying they had forgiven the two suspects.

They said they had no objection to the men's release on bail or acquittal.

The prosecutor opposed their release, arguing that the allegations were serious and warranted further questioning.

The court rejected the police request for physical remand and granted both men bail against surety bonds of 50,000 Pakistani rupees each (approximately £135).

The decision did not amount to a finding that either suspect was innocent.

The case has renewed attention to Punjab's regulation of privately owned big cats.

In July 2025, authorities launched a crackdown after an escaped pet lion injured a woman and two children in Lahore.

Wildlife officials subsequently confiscated 18 illegally kept lions and inspected breeding facilities across the province.

The earlier attack prompted renewed enforcement of licensing and enclosure requirements.

In Talha's case, questions surrounding the farmhouse's permit and safety arrangements remained unresolved in the latest police reporting.

excerpt: Former basketball player Nikita Tyukalo faces six charges over an alleged OnlyFans trafficking operation in Washington state. He has pleaded not guilty.
headline: Who Is Nikita Tyukalo? Former Basketball Player Accused of Luring Women With OnlyFans Riches and Running a Camgirl Empire
html_content:
Nikita Tyukalo, a former college basketball player, allegedly recruited women with promises of lucrative OnlyFans careers before taking control of their accounts. Investigators also allege that some women experienced physical abuse, threats and intimidation.

The allegations are examined in TMZ Studios Presents: Inside the Camgirl Criminal Empire, a documentary that TMZ reported was released on YouTube on 14 November. Prosecutors allege four women were trafficked between July 2024 and June 2026 through an operation involving multiple properties, adult-content platforms and associates working under Nova Talent Management.

Tyukalo has pleaded not guilty to all six charges. These comprise four counts of second-degree human trafficking, one count of money laundering and one count of leading organized crime.

Who Is Nikita Tyukalo?

Garden City Community College's 2024–25 basketball roster lists Tyukalo as a 6ft 7in freshman guard from Seattle who previously attended BFL Prep. The profile establishes his playing background but does not explain why he stopped playing.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Nikita Tyukalo (@nikitatyuka1o)

Prosecutors allege that he directed and financed associates involved in recruiting women, managing accounts and distributing explicit content through Nova Talent Management. Reporting on the charging documents describes a management hierarchy linked to properties in Bellevue and Renton

OnlyFans Recruitment and Account Control

Charging documents include statements from four women who said they were recruited at 17 and persuaded to begin producing sexually explicit content on their 18th birthdays. Investigators allege that the operation involved OnlyFans and Chaturbate.

On June 4, 2026, SWAT stormed an OnlyFans mansion near Seattle with an armored truck and flash bangs.

The man running it was a 6'7" college basketball player who quit the game to manage the models.

What gave him away was a scream on a live stream.

His name is Nikita Tyukalo.… pic.twitter.com/bvYsAuTVRF

— Fatmir (@FatmirReads) November 15, 2026

Tyukalo allegedly described running accounts 'like an agency', offering opportunities to travel on private jets and make 'a substantial amount of money'. One girlfriend was allegedly told that creating explicit content could help pay her school bills.

Women told investigators they had been locked out of accounts created in their names. The documentary's accompanying report alleges that Tyukalo changed their OnlyFans login details, preventing them from accessing the accounts and checking their earnings.

Working Hours and Allegedly Withheld Earnings

Women told investigators they streamed on Chaturbate for 14 hours a day before producing additional OnlyFans content, according to court documents cited by FOX 13 Seattle. They described working seven days a week.

The documents also contain allegations that women were given Adderall to remain awake and received allowances equivalent to about $2 (£1.50) per hour worked. These were reported allegations about working conditions, not independently established employment records.

Investigators identified an account that reportedly generated nearly $230,000 (£174,000) in gross revenue over one year, although the woman associated with the account allegedly could not access the earnings. They also reported finding cashier's cheques and banking documents showing hundreds of thousands of dollars moving through business accounts.

Police Complaints Preceded Trafficking Investigation

Police received numerous complaints and emergency calls concerning the Bellevue property, with officers responding to more than 100 incidents before detectives developed evidence suggesting human trafficking. Investigators reported seizing more than 300 mobile phones, over 50 laptops, financial records and a whiteboard labelled 'Content Plan' during a search.

Women described assaults, restraint, firearm threats and pressure to continue producing explicit material, with multiple associates identified in their accounts. Investigators also alleged that intimate images were used as leverage, including threats to send material to loved ones.

Documentary Coverage and Reported Trial Delay

The documentary, available on YouTube, features an investigator alleging that artificial audience inflation improved performers' visibility on streaming platforms. Its coverage revisits the allegations rather than announcing a conviction.

Tyukalo was arrested on 4 June and pleaded not guilty on 10 June. Axios previously reported that an unnamed attorney who appeared on Tyukalo's behalf had described the operation as a legitimate business.

A 24 September report by The Journal 425 said a judge had postponed the state trial until 15 December 2026. The publication also reported that Tyukalo was the subject of a federal custody detainer linked to a separate sealed case. These reported federal developments have not been independently verified against federal court records for this article.

excerpt: Kristin Logan, a US Air Force veteran with stage 4 ovarian cancer, says she received information about Canada's assisted-dying programme before an oncology appointment and later moved to the United States for treatment.
headline: Stage 4 Cancer Patient Flees Canada After Claiming Doctors Offered Euthanasia Instead of Medical Care
html_content:
Kristin Logan, a US Air Force veteran with stage 4 ovarian cancer, says she received information about assisted dying before seeing an oncologist in Canada.

Speaking to Fox News Digital in an interview published on 14 November 2026, she described feeling 'set up to die' before seeking treatment in the United States.

Logan and her husband, Donovan James, had moved to Canada hoping publicly funded healthcare would protect them from overwhelming medical bills.

They permanently relocated to the US in May 2025 after repeated cross-border journeys for medical treatment.

Logan said her diagnosis in September 2023 led to delays and upsetting discussions about end-of-life care.

Her account has not been independently corroborated by the Canadian clinicians involved.

Kristin Logan Describes Assisted Dying Discussion Before Oncology Care

Logan said she was 43 when diagnosed and received information about Canada's medical assistance in dying programme, known as MAID, before an oncology appointment.

'It was the most heartbreaking experience, to basically be set up to die,' she told Fox News Digital.

She said the timing left her distressed because she had not yet discussed treatment options with a cancer specialist.

James also criticised the programme's expansion, arguing that care should focus on helping patients survive.

'They should be focusing on treating people and helping people live,' James told the publication.

Texas Right to Life, an anti-abortion organisation, reported in April 2026 that Logan alleged assisted dying had been presented as her only option. Its account did not include records from the clinicians concerned.

Canada's MAID programme allows eligible adults to receive medical assistance to end their lives.

Federal rules require a voluntary request, informed consent and assessments by two independent medical practitioners.

Providing information about MAID is not the same as recommending or approving it. The reporting does not establish whether Logan underwent a formal eligibility assessment or whether any medical provider refused cancer treatment because of MAID.

Stage 4 cancer patient flees Canada after allegedly being offered assisted suicide instead of life saving treatment pic.twitter.com/G7uSMRLrHz

— non aesthetic things (@PicturesFoIder) November 15, 2026

Kristin Logan's Emergency Treatment in Seattle and Move to Texas

Logan travelled to the US for initial treatment in September 2023, according to Fox News Digital. She later experienced a bowel obstruction in March 2024 and returned to Canada the following month.

During a subsequent emergency, James said Canadian providers had no immediate surgical plan and could not arrange a helicopter transfer to Vancouver.

He said he took Logan from hospital and drove across Vancouver Island before travelling by ferry towards Seattle.

James said an American surgeon warned that another day's delay could have resulted in fatal sepsis. Neither the reported warning nor the circumstances of the transfer have been independently corroborated through hospital records.

Texas Right to Life reported that Logan received HIPEC surgery and chemotherapy in Seattle. Fox News Digital said her cancer returned in December 2024.

The couple decided in January 2025 to move permanently to the United States and completed the relocation that May.

They later settled in Texas, where Logan continued treatment after further recurrences, according to Texas Right to Life.

British Columbia has separately announced expanded services for women with gynaecological cancers. Health Canada had not responded to Fox News Digital's request for comment when its report was published.

excerpt: Former Pentagon spokesman John Ullyot has renewed his call for Pete Hegseth to resign, arguing that the Secretary of Defense is damaging Donald Trump and the Republican Party.
headline: Pete Hegseth Urged To Quit by Former Pentagon Spokesman Who Says He Is 'Damaging' Trump's Brand
html_content:
Pete Hegseth should resign because he is damaging Donald Trump's political standing, according to former Pentagon spokesman John Ullyot. Speaking on MS NOW on 14 November, Ullyot renewed his call for the Secretary of War to step down, saying Hegseth was 'very much damaging the president's brand, no question about it, and the Republican brand.'

For context, Ullyot held a senior public affairs role at the Pentagon during the early months of Trump's second administration before leaving in April 2025. That same month, he went public in an opinion piece for Politico. In it, he accused Hegseth's team of causing turmoil through staff dismissals and misleading statements.

He described the department as being in 'total chaos.'

Ullyot has continued his criticism in a book published on 10 November 2026. The President Deserves Better: Leadership and Accountability to Keep America Great examines Hegseth and other figures in Trump's administration.

Why Ullyot Says Hegseth Should Resign

In the interview, Ullyot questioned whether the former television host was ever right for the job. He suggested Hegseth would have suited a less demanding public post.

'[Hegseth] could've run the presidential physical fitness council, like Arnold Schwarzenegger did; that would've been a perfect fit,' Ullyot said. 'But to run the Department of Defense is a very serious job, and he didn't take a serious approach.'

He framed stepping down as a test of loyalty. 'You'd get off the stage if you were truly loyal to President Donald Trump,' he said. He added that Hegseth would best serve the president by leaving office.

Ullyot acknowledged Hegseth's military record. Hegseth served three deployments as an infantry officer in the US Army National Guard. Yet Ullyot argued that time in uniform does not automatically equip someone to manage the US military. In his view, serving in the field and running a vast department are different jobs.

He was just as blunt about Hegseth's dealings with the press, calling him a 'Fox News fire-breather' who 'relishes' confronting journalists.

Hegseth's Role in the Iran War and Republican Election Losses

Ullyot also tied his resignation call to the Iran war. He pointed to Vice President JD Vance's comments after Republicans suffered major losses in the 2026 midterm elections.

Vance wrote on 4 November that 'the reason we lost is the war', referring to the Iran conflict.

Ullyot then asked who oversaw munitions stockpiles and who advised the president. His answer was Hegseth, who he said should have removed himself from the role. For Ullyot, the conflict only strengthens the case for Hegseth to step down.

Vance, for his part, blamed the war for Republican losses but did not single out Hegseth personally.

Neither Hegseth nor the Pentagon had publicly responded to Ullyot's remarks in the reporting available at the time. Ullyot's claims are his own views as a former official who has publicly criticised his former boss.

Hegseth remains in office as Secretary of War, a secondary title authorised by Trump's September 2025 executive order. His statutory title remains Secretary of Defense.

Ullyot's demand is clear. In his view, the most loyal thing Hegseth can do for Trump now is leave. He is pressing that case in his book and on air, linking it to the Republicans' midterm losses. Whether anyone in the White House is listening is another question entirely.

excerpt: A 14-year-old girl identified as Ruka reportedly died after falling from a sixth-floor balcony in Japan during a livestream, though key details remain unverified and police have not commented publicly.
headline: Japanese Girl, 14, Reportedly Dies After Balcony Fall During TikTok Livestream, With Viewers Recalling Her 'Last Words'
html_content:
A 14-year-old girl identified in media reports as Ruka reportedly died after falling from a sixth-floor apartment balcony in Japan during a livestream, which the publications covering the incident attributed to TikTok. Accounts of the incident describe viewers hearing her speak before the fall, but do not establish a complete timeline of what happened.

The Free Press Journal describes her as a middle-school student and reports that Japanese police are investigating the incident. However, the report does not identify the police department involved or provide an official statement confirming the inquiry.

Separately, viewers reportedly recalled hearing her say, 'I'm scared', although the timing of that remark has not been established.

The girl's identity, the circumstances of the fall and the reports of her death have not been independently confirmed.

Reported Sixth-Floor Fall

The Free Press Journal reports that Ruka was sitting on the apartment balcony railing before falling. However, the circumstances leading to the fall have not been independently established.

It says footage shows her briefly holding on to the railing before falling, although it remains unclear whether the recording circulating online captures the full sequence of events.

That leaves a distinction between the movements described in the footage and the circumstances surrounding them. The account does not establish what happened before she sat on the railing, why she was there or whether anyone nearby was able to intervene.

She reportedly suffered serious head injuries and later died. However, the report does not identify a hospital, medical professional, emergency service or family member as the source of that information. It also does not say when her death was confirmed or whether she received treatment before she died.

The incident is placed at an apartment building in Japan, without a city, address or exact date. The report does not explain how her age and school status were established, or whether Ruka was her first name, an online identity or a pseudonym.

Viewers Recall Remarks During the Livestream

According to Haberler, a Turkish news website, friends and other viewers who followed the livestream recalled hearing the girl say phrases including 'I'm hungry', 'I'm scared' and 'This is dangerous'. However, no authenticated transcript has been provided to establish the exact wording, sequence of the remarks or how much time passed between them.

Haberler describes the phrases as her 'last words', but provides no authenticated transcript establishing their order or whether she said anything afterwards.

Without that sequence, the quotations cannot reliably be presented as the final exchange before the fall. They also do not, on their own, establish the girl's intentions or explain how she came to fall.

Police Inquiry Lacks Official Confirmation

Japanese police are investigating the girl's death, according to the reporting. Neither account, however, names the police department involved, quotes an officer or includes an official statement confirming the inquiry.

No findings from investigators are provided. The description of a loss of balance therefore remains part of the published account rather than a conclusion attributed to police.

It is also unclear whether anyone else was present at the apartment. The reports do not establish whether the girl was alone, whether anyone witnessed the incident in person or whether investigators have spoken to people who watched the livestream.

Emergency Response Remains Unclear

The TikTok broadcast reportedly ended after the incident. Haberler describes it as ending suddenly after the remarks attributed to the girl, but does not establish the interval between those words, the fall and the transmission ending.

Neither account gives a verified audience figure or explains whether viewers contacted emergency services. There is no clear timeline showing when help was requested, when responders arrived or what assistance the girl received immediately afterwards.

The available accounts therefore leave several parts of the sequence unresolved: what preceded the fall, how people watching responded and what happened once the broadcast stopped. Until those details are supported by attributable evidence, the circulating footage and reported remarks offer only a partial account of the incident.

excerpt: Trump's White House post draws scrutiny amid unverified death rumours, as calendar entries document a Sunday visit to his golf club and return.
headline: Where Is Trump? Death Rumours Resurface as President Posts 'I Am in the White House' After Days Out of Public View
html_content:
Donald Trump said he was 'in the White House having meetings on many subjects' in a Truth Social post on Sunday 15 November, as questions about his whereabouts and unverified death speculation appeared online. His presidential calendar records a visit to his golf club that morning and a return to the White House that afternoon.

The post's displayed timestamp converts to 8.42am Eastern Time, placing it 92 minutes before his recorded departure at 10.14am. The sequence does not suggest a contradiction between his statement and the visit, while the origin, trigger and reach of the death speculation remain unclear.

Trump's Statement Precedes Golf-Club Visit

Aaron Rupar shared a schedule entry stating that Trump would work from early morning until late evening, making calls and holding meetings. Trump echoed that description in his own Truth Social post on Sunday.

President Trump will work from early in the morning until late in the evening. He will make many calls and have many meetings. pic.twitter.com/vaGjBEyfEw

— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 15, 2026

Trump also added: 'Very exciting times for the USA.' The message did not identify the meetings or say it was responding to death speculation, and the timing of the identified speculation relative to the post remains unconfirmed.

Calendar Documents Departure and Return

The presidential calendar records Trump departing the White House at 10.14am and arriving at Trump National Golf Club Washington DC at 10.45am. It lists his departure from the club at 1.26pm and his return to the White House at 2.02pm, completing the recorded outward and return journey.

The calendar also records a White House Press Office travel/photo lid at 2.09pm, seven minutes after Trump's recorded return. It does not detail his activities at the club or after he returned to the White House.

X Posts Raise Different Questions

An indexed excerpt from an X post by ColinTheLefty asked whether Trump was 'already dead', without providing evidence to support the claim. That establishes an instance of speculation, not who originated it or how widely it was accepted, and the excerpt does not reconstruct the surrounding conversation.

Holy shit, y’all.

Is that motherfucker already dead and they’re gonna blame it on Iran? 🤔

— Mac the Lefty (@ColinTheLefty) November 15, 2026

Democratic Representative Ted Lieu separately asked: 'Why does trump feel the need to say that he is in the White House doing meetings today?' His question challenged the explanation of Trump's activities but did not allege a death, so it should not be treated as support for the other account's suggestion.

Why does trump feel the need to say that he is in the White House doing meetings today? https://t.co/gasLgSM9EK

— Ted Lieu (@tedlieu) November 15, 2026

In a separate X post on Saturday, Rupar questioned Trump's public visibility noting that he had not publicly commented on Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop.

Donald Trump has not be seen in public since Wednesday, and he hasn't uttered a single word about yesterday's historic air travel ground stop -- not even on his Truth Social page

— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 14, 2026

FAA Officials Describe Friday Contact

Officials also described contact with Trump during Friday's FAA disruption, providing an earlier account of his communications rather than evidence of his condition on Sunday. At the evening briefing, Sean Duffy said: 'We were in multiple times talking to the president about what was happening in the airspace.'

Duffy also said he and Markwayne Mullin had been in the Oval Office with Trump and that the president had communicated with them multiple times, including shortly before Duffy addressed reporters. Mullin said at an earlier briefing that the president had been briefed, but neither transcript connects the FAA disruption to the subsequent death speculation or establishes its cause.

Earlier Activity Adds to the Timeline

Earlier records also document Trump's public appearances and communications. A transcript dated 11 November records JD Vance introducing him before his Veterans Day remarks at Arlington National Cemetery, while another, dated 12 November, documents an interview with Hugh Hewitt.

The calendar and transcripts provide a record of Trump's movements and officials' accounts of contact with him, rather than an assessment of his health. None of the reviewed material substantiates claims that he has died, and the identified social-media evidence does not establish widespread speculation.

excerpt: Estonia plans to close its three road crossings with Russia on 1 December after officials accused Moscow of directing an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems.
headline: Estonia Blames Moscow for Foiled Arson Plot as Russia Border Closure Raises Fears of a Wider Security Crisis
html_content:
Estonia plans to close its three road border crossings with Russia on 1 December after authorities accused Moscow of ordering an attempted arson attack on a drone manufacturer. Eight people were detained following the incident at Threod Systems in Viimsi, near Tallinn, on Saturday, 14 November, Estonian officials said.

The Estonia-Russia border closure was announced on Sunday, a day after the reported attempt to damage the defence company.

Estonia's Internal Security Service attributes the operation to Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU. That allegation has not been independently established.

Authorities said the incident was thwarted without injuries. The decision places a new restriction on movement between Estonia and Russia, with the government yet to announce a reopening date.

Estonia-Russia Border Closure Follows Drone Maker Attack

Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the planned restrictions were intended to protect people and reduce the risks of further hostile operations.

He accused Russian intelligence services of using border crossings to exert influence.

'Closing the border would reduce the threat to people in Estonia,' Michal said, according to his statement on Sunday.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna described the suspected attack as evidence that threats to European security extended beyond the war in Ukraine.

The accusation forms part of Estonia's broader warnings about what its officials describe as Russian hybrid operations.

In a statement on Sunday, Estonia's Foreign Ministry identified the targeted company as Threod Systems and said the planned closure would also help limit sanctions circumvention.

Tsahkna said he had contacted counterparts in Latvia, Lithuania and Finland about the decision.

The government has not specified whether the closure will be temporary or indefinite. Estonia's three road crossings with Russia are Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa, which have accommodated pedestrian and freight movement.

Tsahkna said he intended to discuss further pressure on Russia with European Union foreign ministers meeting in Brussels on Monday.

Discussions about additional measures do not mean that any new sanctions have already been agreed.

Estonia-Russia Border Closure Draws Ukrainian Support

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha welcomed the announcement in a post on X. He said Estonia's response showed that suspected sabotage could have consequences beyond diplomatic criticism and urged wider European support.

Ukraine stands in full solidarity with Estonia following the attempted arson attack against Estonian defence company Threod Systems.

I fully share your assessment, dear @Tsahkna, and strongly condemn this act of sabotage.

By targeting a European defence company, Russia is… https://t.co/JzMgoAQ6QD

— Andrii Sybiha 🇺🇦 (@andrii_sybiha) November 15, 2026

The diplomatic reaction follows a series of security incidents in Europe that officials have attributed, to varying degrees, to Russia.

CNN cited drone incidents involving Poland and Lithuania, as well as disruptions affecting transport in other European countries.

Those episodes have contributed to concern among NATO members about activity intended to test their security without provoking a direct confrontation.

Responsibility for each incident, however, should be assessed separately rather than treated as conclusively proved.

Russia has repeatedly denied allegations of sabotage in Europe. Moscow had not immediately commented on the latest Estonian accusation when the original report was published.

For travellers and freight operators using Estonia's eastern crossings, the immediate question is practical.

The government has set 1 December as the planned closure date but has not said when traffic might resume.

He said Estonia's response showed that suspected sabotage could have consequences beyond diplomatic criticism and urged wider European support. Ukraine stands in full solidarity with Estonia following the attempted arson attack against Estonian defence company Threod Systems. I fully share your assessment, dear @Tsahkna, and strongly condemn this act of sabotage. By targeting a European defence company, Russia is… https://t.co/JzMgoAQ6QD — Andrii Sybiha 🇺🇦 (@andrii_sybiha) November 15, 2026 The diplomatic reaction follows a series of security incidents in Europe that officials have attributed, to varying degrees, to Russia. excerpt: A House report says federal prosecutors missed chances to stop Epstein, failed to notify survivors and overlooked warning signs in his case.
headline: Jeffrey Epstein Could Have Been Stopped After 2005 but Federal Failures Allowed Further Abuse: House Report Finds
html_content:
Federal prosecutors and investigators missed opportunities to prevent further crimes by Jeffrey Epstein after 2005, according to a Republican-led House Oversight Committee report released 10 November 2026.

The majority staff report follows a 15-month investigation involving 19 transcribed interviews and depositions, as well as a review of Justice Department, estate and financial records. It recommends further scrutiny of people and institutions, alongside legal changes.

The 2007 Agreement Shielded Epstein From Federal Charges

The report criticises the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida for reaching a non-prosecution agreement with Epstein in 2007. Rather than pursue federal charges, prosecutors allowed him to plead guilty to lesser Florida state offences in 2008.

He received an 18-month sentence, served 13 months and was granted extensive work-release privileges. The report says he continued abusing women while on work release.

Prosecutors did not notify survivors about the agreement, which granted immunity to four named women and an unspecified number of unnamed potential co-conspirators. The committee examined possible conflicts involving former prosecutors Matthew Menchel and Bruce Reinhart.

The committee also examined an alleged photograph of Menchel skiing with Epstein in Aspen, Colorado, in the early 2000s. Acosta testified that he was unaware of the photograph, and the committee did not establish its authenticity.

Reinhart left the prosecutor's office on 1 January 2008 and immediately established his own private practice. The report says he had taken steps to establish the firm while still employed at the office and began representing Epstein associates shortly after his departure.

Former U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta could not confirm whether Reinhart improperly influenced the investigation.

Committee Calls for Further Interviews of Epstein Witnesses

The report recommends that the Justice Department interview or reinterview people with information about Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell, his longtime associate convicted of sex trafficking and related offences in 2021. It also calls for further scrutiny of Lesley Groff, Epstein's longtime executive assistant, over what she knew and any role in facilitating criminal activity.

During a committee interview, Sarah Kellen, a longtime Epstein assistant and survivor, alleged that former Miami Beach Mayor Philip Levine and French celebrity hairstylist Frédéric Fekkai sexually assaulted her. Representatives for both men denied the allegations, ABC News reported. The committee recommends further Justice Department investigation.

DOJ Criticised Over Files and Prison Failures

The report faults the Justice Department's handling of records released under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, signed into law on 19 November 2025. It says poor communication with survivors and inadequate redactions exposed sensitive personal information. It recommends giving survivors and their representatives access to unredacted government files.

Epstein died on 10 August 2019 at New York's Metropolitan Correctional Center. The report says understaffing and institutional failures contributed to officers' missing at least 12 security rounds and three inmate counts, leaving inmates without adequate supervision for nearly eight hours.

Report Urges Legal Changes and Financial Scrutiny

The report calls for greater scrutiny of American Express, JPMorgan Chase and Deutsche Bank over dealings with Epstein. It says American Express assigned him a dedicated relationship manager who arranged itineraries intended to facilitate visa approvals for foreign women.

Records included decoy flights and refundable or dummy bookings. Groff testified she recalled only one decoy flight and said it was not intended for a visa application.

The committee recommends that the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) review whether financial institutions met reporting obligations. It also backs the proposed Survivor's Voice Protection Act, H.R. 10389, introduced by committee Chairman James Comer, a Kentucky Republican. It would restrict certain clauses used to silence survivors and introduce reporting requirements for trusted individuals who suspect grooming.

'Epstein operated with impunity, shielded and enabled by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims,' Comer said in the committee's press release.

Republicans and Democrats Dispute Report's Findings

The Republican majority report says witnesses told investigators that, to their knowledge, Trump was not involved in Epstein's or Maxwell's crimes. It also says the committee found no documents implicating the president in criminal activity related to the pair. These findings reflect the majority staff's conclusions and do not constitute an independent judicial determination.

Ranking Democrat Robert Garcia of California challenged the investigation's scope. 'Oversight Republicans have released a report based on an incomplete investigation and zero public hearings on Jeffrey Epstein,' he said. Garcia accused the Justice Department of withholding more than 2.5 million pages and said Democrats planned hearings on Epstein's associates, including Trump.

excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his family relocated to a military base after reported Iranian assassination threats, amid wider security concerns affecting senior Trump administration officials.
headline: Scott Bessent Moves to Military Base With Family After Iran Threats Reach 'More Than an Advanced Stage'
html_content:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated to a military base following reported Iranian assassination threats, with his family also moving, according to an administration official. The official told Fox News on 10 November 2026 that the threats had reached 'more than an advanced stage.'

The move followed growing security concerns among President Donald Trump's senior officials, several of whom have reportedly relocated to military installations.

Bessent confirmed on Friday, 13 November, that he had followed Secret Service instructions to leave his Washington residence.

The Treasury Department said he would not be deterred by threats attributed to the Iranian regime.

Scott Bessent Addresses Iranian Threats Behind Military Base Move

The precise nature of the threats against Bessent remains undisclosed.

A senior administration official told Fox News that the security situation had become sufficiently serious for Bessent and his family to relocate.

The official did not disclose when the move occurred or provide evidence detailing the intelligence assessment.

Speaking to CNBC on 13 November, Bessent defended the decision and described Iran as 'like a dangerous cornered animal.'

He also criticised The Wall Street Journal for publishing an aerial photograph of his Georgetown residence in January 2025.

Bessent argued that the image made his home easier to identify and posed additional security risks.

A person familiar with his arrangements separately told Fox News that security concerns increased following the photograph's publication.

The relocation occurred amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran, including continuing military conflict and economic sanctions.

Bessent has led Operation Economic Outcast since its launch on 24 August, targeting financial networks supporting the Iranian government.

The Treasury Department has imposed sanctions on institutions and businesses accused of helping Tehran evade financial restrictions.

Iran has denied plotting attacks against American officials or individuals on US soil.

Separately, an intelligence memorandum reviewed by Reuters warned that Iranian plots against US personnel and citizens had reached an advanced stage.

No assassination attempt against Bessent has been publicly confirmed.

Scott Bessent's Relocation Adds to Scrutiny of Military Housing

Bessent is among several senior Trump administration officials reportedly living at military installations or other protected government residences.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth have reportedly moved into military accommodation.

White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller has also reportedly relocated to protected housing.

The moves have not all been attributed to Iranian threats. Some followed concerns about domestic political violence.

Former Secret Service agent and former FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino said protection decisions depend on intelligence assessments and documented threats.

He told Fox News that social media had increased the volume of threatening communications requiring investigation.

Former Secret Service agent Barry Donadio suggested that Bessent's relocation indicated unusually serious security concerns.

His assessment did not establish that an assassination attempt had been planned or prevented.

The use of military housing by civilian officials has also attracted congressional scrutiny.

California Democratic Representative George Whitesides secured committee approval in June for proposed Pentagon reporting requirements.

The proposal would examine the threats justifying accommodation, the legal authority for the arrangements and rental costs.

It would also assess whether political appointees received leases and rental rates comparable to those required for the Secretary of Defense.

The committee proposal sets a 1 May 2027 deadline for the report, although its final legislative status requires confirmation.

excerpt: A nationwide US flight ground stop caused thousands of cancellations and delays after a telecommunications failure affected FAA systems, while officials investigated a possible equipment or installation fault.
headline: Trump Blames Biden for US Flight Crisis Despite FAA Saying Root Cause of Nationwide Ground Stop Is Unclear
html_content:
President Donald Trump blamed Joe Biden's administration on Sunday, 15 November, for America's flight crisis after a nationwide ground stop disrupted thousands of journeys. Federal officials were still investigating the precise technical failure behind Friday's shutdown of departures.

The disruption began on 13 November when telecommunications instability affected air traffic control communications and radar systems. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted departures nationwide as a safety precaution before reopening airspace that evening.

Airlines continued cancelling flights throughout the weekend as they struggled to reposition aircraft and crews.

Trump Blames Biden as US Flight Cancellations Mount

Trump addressed the disruption publicly on Sunday morning, nearly two days after the ground stop, blaming his predecessor's administration in posts on Truth Social.

'The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad,' Trump wrote.

He accused Biden's administration of wasting money and worsening ageing aviation infrastructure.

The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began. We have the knowledge and plan for the Flight Control Systems, we need Congress to give the money, FAST! Our FAA… pic.twitter.com/qP5VNbWeJP

— Commentary Donald J. Trump Truth Social Posts On X (@TrumpTruthOnX) November 15, 2026

However, he provided no evidence establishing that decisions made under Biden caused Friday's technical failure.

Trump also pressed Congress to approve funding for a comprehensive overhaul of the air traffic control system.

'Our FAA is doing a great job, and is ready to go,' he wrote.

In a subsequent post, Trump claimed much of the existing infrastructure was 50 years old and urged lawmakers to finance faster modernisation.

The political dispute unfolded as airlines struggled to recover from one of the year's most disruptive periods for American aviation.

FlightAware recorded 9,159 cancellations and 7,190 delays on Friday, according to figures reported by CBS News.

More than 6,400 additional flights were cancelled on Saturday, further complicating travel plans across the country.

FAA Investigation Examines Contractor Work Behind Nationwide Ground Stop

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage occurred during maintenance involving defence contractor L3Harris, which provides telecommunications infrastructure for the FAA.

Workers had been replacing ageing copper connections with fibre technology when a router began overwhelming other equipment with connection requests.

The resulting instability affected communications and radar feeds, prompting authorities to suspend departures.

Duffy said investigators were examining whether installation error or defective equipment caused the malfunction. No definitive finding about the contractor's responsibility had been announced.

L3Harris said it was cooperating with the FAA's investigation into the incident.

🚨 BREAKING: Sec. Sean Duffy announces Friday's FAA nationwide ground stop was caused by L3Harris UPGRADING a discontinued wire to fiber "in at least one of our remote FAA locations" — and it could be incompetence or "faulty piece of equipment"

"The router started FLOODING other… pic.twitter.com/W7RXEQUQu4

— Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh) November 14, 2026

Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford defended the decision to ground flights, citing the need to protect passengers while controllers dealt with unstable systems.

Officials also reported finding no evidence of a cyberattack.

The administration's investigation therefore remained focused on technical failures and maintenance procedures rather than evidence linking the disruption directly to Biden-era decisions.

Duffy said on Sunday that airlines were making progress towards normal operations, although aircraft and crews remained out of position.

He expected flight schedules to recover more fully by Monday, 16 November.

Meanwhile, Trump continued pressing Congress for additional infrastructure funding, maintaining that his administration could replace the ageing system more quickly if lawmakers approved the money.

excerpt: Republican senators are resisting several of Donald Trump's 23 pending judicial nominees, creating uncertainty over whether the Senate can confirm them before Democrats take control in January 2027.
headline: Trump Faces GOP Revolt Over 23 Pending Judicial Nominees as Democrats Prepare To Take Control of Senate
html_content:
President Donald Trump's effort to confirm 23 pending judicial nominees before Democrats take control of the US Senate faces resistance from several Republicans. The dispute centres on a handful of candidates selected for federal judgeships, Reuters reported on Sunday, 15 November 2026.

The confrontation follows Democratic victories in the 3 November midterm elections, which are expected to give the party control of the Senate in January 2027.

Republicans had confirmed 57 of Trump's judicial nominees during his second term by 15 November. But disagreements over several remaining selections could complicate his final confirmation push.

At issue is a Senate tradition allowing lawmakers substantial influence over judicial appointments in their home states.

Trump Judicial Nominees Face Resistance From Republican Senators

Under Senate Judiciary Committee custom, home-state senators can obstruct district court nominations by withholding a 'blue slip' indicating their support.

Oklahoma Republican Senator Alan Armstrong has accused the White House of disregarding qualified candidates recommended by his office.

Armstrong told Reuters that the administration had 'basically ignored' his recommendations in favour of its preferred candidate.

The dispute has already prompted a change in Trump's plans for an Arkansas appeals court vacancy.

On 10 November, the White House withdrew US District Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals.

Arkansas Republican Senators John Boozman and Tom Cotton had opposed Rudofsky.

Trump subsequently nominated Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland for the position.

Retiring North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis has supported colleagues challenging judicial selections made without their backing.

'That's not how it works here,' Tillis told reporters, criticising the administration's approach to consulting senators.

Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn has separately declined to commit to supporting T. Elliot Gaiser for a federal judgeship in Dallas.

Gaiser heads the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel and was selected without Texas's customary senator-led screening process.

Without Cornyn's support, Gaiser could struggle to advance through the Senate Judiciary Committee.

Trump Judicial Nominees Face Deadline Before Democrats Take Control

The White House maintains that it wants all pending nominees confirmed before the end of 2026.

'We expect all judicial nominees pending in the Senate to be confirmed this year,' an administration official told Reuters.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune has made judicial confirmations a priority during the remaining Republican-controlled session.

The Senate scheduled a confirmation vote on Colorado District Judge Daniel Domenico's nomination to the 10th Circuit for Monday, 16 November.

Another disputed candidate is Zachary Paul West, an Oklahoma attorney general's office lawyer nominated for the Eastern District of Oklahoma.

Armstrong initially submitted a favourable blue slip for West but subsequently withdrew his support.

Tillis has backed Armstrong's objections, leaving West without sufficient expected committee votes, according to Reuters.

The Senate Judiciary Committee is scheduled to consider West's nomination on Tuesday, 17 November.

Armstrong's expected replacement by Republican Senator-elect Kevin Hern could alter the situation, although the transition depends on certification and swearing-in arrangements.

Trump confirmed 234 federal judges during his first presidency, including three Supreme Court justices.

Reuters estimates that his appointees now account for roughly one-third of active federal judges.

Cornyn and Tillis, both approaching the end of their Senate terms, retain significant influence over which nominees advance before Democrats assume control.

excerpt: Joe Rogan criticised Donald Trump's administration after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, blaming the Iran war and immigration enforcement while stopping short of changing his political allegiance.
headline: Joe Rogan Turns on Trump After 2024 MAGA Endorsement and Claims He Has Lost 'Most of the Country'
html_content:
Joe Rogan has sharply criticised Donald Trump's administration following the 2026 US midterm elections, saying Republicans have lost 'most of the country'. The podcast host made the remark in an episode released on 13 November, pointing to the Iran war and immigration enforcement.

'They didn't just lose the podcast bros. They lost most of the country,' Rogan said. He did not cite any polling to support the claim, which appeared to reflect his own interpretation of the election results.

For context, Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterm elections, according to the Associated Press. They will assume control when the new Congress convenes in January 2027, giving them greater power to challenge Trump's agenda.

Rogan made the remarks during episode 2,581 of The Joe Rogan Experience, titled Protect Our Parks 18, alongside comedians Shane Gillis, Mark Normand and Ari Shaffir. A transcript places the exchange at approximately two hours and two minutes into the recording. Rogan also told listeners not to take his opinions too seriously. The comments came during a lengthy, wide-ranging conversation with the three comedians rather than in a prepared statement.

Joe Rogan's 2024 Trump Endorsement

The comments stand out because of the role Rogan played in the 2024 presidential race. He interviewed Trump for nearly three hours in an episode released in late October 2024.

On 4 November 2024, Rogan publicly endorsed Trump in a post on X. He shared an interview with Elon Musk, saying the billionaire had made the 'most compelling case for Trump'.

Two years after that endorsement, Rogan's latest comments strike a markedly different tone. He linked the loss of Republican support to the administration entering 'a war that no one wants to be in'. He also criticised the presence of 'militarized police in the streets wearing masks and no ID'.

Even so, he has not withdrawn his endorsement or publicly backed another party or candidate.

Iran War and Immigration Policies Draw Rogan's Criticism

The Iran war has been a source of criticism for Rogan before. In October, during a podcast discussion, he said he did not support the war and questioned why the United States had become involved. He has argued that the conflict contradicts Trump's campaign promise to keep America out of new wars.

His latest remarks continue that criticism. This time, however, he directly linked the issue to the election results.

Immigration enforcement was his second target. Rogan objected to officers operating in local communities while wearing masks and displaying no clear identification. He also criticised the arrests of people who had lived in the United States for years and established ties to their communities.

His criticism focused on enforcement methods, although he continued to praise aspects of Trump's border policy.

'They did some good things. They closed the border, and then crime dropped significantly. Those are good things,' he said.

Rogan provided no figures to support his claim about falling crime, and IBTimes UK cannot independently verify it. Whether tighter border controls contributed to any decline is a separate question.

For now, his criticism centres on two administration policies: the Iran war and the enforcement of immigration rules. He has not announced any change in his political allegiance.

The podcast host made the remark in an episode released on 13 November, pointing to the Iran war and immigration enforcement. 'They didn't just lose the podcast bros. They lost most of the country,' Rogan said. He did not cite any polling to support the claim, which appeared to reflect his own interpretation of the election results. For context, Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterm elections, according to the Associated Press. They will assume control when the new Congress convenes in January 2027, giving them greater power to challenge Trump's agenda. Rogan made the remarks during episode 2,581 of The Joe Rogan Experience, titled Protect Our Parks 18, alongside comedians Shane Gillis, Mark Normand and Ari Shaffir. A transcript places the exchange at approximately two hours and two minutes into the recording. Rogan also told listeners not to take his opinions too seriously. The comments came during a lengthy, wide-ranging conversation with the three comedians rather than in a prepared statement. Joe Rogan's 2024 Trump Endorsement The comments stand out because of the role Rogan played in the 2024 presidential race. He interviewed Trump for nearly three hours in an episode released in late October 2024. On 4 November 2024, Rogan publicly endorsed Trump in a post on X. He shared an interview with Elon Musk, saying the billionaire had made the 'most compelling case for Trump'. Two years after that endorsement, Rogan's latest comments strike a markedly different tone. He linked the loss of Republican support to the administration entering 'a war that no one wants to be in'. He also criticised the presence of 'militarized police in the streets wearing masks and no ID'. Even so, he has not withdrawn his endorsement or publicly backed another party or candidate. In October, during a podcast discussion, he said he did not support the war and questioned why the United States had become involved. He has argued that the conflict contradicts Trump's campaign promise to keep America out of new wars. His latest remarks continue that criticism. This time, however, he directly linked the issue to the election results. Immigration enforcement was his second target. Rogan objected to officers operating in local communities while wearing masks and displaying no clear identification. He also criticised the arrests of people who had lived in the United States for years and established ties to their communities. excerpt: Lithuanian police have identified a British man as a suspect after a golden-coloured Jesus statue was removed from a cross and smashed at a Vilnius church on 11 November.
headline: British Man Accused of Smashing Golden Jesus Statue While Shouting 'Praise the Lord'
html_content:
A British man has been identified as a suspect after a golden-coloured statue of Jesus was removed from a cross and smashed at a church in Vilnius, Lithuania.

Police identified the suspect on 14 November, three days after the incident at the Shrine of Divine Mercy. He was questioned and had his identity document seized as a procedural measure, according to Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT. His British nationality was confirmed separately on 15 November.

Footage circulated online showing two men near the church. One handles the statue while the other records or photographs him. The statue breaks during the incident before the men leave. The video also captures the man carrying the statue saying, 'Listen ... listen ... praise the Lord!', as reported by the New York Post on 14 November.

A man removed a statue of the crucified Jesus from a church in Vilnius and held it up while joking with another man, before smashing it on the street. Both men fled the scene.

A priest has appealed for help identifying the English-speaking suspects. pic.twitter.com/VK97fBWw8v

— Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) November 15, 2026

The incident happened on Dominikonų Street in Vilnius Old Town. Police initially reported that it occurred at about 9pm on 11 November. A subsequent appeal specified a period between 9pm that evening and 12:30am on 12 November. The statue had been hanging from a wooden cross in the church's inner courtyard.

On 15 November, Lithuanian news agency ELTA reported that police spokesperson Tomas Bražėnas confirmed the suspect was a British citizen born in 1989. He was temporarily in Lithuania and was providing explanations to investigators. His identity document was seized, preventing him from leaving the country while the investigation continues.

The second man's nationality has not been publicly established. Some media reports described both men as suspected British tourists. However, police have confirmed the nationality of only one suspect. The initial police report did not identify a suspect or provide any nationality details.

Police Identify British Suspect as Investigation Develops

The 11 November police report said proceedings had begun under Article 284 of Lithuania's Criminal Code, concerning a public-order offence. The 14 November update referred to an investigation under Article 312, concerning the desecration of a grave or another place of public respect.

Police said the suspect had been identified, questioned and formally notified of the suspicion. The seizure of his identity document is a procedural measure, not a conviction. The investigation remains ongoing, and authorities have not publicly named him.

Footage shows the statue being removed from its cross and subsequently smashed. Police are investigating the incident as the alleged desecration of a place of public respect. They have not announced a separate theft charge.

Police have not said why the statue was damaged. TV3's 13 November report described an exclamation heard after the statue broke as 'Dieve!' ('God!'), while the New York Post reported that the footage captured the man saying, 'Listen ... listen ... praise the Lord!'

Church Community Expresses Grief

Elijas Anatolijus Markauskas, identified in Lithuanian reporting as vice-rector of the Shrine of Divine Mercy, spoke publicly about the damage. In an appeal shared by the church community, he described the incident as deeply painful.

'I'm in pain because it's not just a sacred thing. This is the image of the one we love, to whom we pray and entrust the world, the Homeland, our loved ones and ourselves,' he said.

For worshippers, the statue was a focus of prayer and devotion. The church community appealed for help identifying those shown in the footage.

Police and church representatives asked anyone with relevant information to contact investigators. Police have not said who the second man is or whether he faces any suspicion.

Investigators are continuing to establish what role each man played in the incident at the church.

excerpt: Russell Brand was reportedly transferred to HMP Littlehey after sentencing. Epstein survivor Juliette Rose Bryant highlighted a blue butterfly in his message recording.
headline: Russell Brand Reportedly Moved to HMP Littlehey as Epstein Survivor Flags Blue Butterfly in Video
html_content:
Russell Brand has reportedly been transferred to HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire, four days after receiving a sentence of 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault.

Laura Gallacher read Brand's message during an episode of the couple's Sunday Service programme released on 15 November. Brand said he was being held at HMP Littlehey and maintained that he was not guilty of the offences for which he had been jailed. Epstein survivor Juliette Rose Bryant highlighted a blue butterfly in the recording in a post on X that day.

Brand Reportedly Transferred to HMP Littlehey

Brand, 51, was reportedly moved from HMP Wandsworth in south-west London to HMP Littlehey, near Huntingdon, on Friday, 13 November, according to The Sun on Sunday. The move came four days after he was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court. The Ministry of Justice has not publicly confirmed the transfer.

Reports cited concerns about Brand's safety at Wandsworth and an assessment that he posed a low escape risk as possible reasons for the move. The Ministry of Justice has not publicly confirmed the transfer or its reported rationale.

HMP Littlehey is a Category C training prison, principally housing adult men convicted of sexual offences. Category C facilities hold prisoners who cannot be trusted in open conditions but pose a lower escape risk. The prison offers education and vocational courses, alongside facilities including a gymnasium, an all-weather sports pitch and an adult learning centre.

Brand was reportedly placed in a single cell on arrival, although that detail has not been independently confirmed.

Epstein Survivor Flags Butterfly in Brand Recording

Bryant drew attention to the butterfly in a post on X on 15 November, after Gallacher shared the programme recording. She has previously discussed the symbol in connection with her own experiences and those of other women who have spoken about Epstein.

Bryant has said she met Epstein in South Africa in 2002. She has also discussed a blue butterfly she drew in a diary earlier that year, before their meeting. Bryant has cited other examples of butterfly imagery associated with women who have spoken about Epstein, including Virginia Giuffre and Sarah Ransome.

However, the significance Bryant attaches to the symbol is her own interpretation. There is no verified evidence that Brand intended the butterfly in his recording as a reference to Epstein or any of the women who have spoken about him.

Brand Sentenced to 10 Years and Six Months

Brand was sentenced on 9 November by Mr Justice Joel Bennathan at Southwark Crown Court after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. The offences took place between 2004 and 2009. He pleaded not guilty. The jury acquitted him of two further rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The judge imposed a sentence of nine years for rape, alongside sentences of 18 months, nine months and eight months for the three sexual assaults. Those three terms run concurrently with one another but consecutively to the rape sentence, producing a total of 10 years and six months. Brand must serve two-thirds of the term before release on licence and is subject to indefinite notification requirements under the Sexual Offences Act 2003.
