excerpt: Jensen Huang's allies reportedly plan a 'war room' to push for his return as NVIDIA CEO as the board searches for a permanent successor.
headline: Jensen Huang Allies Reportedly Assemble 'War Room' to Bring Him Back as NVIDIA CEO Days After He Quit
html_content:
Jensen Huang's allies are reportedly assembling a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return as NVIDIA chief executive, days after his resignation. According to an unnamed ally cited by the Financial Times, the effort has Huang's backing and would also seek support from the White House.

The campaign comes as NVIDIA's board pursues a permanent successor and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent calls for an outside leader. Employees have separately urged Huang's reinstatement, while Elon Musk has supported a public petition, distinct from the reported private lobbying operation.

Huang Allies Seek White House Support

Huang has discussed a possible return with confidants, and an unnamed ally described the planned executive lobbying group to the Financial Times, as summarised by Capital Brief. The organisers have not been identified, and no timetable for a comeback has been disclosed.

BREAKING

Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia’s chief executive, as allies in Silicon Valley pressure the company’s board to reinstate him days after the tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate.

Huang has… pic.twitter.com/LG4xqDGK8c

— Yashar Ali 🐘 (@yashar) November 15, 2026

No White House involvement has been confirmed, leaving the proposed approach as an intention rather than evidence of administration support. Nor has NVIDIA announced an agreement to reinstate Huang, whose supporters are seeking to change the direction of its leadership transition.

NVIDIA Board Pursues Permanent Successor

NVIDIA announced on 12 November that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately, with finance chief Colette Kress becoming interim chief executive. Kress retained her finance role, while Harvey C. Jones became board chair and directors began a search that would consider internal and external candidates.

Reuters, citing a Financial Times report it could not independently verify, reported that directors had approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas as a possible successor. NVIDIA's board said it had not formally engaged potential candidates and described speculation about individual names as 'premature'.

The Allegations Surrounding Huang's Departure

In an employee email reviewed by WIRED, Huang acknowledged being 'unfaithful to [his] wife' and said there was 'no excuse'. The publication said his acknowledgement followed reports of an alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at NVIDIA customer Megaspeed International, whom US intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. Reuters reported that it had not independently verified whether she had worked for the Chinese government.

WIRED reported that the resignation announcement followed allegations of an affair with a direct report. Reuters subsequently reported allegations of another relationship involving an NVIDIA employee. Huang's acknowledgement of infidelity did not confirm every reported relationship, and NVIDIA's announcement did not specify a reason for his resignation.

NVIDIA Employees Question Handling of Departure

Internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED showed that a suggestion-box submission made before Huang resigned subsequently attracted more than 1,600 comments, most supporting reinstatement. The original appeal asked directors to share their investigation's findings and formally seek employees' views about Huang continuing as chief executive.

🇺🇸 Nvidia employees want their founder BACK.

Jensen Huang resigned yesterday, and an internal suggestion box post asking the board to hear staff out has racked up MORE THAN 1,600 COMMENTS, most of them calling for his return.

Commenters are telling the board that anyone who… pic.twitter.com/00HPjUP5hT

— Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) November 13, 2026

Some employees had expected the investigation to conclude before major leadership changes, while a company-wide email demanded transparency about his departure. 'If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,' one anonymous contributor wrote, expressing support rather than recording a workforce-wide vote.

Bessent Wants Outsider to Lead NVIDIA

Bessent said NVIDIA needed to 'go outside the company' and undergo a 'dramatic shakeup', linking his leadership preference to concerns about events inside the business. His remarks represent political pressure, not a decision about the appointment.

Capital Brief reported that he wanted answers within 10 days about whether NVIDIA had been pressing what he called 'seemingly illicit sales' to boost revenue and earnings. That characterisation remains his allegation, not an established finding.

Musk Supports Public Petition for Huang's Return

The Washington Post reported that Musk had publicly announced his support for Huang's reinstatement, saying he was signing a petition. However, the newspaper noted that it was not immediately clear which petition he had signed. His name was also listed among supporters on the Stand With Jensen website. Capital Brief subsequently reported that the petition had attracted more than 136,000 signatures, although the figure has not been independently verified.

Musk argued NVIDIA could lose 'critical' deals because many were 'a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract'.

A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 13, 2026

His public support does not establish participation in the reported private lobbying operation. The signatures are not a verified measure of shareholder opinion and give petitioners no authority over NVIDIA's chief executive appointment.

excerpt: Researchers in China developed an experimental comb that restored about 97.85% of lost hair in mice by combining electrical stimulation with targeted genetic treatments. Human trials have not yet begun.
headline: Could an Electric Comb Beat Baldness? Scientists Report Nearly 100% Hair Regrowth, But There's a Catch
html_content:
Scientists have developed an experimental electric comb that restored nearly all lost hair in mice, raising hopes for a new approach to treating baldness. However, there is one significant catch: the technology has yet to be tested on humans.

Called Detangle, the comb-shaped device was developed by researchers led by a team at Beihang University in China. Their findings, published in Nature Communications on 3 November 2026, describe a bioelectronic system designed to deliver electrical stimulation and hair-growth treatments directly into hair follicles.

The research could eventually offer another option for people experiencing androgenetic alopecia (AGA), commonly known as male or female pattern hair loss. The condition affects more than 1.5 billion people worldwide, according to the study.

How the Electric Comb Works to Encourage Hair Growth

Although Detangle resembles an ordinary hair comb, its teeth contain specially designed electrodes and drug-delivery compartments.

As the device moves across the skin, it generates small electrical pulses that stimulate hair follicles. Its alternating teeth also create a stronger electric field, helping therapeutic molecules penetrate deeper into the skin.

According to the researchers, the system can deliver an electric field up to nine times deeper into hair follicle regions than conventional external application methods.

The team combined this electrical stimulation with two experimental treatments targeting different causes of hair loss.

The first, a VEGFA plasmid, encourages the development of blood vessels around hair follicles to improve their blood supply. The second, SRD5A2 siRNA, targets a gene involved in producing an enzyme responsible for converting testosterone into dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone associated with follicle shrinkage.

Together, the treatments aim to improve follicle health while encouraging new hair growth.

Tests Show Nearly 98% Hair Regrowth in Mice

The researchers tested Detangle on male mice with experimentally induced pattern hair loss, comparing its performance with conventional treatments.

After 28 days, untreated mice recovered only around 1% of the hair on the shaved area. Electrical stimulation alone increased regrowth to approximately 40%, while mice receiving finasteride and minoxidil achieved around 50% and 70%, respectively.

However, the results improved considerably when the electrical stimulation was combined with the experimental treatments.

Detangle achieved approximately 85% regrowth when paired with SRD5A2 siRNA and 90% when combined with VEGFA plasmid. Using both treatments alongside electrical stimulation produced the strongest results, with hair regrowth covering approximately 97.85% of the shaved area.

The researchers described the findings as evidence that combining electrostimulation with targeted molecular delivery could substantially improve hair restoration.

The Electric Comb Has Yet to Be Tested on Humans

Despite the impressive results, anyone hoping to replace their hair-loss medication with an electric comb will have to wait.

Detangle has only been evaluated in animal experiments, meaning there is currently no evidence that it can produce comparable results in humans. Its safety, effectiveness, and practical use as a treatment for people with pattern baldness still require further investigation.

The technology also relies on experimental genetic treatments, rather than simply using electrical stimulation to encourage hair growth.

Existing options, including minoxidil, finasteride, and hair transplants, remain established approaches to managing hair loss, although their effectiveness varies.

Detangle nevertheless represents a promising development in hair-loss research. If future human trials confirm the findings, the humble comb could eventually become part of a much more advanced approach to fighting baldness.

excerpt: Ukraine says a 100 mph SpaceX speed cap is knocking out the drones it uses to stop Russian jet-Shaheds, as Zelensky urges Musk to lift the limits before winter.
headline: Zelensky Begs Musk To Be on 'Right Side of History' After 100 Mph Starlink Cap Slows Ukraine's Air Defence
html_content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Sunday urged the US and Elon Musk to be on the 'right side of history' after a 100 mph (161 km/h) cap on Starshield terminals left interceptor drones unable to catch Russian drones hitting Ukrainian cities.

One Billionaire's Speed Setting

The restriction is simple and its effect is severe. Ukraine's cheap, domestically built interceptor drones lose their satellite link once they pass 100 mph, Zelensky said, so they can't chase down Russia's jet-powered Shahed drones, known in Russia as the Geran-3, which fly at roughly 230 mph (370 km/h). The speed restriction could determine whether interceptors can reach their targets, leaving Ukrainian air defence teams with fewer options.

Zelensky said Russian forces are aiming the jet Shaheds at electrical substations, and many are getting through while Ukraine heads into winter. Overnight strikes battered energy sites in the Zaporizhzhia, Sumy, Odesa, Zhytomyr, and Kirovohrad regions. 'It is important to be on the right side of history,' he said, asking officials to work as closely as possible with Washington and Musk's company.

Who Pulled the Plug

The cap first appeared on 14 October, when the Institute for the Study of War warned it could disrupt Ukrainian drone interception and intermediate-range strikes. The Wall Street Journal reported that Musk ordered the slowdown after discussions with President Donald Trump, a move that blindsided Kyiv.

Musk confirmed on 24 October that SpaceX had throttled the network. He wrote that using Starlink, a civilian service, 'for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed', and said the company had closed a 'loophole' the previous week. He drew a line between commercial Starlink and Starshield, the military version he says the US government controls. That distinction now sits at the dispute's centre.

Ukraine Calls the Claim Impossible

Kyiv rejected Musk's account. Serhii Beskrestnov, a defence technology adviser to Zelensky, said long-standing limits on the civilian system made offensive use impossible, calling it 'very strange' that Musk appeared unaware of them. Serhii Sternenko, a prominent drone fundraiser, said it was technically impossible to fly deep or medium-range strikes on commercial Starlink and that Ukraine broke no terms.

Zelensky himself has questioned whether Musk could have throttled the military-grade Starshield alone, telling PBS NewsHour on 2 November that Trump backed him in several meetings but said the decision rested largely with Musk.

Senators Want Answers

The dispute has moved to Washington. Senator Richard Blumenthal, the senior Democrat on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, opened an inquiry and set a 12 November deadline for SpaceX to brief investigators. Meanwhile, Zelensky reported the 100 mph cap had returned across the front line and occupied territory.

SpaceX told Axios that nothing had changed. Senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons then gave the company until 30 November to confirm preservation of records and explain who authorised restrictions and which remain active. Their demands put SpaceX under closer congressional scrutiny.

Ukraine confirmed service was restored on 24 October, following high-level US contacts. The unusual part is that control over the restrictions remains disputed. Weeks later, Ukrainian cities are again waiting to see whether a throttle setting will let the drones through.

excerpt: Nicholas Hoult's return to north London has intensified speculation about Bond 26, with reports linking him to the role as Robert Pattinson rises in betting markets.
headline: Is Nicholas Hoult Making a Move for 007? Actor's Family Relocates Back to UK as Robert Pattinson Emerges as Bond Favourite
html_content:
Nicholas Hoult has moved his family from California back to north London, adding intrigue to rumours that he could become the next James Bond. The actor is among five performers reportedly screen-tested for the role, while Robert Pattinson has emerged as a prominent contender in betting markets.

Hoult confirmed the relocation during an appearance on the Therapuss podcast on 12 November. He did not connect the move to Bond, but its timing has encouraged speculation as the search for Daniel Craig's successor gathers pace.

Hoult Reveals Family's Return to London

'We're in London now. Since we moved to London, I've been doing 20,000 steps a day,' Hoult said, explaining that much of the walking comes from taking his children to school. His wife, model Bryana Holly, and their children had previously been based primarily in California.

The actor recently confirmed he and Holly are parents of four, after his How to Rob a Bank co-star Pete Davidson referred to their twins during an interview.

Nicholas Hoult Reportedly Screen-Tested for 007

Reports published in November said Hoult had screen-tested for the next Bond film, joining Robert Pattinson, Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor among the reported candidates.

The auditions are understood to have taken place for director Denis Villeneuve, who is attached to direct the 26th official Bond film. Amazon MGM Studios has not confirmed the reported shortlist or commented on the casting speculation.

Hoult, 36, has experience in major franchises, having played Beast in the X-Men films and Lex Luthor in the Superman film. He was also reportedly a runner-up to Pattinson when the latter was cast as Batman in 2022.

The move to London has fuelled theories because Pinewood Studios, a longstanding production base for the Bond films, is around an hour's drive from north London. However, the proximity does not establish that Hoult has been selected or that the next film will shoot there.

Robert Pattinson Emerges as a Bond Favourite

Pattinson, 40, has reportedly screen-tested and attracted renewed attention from bookmakers. A 15 November update from one betting market showed him moving into odds-on favourite status, ahead of Turner and Lowden.

Those odds reflect betting activity rather than inside knowledge or a casting decision. Other bookmakers have continued to list Turner, O'Connor and Lowden among the leading names, illustrating how quickly the market can change.

Pattinson has worked with Villeneuve on Dune: Part Three, giving the pair an existing professional connection. He is known for The Batman, Twilight and the Harry Potter films.

Bond 26 Still Has No Confirmed Lead

Villeneuve is directing the next instalment, with Steven Knight, creator of Peaky Blinders, writing the screenplay. Producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman are overseeing the project for Amazon MGM Studios, which took creative control of the franchise in 2025.

Producer Pascal previously suggested an announcement before the end of 2026 was possible, but the studio has not committed to a date.

For now, Hoult's relocation is confirmed, while his involvement in the Bond race remains based on reports. Pattinson's rising betting profile adds another twist, but fans will have to wait for Amazon MGM to reveal who will inherit the iconic role.

excerpt: Dana White's Power Slap has sent a cease-and-desist letter to Lingerie Fighting Championships over its Power Spank parody event, which the rival promotion says is protected expression.
headline: Dana White's Power Slap Threatens Legal Action Over 'Power Spank' as Lingerie League Refuses to Back Down
html_content:
Dana White's Power Slap has threatened legal action against Lingerie Fighting Championships over its parody event, Power Spank, which features women spanking one another rather than striking opponents across the face. The dispute began after the rival promotion introduced the competition in Florida, but its organisers say they have no intention of dropping the name.

Power Slap's lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter demanding that LFC stop using Power Spank. LFC CEO Shaun Donnelly has rejected the demand, arguing that the event is protected parody under the First Amendment.

Power Spank Debuted in Florida

Power Spank made its debut on 11 October 2026, at a Lingerie Fighting Championships event in Clearwater, Florida. Eight women, including MMA fighters, exotic dancers and adult performers, competed in a contest that involved spanking opponents on the backside.

The winner, a contestant known as Bebe, received a $500 (£379) prize. The event was presented as a comedic alternative to Power Slap, the competition co-owned by UFC chief executive Dana White.

Power Slap, launched in 2023, sees competitors take turns delivering blows to an opponent's face. Participants cannot block or evade the strikes, a format criticised over the risk of concussion and other brain injuries.

LFC says Power Spank was conceived after one of its fighters was hospitalised following participation in a Power Slap match. Donnelly described the new event as offering the same energy and theatrics without the same risk of head impacts.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Power Slap (@powerslap)

Power Slap Sends Cease-and-Desist Letter

According to USA Today, attorneys representing Schiaffo LLC, the company behind Power Slap, sent LFC a cease-and-desist letter in late October. It demanded that the organisation stop using the Power Spank name.

LFC confirmed on 10 November that it received the letter. The company described Power Spank as an original property and a deliberate parody of Power Slap. It argued audiences would recognise the joke and would not believe the promotions were affiliated.

LFC said the parody would continue to open its US events while it reviewed its legal options.

LFC Refuses to Back Down

Donnelly said LFC respected Power Slap and its founders but would not abandon what it considers protected expression. He said the company was prepared to defend its position, even if the dispute reached the Supreme Court.

The First Amendment protects expressive activity in the United States, including parody, although that does not automatically settle every trademark dispute. Whether a particular name is legally protected can depend on the circumstances, including whether consumers could be confused about a connection between the organisations.

Power Slap has not publicly commented in detail. No formal lawsuit had been filed at the time of the latest reports, meaning the matter remains at the cease-and-desist stage rather than being decided by a court.

What Happens Next?

For now, LFC says Power Spank will remain part of its US events. The company has framed the competition as entertainment and a satirical response to slap fighting's safety concerns.

The disagreement could still be resolved without litigation, but neither side has announced a settlement. Until further action is taken, the central question is whether LFC can continue using a name that deliberately echoes a better-known combat sports brand.

The unusual dispute has placed two forms of spectacle entertainment in the spotlight, with trademark rights and parody at the centre of the clash.

excerpt: A party for two eighth-graders in McLean, Virginia, spread on Snapchat and pulled up to 300 teens to a $3.2 million home, leaving both parents facing criminal charges.
headline: Virginia Couple Arrested After Snapchat Leak Turns Sons' Small Party Into 300-Teen Chaos at $3.2M Mansion
html_content:
A Virginia couple face charges after a small party for their eighth-grade twin sons spread across Snapchat on 6 November and drew an estimated 100 to 300 teenagers to their McLean home, where police reported underage drinking and fireworks.

A Birthday Plan That Collapsed Into Mayhem

Officers reached the home shortly after 9pm following a wave of 911 calls from neighbours who reported between 100 and 300 young people swarming the property, which is valued at around $3.2 million (£2.4 million).

Body-worn camera footage captured teenagers scattering through dark streets and fireworks going off behind the house. 'It reeks like liquor,' one officer said as police described drunk teenagers walking around the area.

Moments later, a loud explosion erupted from the back garden, sending smoke into the night and officers running towards the noise. Some partygoers clambered down scaffolding to escape while others sprinted across neighbouring lawns.

Another blast followed, and the bodycam caught officers shouting at teenagers to go home as the crowd thinned.

How Snapchat Turned a Small Gathering Into a Mob

The event was meant only for the couple's eighth-grade sons and their classmates. According to the family's lawyer, the invitation spread on Snapchat, and older teenagers from a nearby high school arrived uninvited once the address began circulating. Officers reported seeing teenagers who appeared intoxicated.

Aubrey Vaughan, the boys' father, told FOX 5 DC the invitation barred alcohol and backpacks and that the family had no idea high schoolers would show up. He said the couple wanted their children at home where they could watch them, apologised to neighbours, and urged other parents to pay closer attention to apps like Snapchat.

The Charges Facing Lisa and Aubrey Vaughan

Lisa Vaughan, 45, and Aubrey Vaughan, 55, each face one count of contributing to the delinquency of a minor and one count of maintaining a common nuisance. The pair later turned themselves in after police contacted them, and both were released on $1,000 (£750) unsecured bonds.

An unsecured bond meant neither parent had to pay anything upfront to stay free before trial. The Vaughans have insisted they supervised the gathering and that no alcohol was permitted, with Lisa telling officers on camera that there had been none. Their lawyer has disputed the police account of the incident. Both are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

Why This Case Should Worry Every US Parent

Virginia law can hold adults criminally responsible for knowingly maintaining premises used for unlawful drinking. The charges against the Vaughans show how quickly a planned gathering can lead to legal scrutiny once an address escapes onto social media.

Fairfax County Police said the case 'serves as a reminder of the importance of safety and supervision' when minors gather. The department urged homeowners to monitor activities on their property, prevent underage drinking, and contact police when gatherings escalate. Police have not announced charges against the uninvited guests.

For families across the US, the warning is stark. One screenshot can turn a child's gathering into a police investigation, and even parents who say they tried to stop the chaos can find themselves answering to police.

excerpt: A Florida man has been arrested after police allegedly linked him to a peanut butter-smeared greeting card sent to a woman with a severe peanut allergy, amid an alleged divorce-related dispute.
headline: Post Office Kiosk Camera Catches Florida Man Buying Stamps to Mail Peanut Butter to Ex-Wife's Allergic Friend
html_content:
A 68-year-old Florida man has been arrested after a post office kiosk photograph allegedly linked him to a greeting card smeared with peanut butter and mailed to a woman with a severe peanut allergy.

Joseph Gerard Cancellare Jr. was taken into custody on 13 November by the Plantation Police Department. Cancellare faces an aggravated battery with a deadly weapon charge, alongside a separate charge of culpable negligence exposing another person to harm.

Cancellare was booked into a Broward County jail before his bond was set at $20,000 (£15,100), and he has since posted bond.

The Incident and the Victim's Reaction

The victim returned home from work on 14 August 2025 and noticed a blue envelope near her driveway, according to the arrest affidavit.

Upon opening the envelope, she discovered a greeting card bearing unfamiliar handwriting and smeared with a brown substance she immediately recognised as peanut butter. The woman, whose condition was described in police records as severely allergic to peanuts, dropped the mail and rushed inside to wash her hands.

She later told investigators that she developed hives on both arms and experienced a tingling sensation that lasted for approximately six hours following the exposure. Authorities confirmed that the victim's severe medical condition had been previously documented in both police and medical files.

Police noted that Cancellare had known the victim for at least 20 years through her close friendship with his former spouse, and she informed detectives that he was personally aware of the danger posed by peanuts because she routinely alerted restaurant staff to her allergy whenever she dined with the couple.

Kiosk Photograph and Stamp Trail

Investigators traced the August 2025 package back to Cancellare through two postage stamps affixed to the blue envelope, according to reports citing arrest records.

Although the envelope carried the fictitious name 'Goergina Sawals' and a false return address, detectives worked with the US Postal Service to track the postage. Authorities also determined the stamps were purchased on 8 August 2025 at a self-service kiosk in Davie using a Visa card belonging to Cancellare.

Investigators determined he drove to a post office outside his home city and wore sunglasses inside the facility. However, the kiosk camera captured a photograph of the buyer during the transaction.

Investigators showed the photograph to the victim and several people familiar with Cancellare, who identified him as the person pictured, according to the arrest affidavit.

Alleged Motive Stemming From Divorce

Investigators allege Cancellare knowingly sent the peanut butter-covered card despite being aware that exposure could cause the woman serious injury or death, according to the arrest affidavit. According to reports citing arrest documents, investigators believe the act was motivated by Cancellare's contentious divorce from the victim's best friend.

According to investigators, Cancellare largely blamed the woman for the breakdown of his marriage to her best friend. The pair had not spoken since July 2022, when they attended a meeting concerning the division of property during his divorce settlement.

Witnesses also told investigators Cancellare had made multiple remarks expressing a desire to harm individuals connected to the split, including the victim.

Cancellare has not been convicted of the charges, and the allegations against him have not been tested in court.

excerpt: EA has urged Madden NFL 27 players not to uninstall the game before GTA VI launches, using an in-game message to acknowledge Rockstar's reported 212GB pre-load requirement and tease a 17 November reveal.
headline: EA Begs Madden Players Not To Delete Game as GTA 6's 212GB Size Threatens Console Storage
html_content:
Electronic Arts has urged players not to uninstall Madden NFL 27 through an in-game message as Grand Theft Auto VI approaches, highlighting the storage demands of Rockstar's upcoming release.

Screenshots shared on X on 14 November show a notification headed 'Don't Delete!' It says a crew is assembling for a 'high-stakes run' and tells players to await a signal from an insider on 17 November. Its pink-and-purple artwork, featuring palm trees and a city skyline, resembles the visual style associated with Grand Theft Auto VI.

Rockstar says players need up to 212GB of available storage to pre-load the game. It is scheduled to launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on 19 November. EA has not named Rockstar's game in the notification, although its official Madden account previously referred to the 210GB requirement.

Holy desperate EA pic.twitter.com/toCNkFfaLm

— Zirksee🍽️ (@Zirksee) November 14, 2026

GTA VI Pre-Load Requires up to 212GB

Rockstar's support page says pre-loading began on 10 November, with up to 212GB of free space required. PlayStation's UK support page confirms the same requirement for PS5 users. The figure refers to the space needed for pre-loading, not a confirmed final installed size.

The requirement could force players with limited free storage to uninstall games or remove other data. This is particularly relevant to owners of consoles with extensive digital libraries who may need to make room before launch. Deleted games can be downloaded again later.

EA lists 50GB of storage space for the PC version of Madden NFL 27. The figure varies across platforms and with updates, so it should not be treated as the confirmed size of the console versions. It nevertheless illustrates why the football title could become one of the games players consider removing.

EA's Messages Tease a November Reveal

The in-game notification follows a post from the official Madden NFL account on X on 10 November. It read: 'Don't let 210GB get between you and Your League.' The post appeared to acknowledge the storage space players may need for Rockstar's upcoming release.

Don’t let 210GB get between you and Your League.

— Madden NFL 27 (@EAMaddenNFL) November 10, 2026

The newer message points to 17 November, two days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches, but does not identify what EA plans to reveal. Gaming publication Push Square suggested it could involve an update to Madden Ultimate Team, although EA has not confirmed this interpretation.

The reference to an insider and a 'high-stakes run,' alongside artwork resembling Rockstar's promotional style, reinforces the connection between the two games. The actual content of the planned reveal remains unclear.

Storage Pressure Puts Madden in the Spotlight

The timing highlights the competition for players' attention when a major release arrives. Madden NFL 27 includes Ultimate Team, a mode built around ongoing content and in-game purchases. Regular engagement is commercially important for publishers operating games with live-service features.

There is no evidence that EA expects players to abandon Madden permanently because of Rockstar's release. Its messages appear to use humour to acknowledge the storage competition while encouraging users to keep the football game installed.

EA's campaign has made the approaching release part of its own promotional messaging. Whether the 17 November teaser brings new Ultimate Team content or another announcement remains to be seen.

excerpt: Denny's has restored a plaque commemorating the San Jose restaurant where Jensen Huang and NVIDIA's co-founders discussed launching the technology company in 1993.
headline: Denny's Caves and Reinstates Jensen Huang's Plaque Just One Day After Scrubbing It Amid Scandal
html_content:
Denny's has reversed its decision to remove a commemorative plaque honouring former NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang from the California restaurant where the technology giant was conceived.

The reversal came just a day after the display disappeared amid controversy surrounding Huang's departure from NVIDIA and reports linking him to a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence.

Denny's Reverses Decision to Remove Huang Plaque

The plaque was removed from the Denny's restaurant at 2484 Berryessa Road in San Jose, California, on Thursday, 12 November. The move attracted attention because of the restaurant's longstanding association with Huang and NVIDIA, which he co-founded in 1993.

An employee confirmed that the plaque had been taken down the previous evening. However, Denny's headquarters subsequently announced that the tribute would be restored, maintaining that the restaurant's connection to the technology company deserved recognition.

Chief people officer Fasika Melaku told SFGATE on 14 November: 'We're reinstalling the plaque recognizing the conversations at Denny's that helped launch NVIDIA.'

The commemorative display, installed in September 2023, read: 'The booth that launched a $1 trillion company. Congrats NVIDIA! Who knew that an idea started here would change the world?'

The company explained that Huang had started his working life as a dishwasher at Denny's before returning years later with his co-founders to discuss the idea that eventually became NVIDIA.

How Huang's NVIDIA Story Began at Denny's

The restaurant's connection with Huang goes back more than three decades. He started working for Denny's at the age of 15 in Portland, Oregon, taking on duties as a dishwasher, busboy and waiter.

Huang later returned to Denny's in a very different capacity. In 1993, he and fellow engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem met at the San Jose Denny's to discuss their plans for a new technology company. NVIDIA was officially established on 5 April that year, initially focusing on graphics chips for computer gaming and 3D applications.

Huang returned to the restaurant in September 2023 for the plaque unveiling, which celebrated NVIDIA reaching a $1 trillion (£756 billion) market valuation. The occasion was attended by then-Denny's chief executive Kelli Valade.

Denny's also marked the milestone by launching a competition called the Trillion Dollar Incubator, offering a $25,000 (£18,900) prize for the winning business idea. In 2025, the chain introduced a limited-edition menu item called 'NVIDIA Breakfast Bytes', featuring pancakes and four sausage links inspired by Huang's reported breakfast preferences.

Huang's Departure Sparks Controversy Beyond NVIDIA

The plaque controversy unfolded during a turbulent period for NVIDIA. Reports surrounding Huang's alleged extramarital relationships and a woman suspected of having connections to Chinese intelligence raised questions about corporate governance and national security.

Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, while NVIDIA's board announced an investigation into reports that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

The allegations involving the woman, identified in reports as Alice Huang, have not been established as fact. NVIDIA's board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised.

The controversy also put NVIDIA's leadership structure under scrutiny after Huang's 33-year tenure. The company has become one of the world's most valuable businesses, driven largely by demand for its AI chips.

Denny's has not explained who ordered the plaque's removal or whether it was linked to the allegations. Its reversal allows the restaurant to preserve its historic ties to NVIDIA despite the controversy surrounding Huang.

excerpt: Mia Latter, previously known as 'Alice,' has identified herself and described an alleged sexual assault by Russell Brand when she was 16, while calling for changes to UK consent laws.
headline: Russell Brand Accuser Reveals Her Face and Identity for the First Time as She Details Alleged Sexual Assault at 16
html_content:
Mia Latter, the woman previously known only as 'Alice' in reports about Russell Brand, has revealed her identity for the first time and shared a harrowing account of the alleged sexual assault she says she suffered when she was just 16.

Now 37, Latter has waived her legal right to anonymity nearly two decades after she first met the comedian, who was 30 at the time. In an interview with The Sunday Times journalist Rosamund Urwin, she described how their relationship allegedly turned abusive and explained why she has decided to speak publicly following Brand's recent conviction and prison sentence.

Russell Brand Accuser Describes Alleged Rape at 16

Latter alleged that Brand orally raped her towards the end of their three-month relationship in 2006. Recalling the incident, she claimed he forced her against the headboard of his bed, leaving her unable to move.

'He ended up forcing me against the headboard [of the bed] and I couldn't move, and he orally raped me, and I was choking and crying,' she told The Sunday Times.

She said she tried to push him away but eventually had to hit him in the stomach to make him stop. Latter also recalled Brand allegedly telling her afterwards: 'I just wanted to see your mascara run.'

She had previously been identified as 'Alice' in a 2023 investigation by The Times, The Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches, which reported allegations from several women about Brand's behaviour.

How Mia Latter Met Russell Brand When She Was 16

Latter said she first encountered Brand while shopping in central London in 2006. The comedian, who was presenting MTV programmes at the time, approached her and asked for her telephone number.

They exchanged messages before going on a date and eventually returning to his apartment. Latter alleged that Brand knew her age but continued pursuing her.

She also claimed he asked her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends, although people around him knew about it. According to her account, Brand referred to her as 'the child' and sent cars to collect her while she was supposed to be attending school.

Her parents were reportedly distressed by the relationship and attempted to prevent her from seeing him.

Russell Brand's Response to the Allegations

Brand has consistently denied wrongdoing. When the allegations first emerged in 2023, he dismissed them as part of what he described as a campaign by the 'mainstream media' to silence him.

During an April appearance on The Megyn Kelly Show, Brand described his behaviour towards women as 'awful but lawful' and acknowledged that he had been 'exploitative' and had 'manipulated' consent.

Latter rejected that characterisation, arguing that consent obtained through manipulation cannot be considered freely given.

Why Brand's Accuser Has Waived Her Anonymity

Latter said her decision to reveal her identity is linked to her campaign for changes to UK age-of-consent laws. She is calling for a 'staggered' age of consent that would make sexual relationships between adults and 16- or 17-year-olds illegal while protecting relationships between teenagers close in age.

Under current UK law, the age of consent is 16, although additional legal protections apply to young people under 18 in certain circumstances.

Latter was interviewed by police, but her allegations were not included in Brand's recent criminal trial. She said she had been devastated by the decision and was subsequently asked to consider participating in a further trial.

excerpt: Susan Smith is due before a South Carolina parole board again on 19 November 2026. Her ex-husband David Smith plans to oppose her release over the 1994 killings of their sons.
headline: Susan Smith's Parole Bid: Ex-Husband David Smith Fears Running Into Woman Who Drowned Their Two Sons
html_content:
More than three decades after one of the most widely publicised criminal cases in the United States, Susan Smith is due to appear before a parole board once again. The South Carolina mother, convicted of killing her two young sons in 1994, is seeking release for a second time.

Her ex-husband, David Smith, says the thought of crossing paths with her still haunts him. The second parole hearing is set for Thursday, 19 November 2026, in Columbia. David has vowed to ask board members to keep her in prison.

Still Haunted by the 1994 Case

David told CNN that the idea of bumping into his former wife leaves him unsettled after more than three decades. He has not spoken to her since her conviction, and they are not expected to meet in person at the hearing.

He says she has never apologised to him, and he wants her to stay in prison for the rest of her life. 'For me it's still like yesterday,' he said. Susan has spent three decades in prison, but her ex-husband believes that is still too short a sentence for the killings.

The case drew national attention in the 1990s, after a nationwide search for two missing boys ended when Susan admitted responsibility for their deaths.

David Smith just arrived to Susan Smith’s parole hearing. He is her ex husband and the father of the boys she murdered. He wanted the death penalty and now 30 years later has to see her again as she asks the South Carolina parole board to free her. https://t.co/2WdqXjwQxM

— Brian Entin (@BrianEntin) November 20, 2024

What Happened to Michael and Alex Smith

Susan was convicted of killing three-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander by letting her car roll into John D. Long Lake in Union County. She initially told police that a carjacker had taken the boys, but she later confessed.

A jury spared her the death penalty and handed a life sentence with the possibility of parole after 30 years. She is currently held at Leath Correctional Institution near Greenwood.

Why Her First Parole Request Was Rejected

The South Carolina Board of Paroles and Pardons unanimously rejected her request in 2024, after she had served 30 years. Reports said the board considered the seriousness of the crime and her record of prison offences.

She appeared by video link, became emotional and said she would give anything to undo what she did. David attended that hearing and promised to return. 'I will be here every two years going forward,' he told the board.

She cried and begged to be set free. 30 years ago, she drowned her two little boys. Susan Smith: What she said to the parole board still makes people angry: "I know what I did was horrible," she said through tears. She said she would "give anything" to go back and change it. But this was not the first time America saw her cry. October 1994. South Carolina. Susan goes on live TV, crying. She says a Black man jumped into her car and drove away with her sons inside. Michael, 3. Alex, 14 months. For 9 days, the whole country searches. For the boys. And for a man who never existed. Her husband David stands next to her, begging for his sons to come home. But her story doesn't add up. The friend she says she visited that night wasn't even home. On a lie detector, she can't answer one question: "Do you know where your boys are?" November 3, 1994. She confesses. She strapped her sons into their car seats. Then she let the car roll into the lake. Why? The man she loved didn't want a woman with kids. She got life in prison. In 2024, after 30 years, she asked to go free. David was there. He said she never once showed him remorse. "She changed my life for the rest of my life that night." Parole denied. How do you cry for your children on TV, knowing exactly where they are?

— Cold Case Vault (@ColdCaseVaultX) November 13, 2026

Officials and Prosecutors Prepare To Oppose Release

Union County Sheriff's Office Chief Deputy Scott Coffer also plans to attend and oppose parole. He warned that a denial at one hearing does not guarantee the same result next time. Tommy Pope, the prosecutor from her original trial, also urged the board to deny parole during the 2024 proceedings.

Under South Carolina's parole system, Susan Smith becomes eligible for parole every two years until she is released or dies in custody. Her first request drew hundreds of public messages, with only a small number supporting the release.

Parole Board Decision Looms Again

The board is expected to consider the nature of the crimes, Susan's conduct behind bars and statements from the victims' family before deciding. In 2024, the ruling was issued on the day of the hearing.

For many Americans, the case remains one of the most notorious true crime stories of the 1990s. Whatever the outcome, David says his fight to keep her in prison will not stop.

For him, every hearing reopens a wound that three decades have not healed, and the result will be watched closely across the country.

excerpt: Sophie Weiss, an OnlyFans creator known as the 'Barnsley Basher', fears prosecution under new UK rules covering explicit pornographic images depicting strangulation or suffocation.
headline: OnlyFans Model and Martial Artist Fears Legal Trouble Over Sexy Jiu-Jitsu Content Under New 'Choking' Porn Law
html_content:
An OnlyFans creator who makes erotic Brazilian jiu-jitsu videos fears she could face criminal prosecution under Britain's new pornography laws, which outlaw the possession and publication of explicit images depicting strangulation or suffocation.

Sophie Weiss, known online as 'The Barnsley Basher', says she has already deleted a large amount of content and worries the legislation could seriously affect her income.

The 34-year-old martial artist argues that her videos feature consensual sporting techniques she is trained to perform, but the new rules have left her uncertain about what she can legally continue producing.

Weiss Fears New Choking Pornography Law

Weiss produces adult content featuring herself grappling with men and women, often wearing bikinis or athletic clothing. Her videos incorporate Brazilian jiu-jitsu techniques, including headlocks, chokeholds and submission moves.

Weiss maintains that her videos are consensual and that she understands how to perform the techniques safely. However, she fears the sexual nature of the material could bring it within the scope of the new legislation.

'I wrestle women in bikinis, we choke each other, use Brazilian jiu-jitsu moves on each other, it's all consensual. The government classes that as pornography even though we are dressed in bikinis. It is for arousal but at the end of the day men can get aroused by an armpit or a toenail, it's a bit stupid they are saying that.'

She also questioned the government's justification for introducing the restrictions, arguing that her content allows women to take control during physical encounters.

New Law Could Carry Five-Year Prison Sentence

The Crime and Policing Act 2026 introduced new offences covering the possession and publication of certain pornographic material, with the relevant provisions taking effect on 6 November in England and Wales.

Possessing pornographic images that explicitly and realistically depict strangulation or suffocation carries up to two years in prison, while publishing or distributing them can result in a five-year sentence.

However, not every depiction of choking is illegal. Whether material meets the legal definition of pornography and realistically depicts strangulation depends on the circumstances.

Weiss said she had already spent one or two weeks removing videos from various platforms and devices after learning about the restrictions.

'I can face five years in prison for distributing. I didn't think it was going to be real, when a newspaper article came out I thought, "oh it is real".'

She also expressed concern that even videos presented as sporting competitions could attract scrutiny if they featured chokeholds.

Considering Changing Content

The restrictions could force Weiss to reconsider the material she produces, particularly because grappling and submission techniques are central to her online business.

She believes her work boosted her confidence and gives women an opportunity to take control during physical encounters. She also argues that her videos provide companionship and emotional support for some male subscribers.

'It's been the best thing I've ever done in my life. It's a way for us women to take our power back. I never chose this sort of work, it chose me.'

Weiss plans to use alternative techniques, including takedowns, lifting and armlocks, but admitted the change could hurt audience interest, as submission moves attract many subscribers.

The law does not ban Brazilian jiu-jitsu, professional wrestling or legitimate sporting demonstrations, but leaves creators such as Weiss uncertain about the legal boundaries of pornographic choking content.

excerpt: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed is daring Donald Trump to brand Medicare for All as 'TrumpCare', betting the president's appetite for credit can pass single-payer coverage.
headline: Michigan Senator-Elect Abdul El-Sayed Offers Trump 'Trumpcare' Branding So He Can Enjoy Taking the Credit
html_content:
Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed this month dared President Donald Trump to brand universal healthcare 'TrumpCare', offering to let the president claim credit for Medicare for All if it guarantees every American coverage from cradle to grave.

The Deal on the Table

For a politician who built his career on Medicare for All, it is a striking offer. El-Sayed, a physician and former Detroit health director, told Mehdi Hasan on Zeteo's Mehdi Unfiltered on 6 November that he would hand Trump the naming rights outright. He offered to put Trump's name on it, framing single-payer coverage as a legacy achievement the president could own. He is fine with the label if the policy passes.

The pitch flips decades of partisan warfare on its head. Democrats have chased universal coverage since Harry Truman, and here a progressive senator-elect is willing to offer the credit to a Republican president, provided ordinary Americans stop going broke at the pharmacy counter.

A Gold Card With Trump's Signature

On 12 November, El-Sayed sharpened the appeal with a visual. He posted mock-ups of a gold 'TrumpCare' card carrying Trump's signature, resembling the administration's Trump Gold Card visa programme for wealthy foreigners.

In a message aimed straight at the president, he wrote, 'Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave'. The back of the card tells holders they could show it at any doctor, hospital, clinic, or pharmacy in the country.

Pressed by Cable News Network (CNN) anchor Kaitlan Collins on The Source on 10 November about whether the offer was a joke, El-Sayed did not blink. 'I'm absolutely serious,' he said, adding that he does not care what the plan is called so long as people are covered.

Why Your Wallet Is the Real Story

The appeal lands because the numbers are brutal. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reported US health spending of $15,474 (£11,700) per person in 2024, totalling $5.3 trillion (£4 trillion).

A 2024 Peterson-KFF analysis estimated that 20 million adults owed over $250 (£189) in medical debt at the end of 2021, totalling at least $220 billion (£167 billion). He has warned that looming Medicaid cuts could push private insurance premiums into double-digit increases.

El-Sayed, who co-wrote a 2021 book making the case for Medicare for All with physician Micah Johnson, argues that guaranteed coverage with no premium, co-pay, or deductible would end that drain. His bet is blunt. If Trump values the credit enough to support the policy, a deal becomes possible.

The Role Reversal Behind the Offer

El-Sayed won Michigan's open Senate seat on 3 November, defeating former Republican Representative Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim American elected to the chamber. He succeeds retiring Democrat Gary Peters and is not sworn in until January 2027.

No public response from Trump was identified as of 16 November, and 'TrumpCare' remains a branding pitch rather than an agreed policy. Republicans have long rejected single-payer plans as too costly, warning that government-run coverage would raise taxes and limit patient choice.

El-Sayed's wager is that offering Trump credit could help advance a policy Democrats have failed to pass for generations. If the president wants the name, the senator-elect says, the credit is his for the taking.

excerpt: The FDA has rejected Summit Therapeutics' ivonescimab lung cancer treatment, saying trial data did not sufficiently prove patients lived longer despite a 48% lower risk of progression or death.
headline: FDA Rejects Promising Lung Cancer Drug Despite 48% Reduction in Risk of Disease Progression or Death
html_content:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has rejected a lung cancer drug that cut the risk of disease progression or death by 48%. The decision, announced on Sunday 15 November 2026, has surprised patients, investors and cancer researchers.

The drug, called ivonescimab, is developed by the US firm Summit Therapeutics and Chinese partner Akeso. While the treatment significantly delayed disease progression, the FDA concluded that the available evidence did not show a statistically significant improvement in overall survival, a key benchmark for approval.

Why Regulators Rejected Ivonescimab

The FDA issued a complete response letter, which means the application cannot be approved in its current form. According to Summit Therapeutics, regulators concluded that slowing the cancer was not enough to support approval.

The agency said it wanted clear evidence that patients lived longer, known as overall survival. The late-stage trial did not deliver a statistically significant result on that measure. According to Summit, the FDA had previously warned the company about this requirement in May 2025.

What the 48% Figure Means for Lung Cancer Patients

That 48% result comes from the HARMONi study, in which patients were given either ivonescimab alongside chemotherapy or chemotherapy only. Participants had EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer that progressed after earlier targeted treatment.

According to Summit, patients receiving the combination treatment went a median of 6.8 months before their disease worsened, compared with 4.4 months for those receiving chemotherapy alone. That represents a median improvement of 2.4 months.

Treatment-related deaths were reported in 1.8% of patients receiving ivonescimab and 2.3% of those receiving chemotherapy alone.

Summit Cites New Survival Data

Summit has since submitted updated overall survival figures to the FDA. The company says the figures point to a lower risk of death among both Asian and Western patients.

A separate China-only trial, HARMONi-A, met its overall survival target, with a reported 26% lower risk of death, according to Fierce Pharma.

Why This Rejection Matters for Cancer Treatment Hopes

Ivonescimab is a so-called bispecific antibody, meaning one drug that blocks two targets, PD-1 and VEGF. Many industry figures believe this new class could one day challenge Merck's blockbuster immunotherapy Keytruda.

Summit acquired rights to the drug in the US, Canada, Europe and Japan in 2022 in a deal worth up to £3.79 billion ($5 billion). Shares in Akeso fell following the FDA decision.

The Survival Standard Driving FDA Decisions

Progression-free survival is measured by scans that show whether a tumour is growing. Overall survival asks a simpler and tougher question: does the treatment help patients live longer?

The FDA has made clear that it wants a clear answer to that second question, especially when a drug is added to existing chemotherapy. The ruling is likely to be studied closely by other drug developers.

What Happens Next for Patients and Summit

Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, so any new treatment option carries enormous weight for patients and families.

The rejection does not necessarily end ivonescimab's path towards approval in the US, but Summit will need to convince regulators that the drug extends lives. Patients should speak to their doctors about current treatment options.

For now, the decision underscores the FDA's position that delaying cancer progression may be encouraging, but proving that patients live longer remains critical to securing approval.

excerpt: American Doctor surgeon Rizk Abu Shaaira died in Khan Younis as the documentary heads to British screens on 20 November; learn what Israel and his colleagues say about the attack.
headline: Gaza Surgeon From 'American Doctor' Killed in Israeli Strike Just Days Before Film's UK Cinema Release
html_content:
Dr Rizk Abu Shaaira, a surgeon from the documentary American Doctor, died when an Israeli airstrike hit Gaza's Nasser Hospital on Thursday 12 November. The film opens in UK and Irish cinemas on Friday 20 November, eight days later. British audiences will see him operating on screen after his death.

Gaza's Health Ministry said the strike on the hospital's surgery building killed six people, including a 13-year-old boy, shortly after midnight. Abu Shaaira was working a night shift in the surgical ward. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it was targeting a Hamas brigade commander and is reviewing reports that medical workers died.

What Israel and Hospital Staff Say Happened

The IDF and the Shin Bet security service named their target as Muhammad Abu Ismail, whom they described as commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade. The two agencies said Hamas had 'established a presence within the hospital complex and used it as a command center.' The IDF said it used precision munitions and issued advance warnings. The military has not confirmed whether Abu Ismail died, and Hamas denied using the hospital for armed operations.

The hospital's head of surgery, Ayman Abu Obeid, gave a different account. He said staff had no warning and that no fighters were in the building. Goher Rahbour, a British volunteer surgeon, had operated beside Abu Shaaira at 8pm, hours before the strike. Gaza officials called it the seventh direct attack on Nasser, and the Health Ministry says more than 1,600 people have died since the US-backed October 2025 ceasefire.

How Dr Abu Shaaira Appears on Screen

Poh Si Teng's documentary follows three American doctors, Thaer Ahmad, Mark Perlmutter, and Feroze Sidhwa, as they volunteer in Gaza's hospitals. Abu Shaaira, 52, appears operating beside Sidhwa at Nasser. In one scene, the pair weigh whether to operate on a man with severe intestinal injuries. Abu Shaaira insists they try anyway, although the man later died. Sidhwa paid tribute to Abu Shaaira in a post on X, embedded below.

My colleague and friend Dr. Rizk Abu Shaaira was killed yesterday at work when Israel, backed by the US as always, bombed the surgical recovery room at Nasser Medical Complex. Two of his colleagues were badly injured, and many patients were hurt and killed. Dr. Rizk is featured… pic.twitter.com/mXK4ZZ6QSH

— Feroze Sidhwa (@FerozeSidhwa) November 12, 2026

Mohammed Odainy, a second surgeon from the film who also worked at Nasser, suffered critical injuries in the same strike, according to distributor Watermelon Pictures. Teng, the film's director, said on Thursday that Abu Shaaira's death was 'a painful reminder that the crisis documented in our film continues.' Watermelon Pictures, which released the film in the US, has called for accountability, and co-founder Hamza Ali said hospitals must never become military targets.

The Release, the Awards, and the Doctors' Reaction

Conic, the film's distributor in Britain and Ireland, is releasing it after a festival run that began at Sundance. The documentary also led the Cinema Eye Honors nominations, which organisers announced on the day of the strike. Teng received five nominations, more than any other individual.

The Intercept reported Ahmad was in a car with Sidhwa when news of the strike came through. 'I think Rizk is dead,' Ahmad told Sidhwa. Days earlier, an Israeli strike on al-Saraya field hospital in Gaza City seriously wounded another surgeon, Dr Khaled al-Shawa, while he treated patients.

excerpt: Kyle Brennan, son of former CIA director John Brennan, has been charged with transporting child pornography after investigators allegedly found illicit files linked to his account and phone.
headline: Ex-CIA Director John Brennan's Son Arrested on Child Pornography Transportation Charge After FBI Investigation
html_content:
The 40-year-old son of former CIA Director John Brennan has been arrested and charged with transporting child pornography following an investigation involving the FBI and local law enforcement.

The case began in 2024 after technology company Adobe flagged suspicious files uploaded to an online account allegedly linked to Kyle Brennan.

FBI Investigation Leads to Kyle Brennan's Arrest

Kyle Brennan was arrested on Friday, 13 November, and charged with one federal count of transportation of child pornography, according to a criminal complaint filed in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

The investigation began in April 2024, when Adobe submitted a report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) after identifying suspected child sexual abuse material uploaded through an account allegedly belonging to Brennan. A second report followed in June that year.

According to the complaint, three files were uploaded to the account on or around 7 April 2024. Investigators identified one file that appeared to be a manipulated image combining the face of a 12-year-old girl with the naked body of another minor.

Records obtained from internet provider Comcast reportedly linked the IP address used to upload the files to Brennan's address in Warrenton, Virginia. Apple records also connected the account to him, according to investigators.

The reports were subsequently passed to Warrenton police, who worked with the Fauquier County Sheriff's Office to investigate the allegations.

FBI Finds 88 Images on Seized iPhone

Local authorities searched Brennan's residence on 24 July 2024 and seized his iPhone during a traffic stop that day. However, the case was not referred to the FBI until October 2026, when federal investigators took over the inquiry.

A forensic examination of the device reportedly uncovered approximately 88 images depicting girls under the age of 18 engaged in sexually explicit conduct, according to prosecutors.

The criminal complaint described several of the images, including one allegedly showing a nude minor whose wrists and ankles were bound and whose mouth was gagged.

Authorities also identified the girl featured in the manipulated image and interviewed her parent, who confirmed her age.

The FBI's Washington field office is handling the federal investigation. Brennan faces a potential prison sentence of up to 20 years if convicted, with a mandatory minimum sentence of five years.

Son's Arrest Puts John Brennan in Spotlight

Kyle Brennan made his initial appearance in federal court in Alexandria, Virginia, on 13 November and remained in custody pending a detention hearing scheduled for 18 November. His attorney had not publicly commented on the allegations.

His arrest has attracted attention because of his father's political profile. John Brennan served as CIA director from 2013 to 2017 under former President Barack Obama and previously held several senior positions within the agency.

The former intelligence chief has since become a vocal critic of President Donald Trump. He is also facing a separate Justice Department investigation concerning his role in the intelligence community's 2017 assessment of Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election.

The inquiry examines whether officials improperly targeted Trump over alleged Russian ties. Brennan has denied wrongdoing and accused prosecutors of political targeting.

However, there is no evidence that the separate investigation involving John Brennan is connected to his son's criminal case.

Neither John Brennan nor his representatives had publicly commented on Kyle's arrest at the time of reporting. The allegations against Kyle remain unproven, and he is presumed innocent unless convicted in court.

excerpt: Former Miss Deutschland Tatjana Genrich won her professional boxing debut at 33, defeating Andrea Hajnal by unanimous decision after returning to the sport following a 17-year absence.
headline: Who Is Tatjana Genrich? Ex-Miss Germany Just Won Her Pro Boxing Debut at 33, Proving Bullies Chose Wrong
html_content:
Former beauty queen Tatjana Genrich has successfully traded the catwalk for the boxing ring, winning her professional debut at 33 after years away from competitive fighting.

The former Miss Deutschland winner's journey into boxing began as a teenager when she was bullied at school, prompting her to learn how to defend herself.

From Beauty Queen to Boxer

Genrich made her professional boxing debut on 14 November at the Messe Magdeburg in Germany, defeating Hungarian opponent Andrea Hajnal by unanimous decision after four rounds in the atomweight division.

The 33-year-old's victory came 17 years after her last amateur championship and marked a significant return to a sport she first pursued during her school years. Born in Russia, Genrich moved to Germany in 2003 and initially discovered boxing as a way to stand up to classmates who bullied her.

'At school I was often bullied and I wanted to find a way to defend myself. That's how it all started,' she previously told German newspaper Bild.

Her determination eventually translated into competitive success. Between 2007 and 2009, she won the Saxony-Anhalt state amateur flyweight championship three consecutive times before attending a sports school in Halle.

However, Genrich eventually shifted her attention towards modelling and beauty competitions, building a career that culminated in winning the Miss Deutschland title in 2022. She also competed internationally, earning recognition at the Miss Intercontinental pageant.

Tatjana Genrich Beats Andrea Hajnal in Professional Debut

Although she spent years away from competitive boxing, Genrich maintained her connection to the sport. She eventually reconnected with SES Boxing promoter Ulf Steinforth, whom she had known since her amateur days.

Genrich also sponsored ring-card models at the promotion's events, creating an opportunity to return to the ring.

'Since I sponsor the ring girls at his boxing events, he approached me one day and asked if I wouldn't like to get back in the ring. I finally agreed and am now about to make my professional debut,' she previously explained.

Her comeback required considerable preparation under experienced trainer Dirk Dzemski, who previously worked with former world champion Robert Stieglitz. Genrich trained five days a week while balancing her modelling commitments.

Against 19-year-old Hajnal, she secured a unanimous points victory in their four-round encounter. Her opponent suffered a bloody nose during the opening round following a strong punch, although Genrich later admitted that seeing the blood sometimes made it difficult for her to continue attacking.

Around 2,500 spectators watched the contest in Magdeburg. Following the victory, Genrich expressed excitement about finally beginning her professional career, although her trainer believes she needs another six months to reach her desired physical condition.

Ex-Miss Deutschland Sets Sights on Boxing World Title

Beyond boxing, Genrich runs Genrich Model Studios, a modelling agency in Magdeburg representing approximately 80 models. She helps prepare aspiring models for competitions, fashion shows and other events through posture, runway and choreography training.

Despite maintaining her business commitments, she has made it clear that boxing is more than a publicity exercise.

'I want to be a role model for young women and show them that you can be successful in both your career and sports,' she previously said.

Her long-term ambition is to become a world champion. For Genrich, however, winning her debut represents the first step towards fulfilling an ambition that began with wanting to stand up to bullies.

The former Miss Deutschland winner's journey into boxing began as a teenager when she was bullied at school, prompting her to learn how to defend herself. From Beauty Queen to Boxer Genrich made her professional boxing debut on 14 November at the Messe Magdeburg in Germany, defeating Hungarian opponent Andrea Hajnal by unanimous decision after four rounds in the atomweight division. The 33-year-old's victory came 17 years after her last amateur championship and marked a significant return to a sport she first pursued during her school years. Born in Russia, Genrich moved to Germany in 2003 and initially discovered boxing as a way to stand up to classmates who bullied her. 'At school I was often bullied and I wanted to find a way to defend myself. That's how it all started,' she previously told German newspaper Bild. Her determination eventually translated into competitive success. Between 2007 and 2009, she won the Saxony-Anhalt state amateur flyweight championship three consecutive times before attending a sports school in Halle. However, Genrich eventually shifted her attention towards modelling and beauty competitions, building a career that culminated in winning the Miss Deutschland title in 2022. She also competed internationally, earning recognition at the Miss Intercontinental pageant. Tatjana Genrich Beats Andrea Hajnal in Professional Debut Although she spent years away from competitive boxing, Genrich maintained her connection to the sport. She eventually reconnected with SES Boxing promoter Ulf Steinforth, whom she had known since her amateur days. Genrich also sponsored ring-card models at the promotion's events, creating an opportunity to return to the ring. 'Since I sponsor the ring girls at his boxing events, he approached me one day and asked if I wouldn't like to get back in the ring. I finally agreed and am now about to make my professional debut,' she previously explained. Her comeback required considerable preparation under experienced trainer Dirk Dzemski, who previously worked with former world champion Robert Stieglitz. Genrich trained five days a week while balancing her modelling commitments. Against 19-year-old Hajnal, she secured a unanimous points victory in their four-round encounter. Her opponent suffered a bloody nose during the opening round following a strong punch, although Genrich later admitted that seeing the blood sometimes made it difficult for her to continue attacking. She helps prepare aspiring models for competitions, fashion shows and other events through posture, runway and choreography training. Despite maintaining her business commitments, she has made it clear that boxing is more than a publicity exercise. 'I want to be a role model for young women and show them that you can be successful in both your career and sports,' she previously said. Her long-term ambition is to become a world champion. excerpt: The FAA is investigating excessive network traffic linked to facilities in Arkansas and Texas after a four-hour nationwide ground stop disrupted departures on 13 November
headline: FAA Investigates Routers in Two States After Nationwide Flight Halt as Manufacturer Says They 'Did Not Fail'
html_content:
The Federal Aviation Administration is investigating routers linked to two sites in Arkansas and Texas following a nationwide flight halt, as the equipment manufacturer pushes back against suggestions its devices malfunctioned.

The investigation follows the 13 November ground stop, which suspended departures for more than four hours after communications and radar feeds became unstable. Officials have identified excessive network traffic associated with facilities in El Dorado, Arkansas, and Amarillo, Texas, but have not established the root cause.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which owns router manufacturer Juniper Networks, says the equipment behaved as intended. Its response raises a central question for investigators: whether the problem involved the devices, their installation or how they were configured.

Manufacturer Says Equipment Worked as Configured

An HPE spokesperson defended the devices, saying: 'They did not fail.'

In another statement, the company said: 'Based on what we know today, the device functioned as it was configured to by the installer.'

That position does not establish who or what caused the disruption. It distinguishes a hardware malfunction from the possibility that equipment operating according to its settings contributed to wider network instability.

L3Harris, the FAA's network service provider, said it was assisting the investigation and took the nationwide ground stop's consequences for travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously. Equipment is undergoing examination at its laboratory in Florida.

Two Sites Generated Excessive Network Traffic

The FAA identified a radio communications facility in El Dorado and a radar installation in Amarillo as potential sources of the excessive data. According to the agency, its network experienced approximately 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. The traffic destabilised older equipment and affected communications and radar information.

L3Harris had been working at the Arkansas site, including installing a new router. Blocking the two locations stabilised the network, the FAA said. Broadcasting functionality on new routers was also disabled as a precaution.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the Arkansas work involved replacing an ageing copper connection with fibre. When that router was activated, equipment in Texas also began flooding the system, he said.

The Amarillo installation had been replaced roughly three weeks earlier. Why it began generating problematic traffic during the Arkansas work remains part of the investigation.

Nationwide Ground Stop Lasted More Than Four Hours

The FAA issued the ground stop at 3:54pm Eastern Time on Friday, 13 November, and lifted it at 8:15pm. Aircraft already airborne could continue flying, while departing passengers faced delays and uncertainty. Officials said they waited for the network to stabilise before allowing departures to resume.

The agency subsequently said the disruption was not a complete loss of communications. Some radio frequencies and radar feeds remained reliable, enabling controllers to communicate with and track aircraft.

The FAA said every aircraft landed safely and that established safety procedures remained in operation throughout the disruption.

Investigators Have Not Assigned Responsibility

Duffy said FAA personnel were participating in the equipment review and that the FBI had offered assistance. Officials had no indication of a foreign cyberattack, he said, while leaving open the possibility of following other evidence. He also cautioned against announcing a cause before investigators were certain of their findings.

Restoring the network resolved the immediate operational problem. Establishing why routine maintenance triggered widespread instability, and what changes could prevent a recurrence, remains unfinished work.
