excerpt: Police are seeking two men after four live chickens were allegedly released inside a Hadley convenience store in a filmed prank. The birds were unharmed and taken to an animal rescue facility.
headline: Two Men Wanted After Dumping Four Live Chickens on Store Counter While Filming Late-Night Prank
html_content:
Police in Massachusetts are searching for two men after a late-night stunt involving four live chickens left a convenience store employee facing an unexpected encounter in the early hours of Monday, 16 November.

The incident happened shortly before 2am at a Cumberland Farms convenience store on Russell Street in Hadley, western Massachusetts. Officers were called after an employee reported that several live chickens had been thrown at him inside the premises.

According to the Hadley Police Department, investigators reviewed surveillance footage obtained with the help of store management. The video showed two men, both believed to be in their early 20s, entering the shop, with one carrying a large black tote while the other recorded the encounter on his mobile phone.

After a brief interaction with the employee, the man carrying the bag allegedly emptied its contents onto the counter, releasing four live chickens in front of the clerk.

Police later shared images showing three birds on the counter near the cash register, with the fourth on the floor. Although the incident is believed to have been a prank, authorities have not established what prompted the men to carry out the stunt or where they obtained the animals.

Police Suspect Chickens Were Taken Locally as Animal Rescue Steps In

The investigation has since expanded to establish the origin of the chickens and locate their rightful owner. Authorities suspect the birds may have been taken from somewhere in the local area before being brought into the shop.

'Although the incident is believed to be a prank, we are attempting to learn the origin of chickens so that they may be returned to their rightful owner,' the Hadley Police Department said in a public statement.

There was some positive news for the animals, as officers confirmed that none of the four chickens appeared to have been injured. They were subsequently transferred to an animal rescue facility in Colrain, Massachusetts, where they could receive care while investigators worked to establish their ownership.

Police have appealed to residents for information that could help identify the two men and determine where the chickens came from. The department has also warned that the individuals could face criminal charges relating to 'the treatment and the taking of the chickens'.

No arrests or formal charges against the unidentified men had been announced in the latest available reports as of 17 November.

Anyone with information about the incident or the animals' ownership has been asked to contact the Hadley Police Department at 413-584-0883.

Filmed Prank Could Have Legal Consequences Beyond a Practical Joke

Although the men filmed the incident themselves, the store's surveillance footage has helped investigators establish what happened inside the shop. Police have not confirmed whether the second man's mobile phone recording has been recovered or circulated online.

The incident also raises concerns about animal welfare during social media pranks. Deliberately throwing or mishandling live animals can attract criminal charges, particularly if they are stolen, injured or subjected to unnecessary suffering.

Massachusetts law allows penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for certain animal cruelty offences. However, police have yet to announce specific charges in this case.

excerpt: John Jackson, 53, was arrested in Nashville after reportedly asking police officers for a ride and undergoing an identity check that revealed an outstanding Kentucky warrant.
headline: Kentucky Fugitive Busted in Nashville After Allegedly Asking Police for a Ride
html_content:
A Kentucky fugitive's attempt to secure a lift from police officers reportedly ended with his arrest after a routine identity check revealed an outstanding warrant.

John Jackson, 53, was taken into custody on Sunday, 15 November, after approaching Metropolitan Nashville Police Department (MNPD) officers who were conducting a traffic stop in Nashville, Tennessee.

According to an arrest affidavit cited in reports, Jackson allegedly asked the officers for a ride. Rather than arranging transportation, however, they checked his personal information and discovered that he was wanted in Kentucky.

'A query of his information showed he had an outstanding warrant out of Kentucky,' the affidavit stated. 'Officers confirmed the warrant via the records division.'

Following confirmation of the warrant, officers arrested Jackson on the fugitive warrant and transported him to Davidson County Jail. The circumstances surrounding his request for assistance, including where he intended to go, have not been fully disclosed.

The incident highlights how routine identity checks can lead to the discovery of outstanding arrest warrants, even when an individual is not initially approached by police as part of a fugitive investigation.

Jackson Faces $75,000 Bond and Extradition to Kentucky

Jackson's arrest was followed by the start of proceedings to return him to the state where the outstanding warrant originated.

His bond was reportedly set at $75,000 (£56,700), while arrangements were expected to be made for his extradition to Jefferson County, Kentucky.

He was scheduled to appear in court in downtown Nashville on Tuesday, 17 November. However, details of the underlying Kentucky case, including the original allegations and the circumstances that led to the warrant, have not been established in the initial reports.

Extradition is the legal process through which a person arrested in one state is transferred to another jurisdiction to face outstanding criminal proceedings. Tennessee and Kentucky are both parties to interstate extradition procedures, which allow authorities to coordinate the return of individuals wanted elsewhere in the United States.

Jackson's arrest does not establish guilt in the underlying Kentucky case.

Similar Fugitive Arrests After Unexpected Encounters With Police

Jackson's unusual encounter is not the first reported instance of a wanted individual inadvertently approaching law enforcement and ending up in custody.

In July 2017, Jansen Simon, 30, was arrested in Raceland, Louisiana, after flagging down a deputy to request a ride. Simon had reportedly been wanted for four years over an alleged 2013 bar fight in which he was accused of striking another man in the head with a hammer.

The Lafourche Parish deputy was travelling in a marked patrol vehicle when Simon approached him along Highway 182. After checking his identity, the officer discovered an outstanding arrest warrant connected to the alleged assault, as well as two additional warrants for contempt of court.

'It's not clear whether he knew he was flagging down a deputy,' Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office spokesman Brennan Matherne said at the time.

According to an arrest affidavit cited in reports, Jackson allegedly asked the officers for a ride. Rather than arranging transportation, however, they checked his personal information and discovered that he was wanted in Kentucky. 'A query of his information showed he had an outstanding warrant out of Kentucky,' the affidavit stated. 'Officers confirmed the warrant via the records division.' Following confirmation of the warrant, officers arrested Jackson on the fugitive warrant and transported him to Davidson County Jail. The circumstances surrounding his request for assistance, including where he intended to go, have not been fully disclosed. excerpt: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin suggested AI might explain recent US technology outages, but cited no evidence linking it to the incidents and relayed CISA's separate assessment.
headline: Markwayne Mullin Cites 'Guy That's Very Smart With Tech' on AI Theory After US Banks and Flights Are Disrupted
html_content:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin suggested on Monday, 16 November 2026, that artificial intelligence could be behind recent technology outages across the United States, citing an unnamed industry contact during an interview with Fox News host Sean Hannity.

Earlier that day, customers of several major US banks reported difficulties accessing online banking services and processing transactions. The disruption followed a nationwide flight ground stop on Friday and an outage affecting Microsoft Outlook on Thursday.

US transportation officials linked Friday's ground stop to problems during an upgrade of the FAA's ageing communications network, rather than AI. Microsoft stated that Thursday's outage was 'not related to cyber' or artificial intelligence agents.

How Markwayne Mullin Explained the AI Theory

Mullin described approaching the technology industry for an explanation after consulting CISA. One contact suggested that programs capable of writing code and fixing themselves could overwhelm systems unable to accommodate the technology's speed.

The secretary referred to 'SI', meaning super intelligence. His account described a process in which software repairs could trigger further changes elsewhere, comparing it with alterations to a house.

'When you change one thing in a house, everything else starts changing. That's a ripple effect.'

Mullin continued, 'And it causes the systems to be overrun that weren't designed to run as fast as the SI technology is today.'

His account did not identify a particular program or establish that such technology had caused any of the disruptions.

Mullin Relays CISA's Assessment

Hannity framed his question around public concern, referring to five consecutive issues and suggesting that some people were beginning to panic, particularly over banking. He sought reassurance for Americans affected by the outages.

Mullin told Hannity, 'I don't always believe in coincidences until I'm proven wrong.' He described the Department of Homeland Security's responsibilities across several areas, stating, 'We look at everything from sea, air, fiber, cyber, and land.'

He then outlined an assessment from CISA that treated the incidents separately.

He recounted its response as 'Sir, we're not seeing any traffic that would make us think that this is a cyber attack. They're all individually unrelated.'

On the AI theory, Mullin stated, 'And that kind of makes sense to me, because I can tell you with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyber attack.'

He also cited the absence of anyone claiming responsibility and described officials following traffic through systems. 'We're seeing the footprints going in. We're seeing the footprints go out.'

He did not explain how that percentage had been calculated. His account of CISA's assessment concerned whether the outages were connected or indicated an attack. It did not establish artificial intelligence as their cause.

The Tech Contact Mullin Would Not Name

Mullin described the person behind the alternative explanation as 'one guy that's very smart with tech'. The contact had requested that his name remain undisclosed, the secretary explained.

He explicitly ruled out Elon Musk, telling Hannity, 'No, it's not Elon, so let me just put that out.'

Although Mullin described the conversation as a briefing, he did not identify the contact's company or position.

Mullin dated the conversation to earlier that day and placed the briefing about three hours before the interview.

excerpt: Arion Kurtaj has pleaded guilty to cybercrime offences involving Rockstar Games, Uber, Revolut and BT/EE, including the theft of 90 GTA 6 gameplay videos.
headline: GTA 6 Hacker's Guilty Plea Reveals How He Breached Rockstar With Basic Hotel Gear
html_content:
The hacker responsible for leaking 90 Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay videos has pleaded guilty to cybercrime offences, revealing how ordinary hotel equipment helped him continue attacking major companies despite being subject to bail restrictions.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, admitted offences involving Rockstar Games, Uber, Revolut and BT/EE at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, 16 November 2026. His guilty plea came three days before GTA 6's scheduled release on 19 November.

How Hotel Equipment Helped the GTA 6 Hacker

The Crown Prosecution Service revealed that Kurtaj continued his activities after being moved to a hotel for his own protection in September 2022.

Already facing charges relating to earlier cyberattacks, he breached his bail conditions and used a mobile phone, the hotel's television Wi-Fi connection and a Fire Stick to target additional companies.

The equipment was relatively ordinary, but prosecutors emphasised that Kurtaj employed sophisticated hacking techniques. His actions demonstrated that restrictions on conventional computers did not necessarily prevent someone with sufficient technical knowledge from accessing corporate systems.

Among his targets was Rockstar Games, where he obtained 90 videos showing unfinished gameplay from the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI.

Kurtaj subsequently published the material online using the pseudonym TeaPotUberHacker and threatened to release the game's source code. The incident exposed confidential development footage years before Rockstar's planned release.

Rockstar Was Not His Only Target

The investigation revealed that Kurtaj's activities extended beyond the gaming industry.

Between August and November 2021, he accessed BT/EE servers and data files, contributing to unauthorised SIM swaps affecting customers. Such attacks can allow criminals to take control of telephone numbers, potentially exposing personal communications and accounts protected by text-message authentication.

After his relocation to the hotel, Kurtaj also targeted financial technology company Revolut, compromising information belonging to thousands of customers.

In a separate attack against Uber, he stole sensitive information, deleted internal data and accounts, and sent an inappropriate image to employees.

Prosecutors estimated that the Uber incident alone generated costs exceeding $2.8 million, approximately £2.1 million. The wider campaign demonstrated how attacks against different organisations could expose commercially sensitive information and disrupt everyday services.

Prosecutors Reveal How Investigators Identified Kurtaj

City of London Police led the investigation, supported by US law enforcement partners and prosecutors from the Complex Casework Unit.

Despite Kurtaj's use of multiple online identities, investigators reconstructed his activities through digital evidence. The Crown Prosecution Service said examinations of devices established timelines connecting his identity to particular locations and offences.

Specialist Prosecutor Robert Hutchinson described the investigation as exceptionally complex and challenging. He said Kurtaj continued targeting organisations even after being charged with serious offences, demonstrating persistent disregard for the consequences.

Kurtaj also admitted possessing an unauthorised mobile phone in prison in March 2026, which he used to send a mocking message to emergency services. He is scheduled to be sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court on 23 November.

The case highlights a broader cybersecurity concern: sophisticated attacks do not necessarily require expensive or specialised equipment.

For Rockstar, the guilty plea closes an important chapter in the investigation, although the exposure of confidential GTA 6 footage illustrates the lasting consequences of compromised corporate systems.

excerpt: Australian motorcycle racer Tayla Relph says an OnlyFans partnership has helped her continue competing after the costs of world championship racing pushed her to consider retirement.
headline: Motorcycle Racer Says OnlyFans Saved Her Career After Revealing She Pays £130,000 a Year To Race
html_content:
Australian motorcycle racer Tayla Relph says an OnlyFans deal has helped save her professional career after revealing that competing in the FIM Women's Circuit Racing World Championship costs more than A$250,000 (£130,000 or $169,400) a year.

The 29-year-old receives no payment simply for taking her place on the grid, leaving her to cover motorcycles, components, equipment, race entries, travel and training. A crash during a race weekend can add more than A$100,000 (£50,000 or $67,700) to the budget, she told the Brisbane Times.

After relying on crowdfunding for her first two world championship seasons, Relph considered quitting at the end of 2025. She subsequently secured backing from OnlyFans, which has become her primary fundraising channel for the 2026 campaign. She has not revealed how much she earns through the arrangement.

OnlyFans Deal Helps Relph Continue Racing

Relph announced the partnership in January 2026, becoming the first Australian two-wheel motorsport athlete to be sponsored by the platform, according to Just Bikes. Her account was announced as free to subscribe to, with selected premium posts available behind a paywall.

The planned material included onboard footage, race preparation, telemetry, bike set-up discussions and monthly livestreams. The announcement described the content as PG-rated and focused on her professional life.

In an interview published by the Brisbane Times, Relph said her content also included track maps, online rider coaching and photographs of herself training in a bikini. She said contractual terms prevented her from disclosing the precise financial details of the arrangement.

She added that the income had changed how she could manage her expenses during the racing season.

Rising Costs Put Pressure on Athletes

Relph's experience reflects the financial strain facing athletes in sports with limited commercial backing. The Australian Sports Foundation's 2023 'Running on Empty' study found that 46 per cent of elite Australian athletes aged over 18 earned less than A$23,000 (£12,000 or $15,400) a year from all sources.

The study surveyed 2,304 athletes across more than 60 sports, highlighting the financial difficulties competitors can face while trying to sustain their careers. For athletes who receive little or no payment for competing, outside funding can be essential to covering the costs of training and participation.

OnlyFans has expanded its presence in sport, with athletes from mountain biking, snowboarding, skateboarding, fencing and cliff diving using the platform. A spokesperson told Front Office Sports in May that about 285 professional athletes were on the service, including sponsored competitors and those who joined independently.

OnlyFans Content Raises Sponsorship Questions

OnlyFans is widely associated with adult material, but athletes use the platform for different types of content. Relph's January announcement said her account would focus on her life as a professional racer and offer PG-rated material.

Relph has said she is comfortable monetising photographs of her athletic physique, adding that she had worked hard to build her body. 'If it allows me to race, then it's worth it,' she said.

The platform's reputation can create challenges for athletes seeking conventional commercial partners. Front Office Sports has reported that its association with adult content can complicate relationships with traditional sponsors, even when an athlete's own posts are non-explicit.

The arrangement has provided another way to meet the costs of competing at world championship level. After considering retirement because of the financial demands, Relph has been able to continue her racing campaign with support from a platform that also gives her a direct way to reach paying subscribers.

excerpt: John Summit criticised the Grammys after missing out on a nomination as a fatal Florida crash involving a reported tour bus linked to his crew occurred the same morning.
headline: John Summit Goes Viral Ranting About the Grammys Just as His Crew's Tour Bus Gets Wrecked in a Fatal Crash
html_content:
American DJ John Summit found himself at the centre of two major developments on Monday, 16 November 2026, after publicly attacking the Grammy Awards around the time of a fatal road accident involving a tour bus reportedly carrying members of his production crew.

Florida Highway Patrol troopers responded to the collision in Marion County at approximately 8:58am local time. A 40-year-old motorist died after his Toyota sedan struck the stationary bus, while nine passengers and the bus driver escaped without injuries.

John Summit's Grammy Rant Sparks Backlash

Summit criticised the Recording Academy on X, expressing frustration after failing to secure a nomination for the 2027 Grammy Awards.

The electronic dance music producer announced that he would stop submitting his work for consideration unless the organisation changed its approach to dance music.

'Never submitting to the Grammys again unless shit changes,' he wrote, calling the awards process a joke.

Summit argued that established electronic music performers were being overlooked in favour of mainstream pop artists competing in dance categories.

He later clarified that his criticism concerned genre classifications rather than the musical abilities of nominated performers.

His comments prompted reactions from fellow musicians and fans, including Charli XCX, who responded dismissively to his complaints.

The disagreement highlighted continuing tensions over how electronic dance music is represented at major industry awards.

Fatal Florida Crash Involves Summit's Tour Crew

On the same morning, Florida Highway Patrol officers responded to a collision involving a musician's tour bus near Ocala.

Investigators said the bus was stopped at the intersection of Southwest Highway 484 and 20th Avenue Road when an eastbound Toyota sedan left the roadway and struck its front.

The sedan's driver, a 40-year-old Ocala resident, was transported to hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Authorities reported that the motorist was not wearing a seatbelt when the collision occurred.

The bus driver, identified as a 64-year-old Louisiana resident, was wearing a seatbelt. He and the nine passengers escaped injury.

Reports linked the vehicle to Summit's touring operation, although initial police statements did not independently establish the passengers' professional affiliations.

There was no indication that Summit himself was travelling aboard the bus.

Investigators have not announced a final determination regarding the circumstances of the collision.

John Summit's tour bus is involved in a fatal crash in Florida, TMZ reports. pic.twitter.com/Rn9JpgVBUd

— Pop Crave (@PopCrave) November 16, 2026

Will John Summit's Miami Concerts Go Ahead?

The bus was reportedly travelling towards Miami, where Summit is scheduled to perform at Kaseya Center on 20 and 21 November.

A replacement vehicle reportedly collected the crew following the accident, allowing them to continue their journey. However, the collision raised questions about whether the incident would affect preparations for the forthcoming performances.

The venue's official event calendar continued to list both performances, with no confirmed cancellation or postponement announced in the initial reports.

The scheduled concerts place additional attention on the touring operation, particularly as the production team prepares for two consecutive performances following the fatal incident. Summit's Grammy criticism and the fatal accident occurred on the same morning.

The investigation remains ongoing, with attention now focused on establishing the circumstances surrounding the motorist's death while Summit's touring schedule continues.

excerpt: Media Nov Records removed Samantha Shokin's YouTube recording of the public-domain Bulgarian folk song 'Bre Petrunko'. The claim was later withdrawn.
headline: AI Music Company Running 500 YouTube Channels Gets a Real Musician's Original Song Taken Down Over Copyright Claim
html_content:
Musician Samantha Shokin's recording of the public-domain Bulgarian folk song 'Bre Petrunko' was removed from YouTube following a copyright complaint from Media Nov Records, a music distribution company that says it operates 500 YouTube channels.

An investigation by 404 Media linked the company to channels featuring AI-generated music and art assets. Shokin submitted two unsuccessful counter-notifications before the company withdrew its complaint following media enquiries.

How a Folk Song Sparked a Copyright Dispute

Shokin recorded a 50-second rendition of the Bulgarian folk song 'Bre Petrunko' during the pandemic and uploaded it to SoundCloud. Two years later, she posted the recording on YouTube, where it accumulated approximately 125,000 views over four years.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by 404 Media (@404mediaco)


Last summer, she discovered that DJs and electronic music producers had been sampling her voice without her knowledge. One track featuring her vocals had attracted more than four million views.

'The first thing that comes to mind is, "Oh my god, someone stole my voice and didn't credit me,"' Shokin told 404 Media. She eventually traced the samples to Loopmasters, which had included her recording in its 'Folk Legends' collection.

After she contacted the distributor, the company apologised and arranged royalties for her. However, another copyright dispute soon emerged.

YouTube Rejects Musician's Appeals

Last month, Shokin discovered that YouTube had removed her original recording following a copyright complaint from Media Nov Records. Despite possessing the original audio files and evidence of her earlier publication, she struggled to reverse the decision.

YouTube declined to process two counter-notifications, saying it could not determine whether she had valid grounds to dispute the takedown. She also attempted to contact Media Nov Records directly, without success. According to 404 Media, corporate records showed that the Ireland-registered company was established just over a year earlier, with shareholders listing addresses in Turkey.

The outlet identified various YouTube channels managed by Media Nov Records, each featuring hundreds of videos. Many uploads included AI-generated art and music, with some tracks appearing across multiple channels.

The content largely consisted of looping electronic beats, resembling the lo-fi music commonly found on streaming platforms. The company told the outlet it operates 500 YouTube channels and collaborates with 'various artists, content creators, and music partners.'

Company Withdraws Claim After Media Questions

Following enquiries from 404 Media, Media Nov Records contacted Shokin requesting evidence that she owned the recording. The company disputed Shokin's ownership claim, saying that 'recording your own cover or performance does not automatically establish ownership of the underlying composition or arrangement. Likewise, rights in the underlying musical work do not automatically establish ownership of your particular recording.'

Copyright lawyer Alfred Steiner questioned the dispute. 'If it's her voice and her playing instruments, what could she possibly be infringing if it's a folk song from the 19th century?' he said.

Shortly afterwards, Media Nov Records announced it would withdraw its takedown request. However, the company stressed that 'this decision does not constitute a waiver of any rights we may hold' and reiterated, 'We intend to initiate appropriate legal proceedings regarding the underlying copyright dispute.'

YouTube subsequently restored Shokin's video, confirming that the claimant had withdrawn its complaint. Although relieved, Shokin criticised the difficulty of challenging the removal without outside intervention. 'The whole system is broken. It feels like a broken system,' she said.

Two years later, she posted the recording on YouTube, where it accumulated approximately 125,000 views over four years. View this post on Instagram A post shared by 404 Media (@404mediaco) Last summer, she discovered that DJs and electronic music producers had been sampling her voice without her knowledge. One track featuring her vocals had attracted more than four million views. 'The first thing that comes to mind is, "Oh my god, someone stole my voice and didn't credit me,"' Shokin told 404 Media. She eventually traced the samples to Loopmasters, which had included her recording in its 'Folk Legends' collection. After she contacted the distributor, the company apologised and arranged royalties for her. However, another copyright dispute soon emerged. YouTube Rejects Musician's Appeals Last month, Shokin discovered that YouTube had removed her original recording following a copyright complaint from Media Nov Records. Despite possessing the original audio files and evidence of her earlier publication, she struggled to reverse the decision. YouTube declined to process two counter-notifications, saying it could not determine whether she had valid grounds to dispute the takedown. She also attempted to contact Media Nov Records directly, without success. According to 404 Media, corporate records showed that the Ireland-registered company was established just over a year earlier, with shareholders listing addresses in Turkey. The outlet identified various YouTube channels managed by Media Nov Records, each featuring hundreds of videos. Many uploads included AI-generated art and music, with some tracks appearing across multiple channels. The content largely consisted of looping electronic beats, resembling the lo-fi music commonly found on streaming platforms. The company told the outlet it operates 500 YouTube channels and collaborates with 'various artists, content creators, and music partners.' Company Withdraws Claim After Media Questions Following enquiries from 404 Media, Media Nov Records contacted Shokin requesting evidence that she owned the recording. The company disputed Shokin's ownership claim, saying that 'recording your own cover or performance does not automatically establish ownership of the underlying composition or arrangement. Likewise, rights in the underlying musical work do not automatically establish ownership of your particular recording.' Copyright lawyer Alfred Steiner questioned the dispute. 'If it's her voice and her playing instruments, what could she possibly be infringing if it's a folk song from the 19th century?' he said. Shortly afterwards, Media Nov Records announced it would withdraw its takedown request. However, the company stressed that 'this decision does not constitute a waiver of any rights we may hold' and reiterated, 'We intend to initiate appropriate legal proceedings regarding the underlying copyright dispute.' YouTube subsequently restored Shokin's video, confirming that the claimant had withdrawn its complaint. Although relieved, Shokin criticised the difficulty of challenging the removal without outside intervention. 'The whole system is broken. It feels like a broken system,' she said.

excerpt: More than 185,000 people have signed a petition calling for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, as an independent investigation examines allegations surrounding his sudden resignation.
headline: Tech Billionaires Suspect Possible Plot Behind Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit as 185,000 Demand His Return
html_content:
Silicon Valley figures are increasingly questioning the circumstances surrounding Jensen Huang's sudden exit from Nvidia. While the company has moved ahead with interim leadership, a growing campaign is calling for the return of the chipmaker's co-founder.

More than 185,000 people have now signed a petition urging Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang. Despite that support, Reuters reports that the board is not planning to reverse course after the longtime chief executive's resignation on 12 November.

Nvidia Left Without Its Longtime Leader

Nvidia announced on 12 November that Huang had stepped down as chief executive, president and board member with immediate effect. Chief financial officer Colette Kress took over as interim chief executive, while Harvey Jones was appointed the company's first board chair.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and helped build it into a central player in the global AI boom. Reuters reported Nvidia shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading following the announcement.

The company did not publicly provide a reason for Huang's departure. However, it followed reports about alleged extramarital affairs, including one involving Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has been the subject of scrutiny over suspected links to Chinese intelligence. She has denied the allegations, and Beijing has rejected claims she is a spy. Reuters reported that US authorities are examining allegations concerning her connections.

Nvidia's board has also launched an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding the allegations and their potential implications for the company.

Tech Leaders Cast Doubt on Espionage Claims

A theory circulating among some technology executives suggests the controversy surrounding Huang may have been engineered. Venture capitalist David Sacks argued that recent reporting had weakened the case for describing Alice Huang as a spy. Sacks said the espionage allegation was a key factor in Huang's departure.

Replit chief executive Amjad Masad called the timing suspicious, saying anyone wanting tighter control of AI development could benefit from Huang's removal. Neither executive has provided evidence that a plot occurred.

High-Profile Backers Rally Behind Huang

The online petition has gathered around 185,000 signatures, including Elon Musk, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Y Combinator chief Garry Tan and Shopify chief executive Tobias Lütke. The letter calls on Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang while an independent review establishes the facts. Supporters argue suspicion alone should not end his leadership.

The petition website says more than 9,000 signatories are current Nvidia staff, though it notes that affiliations are self-reported and unverified. US President Donald Trump has also said he would not mind seeing Huang return.

Board Appears Unmoved by Campaign

For now, Huang's return seems unlikely. Reuters reported Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged an outside candidate instead.

Investors including Gavin Baker and Brad Gerstner have urged the board not to rush into naming a successor before investigations are complete. Supporters argue Nvidia cannot easily replace a founder who has led the company for three decades.

Nvidia is scheduled to report its first earnings since Huang's resignation on 17 November. The results could shape investor sentiment as the company navigates the leadership transition, while ongoing investigations continue.

excerpt: From ignored complaints to fears of career damage, the Brand and Walliams cases put pressure on Britain's entertainment industry to change
headline: 'Who Was Protecting Them?': Brand's Conviction and David Walliams' Allegations Put UK Entertainment Under Fire
html_content:
Russell Brand's 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence and allegations against David Walliams have intensified scrutiny of Britain's entertainment industry, as women describe career fears. A BBC review examined eight complaints about Brand, but only one was formally made to the corporation. That 2007 complaint was not handled effectively.

Three of Brand's four victims worked in media. He was convicted at Southwark Crown Court on 5 November of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women between 2004 and 2009. He was sentenced on 9 November.

Women Feared Speaking Out

Some victims said they feared they would not be believed or could lose work because of Brand's celebrity status. The BBC review found colleagues felt unable to raise concerns, believing he would always get his way. Channel 4 also apologised after a complaint about Brand was not escalated to senior management.

Comedian Lucy Beaumont helped media organisations investigate allegations concerning Walliams. She said she feared losing work herself: 'No one wants to mess that up'.

Multiple women allege Walliams used his status to pursue them as teenagers or young women. One woman described an alleged encounter when she was 15 as sexual assault. Walliams denies all allegations, saying he did not abuse his position or break the law.

Police Investigation and Legal Pressure

The Metropolitan Police announced on 13 November that it was investigating separate allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man in his 50s, identified in reports as Walliams. The force said these were separate from allegations reported by ITV News and the Guardian, but detectives were reviewing that reporting. No arrest had been announced on 13 November.

Walliams unsuccessfully sought a High Court injunction against ITV News and the Guardian, arguing that publication would expose him to a serious risk of suicide. The judge accepted that publication would materially increase a genuine and grave risk but refused the injunction, finding no proper legal basis for the restraint and giving substantial weight to freedom of expression and the public interest. The proceedings did not determine whether the allegations were true.

Beaumont said a woman who met Walliams signed an NDA barring her from discussing the alleged encounter with friends, family or a therapist.

Nandy Presses Entertainment Leaders

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy met representatives from the BBC, Sky, Channel 4, Netflix, HarperCollins, the Football Association and BAFTA on 16 November. She asked how organisations would challenge bullying, empower whistleblowers and protect freelancers.

Bectu head Philippa Childs said broadcasters recognised they needed to do better and had signed up to the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority (CIISA). She warned freelancers feared blacklisting. Bectu wants NDA protections extended to freelancers and CIISA funded through mandatory industry contributions.

Can the Industry Change?

CIISA offers workers across the creative industries a confidential route to raise concerns. It can identify patterns of harmful behaviour across the sector, rather than investigate individual cases.

Nandy urged the industry to 'get its house in order' or face a government crackdown. Ministers are considering stronger protections around non-disclosure agreements and whether participation in industry standards should become compulsory. No such requirement has been introduced.

excerpt: Josh O'Connor reportedly turned down the James Bond role shortly before Robert Pattinson was announced as Daniel Craig's successor, although the claim remains unconfirmed.
headline: Josh O'Connor Reportedly Turned Down James Bond Role Before Robert Pattinson Announcement
html_content:
Josh O'Connor reportedly turned down the opportunity to play James Bond before Robert Pattinson was officially announced as Daniel Craig's successor, adding another twist to the closely watched 007 casting process.

The Challengers and The Crown actor had been linked to the iconic British spy alongside several other high-profile names, including Jack Lowden and Callum Turner. However, a report published on 11 November claimed that O'Connor had rejected the role.

According to the Daily Mail, an unnamed source claimed that O'Connor had turned down the Bond role, stating: 'Josh has turned down the Bond role.' Neither the actor nor Amazon MGM Studios has publicly confirmed that he received a formal offer or rejected the part.

Just days later, on 16 November, Pattinson was officially named as the new James Bond, bringing months of speculation to an end.

Why Did Josh O'Connor Reportedly Turn Down James Bond?

The reported decision emerged after O'Connor discussed his plans for 2027 during an appearance at a screening of National Theatre Live's filmed production of Golden Boy, which originally ran at London's Almeida Theatre.

Asked about the possibility of becoming the next 007, the actor played down the speculation, responding: 'No, no, no. We'll see, but I doubt it.'

He also revealed that he had a project scheduled for January before planning to take some time away from acting.

'I'm doing something in January, but then yeah, I'm taking some time out,' he said.

His comments prompted questions about whether he would be available for the demanding filming schedule associated with the Bond franchise. However, O'Connor did not explicitly connect his planned break to the reported rejection.

Was Josh O'Connor Considered for the James Bond Role?

O'Connor was among the actors reportedly considered for the role. In October, it was reported that he, Jack Lowden and Callum Turner were among those offered final screen tests, alongside an unnamed fourth candidate. Subsequent reports also linked Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult to the casting process.

The latest reports contradicted an earlier story published by The Sun, which claimed that a fellow Golden Boy cast member had told someone at a London pub that O'Connor had privately revealed he had secured the Bond role.

However, the account relied on an unnamed source and was never independently verified. O'Connor did not confirm the claim.

Robert Pattinson Officially Becomes the Next James Bond

Amazon MGM Studios confirmed on 16 November that Pattinson would take over the role, making him the seventh actor to portray the famous spy in the film franchise.

The star of The Batman expressed his gratitude in a statement, describing the opportunity as the honour of a lifetime. Director Denis Villeneuve also welcomed the casting, praising Pattinson's qualities and saying he was delighted to have him as the new 007.

Pattinson will lead the next Bond film, which will be directed by Villeneuve and written by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight. Producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman are overseeing the project.

What Happens Next for the James Bond Franchise?

Pattinson's appointment marks a new chapter for the long-running franchise following Daniel Craig's final appearance in No Time to Die in 2021.

Although O'Connor's reported rejection has not been independently confirmed by the actor or the studio, his name was among those discussed during the casting process.

With Pattinson now officially taking over the role, the speculation surrounding the next 007 has ended. The focus can turn to the upcoming film and how the new Bond will shape the franchise's future.

excerpt: Pope Leo XIV was struck near the eye by a rosary during a farewell appearance in Lima, Peru, but later joked about the incident and praised the worshipper's faith.
headline: Pope Leo XIV Was Hit Near the Eye by a Rosary in Peru, and His Response Was Not What You Might Expect
html_content:
Pope Leo XIV was struck near the eye by a rosary thrown from a crowd in Lima, Peru, on Monday, 16 November 2026.

He later made light of the incident and praised the faith of the worshipper who had tried to give him the prayer beads.

The moment unfolded as Leo travelled through the crowd in his popemobile at Las Palmas Air Base, ahead of a farewell Mass.

The service concluded his six-day visit to Peru, the final stop on a 12-day South American tour that also included Uruguay and Argentina.

Leo Jokes About Rosary That Struck Him

Video of the encounter showed an object flying towards the pontiff as he greeted people lining his route. He reached towards it but appeared to miss the catch, then winced and touched his eye. The Mass proceeded as scheduled, and Reuters reported no indication that he had been injured.

The episode came up later during a news conference aboard the papal plane bound for Rome. Peruvian television journalist Fátima Saldonid told Leo that viewers had been concerned by the footage, while stressing that the gesture had been made out of affection.

BREAKING: Pope Leo XIV was STRUCK NEAR THE EYE by a rosary thrown from the crowd while riding in his popemobile in Lima, Peru. pic.twitter.com/KupScWr9hW

— Daily Loud (@DailyLoud) November 17, 2026

Leo thanked those who had welcomed him throughout his visit. He said the person who threw the rosary had acted with faith and simply wanted to offer him a religious gift.

He added that such experiences stay 'in the heart... perhaps in the eye as well', according to the Vatican's published transcript of his remarks.

The pope went on to describe the enthusiasm he had witnessed, saying it reflected deep faith and a desire to receive a blessing. He said the person had wanted to offer him a religious gift.

Gifts Thrown at Papal Events Pose Security Challenges

Leo has longstanding ties to Peru. Born Robert Francis Prevost in Chicago, he spent roughly two decades working there as a missionary and bishop. He also holds Peruvian citizenship and referred to the country as his homeland during the visit.

The Vatican said approximately 1.5 million people attended the Mass at Las Palmas Air Base, citing local authorities. Others gathered along the route to see the pontiff pass.

Pilgrims often throw rosaries, soft toys, flags and other gifts towards passing popes, hoping they will catch or bless them. Leo has caught objects from crowds, although he has not always avoided mishaps.

During an earlier appearance in Rome, he accidentally struck a Vatican camera operator while attempting to catch a thrown item. Reuters reported that he subsequently apologised to the operator.

For papal security personnel, even well-intentioned gifts present a practical concern. The Associated Press reported that Leo's bodyguards regard objects thrown towards him as a significant risk during public appearances.

Leo's comments came later, after Saldonid raised viewers' concern during the flight to Rome. He focused on the worshipper's apparent intention to offer a religious gift and on the faith he had seen among those who came to greet him. The available account records no injury and no change to the Mass schedule. It also does not say whether security staff took any further action after the incident.

Monday's rosary incident illustrated that tension: the pope wanted to remain close to the crowd, but a gesture of devotion still managed to catch him off guard.

excerpt: Kate Middleton joined Prince William, Sachin Tendulkar and local children for a Mumbai street cricket match, with an expert interpreting her animated reactions as signs of enjoyment.
headline: Kate Middleton Shows 'Genuinely Enthusiastic' Side on India Tour After Mumbai Cricket Match, Expert Says
html_content:
Kate Middleton's animated reactions during a street-cricket match in Mumbai showed she was 'genuinely delighted to be there', a body language expert said. The Princess of Wales joined Prince William, local children and former India captain Sachin Tendulkar for the game at Ballard Estate on Monday, 16 November 2026.

The three-day visit is the couple's first joint trip to India since 2016 and their first official overseas tour together since attending the Earthshot Prize awards in Boston in 2022. Mumbai is hosting this year's ceremony on Tuesday, 17 November.

Kate's Cricket Reactions Draw Expert's Attention

William and Kate took turns batting during a game of gully cricket, an informal version of the sport commonly played on Indian streets. The match brought them together with local youngsters and Tendulkar in a setting less formal than a traditional royal engagement.

Speaking to Betfair Casino, according to Marie Claire, body language expert Stanton said Kate appeared 'genuinely delighted to be there'.

After examining footage of the game, he described the Princess as 'incredibly expressive' and suggested her animated reactions revealed a competitive side not often seen during formal engagements.

Kate was seen laughing, grimacing and exchanging high-fives during her turn at batting. Stanton interpreted those reactions as signs that she was enjoying the activity, rather than simply fulfilling an official obligation.

He also highlighted her willingness to take part without maintaining the more restrained manner often associated with royal appearances.

Stanton said Kate's 'willingness to let her guard down is a really important part of what makes her so relatable'.

Body language cannot establish a person's private feelings or intentions. Stanton's observations are his interpretation of Kate's public behaviour, rather than independently verified psychological conclusions.

Cricket Match Puts Youth Initiatives in Focus

The Mumbai engagement also highlighted organisations using cricket to support young people and encourage wider participation in the sport.

William and Kate learned about the Sachin Tendulkar Foundation, which supports initiatives involving sport, health and education for underprivileged children.

They also met representatives of organisations working to make cricket more accessible, particularly for women and girls.

The young players took part in the match alongside the visiting royals, placing their participation at the centre of the engagement. The event also drew attention to efforts to widen access to cricket.

Tendulkar's involvement connected the visit with local sporting initiatives. It gave the young participants an opportunity to play alongside the former India captain as well as William and Kate.

Stanton suggested Kate viewed engagements of this kind as opportunities to connect with people. His assessment focused on her interactions with participants, although her intentions cannot be established through footage alone.

Mumbai Visit Leads Into Earthshot Ceremony and Delhi Meetings

The cricket match was part of a wider Mumbai itinerary that included a journey on the city's Line 3 Metro, known as the Aqua Line. The visit highlighted sustainable urban transport during a trip centred on Prince William's environmental initiative.

According to The Earthshot Prize, the 2026 ceremony will recognise environmental innovations addressing challenges involving climate, nature, waste and pollution.

Following the Mumbai engagements, William and Kate are scheduled to travel to New Delhi on Wednesday, 18 November, for a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

excerpt: Natalie Harp faces a potential court restriction as a lawsuit challenges Trump's Truth API, where subscribers reportedly pay up to $100,000 monthly for faster presidential updates.
headline: Trump's 'Human Printer' Natalie Harp Faces Court Bid That Could End Her Truth Social Reign
html_content:
Donald Trump's trusted aide Natalie Harp could have her role in the president's Truth Social operation curtailed as a federal lawsuit challenges an increasingly controversial arrangement allowing wealthy subscribers to receive presidential posts ahead of ordinary users.

Known as Trump's 'Human Printer', Harp has become one of his most recognisable aides, regularly helping with his online communications. The former One America News Network presenter earned her nickname during the 2024 presidential campaign by carrying a portable printer and supplying Trump with physical copies of favourable news articles and social media posts. She has worked with Trump since 2022 and became his executive assistant and special assistant after he returned to the White House.

White House aide Natalie Harp may be permanently barred from managing Trump’s social media after a new Federal Court filing proposes blocking her & other aides from posting for him.This comes after Intercept filed a lawsuit challenging Truth Social’s paid subscription feature. pic.twitter.com/7eGLaO0CVH

— Suzie rizzio (@Suzierizzo1) November 17, 2026

Now, her involvement in his digital operation has landed her in an extraordinary legal dispute.

Natalie Harp and Dan Scavino Face Potential Posting Restrictions

In a filing submitted on Friday, 13 November, The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation argued that US District Judge J. Paul Oetken could restrict Harp and White House deputy chief of staff Dan Scavino from publishing official government announcements on Trump's behalf.

The proposal is an alternative to the plaintiffs' broader request to restrict Trump himself from using Truth Social to publish official announcements while the paid subscription service remains in operation.

Their argument is that restricting aides who regularly post for the president could prevent paying subscribers from receiving certain government updates ahead of the wider public.

Trump's $100,000-a-Month Truth API Controversy

At the heart of the Donald Trump Truth Social lawsuit is Truth API, a paid data service introduced by Trump Media & Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social.

Reuters reported that the service gives paying customers faster access to Trump's posts, reportedly about 50 milliseconds ahead of ordinary users. The reported price is $100,000 (£75,840) a month, with a discounted rate of $60,000 (£45,504) a month for customers committing to a three-year subscription.

Reuters reported that Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading had signed up for the service. For high-frequency trading firms, even milliseconds can matter when presidential announcements about tariffs, economic policy or international conflicts move financial markets.

'No Right to Sell': Explosive Accusation Against Trump

The plaintiffs argue that the arrangement gives wealthy customers preferential access to government information that should be public.

When the lawsuit was filed in August, Intercept editor-in-chief Ben Muessig delivered a blistering accusation.

'Trump is trying to enrich himself by privatizing government information that he has no right to sell,' Muessig said.

The Trump administration disputes the allegations, arguing that Truth API does not violate the Constitution and that the plaintiffs cannot demonstrate harm the court can remedy. Trump Media has also defended the service, pointing to the availability of presidential communications through other platforms and subscription-based news outlets.

What Happens Next?

Judge Oetken is expected to hear arguments on Thursday, 19 November, over the administration's motion to dismiss, including whether the plaintiffs have legal standing to pursue the case.

The hearing will not automatically decide Harp's future, but the lawsuit puts her unusual position in Trump's communications operation under scrutiny. An aide known for helping shape the president's online messaging could find her ability to publish official announcements challenged in court, as questions mount over whether access to presidential information should come with a six-figure monthly price tag.

excerpt: Britons targeting retirement in 2027 should check State Pension timing, trace lost pension pots, compare income options and test their budgets before leaving work, as inheritance tax changes approach.
headline: Want To Retire in 2027? Experts Explain the Pension, Budget and Lifestyle Checks You Should Make Now
html_content:
Britons aiming to retire in 2027 need to establish when their pensions will pay, whether their savings can cover everyday costs and what life after work might look like. Retiring before State Pension age could leave an income gap.

The uncertainty is widespread. Just Group's GenVoices research, published in September 2025, found that 41 per cent of working respondents aged 60 to 69 felt prepared for retirement. The findings came from a wider survey of 3,500 UK adults.

Check Pensions Before You Retire in 2027

Begin with a State Pension forecast and National Insurance record. These show when payments may start, estimated entitlement and any contribution gaps. Missing years do not always justify voluntary payments, so check whether filling them would increase your pension.

State Pension age is rising from 66 to 67 between April 2026 and April 2028. Anyone planning to stop work earlier must identify how to fund the intervening months or years.

Workplace and personal pensions need attention too. Review balances, charges, investments and withdrawal options. For defined benefit schemes, request an estimate of the income payable at your proposed retirement date, including any reduction for claiming early.

Some savings may have been forgotten. The Pensions Policy Institute estimated in October 2026 that around three million UK pension pots were lost, holding approximately £18.7 billion. The government's Pension Tracing Service can identify scheme contact details, although it cannot confirm ownership or value.

Choose How Retirement Income Will Last

Defined contribution pensions can fund flexible drawdown, an annuity or both. Drawdown leaves money invested but exposes savings to market losses and the risk of withdrawals becoming unsustainable.

A lifetime annuity offers guaranteed income. Most have a 30-day cooling-off period, after which cancellation is generally unavailable. Inflation-linked increases or continuing payments to a surviving partner may reduce the initial amount offered.

Ross Lacey, director at Fairview Financial Management, told MoneyWeek that retirees should not assume recent investment gains will continue. He described clients seeking dependable income for essentials while allowing greater spending on leisure earlier in retirement.

Before transferring pensions, check whether valuable guarantees would be lost. Regulated advice is required for qualifying defined benefit transfers worth more than £30,000. Those aged 50 and over with defined contribution pensions can also obtain free guidance from Pension Wise.

Test Your Budget and Life After Work

Use bank statements to separate essential spending from optional costs. Include debts, maintenance, holidays and possible care expenses. Compare expected spending with income after tax, allowing for inflation, poor investment returns and changes following a partner's death.

Large taxable withdrawals can increase income tax bills. From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will also count towards estates for inheritance tax purposes, although existing exemptions remain. The change warrants reviewing estate plans rather than withdrawing savings hastily.

Philly Ponniah, a chartered wealth manager and financial coach at Philly Financial, told MoneyWeek that prospective retirees should practise living within their proposed budget. She also encouraged them to consider how they would replace the routine and social connections of work.

For some, reducing working hours may provide a more manageable transition than leaving employment altogether.

excerpt: Serbia has formally ended Jared Kushner's Belgrade hotel deal after protests, a criminal investigation and Affinity Partners' earlier withdrawal
headline: Jared Kushner's Serbia Hotel Project Is Officially Dead After Protests and Legal Row: 'Love This for Him'
html_content:
Jared Kushner's Belgrade hotel project has been terminated, after his investment firm withdrew. The cancellation ends a Trump-branded luxury development plan on a site damaged by NATO bombing, after protests and a criminal investigation. A Threads post reacting said: 'Love this for him.'

Serbia Formally Ends Kushner Agreement

Serbia's caretaker construction minister, Aleksandra Sofronijević, confirmed on 16 November that the termination agreement with Atlantic Incubation Partners LLC, linked to Kushner, had been signed. She said both parties had no outstanding claims against each other, completing the process under a Serbian government decision adopted in August 2026.

The contract was signed in May 2024. It provided for a free 99-year land lease. The planned joint venture would have given the investor a 77.5 per cent stake and Serbia a 22.5 per cent stake, giving the American partner control of the company. The agreement required the state to remove the site's protected status, demolish the existing buildings at its own expense and provide the land without charge. If Serbia failed to meet its obligations by May 2026, the investor could potentially seek compensation, with the reported contractual liability capped at €50 million ($55 million).

Affinity Partners had already announced its withdrawal on 15 December 2025, the same day prosecutors filed an indictment proposal against four Serbian officials. The November 2026 agreement therefore marks the formal contractual end, rather than the date Kushner first stepped away.

Protests Over Belgrade's Historic Site

The proposed development would have replaced the former Yugoslav Army General Staff complex with a luxury hotel, casino, residences, offices and shops.

The buildings were designed by modernist architect Nikola Dobrović after the Second World War and were damaged during NATO's 1999 bombing campaign.

Protests by students, architects and heritage campaigners challenged the plan and the government's decision to remove the complex's protected cultural-property status in November 2024. Opposition intensified after the Serbian parliament passed special legislation intended to facilitate the redevelopment.

Legal Row Involved Serbian Officials

Serbia's organised crime prosecutors filed an indictment proposal against Culture Minister Nikola Selaković, ministry secretary Slavica Jelača and heritage officials Goran Vasić and Aleksandar Ivanović. All four faced abuse of office; three faced document falsification, while Ivanović faced a separate charge of aiding the offence.

All four defendants pleaded not guilty when their trial began in February 2026. In May 2025, Serbia's organised crime prosecutor's office said Vasić had admitted the act of falsification during questioning. That earlier statement was not a court conviction, and Vasić subsequently denied the charges in court. Selaković has also denied wrongdoing. The allegations concern Serbian officials; there is no indication that Kushner or Affinity Partners were accused of participating in the alleged document falsification.

Serbia's Political Backdrop

The cancellation comes amid a political shift. In parliamentary elections held on 25 October 2026, the student-backed Student List won 53.01 per cent of the vote and secured 140 of the National Assembly's 250 seats, defeating the list led by the Serbian Progressive Party.

The result followed anti-corruption protests and public anger. It provides context for the political climate surrounding the project, although there is no evidence that the election itself caused the termination.

The signed agreement removes the prospect of mutual financial claims, according to reporting on its terms. The future of the former General Staff buildings, however, remains unresolved.

excerpt: A Chinese diplomat has accused Europe of limiting access to advanced ASML chipmaking equipment over fears of technology theft, warning that Beijing could respond with restrictions of its own.
headline: Chinese Envoy Says Dutch ASML Export Curbs Reflect Europe's Fear China Will 'Rob' Its Technology
html_content:
A Chinese diplomat has accused Europe of restricting access to advanced ASML chipmaking equipment because it fears China could steal its technology. Qu Xun, China's minister-counsellor in Madrid, made the accusation in an interview with Reuters on Tuesday, 17 November.

He warned that Beijing could respond by limiting technology-sharing if European countries continued restricting Chinese access to advanced equipment.

The Dutch government has restricted exports of advanced chipmaking equipment manufactured by ASML to China since 2019.

The United States is also pushing for additional restrictions on less advanced machines to limit China's ability to manufacture sophisticated semiconductors. However, it remains unclear whether US lawmakers will approve the proposed measures.

The dispute threatens to complicate wider trade negotiations between Brussels and Beijing. EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic and China's commerce minister, Wang Wentao, are expected to resume discussions in 2027 following an October agreement on quotas for Chinese hybrid-car exports.

Disagreements over technology transfers, investment restrictions and industrial policy remain unresolved.

Chinese Envoy Accuses Europe of Fearing Technology Theft

'We want to import ASML goods,' Qu told Reuters, without specifying which machines China wanted to access. He said the technology currently available to Chinese buyers was generations behind the most advanced equipment.

'We want the European Union to make its own decisions and not follow the instructions of others,' he said.

Qu then accused European governments of restricting access because of concerns about Chinese technology theft. 'Europe is forbidding it because it is afraid China will rob its technology,' he said. 'If Europe thinks that way, China will too.'

ASML declined to comment on the remarks. Qu's warning suggested that China could reconsider sharing its own technology if it believed European companies were receiving unfair treatment. He did not announce any new Chinese restrictions.

ASML Export Restrictions Complicate EU-China Trade Relations

The existing restrictions were imposed by the Netherlands, rather than the European Union as a bloc. Washington is separately pressing for tighter controls on lower-level semiconductor manufacturing equipment, potentially affecting ASML and Japanese manufacturer Tokyo Electron.

The wider disagreement extends beyond semiconductors. European proposals include requirements for local content and technology transfers, alongside restrictions on foreign investors' asset ownership in sectors such as electric vehicles, batteries and cars.

Qu described technology transfer as a 'pillar' of China's foreign direct investment strategy but insisted that Beijing expected reciprocal treatment. 'China is not looking to eat up the European market. We are seeking a fair, non-discriminatory position, based on equality and reciprocity,' he said.

He added that China was 'fully capable' of withstanding deteriorating relations if Chinese companies were treated unfairly. 'Both sides need to approach each other with goodwill,' he said.

Chinese Investment in Spain Highlights Wider Trade Stakes

Chinese investment in Spain has also become an important part of the relationship. Reuters reported that the value of Chinese investment stock in the country had tripled over the past decade to €12 billion (£10 billion).

Qu said companies were waiting two to three years to assess existing investments before committing additional funds. Chinese carmakers SAIC and Chery, alongside battery producers CATL and AESC, have invested in Spain independently or through joint ventures with European companies.

Qu dismissed the description of China as a 'systemic rival' used by Spain's opposition People's Party, saying Beijing judged politicians by their actions rather than their words.

'Spain has many advantages... We aren't coming here for half a year – we are coming for the next 20, 30, 50 years,' he told Reuters. 'We are betting on Spain 100%.'

The comments highlight the competing interests shaping European relations with China. While Beijing wants greater access to advanced manufacturing technology, European governments face pressure to protect strategic industries and address concerns about technology security.

The next round of EU-China trade negotiations will test whether both sides can find common ground on export controls, investment and technology transfers without further damaging their commercial relationship.

excerpt: The 2027 Grammys will feature five new competitive categories, including awards for Asian pop, Latin songwriting, traditional folk, traditional pop and R&B collaborations
headline: 2027 Grammys Add Five New Categories: What the Biggest Awards Shake-up Means for Artists
html_content:
The 2027 Grammy Awards are introducing five new competitive categories, expanding the prestigious ceremony to a total of 100 awards across 12 fields for the first time in Recording Academy history.

Unveiled alongside this year's nominations, the landmark overhaul seeks to recognise underrepresented musical genres and global communities spanning Asian pop, Spanish-language songwriting, collaborative R&B, traditional folk, and classic vocal pop.

However, the headline addition, Best Asian Pop Music Performance, immediately encountered a high-profile setback after South Korean superstars BTS boycotted the category.

Members of the chart-topping group shared an identical public statement expressing their hope that music will be heard and loved for what it is rather than being divided by region or language.

Despite the boycott, the inaugural ballot delivered historic milestones, placing Filipino acts BINI and SB19 alongside Japan's BABYMETAL and LiSA and South Korea's IVE and KiiiKiii.

Arriving as female artists including Raye, Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, and Ella Langley dominate the year's top races, the expansion signals a decisive effort by the Recording Academy to reflect an increasingly interconnected global music industry.

New Categories Expand Global Recognition

Throughout its history, the Recording Academy has periodically reshaped the Grammys to reflect structural shifts across the global music industry.

Observers note that this year represents one of the institution's most consequential updates, creating fresh opportunities for both established stars and first-time nominees whilst signalling a broader definition of mainstream music.

The headline addition, Best Asian Pop Music Performance, has met a setback during its announcement, with notable Korean groups like BTS boycotting it.

The Best Asian Pop Music Performance category is created to honour performances originating from, or widely recognised within, Asian music markets that feature meaningful use of one or more Asian languages.

Commentary surrounding the nominations notes that while the new award broadens representation, it also highlights the variety of music the region offers, bringing together K-pop, J-pop and P-pop under a single banner.

The first ballot places Filipino artists BINI and SB19 among the first nominees, giving Original Pilipino Music or Pilipino Pop, a place in Grammy history.

Best Latin Song is another new addition, which shifts the spotlight from performers to songwriters by recognising newly written Spanish-language songs. The inaugural nominees include works by Karol G and Drake, Jorge Drexler, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso featuring Sting, Rosalía, and Milo J.

More Room for Traditional and Collaborative Music

The Recording Academy has also introduced Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, recognising contemporary collaborative R&B recordings, alongside Best Traditional Folk Album, which honours excellence in traditional folk recordings.

The categories broaden recognition for styles that previously had limited opportunities within the Grammy framework.

Completing the expansion is Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, which celebrates singles and tracks rooted in classic pop traditions.

The first nominees include Olivia Dean, Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande, Laufey, Raye, and Nicole Zuraitis with Gilad Hekselman, reflecting a blend of veteran performers and contemporary artists influenced by timeless vocal styles.

The changes arrive as women dominate the 2027 nominations, with artists including Raye, Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo and Ella Langley leading the year's biggest categories.

The introduction of five new awards acknowledges musical communities that have grown in influence far beyond their traditional markets.

Whether these new additions will continue to evolve will depend on how artists, labels and Grammy voters respond over the coming years.

For now, the Recording Academy has made its clear statement that the world's biggest music awards are widening their scope to reflect a global and diverse industry.

Unveiled alongside this year's nominations, the landmark overhaul seeks to recognise underrepresented musical genres and global communities spanning Asian pop, Spanish-language songwriting, collaborative R&B, traditional folk, and classic vocal pop. However, the headline addition, Best Asian Pop Music Performance, immediately encountered a high-profile setback after South Korean superstars BTS boycotted the category. Members of the chart-topping group shared an identical public statement expressing their hope that music will be heard and loved for what it is rather than being divided by region or language. Despite the boycott, the inaugural ballot delivered historic milestones, placing Filipino acts BINI and SB19 alongside Japan's BABYMETAL and LiSA and South Korea's IVE and KiiiKiii. Arriving as female artists including Raye, Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, and Ella Langley dominate the year's top races, the expansion signals a decisive effort by the Recording Academy to reflect an increasingly interconnected global music industry. New Categories Expand Global Recognition Throughout its history, the Recording Academy has periodically reshaped the Grammys to reflect structural shifts across the global music industry. Observers note that this year represents one of the institution's most consequential updates, creating fresh opportunities for both established stars and first-time nominees whilst signalling a broader definition of mainstream music. The headline addition, Best Asian Pop Music Performance, has met a setback during its announcement, with notable Korean groups like BTS boycotting it. The Best Asian Pop Music Performance category is created to honour performances originating from, or widely recognised within, Asian music markets that feature meaningful use of one or more Asian languages. Commentary surrounding the nominations notes that while the new award broadens representation, it also highlights the variety of music the region offers, bringing together K-pop, J-pop and P-pop under a single banner. The first ballot places Filipino artists BINI and SB19 among the first nominees, giving Original Pilipino Music or Pilipino Pop, a place in Grammy history. Best Latin Song is another new addition, which shifts the spotlight from performers to songwriters by recognising newly written Spanish-language songs. The inaugural nominees include works by Karol G and Drake, Jorge Drexler, Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso featuring Sting, Rosalía, and Milo J. The categories broaden recognition for styles that previously had limited opportunities within the Grammy framework. Completing the expansion is Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, which celebrates singles and tracks rooted in classic pop traditions. The first nominees include Olivia Dean, Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande, Laufey, Raye, and Nicole Zuraitis with Gilad Hekselman, reflecting a blend of veteran performers and contemporary artists influenced by timeless vocal styles. The changes arrive as women dominate the 2027 nominations, with artists including Raye, Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo and Ella Langley leading the year's biggest categories. The introduction of five new awards acknowledges musical communities that have grown in influence far beyond their traditional markets. Whether these new additions will continue to evolve will depend on how artists, labels and Grammy voters respond over the coming years. For now, the Recording Academy has made its clear statement that the world's biggest music awards are widening their scope to reflect a global and diverse industry.

excerpt: Donald Trump's windblown hair attracted online attention during his arrival in Manila, while the president attended ASEAN-related meetings and prepared for a subsequent China visit.
headline: 'What's Happened to His Hair?': Trump's Windblown Look Draws Attention During His ASEAN Arrival in Manila
html_content:
President Donald Trump's windblown hair drew attention in Manila, Philippines, on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, as he arrived for the final day of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and related meetings.

Footage of his airport welcome showed gusts lifting his hair, prompting online questions about its noticeably darker appearance.

Air Force One landed at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City at 5.33 pm local time, according to GMA News.

Trump had arrived near the close of the three-day gathering, ahead of talks with regional leaders and a planned onward journey to China.

The Philippines hosted the 15–17 November gathering under its 2026 ASEAN chairmanship.

Trump last visited the country in November 2017, during his first presidential term. At this year's closing ceremony, Manila was preparing to hand the regional bloc's chairmanship to Singapore.

Trump's Windblown Hair Steals Attention at Manila Airport

Wearing a navy suit and red tie, Trump descended from the presidential aircraft and greeted officials on the tarmac. Executive Secretary Ralph Recto and House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos were among those welcoming him, alongside Philippine and US diplomatic representatives.

The formal reception featured music and dancing. A marching band performed 'YMCA', a familiar song at Trump's campaign rallies, while a child presented him with miniature US and Philippine flags, which he waved during the ceremony, ABC News reported.

Trump must have dyed his hair on Air Force One, cuz it wasn’t that color when he left the White House headed to Asia yesterday. pic.twitter.com/PktKihNwor

— Christopher Webb (@cwebbonline) November 17, 2026

The lighter moment that travelled online, however, came from the weather rather than the programme. As wind caught the president's swept-over hairstyle, sections shifted and parts of his scalp appeared briefly visible. Some viewers also thought his hair looked darker than the blond shade associated with him.

An AOL report on 17 November collected responses to the footage. One commenter asked, 'What's happened to his hair?' Another wrote, 'He is sweating and did he change his hair color again!' A separate user joked about the wind nearly carrying his hair away.

These were social media reactions, not evidence that Trump had changed his hair colour or undergone any treatment. The available footage does not establish why his hair appeared different, and there has been no verified explanation for the apparent change.

Manila Visit Comes Ahead of China Summit

The online discussion echoed a similar episode in September. Photographs taken as Trump arrived in New Jersey on 4 September showed his hair looking darker, prompting questions about its colour. IBTimes UK reported on the reaction at the time.

In Manila, the diplomatic programme carried considerably greater weight than the airport chatter. Trump met leaders from Australia, India and Japan in the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or Quad, to discuss regional and economic security. Reuters reported that the group also discussed artificial intelligence.

The Quad meeting brought together the four countries amid continuing disagreements over trade, security and China's influence across the Indo-Pacific region.

His schedule also included an ASEAN-US Special Summit and talks with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., with defence, investment and regional developments among the areas of interest, according to the Philippine News Agency.

Trump was subsequently expected in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting on 18–19 November, dates confirmed by China's foreign ministry. Yet for viewers sharing the arrival clip, an unexpected gust of wind had briefly overshadowed the diplomatic occasion.
