excerpt: About 1,500 protesters gathered in Manila to oppose US influence and criticise Donald Trump ahead of his arrival for the 49th ASEAN Summit.
headline: Protest Leader Calls Donald Trump 'Such a Loser' as Manila Demonstrators Demand Independent Foreign Policy
html_content:
A protest leader called US President Donald Trump 'such a loser' as about 1,500 demonstrators rallied in Manila on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, demanding an independent foreign policy ahead of his arrival for the 49th ASEAN Summit, the Associated Press reported.

Earlier demonstrations on Sunday, 15 November, had led to clashes with police. Eleven protesters were reported arrested in Manila, while protest groups cited 276 arrests in Muntinlupa.

The National Capital Region Police Office later said it had completed inquest proceedings involving 213 arrested people. Those arrested retain the presumption of innocence.

Manila Protesters Slam Trump Over US Influence

At Liwasang Bonifacio, protesters waved red flags and carried a banner declaring, 'Resist U.S. war and plunder!' Riot police carrying shields and wooden truncheons monitored the gathering, according to the Associated Press.

Protest leader Teddy Casiño criticised Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for maintaining close ties with Washington, urging him to 'stop being a puppet of Donald Trump'.

Casiño argued that the Philippine government should not deal with 'such a loser' and called for a foreign policy independent of American influence.

During an earlier demonstration on Sunday, Casiño also told reporters that Trump was 'not welcome here'. His remarks reflected wider opposition to US policies that activists say threaten Philippine sovereignty.

One concern was Pax Silica, a US-led initiative intended to strengthen global supply chains for semiconductors, critical minerals and other advanced technologies.

The proposed manufacturing hub in New Clark City, Tarlac, has drawn criticism from campaigners who fear it could displace Indigenous Aeta communities and cause environmental damage.

Those concerns remain allegations, rather than established consequences. The US State Department told CBS News that Philippine authorities proposed the location and would decide whether the project proceeds under domestic law.

Marcos has supported the initiative, citing potential economic opportunities and the development of advanced manufacturing industries.

Tuesday's protests also featured an effigy depicting Trump inside a coffin. Other demonstrators destroyed an effigy portraying the president as an excavator, according to images and footage from the gathering.

Trump Welcomed Despite Manila Protests

Trump received an official welcome at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City, where a child presented him with miniature American and Philippine flags.

He waved the flags as a marching band played 'YMCA'. The airport welcome took place as anti-Trump demonstrations were held elsewhere in the capital.

The president later met leaders from Australia, India and Japan during Quad discussions on regional cooperation. He also took part in ASEAN engagements as Washington sought to strengthen its diplomatic and economic relationships.

His arrival marked his first overseas trip since Republicans suffered substantial losses in the US midterm elections.

On Wednesday, 18 November, Trump was scheduled to receive full military honours from Marcos at Malacañang Palace, followed by a state banquet. The leaders were expected to reaffirm their longstanding defence alliance.

Trump was then due to travel to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and planned discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

He also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, although no such meeting had been confirmed.

excerpt: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin travelled to an LSU–Texas game on a government aircraft after an FAA ground stop caused thousands of cancellations and delays nationwide.
headline: Markwayne Mullin Took Government Plane to LSU–Texas Game as Travellers Faced FAA Ground Stop Fallout
html_content:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin travelled to an LSU–Texas football game in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, aboard a government aircraft on Saturday, 14 November 2026, as commercial passengers dealt with widespread flight disruption, according to the New York Post.

The trip followed a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop on Friday, 13 November, caused by an air traffic control equipment failure.

Departures resumed that evening, but cancellations continued throughout the weekend.

Markwayne Mullin's Flight Followed Nationwide Disruption

Mullin attended the game at Tiger Stadium, where Texas defeated Louisiana State University 22–21. The previous day, he had joined Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy at a White House briefing about the aviation shutdown.

The ground stop lasted roughly four and a half hours. By Saturday morning, FlightAware had recorded 9,132 cancellations and 7,030 delays for Friday alone, according to ABC News. More cancellations followed as airlines struggled to reposition aircraft and crews.

The timing drew attention because commercial passengers were still trying to reach their destinations when Mullin flew to Louisiana for the match.

A government source told the Post that Mullin's flight received no exemption from FAA restrictions, which had already been lifted. The aircraft reportedly departed roughly 24 hours after the ground stop ended.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said Mullin was required to use government aircraft to maintain secure communications and ensure continuity of government during emergencies.

'Any flight not related to his service as DHS Secretary he pays for personally,' a department spokesperson said.

DHS said Mullin paid for the personal trip, although it did not provide payment records or specify the amount. The statement did not establish whether he reimbursed the full operating cost of the aircraft.

Bollinger Shipyards Contract Adds Scrutiny to Stadium Visit

The Post also reported that Mullin spent part of the game in a private box belonging to Ben Bordelon, president and chief executive of Louisiana-based Bollinger Shipyards.

Bollinger has longstanding business with DHS through the US Coast Guard. In July 2026, the company finalised a contract worth approximately $2.2 billion (about £1.7 billion) to build four Arctic Security Cutters. A separate deal covers two vessels to be built in Finland.

The reported encounter drew attention because Bordelon's company holds substantial federal contracts. However, no evidence has emerged that the two discussed government business or that Bollinger received preferential treatment.

A source told the Post that Mullin had not previously met Bordelon. According to the same account, Mullin obtained his tickets through a close friend and paid their fair market value.

'Secretary Mullin abides by all ethics requirements,' a DHS spokesperson said. Bollinger did not respond to the newspaper's request for comment.

Earlier on Saturday, Mullin had attended a Coast Guard Academy–Merchant Marine Academy football game in Washington before travelling to Baton Rouge.

At Friday's briefing, Mullin suggested newer equipment had overwhelmed older FAA technology. He said there was no indication of a cyberattack at that stage and argued that piecemeal upgrades would not work.

'We need one complete system,' he said.

The disruption also forced the postponement of the Ole Miss–Oklahoma game until Sunday.

On Sunday's Fox News programme The Sunday Briefing, Mullin said, 'I don't think anybody's going to get fired over this.' He added: 'This was an issue with the equipment.'

excerpt: Robert Pattinson has been announced as the seventh actor to play James Bond, following Daniel Craig, after a career spanning Harry Potter, Twilight, independent films and Batman
headline: From Harry Potter to James Bond: Robert Pattinson Roles You Need To Watch Before His 007 Debut
html_content:
Robert Pattinson has been named the new James Bond, marking the latest chapter in a career that has moved from the magic of Harry Potter to the glittering vampire world of Twilight. The 40-year-old actor, best known to many fans as the undead heartthrob Edward Cullen, has been unveiled as the seventh actor to play the iconic Agent 007, taking over from Daniel Craig.

Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson's appointment on Monday, ending years of speculation over who would inherit one of cinema's most recognisable characters. The actor said playing Bond was 'the honour of a lifetime', calling the opportunity a dream come true.

Robert Pattinson Roles That Built His James Bond Future

The news marks a surprising but carefully built journey for an actor who has repeatedly avoided being defined by his biggest franchises.

Pattinson first gained global attention in 2005 when he appeared as Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire. His role was not at the centre of the story, but his performance introduced him to a worldwide audience before his career dramatically changed three years later.

In 2008, Pattinson starred as the mysterious 'vegetarian' vampire Edward Cullen in Twilight, opposite Kristen Stewart's Bella Swan. The five-film franchise is based on the novel series by Stephenie Meyer. The role catapulted him to worldwide fame as an international star and teenage phenomenon. However, Pattinson soon moved away from the polished image associated with the character.

Instead of following the traditional Hollywood leading-man path, he moved towards stranger, riskier projects. He worked with acclaimed directors, including David Cronenberg in Cosmopolis, the Safdie brothers in Good Time and Robert Eggers in The Lighthouse.

Those performances reshaped the way audiences viewed him. Pattinson was no longer simply an actor from a blockbuster romance series. He became known for choosing unpredictable characters and challenging material.

Film critic Luke Goodsell described his career as 'compelling to watch', highlighting how Pattinson and his Twilight co-star Stewart managed to rebuild their careers after being closely associated with the franchise.

Robert Pattinson James Bond Era Begins After Batman

Pattinson's return to major franchises came with Christopher Nolan's Tenet in 2020. He played Neil, a sharp-suited intelligence operative. The role reminded audiences that he could combine blockbuster appeal with eccentricity, a quality that may now shape his version of Bond.

In 2022, he took on the role of the legendary Bruce Wayne in The Batman. Matt Reeves' darker interpretation of the character attracted strong audience interest and showed that Pattinson could carry a major action franchise.

The Bond casting follows a long search that reportedly considered actors including Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Instead, producers chose an established global star with experience across fantasy, superhero and independent cinema.

Denis Villeneuve, who will direct the next Bond film, said Pattinson brought a fresh quality to the role.

'He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new,' he said.

The appointment also begins a new era for the franchise following Amazon MGM Studios' assumption of creative control. It marks the end of longtime Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson's creative control over the film series.

Pattinson joins a select group of actors who have portrayed James Bond, following Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig.

excerpt: Avery Woods addressed disputed photo claims on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, saying her former OnlyFans account contained four non-nude images and defending her right to move beyond her past.
headline: Mormon Wives Star Avery Woods Says 'I'm Not Ashamed of My Past' After Old Onlyfans Photos Resurface
html_content:
Disputed images said to show The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Avery Woods have resurfaced online, but their authenticity and origins remain unverified. Woods has defended her former OnlyFans account, saying she has no regrets about her past despite the issue becoming a storyline on the Hulu reality series.

The show premiered on 12 November, introducing a new group of women alongside returning star Jen Affleck. Woods, a former paediatric intensive care nurse turned content creator, found herself facing questions about photographs she believed were gone permanently.

Avery Woods Addresses OnlyFans Photo Claims

The controversy began when castmate Jordan McClanahan discussed Woods' previous OnlyFans activity with other women, including McCall DaPron and Mayci Neeley.

Woods acknowledged opening an OnlyFans account approximately four and a half years ago. She said she had uploaded only four photographs, none of which contained nudity.

Other cast members, however, claimed they had found nude photographs purportedly depicting Woods elsewhere online.

According to Bustle, fellow cast member Bobbi Althoff later discussed images circulating on another website that allegedly showed Woods but were not actually of her. The women also questioned whether some photographs could have been generated using artificial intelligence.

The authenticity and origins of the disputed images remain unverified.

McClanahan had also expressed concern that Woods' online history could affect the group's reputation and religious standing. Woods questioned why her private decisions were being discussed publicly.

In an interview with People, Woods said she had never expected her former account to become a storyline. She also said the possibility of personal photographs being shared without her knowledge raised concerns about privacy and consent.

Woods said her decision to use OnlyFans was motivated by financial considerations, particularly supporting her family.

'I'm not ashamed of my past,' she said.

The reality star said people should be allowed to grow beyond earlier decisions. As a mother, she wanted to acknowledge her history without allowing it to define her family or future.

Avery Woods Leaves Filming in Tears

The disagreement came to a head in Woods' final scene of the season, when she confronted McClanahan about the discussion. The exchange ended with Woods asking for her microphone to be removed. She walked away in tears and said she no longer wanted to participate in filming.

'I think in the moment, it was just really overwhelming,' Woods told People.

She explained that receiving unexpected information while surrounded by cameras and production staff made the situation particularly difficult.

Woods said she needed privacy to process her emotions rather than continue arguing. She described stepping away and regrouping as her usual response when she feels overwhelmed.

Despite the fallout, Woods has not ruled out resolving her differences with McClanahan. In a separate interview with Bustle, she said further conversations were necessary but that she would prefer to have them away from the cameras.

The show premiered on 12 November, introducing a new group of women alongside returning star Jen Affleck. Woods, a former paediatric intensive care nurse turned content creator, found herself facing questions about photographs she believed were gone permanently. Avery Woods Addresses OnlyFans Photo Claims The controversy began when castmate Jordan McClanahan discussed Woods' previous OnlyFans activity with other women, including McCall DaPron and Mayci Neeley. Woods acknowledged opening an OnlyFans account approximately four and a half years ago. She said she had uploaded only four photographs, none of which contained nudity. Other cast members, however, claimed they had found nude photographs purportedly depicting Woods elsewhere online. According to Bustle, fellow cast member Bobbi Althoff later discussed images circulating on another website that allegedly showed Woods but were not actually of her. The women also questioned whether some photographs could have been generated using artificial intelligence. The authenticity and origins of the disputed images remain unverified. McClanahan had also expressed concern that Woods' online history could affect the group's reputation and religious standing. Woods questioned why her private decisions were being discussed publicly. She also said the possibility of personal photographs being shared without her knowledge raised concerns about privacy and consent. Woods said her decision to use OnlyFans was motivated by financial considerations, particularly supporting her family. 'I'm not ashamed of my past,' she said. excerpt: National Grid has rejected a fake social media post claiming a nationwide blackout on 19 November 2026, while guidance outlines practical steps for preparing for power cuts.
headline: UK Blackout Rumours Debunked: What You Really Need To Do if Power Cuts Hit Your Area
html_content:
National Grid has dismissed the false UK blackout rumours after a fake social media post claimed that a nationwide power outage would take place on Thursday, 19 November 2026. While there is no planned national blackout, the claims have renewed attention on what households should do to prepare for power cuts.

The post bears a striking resemblance to a National Grid announcement and claims an outage would happen because of a 'critical fault in the national grid'. The energy company said the image was fake. It also urged people to check and verify official channels for accurate updates rather than relying on viral posts.

What To Keep at Home Before an Outage

Planned emergency power cuts are not routine events. Guidance states that Rota Load Disconnections would only happen if other measures had failed to manage electricity supply and emergency disconnections were considered necessary.

In the event that an outage was announced, households would receive information about affected areas and timings through official announcements. The system would use postcode-linked block letters to identify areas involved in any planned disconnections.

Even with a confirmed outage, basic preparation would make a temporary loss of electricity easier to manage. Households are advised to keep a torch available with spare batteries because it is safer than using candles during a blackout. People should also keep phones, laptops and portable batteries charged so they can stay connected in case of power interruptions.

Warm clothing, blankets and other supplies can also help, especially during colder months. The guidance recommends preparing a flask of boiled water for hot drinks and keeping a hot water bottle available to help stay warm.

Food and water supplies are also a key part of emergency planning. The government's Be Ready campaign encouraged households to keep a three-day supply of essential items. Keep canned food and bottled water available as a precautionary measure. Panic-buying and stockpiling are not encouraged.

What To Do When Electricity Goes Off

During an actual power cut, households should keep heat inside by keeping doors closed and limiting unnecessary movements between rooms. People should avoid repeatedly opening fridges and freezers to help food stay cold for longer.

Those using gas cookers should remember that electronic ignition may not work without electricity. Guidance recommends having an alternative way to light the cooker.

Taking the initiative to check on neighbours who may need extra assistance may also be necessary, especially older and vulnerable individuals. Households with medical equipment that relies on electricity are encouraged to register for additional support through the Priority Services Register.

The spread of the latest UK blackout rumours shows how quickly misinformation can travel online. But preparing for a genuine power cut does not require panic. Securing supplies, having an adequately charged alternative power source or battery, and having a clear plan will lessen the impact of a temporary disruption.

National Grid has advised people who encounter false outage claims to report them and rely on official updates for information about electricity supplies.

excerpt: Mia Latter has condemned Russell Brand's prison message denying his convictions, while officials consider whether the broadcast breached prison rules and she campaigns for changes to UK consent law.
headline: Russell Brand Rape Accuser Calls Prison Message 'Appalling' and 'Absolute Lies' After Denial on YouTube
html_content:
Russell Brand is facing a new wave of criticism after a woman who accused him of rape criticised his latest message from prison. Brand insisted he was innocent despite being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Mia Latter, 37, said she was shocked and upset after Brand's wife, Laura, read a statement from the comedian during their Sunday Service show on YouTube. Latter, who alleges Brand raped her when she was 16, described the message as 'appalling' and criticised him for spreading what she called 'absolute lies' while presenting himself as a Christian.

Her complaints come as Brand serves a 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence following his convictions for offences involving four women. Latter was not among the four complainants in the criminal trial, and Brand has denied her separate allegations.

Russell Brand Accuser Calls His Message Called 'Appalling'

Latter made her outrage known on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, shortly after Brand's wife delivered his message to viewers. During the YouTube broadcast, Laura read a statement in which Brand maintained his innocence.

'I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for,' the comedian asserted.

For Latter, having those words accompanied by a religious message was disturbing.

'It was really shocking to me... it was appalling, frankly, it was upsetting to watch,' she said.

She also criticised 'this Christian message alongside absolute lies'.

Latter said her thoughts immediately turned to the four women whose allegations resulted in Brand's convictions.

'I just felt for those women that stood trial and everything they went through,' she explained.

She argued that Brand's continued denial did not change the outcome of the legal proceedings.

'They got their verdict, and for him to say, "I'm innocent, I'm not guilty" – well, you are, you're a convicted rapist now. There's no arguing with that,' Latter said.

Russell Brand's Prison Message Raises Concerns From Government Officials

Brand's message attracted attention from government officials, raising questions about whether he violated prison regulations by communicating publicly through his wife. According to the BBC, Downing Street said action would be expected if Brand was found to have breached prison rules.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris also addressed the controversy, emphasising the restrictions on prisoners.

'Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims,' said Norris.

The comments suggested that the authorities would be investigating the circumstances surrounding the broadcast, although the BBC report did not indicate whether Brand had violated any specific rule.

Russell Brand Accuser Pursues Legal Reform After Recounting Abuse

Latter also discussed her own allegations against Brand, which first became public through a 2023 investigation by The Times, The Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches. She was one of six women who made separate allegations against the comedian during the investigation. None of the six women was among the four complainants in his criminal trial.

Latter alleges she was 16 when she met Brand, who was then 30. In a separate interview with The Sunday Times, she claimed Brand instructed her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends. She also claimed that Brand referred to her as 'the child' in front of members of his entourage. Brand denies these allegations.

Latter said prosecutors ultimately decided not to include her case in the trial that resulted in Brand's convictions. She claimed the police wanted her involvement in subsequent proceedings, but she decided not to continue with the process so she could focus on campaigning for legal reform.

She has since waived her right to anonymity and is advocating for a staggered age of consent in the UK. Her proposal would make sexual relationships between adults and 16- and 17-year-olds illegal. Latter believes such legislation would have prevented her alleged experience with Brand.

'It would have 100% made a difference because my parents tried to stop the relationship,' she told the BBC.

She added that her parents attempted to prevent her from seeing him but lacked the legal grounds she believes would have been necessary.

'If it had been a criminal offence for him to be having a relationship with me, none of the subsequent abuse would have ever happened because they would have been able to stop the relationship dead in its tracks,' she claimed.

excerpt: 50 Cent described Leonardo DiCaprio's 52nd birthday celebration as 'crazy' after attending the Beverly Hills party, where celebrity guests and a group of women arriving together drew attention.
headline: 50 Cent Says 'Leo S--- Was Crazy!' After Busload of Women Arrives at DiCaprio's 52nd Birthday Party
html_content:
Nine women were filmed arriving together in a white minibus at Leonardo DiCaprio's 52nd birthday celebration in Beverly Hills. After attending the party on Saturday, 14 November 2026, rapper 50 Cent called the night 'crazy' in an Instagram post.

DiCaprio turned 52 on Wednesday, 11 November, and celebrated with friends three days later. The private party drew several Hollywood figures, including Tobey Maguire, Jonah Hill and Al Pacino.

50 Cent Reacts to DiCaprio's Birthday Bash

The 51-year-old rapper shared a montage of photographs from the celebration on Instagram, teasing those who had missed the invitation.

'You wasn't invited to the party, damn. what does this mean? Leo S— was crazy!' he wrote.

View this post on Instagram

50 Cent offered few details about what happened inside. His caption did not explain whether his remark had any connection to the women filmed arriving together.

According to Page Six, approximately nine women stepped out of a white minibus before heading towards the residence. The report did not identify who arranged their transport or explain why they travelled together.

Among the group was Courtney Boerner, a former Love Island USA contestant, who wore a white minidress with sheer detailing. Most of the other women were not identified in the published coverage.

There is no verified information establishing that DiCaprio personally arranged the women's arrival. The footage shows them travelling together, but does not establish the circumstances behind the journey or their connection to the party.

Photographs published by People showed Casey Affleck, Edward Norton, Adrien Brody, Orlando Bloom and Cara Delevingne attending. Other guests included rapper Ice Spice, Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos. Former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau was also reportedly among those present.

The guest list brought together film stars, musicians and public figures. However, photographs of arrivals provide only a partial view of the private celebration, and do not establish what happened inside.

DiCaprio's Dating History Draws Fresh Attention

The minibus footage prompted comparisons with The Social Network, the 2010 film featuring a college-party scene in which women arrive by bus. The resemblance does not establish that the circumstances of the film scene and DiCaprio's birthday party were alike.

Online discussion also revived jokes about DiCaprio's dating history and the ages of some of his former partners. His relationship with actress Camila Morrone lasted about five years and ended in 2022, shortly after she turned 25.

He previously dated Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bündchen from around 2000 to 2005. His relationship with Israeli model Bar Refaeli ran intermittently from 2005 until 2011, when she was 25.

The timing of those break-ups has been cited in the recurring online joke, but does not establish why either relationship ended. The birthday footage provides no new evidence about DiCaprio's personal life or the guests' private arrangements.

The suggestion that DiCaprio refuses to date women over 25 remains an internet joke, rather than a confirmed personal rule. He was also romantically linked to Gigi Hadid in September 2022, following his separation from Morrone.

According to People, DiCaprio has been romantically involved with Italian model Vittoria Ceretti, 28, since 2023. Page Six reported, citing unnamed sources, that Ceretti attended Saturday's birthday celebration.

excerpt: Florida voters approved Amendment 3, expanding property tax exemptions for eligible homeowners from 2027 while state economists forecast billions of dollars in reduced local government revenue.
headline: Florida's Property Tax Cut May Save Owners Money but Leave Local Budgets Facing an $11.8B Gap by 2031
html_content:
Florida voters approved a sweeping property tax cut on 3 November 2026, offering relief to qualifying homeowners while raising concerns over local government finances.

State economists project the change could reduce annual property tax revenue by $11.83 billion (approximately €10.76 billion and £9.0 billion) by fiscal year 2031–32.

Amendment 3 passed with around 62 per cent of the vote, clearing the 60 per cent threshold required to amend Florida's constitution.

It expands exemptions on primary residences, potentially leaving counties and cities with less money for essential services.

Florida Property Tax Cut Expands Exemptions

From 2027, eligible homeowners can exempt up to $150,000 (approximately €136,447.50 and £113,700) of their property's assessed value from non-school property taxes. The allowance rises to $250,000 (approximately €227,412.50 and £189,500) in 2028, with annual inflation adjustments beginning in 2029.

The change does not mean homeowners receive a payment of that amount. Instead, it lowers the portion of their property's value used to calculate certain taxes.

School district property taxes remain payable. A separate exemption of up to $25,000 (approximately€22,741.25 and £18,950) continues to apply to qualifying homes for school taxes.

Savings will vary according to assessed property values and local tax rates. Some homeowners may see substantial reductions, while others with lower-valued properties could benefit less.

The eligibility rules also distinguish between established residents and newcomers. People who were not permanent Florida residents on 31 December 2026 initially qualify for a smaller non-school exemption of up to $50,000 (approximately €45,481.00 and £37,900) once they obtain homestead status.

They generally become eligible for the larger exemption in their fifth qualifying year, although the amendment allows limited local exceptions subject to legal requirements.

Amendment 3 also lowers the annual cap on increases in assessed values for non-homestead properties, including rental homes and second properties, from 10 per cent to 5 per cent for non-school taxation.

Local Governments Face Revenue Pressures

The Florida Revenue Estimating Conference projects a $4.93 billion (approximately €4.48 billion and £3.7 billion) reduction in local tax collections in fiscal year 2027–28.

The annual impact is expected to grow to $11.83 billion (approximately €10.76 billion and £9.0 billion) by fiscal year 2031–32. Across five fiscal years, the cumulative reduction is estimated at $45.84 billion (approximately €41.70 billion and £34.7 billion).

Counties are expected to bear the largest share, with municipalities and special districts also affected. Lower collections could complicate decisions about funding emergency services, roads and other local responsibilities.

These estimates are forecasts, not confirmed deficits or automatic service cuts. They depend partly on assumptions about property values, tax rates and population changes.

Local officials could review spending, adjust tax rates within legal limits or consider additional fees. Any response could influence whether homeowners' initial savings are partly offset by other costs.

The amendment also limits how counties and municipalities can spend property tax revenue, specifying areas including public safety, infrastructure, education, debt obligations and government operations.

It requires state lawmakers to establish a process for further local exemptions, but does not set a deadline or guarantee that authorities will adopt them.

According to the Florida Department of Revenue, the changes take effect on 1 January 2027 and first apply to the 2027 property tax roll. The agency plans further guidance on administrative rules and tax forms as local governments prepare for implementation.

excerpt: Hackers exploited an Optimizely vulnerability to inject malicious JavaScript into scripts linked to 178 organisations, potentially exposing visitors to cryptocurrency theft, payment-data theft and browser surveillance.
headline: How Hackers Targeted 178 Websites Including CNN, Zoom and IKEA Through Optimizely
html_content:
Hackers exploited a security vulnerability in Optimizely to deliver malicious JavaScript through websites associated with 178 organisations, including CNN, Zoom and IKEA. Cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme disclosed the attack on Monday, 16 November 2026, revealing attempts to steal cryptocurrency, payment information and browser data.

Malicious scripts were also identified on websites associated with HSBC, Equifax and Salesforce, highlighting how compromised third-party software can expose visitors to security threats even when a company's internal systems remain unaffected.

Rather than breaking into each company's internal systems, the attackers targeted a shared platform that allowed malicious instructions to reach visitors' browsers.

The method meant ordinary websites could distribute harmful code without their visitors deliberately downloading suspicious software.

How Hackers Exploited Optimizely to Target Major Websites

Optimizely provides experimentation software that businesses use to test website designs, personalise content and improve online performance.

Its customers load JavaScript files from the platform, allowing Optimizely to execute instructions directly in visitors' browsers.

According to Helme's technical investigation, attackers inserted malicious instructions into the Project JavaScript sections of customer accounts.

Those instructions were then distributed through legitimate Optimizely scripts already trusted by affected websites.

Helme's team examined 1,611 scripts and found malicious code in 188 associated with 178 organisations.

The malware was designed to replace legitimate cryptocurrency wallet addresses with addresses controlled by the attackers.

A visitor copying a wallet address from an affected webpage could unknowingly send funds to a criminal-controlled account.

Other functions attempted to capture payment-card numbers, expiry dates and security codes entered into online forms.

The scripts could also collect accessible browser cookies and webpage screenshots.

The malicious scripts also attempted to deliver the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits to iPhones and iPads running vulnerable software. However, researchers have not established that the campaign successfully compromised any devices.

The attack therefore extended beyond cryptocurrency theft, although investigators have not established how many visitors experienced successful data theft or device compromise.

Helme warned that the attackers could potentially have added more damaging functions to the scripts.

His investigation identified transactions involving attacker-controlled cryptocurrency wallets, but the precise losses attributable to this campaign remain uncertain.

Optimizely Removes Malicious Code as CNN, Zoom and IKEA Face Exposure Questions

Optimizely confirmed that an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup process.

The company said it blocked the vulnerable route, removed injected code, terminated active sessions and revoked affected access tokens.

In an update on Tuesday, 17 November, Helme reported that all 188 identified infected scripts had been cleaned by 11.11pm UTC on Monday.

Cybersecurity firm Hudson Rock separately told Reuters it found evidence that affected websites had served malicious code to visitors.

Salesforce said it was investigating unauthorised script modifications and disabled Optimizely as a precaution.

Equifax stopped using the platform and reported no evidence that its internal systems had been compromised.

IKEA said it was assessing possible effects on its digital services and customers.

HSBC told Reuters that unauthorised scripts were not active on its websites.

The findings do not establish that every affected company experienced an internal breach or that all visitors suffered financial losses.

Helme advised people who used affected websites on 16 November to check cryptocurrency transfers, monitor payment-card statements and update vulnerable Apple devices.

Optimizely said it would continue investigating the incident while strengthening protections for customer accounts.

Cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme disclosed the attack on Monday, 16 November 2026, revealing attempts to steal cryptocurrency, payment information and browser data. Malicious scripts were also identified on websites associated with HSBC, Equifax and Salesforce, highlighting how compromised third-party software can expose visitors to security threats even when a company's internal systems remain unaffected. Rather than breaking into each company's internal systems, the attackers targeted a shared platform that allowed malicious instructions to reach visitors' browsers. The method meant ordinary websites could distribute harmful code without their visitors deliberately downloading suspicious software. How Hackers Exploited Optimizely to Target Major Websites Optimizely provides experimentation software that businesses use to test website designs, personalise content and improve online performance. Its customers load JavaScript files from the platform, allowing Optimizely to execute instructions directly in visitors' browsers. According to Helme's technical investigation, attackers inserted malicious instructions into the Project JavaScript sections of customer accounts. Those instructions were then distributed through legitimate Optimizely scripts already trusted by affected websites. Helme's team examined 1,611 scripts and found malicious code in 188 associated with 178 organisations. The malware was designed to replace legitimate cryptocurrency wallet addresses with addresses controlled by the attackers. A visitor copying a wallet address from an affected webpage could unknowingly send funds to a criminal-controlled account. Other functions attempted to capture payment-card numbers, expiry dates and security codes entered into online forms. The scripts could also collect accessible browser cookies and webpage screenshots. The malicious scripts also attempted to deliver the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits to iPhones and iPads running vulnerable software. However, researchers have not established that the campaign successfully compromised any devices. The attack therefore extended beyond cryptocurrency theft, although investigators have not established how many visitors experienced successful data theft or device compromise. excerpt: Anna Wintour's appearance at Vogue India celebrations for the Earthshot Prize has renewed speculation about her relationship with Meghan Markle, despite their friendly interaction in Paris.
headline: Meghan Markle Faces Fresh 'Snub' Speculation as Anna Wintour Joins Prince William and Kate in Mumbai
html_content:
Meghan Markle has been subject to fresh speculation about her relationship with fashion powerhouse Anna Wintour after the former Vogue editor-in-chief appeared at celebrations connected to Prince William and Kate Middleton's Earthshot Prize in India.

Wintour attended a glamorous gathering hosted by Vogue India ahead of the environmental awards ceremony in Mumbai, adding another high-profile name to the celebrations surrounding the Waleses' visit.

Her appearance attracted attention because of previous reports suggesting that Meghan's relationship with the fashion icon had become strained, despite their warm interaction in Paris last year.

Meghan Markle Faces Fresh Rumours as Anna Wintour Joins Earthshot Celebrations

Wintour was one of the high-profile guests at a Vogue India gathering connected to Prince William's Earthshot Prize celebrations in Mumbai. According to Geo News, the fashion icon attended the event alongside celebrities and influential figures supporting the environmental initiative. The gathering brought together prominent names from fashion, entertainment and international politics, including Rami Malek, Simone Ashley and former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern.

The occasion was part of the wider celebrations surrounding the Earthshot Prize, which Prince William established to recognise innovative solutions to environmental challenges. However, Wintour's involvement sparked speculation about her relationship with Meghan, who has reportedly been eager to strengthen her standing in the fashion industry.

The outlet suggested that Wintour's involvement with the Earthshot Prize could mean another disappointment for the Duchess of Sussex amid rumours of tension between the two women. The gathering was associated with William's environmental initiative, although Wintour's attendance does not confirm that she has distanced herself from Meghan.

Rumours of Meghan and Anna Wintour's Strained Relationship Complicated by Interaction in Paris

Meghan and Wintour have been linked to rumours of a strained relationship for several years. The speculation intensified following reports about Meghan's dealings with British Vogue during Edward Enninful's tenure as editor-in-chief. According to Page Six, Meghan's attempts to secure prominent magazine coverage created friction behind the scenes. The outlet claimed the Duchess had previously reached out to both British and American Vogue.

Her association with Enninful was also reportedly a source of tension, although neither Meghan nor Wintour publicly confirmed a falling-out. Wintour has maintained long-standing connections with the British royal family, including Queen Camilla, contributing to speculation about Meghan's standing with her.

Despite the reported tensions, Meghan and Wintour appeared to be on friendly terms when they crossed paths during Paris Fashion Week in October 2025. The Duchess of Sussex attended the Balenciaga show, where she was filmed greeting the fashion executive. According to Marie Claire, the women exchanged kisses on the cheeks and appeared pleased to see each other. Wintour also complimented Meghan's appearance.

'Beautiful, Cherie. You look amazing,' she reportedly told the Duchess.

The friendly interaction attracted attention because it contradicted earlier claims that their relationship was on the rocks. However, Geo News cited unnamed insiders who suggested that the interaction did not mean tensions had been resolved. The outlet claimed Meghan had been eager to improve relations with Wintour as she pursued opportunities in the fashion industry.

Prince William and Kate Middleton Gather Hollywood Stars to the Earthshot Prize

William and Kate's visit to Mumbai brought together a prominent group of celebrities and environmental activists. According to ITV News, the 17 November Earthshot Prize ceremony featured guests including Malek, Ashley, Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor, and Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar. British pop group Take That also performed at the ceremony, alongside Indian singer Shreya Ghoshal.

The event recognised environmental projects seeking practical solutions to major climate problems. The ceremony recognised five winners from 15 finalists, with each receiving £1 million to expand their environmental initiatives.

The renewed attention on Wintour comes as Meghan continues building her public identity outside her role as a former working royal. Her appearances at high-profile fashion events have generated interest in whether she wants to establish herself further within the industry. However, her relationship with Wintour remains a subject of speculation.

excerpt: Three forensic experts have presented an unpublished analysis disputing the official suicide ruling in Jeffrey Epstein's death, but authorities say no evidence has established homicide.
headline: Was Jeffrey Epstein Murdered? Three Forensic Experts Challenge Suicide Ruling and Raise Fresh Questions
html_content:
Three researchers have challenged the official finding that Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide, presenting new analysis in London on Monday, 16 November 2026. Their findings suggest the convicted sex offender may have been strangled by another person inside a New York jail.

The analysis revisits Epstein's death at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in Manhattan on 10 August 2019, while he awaited trial on federal sex trafficking charges.

New York City's Office of Chief Medical Examiner ruled that Epstein died by suicide by hanging. Federal investigations later found no evidence establishing homicide, despite identifying serious failures in his supervision.

The new analysis disputes the medical interpretation but has not overturned the official ruling.

Jeffrey Epstein Murder Claims Renewed by Forensic Examination

Michael Freeman, a forensic medicine specialist, spent months examining autopsy records and photographs supplied by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein.

He worked with Anders Eriksson, a forensic pathology professor at Sweden's Umeå University, and Itiel Dror, a researcher specialising in forensic decision-making.

Their findings were presented in London on Monday, challenging how injuries to Epstein's neck and body were originally interpreted.

Freeman argued that the evidence was more consistent with homicidal strangulation than suicide by hanging.

'The injuries that were documented by the medical examiner were not consistent with the suicidal hanging,' he told CBS News.

He identified a second, differently angled ligature mark that he said was difficult to explain through hanging.

Freeman also questioned injuries to Epstein's shoulder and back, suggesting they could indicate a physical struggle.

However, the original medical examiner reported finding no defensive wounds characteristic of an assault.

Freeman constructed three-dimensional models using autopsy photographs and a prison officer's later description of the death scene.

He suggested that a narrow, knotted fabric ligature found in the cell might explain the injuries. The fabric he identified was not collected for the medical examiner's investigation.

The reconstruction remains an interpretation of existing evidence. It does not identify an attacker or establish that another person entered Epstein's cell.

Freeman acknowledged that an academic journal had rejected his manuscript. He said reviewers considered it inappropriate to criticise a medical examiner's findings in a peer-reviewed publication. He plans to resubmit the work.

Jeffrey Epstein Suicide Ruling Remains Unchanged Despite New Findings

New York City's Office of Chief Medical Examiner has maintained its original determination.

'Our office stands by its determination,' a spokesperson told CBS News.

A 2023 Justice Department inspector general investigation documented serious failures at the prison, including missed checks, falsified records and surveillance problems.

However, the investigation did not find evidence contradicting the FBI's conclusion that Epstein's death involved no criminality.

In July 2025, the Justice Department and FBI reaffirmed the suicide finding.

Their review cited surveillance footage that investigators said showed nobody entering the relevant housing tiers during the overnight period. The recording covered a common area and parts of the stairways, rather than Epstein's cell door.

Questions about the footage's interpretation and the preservation of evidence have nevertheless continued.

Freeman's findings also echo earlier objections from forensic pathologist Michael Baden, who examined Epstein's death at his brother's request.

In 2020, Baden argued that the neck injuries were more consistent with homicidal strangulation.

Neither independent assessment has changed the official classification of Epstein's death.

Forensic specialists can disagree about injuries associated with hanging and strangulation, particularly when relying on photographs and incomplete scene records.

Freeman's analysis has not identified a suspected killer, and authorities have announced no new homicide finding.

excerpt: Around 2,000 protesters demonstrated in Manila against Donald Trump's visit for the ASEAN summit, burning effigies and opposing US foreign policy and the proposed Pax Silica initiative.
headline: Trump Branded 'World's Number One Terrorist' as Thousands Protest His Arrival in the Philippines
html_content:
US President Donald Trump faced demonstrations in Manila, Philippines, on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, as protesters opposed his arrival for the ASEAN summit. Demonstrators burned effigies of the American leader, while placards displayed during earlier rallies branded him the world's 'number one terrorist'.

The protests followed several days of opposition to American foreign policy and a proposed technology partnership with the Philippines. Demonstrators also criticised President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s relationship with Washington, demanding greater independence in Philippine foreign policy.

The demonstrations coincided with the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, which brought regional leaders to the Philippine capital. Protesters opposed Trump's participation and the US-led Pax Silica initiative, citing concerns about military influence, land rights and economic dependence.

Trump Protest in Manila Sees Effigies Burned as Thousands Rally Against US President

At Liwasang Bonifacio, activists displayed an effigy depicting Trump lying inside a coffin. Members of the cultural group Panday Sining presented the artwork, which became a prominent symbol of opposition to his visit.

The coffin also carried messages from different sectors, including Indigenous Aeta communities, with slogans such as 'Reject Pax Silica' and 'Trump Out'.

Members of the Indigenous Ayta community were also shown setting fire to an effigy bearing Trump's likeness, according to footage shared on social media. The demonstrations reflected opposition to American influence and concerns about proposed development projects affecting local communities.

Members of the Indigenous Ayta community in the Philippines set fire to an effigy bearing Trump’s likeness. pic.twitter.com/sdCxWA3hN8

— Molly Ploofkins (@Mollyploofkins) November 17, 2026

AFP reported that approximately 2,000 demonstrators faced police while carrying banners reading 'Trump out now' and 'Reject Pax Silica'. Organisers had anticipated as many as 10,000 participants, although that figure was an estimate rather than confirmed attendance.

The protests also featured accusations against Trump's foreign policy. Placards displayed during earlier demonstrations described him as the world's 'No 1 terrorist', reflecting campaigners' opposition to American military involvement overseas.

Tensions escalated when police blocked protesters from approaching secured summit areas. Reports described confrontations between demonstrators and officers, with police saying some personnel were injured during the clashes.

The National Capital Region Police Office reported that inquest proceedings had been completed for 213 people arrested during Sunday's demonstration in Muntinlupa. The proceedings concerned possible criminal complaints and did not establish guilt.

Trump Protest in Manila Targets Pax Silica and Washington's Influence

Beyond the demonstrations against Trump, protesters opposed Pax Silica, a US-led initiative focused on strengthening technology supply chains and access to strategic resources.

The proposed development of a semiconductor and industrial hub in New Clark City, Tarlac, has raised concerns among campaigners about displacement and the project's potential effects on Indigenous communities. Protesters have also questioned its implications for local land, water and energy resources. The Philippine government has clarified that the proposed hub will not host AI data centres.

Protest leader Teddy Casiño criticised the Marcos administration's relationship with Washington, urging Philippine leaders to pursue an independent foreign policy rather than follow Trump's priorities.

Trump arrived at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City on Tuesday for diplomatic meetings with regional leaders. His programme included discussions with Quad partners India, Japan and Australia on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit.

🇺🇸🇵🇭

President Trump arrives in Manila, Philippines, where he will attend the ASEAN Summit. pic.twitter.com/RvAtXkfzPY

— The White House (@WhiteHouse) November 17, 2026

The Philippine National Police said it had detected no major security threats before his arrival, despite heightened security around summit venues.

Meanwhile, authorities continued processing complaints against people arrested during earlier demonstrations, as protesters maintained their opposition to Trump's visit and the proposed Pax Silica initiative.

excerpt: JetBlue Flight 1717 landed safely in Fort Lauderdale after severe turbulence on a flight from Puerto Rico. Five people reported injuries or required medical evaluation, but none went to hospital.
headline: Jetblue Flight 1717 Lands in Florida After Turbulence Leaves Five People Needing Medical Evaluation
html_content:
JetBlue Flight 1717 landed safely in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, after reportedly encountering severe turbulence during a flight from Ponce, Puerto Rico. Five people reported injuries or required medical evaluation, according to Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue.

Emergency crews responded at approximately 6.25am after receiving reports of multiple injuries aboard the incoming aircraft. The plane landed at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport at around 6.58am and proceeded to Terminal 3, where medical personnel were waiting to assess those affected.

JetBlue Flight 1717 Lands Safely After Severe Turbulence

Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue identified five people who had reported injuries or required medical evaluation. All five declined transportation to nearby hospitals, and no one was taken to hospital following the incident.

The authorities did not disclose the nature or severity of the reported injuries or provide a breakdown of how many of the five people were passengers and how many were crew members.

Officials also reported no structural damage to the aircraft. However, the absence of reported damage does not establish the extent of any injuries sustained by those on board.

Local 10 reported the incident on Tuesday and said it had contacted JetBlue for comment. The airline separately confirmed to CNN that Flight 1717 had experienced turbulence and that medical personnel evaluated customers and crew members after landing.

The available information confirms that five people reported injuries or needed assessment, but it does not establish that all five sustained medically diagnosed injuries. No further medical findings were included in the initial reports.

Five People Assessed After JetBlue Flight 1717 Arrives

Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue said crews responded at approximately 6.25am after receiving reports of multiple injuries aboard the incoming aircraft. The plane landed at around 6.58am and proceeded to Terminal 3, where rescue personnel were standing by.

The initial reports did not establish where along the route the turbulence occurred, how long it lasted or what conditions caused it. CNN meteorologist Brandon Miller said thunderstorms were affecting the Turks and Caicos and southern Bahamas that morning, and the flight may have been navigating the area. He also noted that other aircraft had reported light to moderate turbulence.

There was no confirmation in the initial accounts that the pilots had declared an emergency or diverted from the planned route. The aircraft continued to Fort Lauderdale and landed safely.

In a statement reported by CNN, JetBlue confirmed that Flight 1717 from Ponce to Fort Lauderdale had experienced turbulence. The airline said medical personnel evaluated customers and crew members after the aircraft landed, and no one was transported to hospital.

The airline reiterated that the safety of its customers and crew members remained its top priority.

excerpt: US officials and Microsoft say there is no evidence AI caused the November disruptions, attributing the Microsoft outage to a software defect and the FAA ground stop to network problems.
headline: Did AI Cause the Microsoft Outage or US Flight Groundings? What Officials Have Revealed About Both Incidents
html_content:
Microsoft and US aviation officials have found no evidence that artificial intelligence caused the separate disruptions affecting Microsoft 365 services and the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) air traffic control network on 12 and 13 November 2026.

The Microsoft outage disrupted workplace services worldwide, while a telecommunications failure prompted the FAA to suspend flight departures across the United States on 13 November. Although the incidents occurred within a day of each other, the available findings point to different technical failures rather than a shared AI-related cause.

Microsoft explicitly said its outage was unrelated to cyber activity or AI agents. Separately, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said investigators had found no evidence of an AI-related cause for the aviation disruption.

Microsoft Outage Exposes Software Defect and Network Problems

Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report traced the global outage to a previously undetected software defect in its networking gateway servers. The defect had been introduced in July but remained undetected until traffic conditions exposed the problem.

Three factors combined to worsen the incident. A routine Microsoft Teams failover increased traffic through the affected gateway, while approximately 14 per cent of server capacity was already unavailable because of an unrelated issue.

As affected servers became unresponsive, traffic was redirected to the remaining infrastructure, spreading the disruption. Microsoft reported that more than 80 per cent of its networking gateway servers became unresponsive at the incident's worst point.

The outage affected Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and Copilot, among other Microsoft 365 services. Users experienced difficulties accessing email and workplace tools, with some messages delayed.

Microsoft said the incident was a technical issue unrelated to cyber activity or AI agents. Engineers worked to restore capacity and stabilise network traffic, with services recovering fully after more than 24 hours of disruption.

The preliminary findings explain how an AI product such as Copilot could be affected by an infrastructure failure without AI being responsible for causing it. The report was labelled preliminary, meaning further technical findings could follow.

FAA Ground Stop Traced to Telecommunications Upgrade

On Friday, 13 November, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop after communications problems affected its air traffic control network. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the restriction as a safety precaution amid unreliable information reaching controllers.

The FAA's initial investigation identified excessive data traffic as a central problem. The agency said its legacy telecommunications equipment became unstable after receiving approximately 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Investigators identified two potential locations involved in the disruption: a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas.

Contractor L3Harris had been carrying out work at the El Dorado facility, including installing a new router. The FAA said it blocked the two locations after identifying inconsistencies in the data, helping to stabilise the network. It also disabled the broadcasting function on the new routers as a precaution.

At a 14 November briefing, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said there was 'zero evidence of anything nefarious' and 'zero evidence of anything AI-related'. He said investigators were still working to identify the defective equipment and establish the root cause.

The FAA reported approximately 12,462 flight cancellations on 13 November, including 9,082 involving major airlines. It cautioned that not all cancellations were directly caused by the ground stop.

Flight operations resumed after the restriction was lifted at approximately 8.15pm ET. However, disruption continued as airlines worked to restore their schedules.

The FAA said some radar feeds and radio frequencies remained operational throughout the incident, allowing controllers and pilots to maintain essential communications and safely land aircraft. Its investigation has focused on the telecommunications network, including the equipment at the two identified sites.

excerpt: Camille Herron compares OnlyFans income with her first Nike deal, offering a personal account of earning beyond traditional sports sponsorship.
headline: World Champion Runner Camille Herron Reveals She Made More on OnlyFans in One Month Than Nike Paid Her in a Year
html_content:
Camille Herron says she earned more in one month creating adult content on OnlyFans than she received in an entire year under her first Nike sponsorship contract, according to her interview with NBC News. The world champion ultrarunner defended the financial motivation behind her decision, saying she had been without major sponsors and was effectively sponsoring herself.

'Well, heck yeah, I'm doing it for the money,' Herron said, responding to criticism of her decision to produce adult content. She also told NBC News that one month's earnings exceeded those from her highest-paid former sponsor 'by a lot', without identifying the company or disclosing the amounts involved.

Sponsorship History and Legal Dispute

In a separate interview with GearJunkie published on 25 September 2026, Herron discussed the controversy surrounding Wikipedia edits to her biography and those of other ultrarunners. She said her husband, Conor Holt, had edited other athletes' pages and denied being involved herself.

Herron also told GearJunkie that she had been without major sponsors for two years and was 'basically sponsoring myself now'.

GearJunkie also reported that lululemon acknowledged ending its sponsorship partnership with Herron 'without cause' and not because of misconduct on her part.

The legal dispute arising from the controversy subsequently reached the US District Court for the District of Arizona.

According to the court's order dated 31 August 2026, Judge Rosemary Marquez granted Gripped Publishing Incorporated's motion to dismiss Herron's lawsuit for lack of personal jurisdiction. The lawsuit included claims of defamation and intentional interference with business contract and expectancies.

The dismissal was without prejudice. The court did not determine the merits of Herron's allegations or rule on whether the publisher had defamed her or interfered with her business relationships.

Established Runner Pursues a Creative Outlet

Herron told GearJunkie that she created her OnlyFans account in February, although it attracted significant attention only later. She explained that she had long wanted to pursue artistic nudity and viewed content creation as an opportunity to explore interests beyond running.

Her sporting achievements are documented on her official website, which identifies her as a multiple-time international ultrarunning champion and world-record holder.

Her biography lists individual IAU World Championship victories in the 50km and 100km events in 2015 and the 24-hour event in 2019, as well as victories in the corresponding team competitions. It also records her 2017 Comrades Marathon victory.

These achievements provide context for her career as an established athlete, although they do not independently establish the value of her previous sponsorship contracts.

Family Encouragement Contrasted With Criticism

In her NBC News interview, Herron said she had discussed her decision with her husband and family, describing their response as supportive.

She recalled sending her mother pictures she was sharing when she began creating adult content, saying her mother praised her body and encouraged her with the words: 'Yes, go for it, girl'.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Camille (@runcamille)

Her husband also encouraged the move, she told GearJunkie. However, Herron described a different response from some people after publicly discussing identifying as a 'hotwife'.

She said some people unfollowed her and called her a sex worker, reactions she associated with shame and stigma rather than support for her choices.

Herron Says She Reviewed Sporting Policies

Addressing potential sporting regulations, Herron told NBC News that she had 'thoroughly vetted' her decision with the US Olympic and Paralympic Committee's Athlete Ombuds office and reviewed her governing body's policies.

The USOPC describes its Athlete Ombuds office as an independent and confidential resource providing advice and assistance to Team USA athletes on sport-related matters. However, its published information does not independently confirm Herron's account of consulting the office. The office's advisory role should also not be interpreted as formal approval of her activities.

Herron qualified her own conclusion, saying: 'So as far as I know, I haven't done anything wrong'. Her statement should not be interpreted as an official USOPC endorsement or a determination that her activities comply with every applicable sporting regulation.

Herron also described OnlyFans as a 'safe, consensual 18-plus platform' and said her decision was partly motivated by what she sees as financial inequalities facing female athletes. 'I want to be sexualized because this is a way to increase my earning power as a female athlete,' she said.

Research has documented financial pressures experienced by women in sport, although the available studies do not establish the earnings gap between Herron and comparable male athletes.

A 2024 BBC survey of 143 elite British sportswomen found that more than three-quarters earned less than £30,000 a year from sport, while more than four in 10 earned less than £10,000.

Separately, a 2024 Parity survey of 500 professional women athletes across 55 sports found that 78% earned $50,000 (about £37,000) or less from sport. Half of the respondents reported no net income after accounting for out-of-pocket sporting expenses.

These findings highlight financial challenges experienced by women athletes but do not establish that gender alone determines individual sponsorship earnings or explain Herron's personal financial circumstances.

For Herron, OnlyFans offers an additional source of income and an opportunity to monetise her image while continuing her sporting career.

excerpt: Curry Barker's horror film Obsession is now streaming on Netflix in the United States after a theatrical run that generated more than $500 million worldwide, according to two box-office trackers.
headline: Obsession Is Now on Netflix US After Turning a Tiny Budget Into a $524 Million Horror Success
html_content:
Obsession is now streaming on Netflix in the United States following a theatrical run that Box Office Mojo values at $524,407,429 (£397.7 million) worldwide. That figure puts Curry Barker's horror film above the half-billion-dollar mark, although The Numbers records a lower total of $521,252,715 (£395.3 million). Both databases agree on domestic earnings, so the difference lies in their international estimates.

The Netflix release gives the film another subscription-streaming home rather than its first. Peacock confirmed that Obsession began streaming on its service on 17 July 2026. Netflix subsequently listed it among its US arrivals for 17 November.

Obsession's Worldwide Box Office Figures Differ

Box Office Mojo breaks its worldwide total into $263,451,715 (£199.8 million) from domestic markets and $260,955,714 (£197.9 million) internationally. The Numbers records the same domestic earnings but puts the international figure at $257,801,000 (£195.5 million). That produces its lower worldwide total, despite the databases agreeing on the domestic figures.

The gap is $3,154,714 (£2.4 million). It does not change the broader picture, as both trackers place the film above $500 million worldwide. However, the distinction matters when quoting an exact figure. The $524.4 million headline figure is a rounded version of Box Office Mojo's estimate, not a total agreed upon by both databases.

The theatrical dates also depend on the territory. Focus Features lists 15 May 2026 as the US release date, while The Numbers records international openings in France, Belgium and Finland on 13 May. The film therefore reached some overseas cinemas before its US debut. Describing 15 May as its worldwide opening would be inaccurate.

What Obsession Brings to Netflix

Barker wrote and directed the film. Michael Johnston plays Bear, while Inde Navarrette portrays Nikki. Cooper Tomlinson, Megan Lawless and Andy Richter play Ian, Sarah and Carter, respectively. Bear is a hopeless romantic who struggles to tell Nikki how he feels, but she does not reciprocate his feelings.

Desperate to win her affection, Bear eventually turns to a mysterious object called the One Wish Willow, hoping it will make Nikki fall in love with him. The wish appears to work, but things take a dark turn when the affection that follows becomes obsessive and frightening. What Bear wanted was simple enough. Living with the result is not.

Bear's decision avoids the possibility of rejection, but it also means Nikki has no say in how the relationship begins. That imbalance takes the film's horror in a more unsettling direction. In a conventional romance, Bear would have to risk rejection and accept Nikki's answer. The One Wish Willow removes that uncertainty, raising a darker question about whether affection obtained through a wish can ever be genuine.

Peacock describes the film as a contemporary reworking of W. W. Jacobs' short story The Monkey's Paw, bringing its wish-gone-wrong premise into a modern relationship. The connection places Barker's story within a familiar horror tradition, while keeping its central conflict focused on Bear and Nikki.

Netflix's announcement applies specifically to the United States. It does not establish that the film is arriving on the service in every country on the same day. Viewers elsewhere will need to check their regional Netflix catalogues for availability.

excerpt: Director Francis Lawrence says The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will condense sections before and after the 50th Games without confirming which specific scenes may change.
headline: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Director Reveals Why the Film Changes Suzanne Collins' Book
html_content:
Francis Lawrence has explained why The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will compress parts of Suzanne Collins' novel, identifying the period before the 50th Hunger Games and the story's aftermath as sections that need a tighter approach on screen. Speaking to Digital Spy in an interview published on 15 November, the director said he had discussed the adaptation with Collins after reading the manuscript twice. The film opens in UK cinemas on 20 November 2026.

Lawrence said the production's established process is to spend about a week in New York with Collins, breaking down the book before deciding how its narrative can work as a film. One section he singled out comes between a late-night visit in which Beetee brings Haymitch part of the plan and the start of the Games. That stretch would probably need compression, he said. He also identified the material after the Games as an area where the filmmakers would have to tighten the novel's structure.

That does not mean every major event will necessarily appear unchanged. Lawrence said compression would not automatically mean losing story points; the filmmakers would need to rearrange material to suit the pace and structure of the film. He did not provide a scene-by-scene account or confirm which individual events, if any, would be removed.

Why the 50th Hunger Games Creates a Different Challenge

Based on Collins' 2025 novel, Sunrise on the Reaping takes place 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games. It follows 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, played by Joseph Zada, from District 12 as he is drawn into the 50th annual Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell. For this edition, each district must send twice its usual number of tributes, making it the largest Games to that point.

The film's official synopsis says Haymitch forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner, played by Mckenna Grace, and joins a coalition seeking to challenge the Capitol's control. The story follows his attempt to undermine the Games from within the arena, with events that help set a wider rebellion in motion.

Lawrence said he found this novel easier to adapt than Collins' earlier prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, which he described as more difficult structurally. That is his assessment of the adaptation process, not a suggestion that Sunrise on the Reaping presented no challenges. His comments identify specific passages that need to be condensed rather than offering a complete account of the changes.

A Return To Familiar Hunger Games Spectacle

Lawrence has also compared Sunrise on the Reaping with 2013's The Hunger Games: Catching Fire. He said the new film brings back elements audiences associate with the franchise, including reaping ceremonies, train journeys to the Capitol, chariot appearances and tribute interviews.

He noted that these features do not appear in the same way in the Mockingjay films or The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes. The comparison helps explain what he means by a return to form: alongside Haymitch's story, the film revisits the public rituals and spectacle surrounding the Games.

Lawrence has not disclosed the full extent of the adaptation's changes. His comments establish where the film is likely to move more quickly, but not how every sequence will differ from Collins' book.
