excerpt: Nathan Cofnas refuses to apologise to Jason Arday's family during an Oxford speech as hundreds protest outside Oriel College over his controversial appearance.
headline: Nathan Cofnas Refuses to Apologise to Jason Arday's Family as Hundreds Protest His Oxford Speech
html_content:
Academic Nathan Cofnas refused to apologise to the family of late Cambridge professor Jason Arday during a controversial speech at Oxford University on Tuesday, 17 November, as hundreds of protesters gathered outside Oriel College. The confrontation followed months of controversy over Cofnas's allegations about Arday's academic work, which preceded the professor's resignation and death in August.

Despite a petition attracting more than 30,000 signatures opposing the event, Cofnas delivered his lecture on diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policies to a relatively small audience. Demonstrators condemned his views and questioned the university's decision to provide a venue.

Cofnas Refuses to Apologise Over Arday Allegations

During the question-and-answer session, Cofnas was asked whether he wanted to apologise to Arday's family. According to The Guardian, Cofnas declined to apologise, arguing that the question implied 'we shouldn't criticise powerful figures'.

He subsequently criticised Cambridge University, alleging that officials had protected Arday from criticism concerning his academic work. His response reportedly received brief applause from some attendees.

Cofnas had publicly questioned aspects of Arday's doctoral thesis and personal biography earlier this year, contributing to a wider debate about the professor's academic record. Arday denied plagiarism but acknowledged mistakes in his doctoral work. Liverpool John Moores University, which awarded his doctorate, investigated the concerns and upheld its decision to award the qualification.

Hundreds Protest Cofnas's Oxford Speech

Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside Oriel College, carrying placards bearing Arday's name and chanting in his memory. According to The Guardian, approximately 40 people attended Cofnas's lecture, leaving much of the venue empty. The Times reported a lower estimate of 26 attendees.

The demonstration remained audible inside the building, while police attended towards the end of the event to clear entrances. Photographer Misan Harriman joined protesters, criticising the decision to allow Cofnas to speak. The event, titled An Evening With Nathan Cofnas: Is DEI Undermining Higher Education?, was organised by the Oxon Universities' Reform Society, a student group supporting Reform UK.

Crowds have gathered at Oxford University’s Oriel College in protest against a talk by sacked Cambridge researcher Nathan Cofnas who sparked media frenzy over Professor Jason Arday. Video from Oxford student newspaper Cherwell. https://t.co/1PcYnmi5oG

— Melissa Sigodo (@melissasigodo) November 17, 2026

Arday's Death and Academic Controversy

Arday, who became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023, resigned from his position on 5 August following weeks of allegations and public criticism.

He died at his London home on 14 August, aged 41. His family subsequently condemned what they described as a campaign of misinformation and appealed for an end to unwanted contact from journalists.

An inquest into his death opened later that month, with police stating that the circumstances were not suspicious. No final conclusion had been publicly established as of 18 November.

There has been no official finding that Cofnas's actions caused Arday's death.

Why Oxford Allowed Cofnas To Speak

The invitation attracted opposition from nearly 50 Oriel academics, who criticised Cofnas's views as racist and lacking scientific foundation. However, more than 170 academics reportedly supported allowing the event to proceed on freedom-of-speech grounds.

Oriel College maintained that providing a venue did not amount to endorsing Cofnas's views. The controversy also prompted questions about student safety, with university officials defending their responsibility to protect lawful expression while assessing potential risks.

Cofnas's refusal to apologise came nearly three months after Arday's death. His family had previously condemned the public allegations against him and asked journalists to respect their privacy. There has been no reported response from the family to Cofnas's remarks at Oxford.

excerpt: Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo Fiona is under intensive veterinary supervision after swallowing a knitted hat that entered her enclosure through an unlikely chain of events.
headline: Cincinnati Zoo Hippo 'Fiona' Under 24-Hour Care After Swallowing A Visitor's Knitted Hat
html_content:
Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippopotamus Fiona is receiving round-the-clock veterinary attention after swallowing part of a visitor's knitted hat that accidentally entered her enclosure. The incident has prompted concern among her followers, with specialists facing a challenging task to help the nine-year-old animal pass the foreign object safely.

The Cincinnati Zoo confirmed on 16 November that Fiona had ingested an object accidentally thrown into her habitat earlier in the month. The item was identified as a knitted hat that entered the enclosure on 8 November following an unusual chain of events.

According to zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley, a child tossed the hat into the air near Fiona's habitat. It became caught in a ceiling fan, which propelled it through a one-foot (30cm) opening above the enclosure's 12-foot-tall (3.7m) viewing windows.

'We probably couldn't make that happen again if we tried. It was clearly an accident,' Curley told local media.

'Her care team is cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self,' the zoo said in a social media statement.

Fiona has since been removed from public view while her condition is monitored. The zoo also urged visitors to secure their belongings and immediately notify staff if anything falls into an animal habitat.

Veterinary Team Faces Challenges Treating Famous Hippo

An update on 17 November revealed that Fiona's appetite had decreased, prompting further medical intervention. Her care team administered fluids, enemas and medication to help move the material through her digestive system.

Specialists from Columbus Zoo also assisted with a colonoscopy using a nine-foot-long (2.7m) scope. However, the procedure could not reach far enough to locate the material.

Cincinnati Zoo director of animal health Dr Mike Wenninger explained that surgery was not a viable option for a fully grown hippopotamus.

'The scope's about nine feet long, and we weren't able to reach any farther than that,' he said.

An ultrasound showed some bunching of Fiona's intestines, suggesting that material might be moving through her small intestine. Vets are continuing supportive treatment, including pain relief and anti-nausea medication, while monitoring her progress.

'The best chance for success is if she can pass this on her own,' Wenninger said.

The situation remains concerning because swallowed foreign objects can cause intestinal blockages, internal injuries and potentially life-threatening complications.

Fiona's Early Survival and Other Zoo Incidents

Fiona became an international sensation after arriving six weeks prematurely in January 2017. She weighed just 29 pounds (13.2kg), considerably below the normal birth weight for a Nile hippopotamus, and initially required intensive care because she could not stand or nurse independently.

Her survival attracted millions of followers online and turned her into one of Cincinnati Zoo's most recognisable animals.

Her latest medical emergency also highlights a recurring problem at wildlife attractions: animals swallowing objects introduced into their habitats by visitors. Zoo Miami's former communications director Ron Magill has previously discussed similar incidents involving captive animals swallowing items such as water bottles and sunglasses, sometimes requiring surgical removal.

For now, Fiona remains under close veterinary supervision, with the zoo expected to provide further updates as her care continues.

excerpt: Former UFC fighter Felice Herrig said OnlyFans earnings exceeded her MMA income, helping fund rehabilitation and allowing her to delay returning after two knee operations.
headline: I Make More Money Than Fighting: Former UFC Star's OnlyFans Revelation After Two Brutal Knee Surgeries
html_content:
Former UFC fighter Felice Herrig revealed that her OnlyFans earnings surpassed what she made in mixed martial arts, explaining how the income helped her recover from two serious knee operations without rushing back into competition.

The comments, reported in July 2022, have resurfaced in coverage published on 17 November 2026. Herrig described the financial pressures facing injured fighters and the freedom that an alternative income provided during her lengthy rehabilitation.

How OnlyFans Changed Herrig's Recovery

Herrig underwent two anterior cruciate ligament operations and spent much of the following two years away from the Octagon.

Without regular fights, she faced the prospect of extended periods without competition pay, even as treatment and recovery expenses continued.

Speaking on the Fighter vs. the Writer podcast in 2022, Herrig said she earned more from OnlyFans than she had earned through fighting.

She explained that the subscription platform paid her weekly, removing some of the pressure to return before she felt physically prepared.

Herrig said she might otherwise have resumed fighting earlier because of financial necessity, despite concerns about whether her knee was ready.

The additional income also helped cover services she chose to pay for herself, including regular massages and specialist treatment during rehabilitation.

Although she acknowledged the UFC's medical resources, Herrig noted that she lived outside Las Vegas and could not easily access its Performance Institute on a daily basis.

She distinguished between treatment covered by existing arrangements and the extra support she personally wanted throughout recovery.

Why Two Knee Surgeries Threatened Her Career

The anterior cruciate ligament helps stabilise the knee, particularly during twisting and sudden changes of direction common in combat sports.

Recovering from reconstruction typically involves progressive rehabilitation to rebuild strength, movement and confidence before an athlete returns to demanding activity.

The NHS advises that recovery can take several months, while returning to sport may take up to a year, depending on individual progress.

Herrig's situation illustrated a financial dilemma for competitors whose earnings depend heavily on being healthy enough to compete.

The Fight That Marked Her UFC Farewell

Herrig returned against Karolina Kowalkiewicz at UFC Vegas 56 on 4 June 2022, losing by submission in the second round.

She announced her retirement from mixed martial arts afterwards, explaining that she had wanted to prove she could return following both operations.

The American had spent eight years in the UFC and around two decades involved in combat sports, which she said had taken a physical toll.

Her retirement did not immediately end her involvement in fighting. In July 2022, she signed with Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship to pursue another opportunity in boxing.

In a separate July 2022 interview, Herrig said BKFC had tripled her UFC contract and would also allow her to take professional boxing bouts, giving her another potential route to earn money through combat sports.

Herrig's financial comparison was her own account, not an independently audited breakdown of income from either activity.

Nevertheless, her remarks highlighted how earnings outside competition can change an injured athlete's options, allowing recovery decisions to depend less directly on the timing of the next payday.

excerpt: Kysre Gondrezick was the fourth pick of the 2021 WNBA draft and played just 24 games. Now she is monetising her brand on Fanvue as the league's new deal sends salaries soaring.
headline: Former No. 4 WNBA Pick Kysre Gondrezick Turns to OF Alternative Fanvue After Just 24 Career Games in the League
html_content:
Kysre Gondrezick was the fourth pick of the 2021 Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) draft. Five years and just 24 games later, the guard most fans never saw play is monetising her life on Fanvue, the London-based subscription platform rivalling OnlyFans.

From Lottery Pick to Repeated Cuts

Gondrezick arrived in Indianapolis as the highest draft pick in West Virginia University history, a scorer who once averaged more than 40 points a game in high school and was named Michigan's Miss Basketball.

The professional fit never held, despite her impressive college basketball credentials. Indiana waived her in January 2022, before her rookie deal ran out, the second straight lottery pick the Fever cut early.

A short stint with the Chicago Sky ended the same way in June 2024. League records showed 24 career games, 41 total points, and an average of 1.7 points a game. Her Hoop Stats records $70,040 for 2021 and $30,489 for 2024, totalling $100,529 (£79,000) in reported salary figures.

The Pay Revolution She Missed

Her timing stings. In 2026, the WNBA and its players' union signed a new collective bargaining agreement that lifted the salary cap from $1.5 million (£1.14 million) to $7 million (£5.32 million) projected the average salary at $583,000 (£443,330), and more than quadrupled the minimum salary.

The rookie minimum now sits at $270,000 (£213,000), and 2026 No. 1 pick Azzi Fudd earns $500,000 (£394,000) in one season, with more than $2.2 million (£1.7 million) possible across four years.

The pay gap had become a flashpoint, with stars publicly questioning why a league breaking attendance and viewership records still ran on an old scale.

Paige Bueckers, the 2025 No. 1 pick, earned $78,831 (£62,000) as a rookie, less than Gondrezick's combined recorded WNBA salary.

A top-five pick today would exceed that amount in weeks. She left the league before the money arrived.

A Brand Beyond Basketball

While the basketball dried up, the brand grew. Gondrezick became a New York Fashion Week regular, sat front row with NBA star Jaylen Brown, turned up at the Victoria's Secret show, and in October 2025 was named Playboy's Miss June, becoming what she described as the magazine's first Black professional athlete Playmate.

Fashion appearances followed even as her on-court minutes vanished. She framed the modelling move as planned, not forced. 'What people label as a transition, I embody as evolution,' she said in remarks reported by TMZ. 'I'm building a multidimensional brand.'

Not OnlyFans, She Insists

The Fanvue move, revealed to Page Six in May 2026, fits that arc, extending her growing reach beyond basketball.

The London-based, AI-powered platform lets creators charge monthly fees, and Gondrezick's page promises lifestyle, fashion, beauty, and training content rather than adult advertising.

She pushed back hard on assumptions that she had joined OnlyFans, even threatening legal action over the rumours. 'This version of me grants permission to be human rather than performative,' she said.

Gondrezick is not alone. Swiss footballer Alisha Lehmann joined the same platform, part of a wave of young women athletes monetising audiences online as leagues debate what they are owed. A torn Achilles sustained in January 2026 now clouds her playing future.

For one of the highest picks of her draft class, the court has become the smallest part of the story.

excerpt: Taylor Swift will return to the CMA Awards after 13 years as a TikTok compilation of her early performances prompts debate about her vocals
headline: Taylor Swift Returns to CMA After 13 Years as Old Performance Clips Resurface and Fans Debate Her Vocals
html_content:
Taylor Swift is preparing to return to the Country Music Association (CMA) Awards stage on Wednesday, 18 November, 13 years after her last performance at the ceremony. Her comeback comes as a compilation of her CMA performances from 2007 to 2013 circulates on TikTok, prompting debate about her early vocals and development as a singer.

Shared on TikTok, the footage has drawn contrasting reactions. Some users criticised Swift's pitch, delivery and accent, while others defended her, arguing that she was young and still developing as an artist.

Swift's return will take place at the 60th Annual CMA Awards in Nashville. Although she last performed at the ceremony in 2013, she attended in 2016, presenting Garth Brooks with the Entertainer of the Year award. Her upcoming appearance marks her return to the performance lineup, not her first appearance at the event in 13 years.

Taylor Swift's CMA Return After 13 Years

The CMA and ABC announced on 13 November that Swift would perform at this year's ceremony. She first attended the CMAs in 2006 and won the Horizon Award in 2007. In 2009, she became the youngest artist to win Entertainer of the Year, a record she still holds. She has won the category twice.

Swift is also nominated for Single of the Year for 'I Knew It, I Knew You', giving her 26 career CMA nominations.

TikTok Compilation Revisits Early CMA Performances

The TikTok compilation brings together Swift's CMA performances from 2007 to 2013, allowing viewers to revisit her early appearances ahead of her return.

Some commenters described her singing as 'pitchy' and questioned her vocal ability. Others criticised her accent and delivery, with some saying the performances were less impressive than they remembered.

The responses were not uniformly negative. Other users pointed to Swift's age during the early performances and argued that her voice and stage presence developed over time. Some praised her for singing live and said her growth as a vocalist should be considered when judging the footage.

What Swift Performed at the CMAs

Swift's final CMA performance took place in 2013, when she received the Pinnacle Award and sang 'Red' alongside Vince Gill and Alison Krauss. It was her last time performing on the CMA stage.

The footage traces her rise from a country performer to an established, internationally recognised artist before she expanded her career beyond the genre.

What To Expect From the 2026 Ceremony

The 60th Annual CMA Awards will take place at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday, 18 November. Hosted by Lainey Wilson for the third consecutive year, the ceremony will air from 8pm to 11pm Eastern Time on ABC and Disney+, with streaming on Hulu the following day.

Swift is among the announced performers, alongside Luke Combs, Miranda Lambert, Kacey Musgraves, Megan Moroney and Tim McGraw. The programme will also include a tribute to Dolly Parton and special collaborations involving Chris Stapleton.

The CMA has confirmed Swift's performance but has not announced her setlist. Her return puts her back on the stage where she last sang in 2013, as viewers revisit the performances that marked her early years in country music.

excerpt: Kate Middleton wore a red Mahima Mahajan Anarkali at the Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai, after Kensington Palace arranged alterations to a garment stocked by a London boutique.
headline: Kate Middleton's Red Anarkali Steals the Show at Mumbai Earthshot Gala as Prince William Matches Her in Black
html_content:
Kate Middleton made a striking return to the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Tuesday, 17 November, wearing a red Anarkali by Indian designer Mahima Mahajan. Prince William wore a black bandhgala designed by another Indian designer, Manish Malhotra, with both royals choosing Indian fashion for the environmental awards ceremony.

The appearance also revealed an unexpected story behind Kate's outfit. According to Mahajan, the dress was originally stocked at a London boutique before Kensington Palace requested alterations for the Princess.

Red Anarkali's London Boutique Backstory

In an interview with Variety India published on 18 November, Mahajan revealed that Kensington Palace had approached Lily's Boutique in London approximately a month before the ceremony. The boutique already stocked her Neelam Anarkali, which was subsequently sent to Kate for a fitting.

'She fell in love with the garment,' Mahajan told the publication. However, the available size was too large, prompting the Palace to contact the designer's team for alterations. Mahajan said her team received photographs outlining the adjustments required, although they were initially unaware whether the Princess would wear the outfit publicly.

The revelation clarified that Kate's Anarkali began as an existing boutique garment rather than an entirely new design commissioned for the occasion. The floor-length outfit featured a rich vermilion shade, handwoven silk georgette and gold Banarasi detailing, alongside intricate embroidery and glass-bead embellishments.

A royal affair! ✨ #PrinceWilliam and #KateMiddleton bring regal elegance to the #EarthshotPrize2026. #FilmfareLens https://t.co/ITwdDWMB1L

— Filmfare (@filmfare) November 17, 2026

Kate Wears Queen Elizabeth II's Emerald Jewellery

Kate paired the Indian-designed outfit with a diamond-and-emerald necklace and matching earrings from Queen Elizabeth II's Emerald Tassel Suite. According to British Vogue, she completed the ensemble with a burgundy velvet Prada evening bag.

The jewellery added a royal connection to the Indian outfit, with the Princess reportedly wearing the necklace for the first time. Kate's appearance was also her first at an Earthshot Prize ceremony since Boston in 2022, following her absence from the events in Singapore, Cape Town and Rio de Janeiro.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by The Prince and Princess of Wales (@princeandprincessofwales)

Prince William Wears Black Manish Malhotra Bandhgala

Prince William complemented Kate's red Anarkali with a bespoke black bandhgala by Indian designer Manish Malhotra. The traditional high-collared jacket featured a structured silhouette and was paired with black trousers and formal shoes.

Their outfits brought together two prominent Indian designers at an international event celebrating environmental innovation. The Mumbai ceremony also marked the couple's return to India approximately a decade after their previous official visit in 2016.

Earthshot Prize 2026 Winners Announced in Mumbai

The sixth Earthshot Prize ceremony took place at Mumbai's Jio World Convention Centre, with approximately 5,000 guests attending, according to the organisation. Hosted by filmmaker Karan Johar, the evening featured appearances by Alia Bhatt, Sachin Tendulkar and Rami Malek, alongside performances by Shreya Ghoshal and Take That.

Five environmental initiatives received £1 million each. According to the Earthshot Prize's official announcement, the winners included India's Mahindra Last Mile Mobility for clean air, Bhutan for nature restoration, Niue Ocean Wide Trust for ocean conservation, PFAS-Free France for waste reduction and Denmark's Ørsted for climate action.

Mahindra's recognition highlighted India's growing electric transport sector, with the company developing electric rickshaws as an alternative to conventional vehicles. Earlier in the visit, William had driven one of the company's electric three-wheelers during an engagement focused on sustainable transport.

excerpt: Christopher Nolan says he is not troubled by The Odyssey being watched on mobile devices, as the IMAX-shot epic reaches streaming amid growing Oscar speculation.
headline: Christopher Nolan Says 'As Long As I'm Getting Paid' on Watching 'The Odyssey' on Mobile Devices
html_content:
The first-ever feature film shot on IMAX is now available on streaming. For the visual architect behind it, it's no big deal if his masterpiece is now playing on mobile screens.

While Christopher Nolan clearly poured his heart and soul into the making of The Odyssey, which is now available on digital platforms, he doesn't appear to be fazed by the reality that his film will now be displayed on a smaller scale.

'As long as I'm getting paid,' Nolan said. 'It's actually fun to see people watching my films on planes. Because it's a very concentrated experience.'

For over two decades, Nolan has directed blockbuster flicks that are as dazzling with their cinematography as they are dense in plot construction. But The Odyssey, starring Matt Damon as Homeric protagonist Odysseus, took the visual spectacle to another level as the first feature film shot entirely with IMAX 15-perf/65mm film cameras.

A movie with that level of technical craftsmanship sounds like an experience meant to be enjoyed in a sophisticated cinema. Nolan, however, recognizes that the consumption of The Odyssey is not something that he can gatekeep.

'People watch movies the way they want to watch movies. In the course of my lifetime, the way we're able to engage with movies at home has gone forward leaps and bounds, from VHS to DVD to streaming at 4K. I'm actually excited for it to reach a new audience,' he said.

The Oscar Buzz Surrounding 'The Odyssey'

Whether The Odyssey is playing inside a moviehouse or streaming on a tablet, the acting performances in this Greek epic come across clearly as top-tier. Since the film came out this past summer, there's been buzz surrounding Damon and the end of his decades-long acting Oscars drought. In late July, Variety quoted an anonymous Oscar voter as saying, 'I think Matt has to win the Oscar. He has to.'

When the same outlet released its predictions for Oscar nominations and winners last week, it wasn't just Damon who made the cut. John Leguizamo, who plays Odysseus' loyal slave Eumeus, was named an Oscar nominee for Best Supporting Actor. Anne Hathaway (Penelope) and Samantha Morton (Circe) were projected to get nods for Best Supporting Actress, with Hathaway eyed by Variety as the winner.

As for technical Oscars, the record books show that Nolan has a strong track record. Films like 2008's The Dark Knight, 2010's Inception, and 2017's Dunkirk have been nominated in categories like cinematography, art direction, and visual effects. At the 2024 Academy Awards ceremony, Oppenheimer took home Best Cinematography and Best Film Editing, along with the grand prize of Best Picture.

In all likelihood, The Odyssey will be in the running for several categories when the Oscar nominations are announced in January. By then, legions of fans will have replayed, dissected, and appreciated the film on a host of mobile gadgets. That wasn't exactly the viewing experience that Nolan was gunning for when he worked on The Odyssey, but for more than one good reason, the Academy Award-winning director doesn't appear to mind.

excerpt: Jaylin and Cardo's alleged breakup sparks debate as TikTok viewers question whether their latest relationship drama is genuine or another staged skit
headline: Jaylin and Cardo's Breakup Drama Leaves Fans Asking if Their Rolex and Chanel Row Is Just Another Skit
html_content:
Jaylin and Cardo's alleged breakup has prompted debate on TikTok, with viewers questioning whether the Rolex and Chanel row marks a genuine split or another staged relationship storyline.

The names Rolex and Chanel refer to Jaylin and Cardo, who became known by the nicknames following their famous Rolex and Chanel video. Their videos have also included breakup claims and pranks. That history has become important to the reaction, with some viewers treating the latest posts as another instalment rather than confirmation that the pair have separated.

TikTok Posts Fuel Breakup Speculation

One TikTok post claims, 'so basically they both cheated yall hating on jalyn but it both of them', putting cheating allegations at the centre of the discussion. However, the caption does not establish that either creator was unfaithful.

A separate TikTok shows Jaylin and Cardo appearing on a live call from different locations, with Jaylin seemingly sitting in a garage. During the exchange, Cardo said: 'No matter how much ... work I put in to save the ... relationship ... they still would have told you to do it'.

The footage has fuelled speculation about whether the breakup is genuine or another staged storyline. One viewer commented, 'He sitting in the garage', while others questioned whether the pair had separated. Cardo's remarks suggest frustration over efforts to save the relationship, but the available excerpt does not establish what prompted them or confirm that the pair have split.

Why Viewers Suspect Another Skit

The scepticism has a history. The pair's breakup-themed uploads stretch back several years, including a YouTube video titled 'We broke up... & heres what happened', published on 9 August 2020, and 'HE BROKE UP WITH ME PRANK GONE WRONG', published on 18 September 2024.

More recent uploads have kept similar themes in circulation. Videos titled 'we broke up?' and 'Divorce' appeared on 23 and 30 October 2026, respectively. Their titles do not prove the latest dispute is staged, but they help explain why viewers are questioning whether the current drama is genuine.

The comments reflect that divide. 'They do this every year' and 'They didn't even break up' challenge the idea that the posts document a real separation. Others were less convinced, with one commenter writing, 'It's a skit y'all', while another said, 'I don't believe this'.

Other reactions add to the uncertainty. One commenter claimed to have checked the pair's account and found them still together, presenting a contradiction to the breakup claims. That comment is not independent confirmation that Jaylin and Cardo remain together.

Another asked, 'What about the baby?' This comment does not independently establish family circumstances or provide evidence about the relationship.

The cheating claims, live-call footage and comments remain competing pieces of an incomplete picture. Neither the supplied posts nor the reactions confirm that Jaylin and Cardo have ended their relationship. Their history of breakup-themed content gives viewers a reason to question the latest storyline, but it is not proof that this row is a skit.

Recycled formats can encourage suspicion, but cannot establish what happened privately between them.

excerpt: Screenshots circulating on X allegedly show a Spanish professor suspending homework and postponing an exam for GTA VI's launch, but the email and academic changes remain unverified.
headline: Professor Allegedly Cancels Homework for GTA 6 Launch Week After Recalling GTA 5 in 2013
html_content:
A viral email circulating online claims that a professor in Spain cancelled homework and postponed an examination so students could enjoy the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, reportedly drawing inspiration from his own memories of GTA V's launch in 2013.

Screenshots of the purported message were shared on X on Monday, 16 November 2026. However, the email has not been independently authenticated, and there is no verified confirmation that the alleged changes to students' academic schedules occurred.

Viral Email Claims Professor Remembered GTA 5's Launch

The screenshots, shared by an X account called ElBuni, appeared to show a professor explaining why he wanted students to enjoy GTA VI's anticipated release on Thursday, 19 November.

The purported sender recalled being the same age as his students when GTA V launched in September 2013. According to the circulating message, he remembered the excitement of returning home to play the game and discussing it with friends.

The email suggested that those memories inspired the alleged decision to give students additional free time. It claimed that homework, projects, and submission deadlines would be suspended for the professor's subject during launch week.

An examination supposedly scheduled for 23 November would also be postponed until 30 November. However, neither the professor's identity nor the institution involved has been independently verified.

No authenticated school announcement or confirmed student testimony has established that these arrangements were implemented.

Un profesor ha querido dar una sorpresa a sus alumnos por el lanzamiento de GTA VI: les ha enviado un correo electrónico librándole de deberes y atrasándoles un examen para que puedan jugarlo. pic.twitter.com/jkn6da3Ura

— ceciarmy (@ceciarmy) November 16, 2026

The Unexpected Catch Behind the Alleged Break

The circulating message also offered an explanation for why students had reportedly faced a heavier workload before the anticipated release. According to the screenshots, the professor apologised for assigning additional work during the previous week.

He allegedly explained that advancing through the syllabus had created enough time to reduce academic responsibilities during GTA VI's launch.

The supposed arrangement therefore involved completing work earlier rather than abandoning academic requirements entirely.

The message also reportedly encouraged students to enjoy the game responsibly, acknowledging that some content might not be suitable for their age. The message also warned that normal coursework would resume after launch week ended.

These details have attracted attention because they suggest an unusual attempt to balance academic expectations with enthusiasm for a major entertainment release. Nevertheless, they remain claims contained in an unauthenticated message.

Multiple publications reproducing the same screenshots do not independently establish that the email was genuine.

What Is Confirmed About GTA 6?

Rockstar Games has officially scheduled Grand Theft Auto VI for release on 19 November 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The game takes players to Vice City and the fictional state of Leonida, marking the franchise's return more than 13 years after GTA V's original release. That lengthy gap provides context for the nostalgia described in the alleged professor's email.

However, Rockstar's confirmed release information does not substantiate the separate claims about classroom arrangements.

For now, the story remains an example of the interest surrounding GTA VI rather than a verified account of a professor changing students' schedules. Whether the alleged academic concessions actually occurred remains unconfirmed.

The viral claim has attracted attention, but independent confirmation remains unavailable.

excerpt: The Leonid meteor shower reaches its 2026 peak overnight on 17–18 November, with the best viewing after moonset, before dawn and away from artificial light.
headline: Leonid Meteor Shower 2026: When and Where to Watch the Peak Pre-Dawn Viewing Hours After Moonset
html_content:
The Leonid meteor shower is reaching its annual peak on 17 and 18 November 2026, offering skywatchers across the UK, United States and other regions an opportunity to see shooting stars before sunrise.

NASA recommends watching during the early morning hours after the Moon sets, when darker skies improve visibility. Under ideal conditions, observers could see approximately 15 meteors per hour, although actual sightings may be considerably fewer.

When Is the Best Time to Watch the Leonids?

The strongest viewing opportunities fall overnight from 17 into 18 November, with the hours between midnight and dawn generally offering favourable conditions.

In the UK, observers should look to the sky after midnight GMT, especially in the hours before sunrise. Across the United States, the same midnight-to-dawn guidance applies in each local time zone, provided skies remain clear.

The Moon reaches its first-quarter phase on 17 November, meaning moonlight could initially obscure fainter meteors. However, its setting around midnight in many locations should leave darker skies during the most promising viewing period.

Exact moonset times vary geographically, making local astronomical forecasts useful when planning an observation session. Although the predicted maximum occurs around these dates, the shower remains active beyond its peak.

Where Can You See the Leonid Meteor Shower?

The Leonids are visible from both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, although viewing conditions differ depending on location.

The meteors appear to originate from Leo, the constellation that gives the shower its name. However, NASA advises observers not to concentrate exclusively on Leo because meteors can streak across different parts of the sky.

Instead, viewers should choose an open location away from streetlights and buildings, allowing a wide view overhead.

NASA recommends lying comfortably with feet facing east and allowing approximately 30 minutes for eyesight to adjust to darkness. Telescopes and binoculars are unnecessary because they restrict the field of view needed to spot passing meteors.

Cloud cover, artificial lighting, and the height of Leo above the horizon can all influence the number visible.

How Many Shooting Stars Could Appear?

NASA's November skywatching forecast suggests the Leonids could produce around 15 meteors per hour under ideal conditions.

However, its dedicated meteor shower guidance provides a more conservative expectation of fewer than three visible meteors per hour under dark skies. These figures should not be interpreted as guaranteed sightings.

The Leonids originate from debris released by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which completes an orbit around the Sun approximately every 33 years. As Earth encounters this material, particles enter the atmosphere at tremendous speeds, producing brief streaks of light.

The meteors travel at approximately 71 kilometres per second and can occasionally produce bright, colourful fireballs. Although the Leonids have historically generated spectacular meteor storms, no comparable outburst is predicted for 2026.

For anyone hoping to catch the display, the practical advice remains straightforward: wait until after moonset, find dark skies and watch patiently before dawn. Observers who miss the peak may still spot occasional Leonid meteors on subsequent nights, although activity generally declines.

Checking local weather forecasts and moonset times beforehand can help identify the clearest, darkest viewing window without requiring any specialised astronomical equipment.

excerpt: An Illinois man who legally changed his name to Captain Cautious America has been charged with first-degree murder in the death of Peoria resident Khanh Dinh.
headline: Illinois Murder Suspect Legally Named Captain America Changed Name About a Decade Ago to Run for Office
html_content:
An Illinois man who legally changed his name to Captain Cautious America in an effort to stand out as a potential political candidate has been charged with first-degree murder in the death of a 63-year-old Peoria resident.

Captain C. America, as he is identified in court and jail records, was charged Monday in Peoria County Circuit Court in connection with the killing of Khanh Dinh, whose body was found Friday during a welfare check at a home in the 2700 block of North Sheridan Road.

Prosecutors said Dinh died from blunt-force trauma to the head. America also faces separate felony charges in neighbouring Tazewell County, including aggravated vehicular hijacking, attempted armed robbery and aggravated unlawful restraint.

Those charges stem from an alleged incident involving Dinh's girlfriend.

The Charges and the Note

The criminal investigation began on Friday, 13 November, when Dinh's girlfriend agreed to drive America, whom she knew as her partner's co-worker.

According to a statement from the Peoria County State's Attorney's Office, America handed the woman a note during the journey informing her that Dinh was dead and demanded 'all of her money'.

The woman managed to escape the vehicle and contacted law enforcement in neighbouring Tazewell County. Officers located America shortly afterwards and took him into custody. Prosecutors said they recovered the note after removing him from a patrol car.

Based on the information contained in the note, Peoria Police Department officers conducted a welfare check at roughly 7:15pm on Friday at Dinh's residence in the 2700 block of North Sheridan Road, where they found him deceased.

A preliminary autopsy conducted by the Peoria County Coroner's Office indicated Dinh died from blunt-force head trauma.

A Decade-Old Name Change for Political Ambition

America, formerly known as Mark Anderson, legally changed his name about a decade ago in an effort to attract attention if he pursued elected office, according to reports.

Local reporting from that period documented that he pursued the legal alteration specifically to run for political office and attract voter attention on a ballot.

At the time, he told reporters he figured he should run for president someday and believed the name 'Captain America' would get noticed by the electorate. Court records in central Illinois continue to list his legal middle name as Cautious.

Multiple Charges Across Two Counties

America remains in custody at the Tazewell County Jail while proceedings continue in both jurisdictions. In addition to the first-degree murder charge filed in Peoria County, he faces aggravated vehicular hijacking, attempted armed robbery and aggravated unlawful restraint charges in neighbouring Tazewell County, according to a 17 November report.

A probable-cause affidavit cited in the report alleges America threatened Dinh's girlfriend with a firearm during the incident and subsequently took her vehicle after she escaped.

He appeared in Tazewell County court on Monday, 16 November, and was ordered held in custody. If convicted of the Tazewell County offences, he could face up to 45 years in prison, according to the same report.

America is scheduled to return to Tazewell County court on 10 December for arraignment on those charges. Authorities have not publicly disclosed a motive for Dinh's killing. The murder investigation remains ongoing, and Peoria police are asking anyone with information to contact the department at 309-673-4521.

excerpt: Apple restored iCloud sign-ins, the App Store and other services after an internal update caused a disruption. Apple said the incident was not a cyberattack, while user reports also flagged Apple Pay problems
headline: Apple Blames Internal Update After Outage Hits iCloud and Apple Pay, Rules Out Cyberattack
html_content:
Apple restored its consumer services on Tuesday, 17 November, after an internal update disrupted iCloud sign-ins, the App Store and other products. The company said the incident was not caused by a cyberattack. Its consumer System Status page showed services back to normal by about 10:46pm GMT (5.46pm US Eastern time), according to an Apple spokesperson.

The disruption eased in stages. Apple's status records put the iCloud sign-in issue at roughly four and a half hours, from 4:45pm to 9:15pm GMT. Access to iCloud.com was also disrupted and was marked as restored at 9:15pm. The App Store was marked as restored earlier, at 8pm GMT. That meant a customer could regain access to the App Store while still having trouble signing in to iCloud.

What Was Affected During the Apple Outage?

Apple's status page also flagged problems with Apple Music and AppleCare purchases made on devices. The impact extended beyond personal accounts: Apple Business, Apple School Manager and Schoolwork appeared on the status page during the incident, with their issues marked as resolved by 10pm GMT. Apple did not specify which internal system it had updated or explain how the change disrupted the affected services.

The iCloud notice concerned account access. Apple warned that sign-in could be slow or unavailable, and it listed a separate issue involving iCloud web apps. The notices described difficulty reaching those services; they did not report that customers' files had been deleted. An Apple Account is also used to access the App Store and Apple Music, which helps explain why sign-in errors can interrupt more than one task.

What the Apple Pay Reports Showed

Downdetector recorded around 2,300 US reports of Apple Pay problems at about 5:20pm GMT. Reports involving iCloud reached around 1,800 at their peak. Those figures are based on user submissions and do not establish the total number of people affected.

Apple Pay complaints surfaced during the wider disruption, but the available consumer status records did not list a separate Apple Pay outage. The complaints therefore do not establish that the entire payments network went offline, or that Apple Pay and iCloud stopped working for the same length of time.

Apple's separate developer dashboard was still listing an App Store Connect outage after its consumer dashboard showed services had recovered. App Store Connect is the portal developers use to submit apps and updates for review. The two dashboards track different services, so the return of App Store downloads did not mean developers could immediately resume submitting updates.

Expo, a platform that helps developers build and submit mobile apps, reported that iOS submissions could fail while retrieving app information or uploading a build. Expo marked its own incident resolved at 9:48pm GMT on 17 November, before Apple's later consumer status update.

What to Check if iCloud, App Store Still Won't Load

Apple advises customers who cannot connect to a service to start with its System Status page and check for an outage in their country or region. If the relevant service is listed as available, Apple suggests checking whether other websites load on the same device or trying a different network. If the Apple Account sign-in screen keeps loading or shows a server connection error, Apple also directs users to the status page before they troubleshoot further.

excerpt: Seoul police booked 86 people after a 22-month investigation into face-to-face drug deals, seizing 1.3kg of methamphetamine and identifying alleged links to cannabis and LSD.
headline: Seoul Police Bust Face-to-Face Meth Network, Seize $3.2M in Drugs Equal to 43,000 Doses and Book 86 Suspects
html_content:
Seoul police seized enough methamphetamine for an estimated 43,000 doses in an investigation into face-to-face drug deals across South Korea, the force announced on 17 November 2026. Officers valued the seizure at $3.22 million (£2.44 million) and booked 86 people.

The inquiry began in January 2025 with a tip about a methamphetamine buyer. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's narcotics team spent 22 months tracing distribution routes. The agency arrested 29 of the suspects and referred them to prosecutors.

An Office Drawer Held Most of the Meth Seoul Police Seized

Officers found 1.2kg (2.6lb) of methamphetamine in a drawer at the office of a cosmetics distribution company in Gyeonggi Province. That accounted for nearly all the methamphetamine they recovered during the inquiry, a total of 1.3kg (2.9lb).

The man who runs the company is in his 60s. He had no previous drug convictions, and investigators did not suspect him of taking drugs himself. Officers arrested him on suspicion of selling methamphetamine.

Police valued the methamphetamine in the drawer at 4 billion won ($3,003,566) and the full seizure at 4.3 billion won ($3,228,834) . Separately, police seized or secured 127 million won ($95,363) in suspected drug proceeds through confiscation and pre-indictment asset preservation.

Seoul Police Trace Drug Deals Through Personal Ties

Investigators suspect 45 people of selling or giving away drugs between July 2024 and September 2026. The alleged exchanges were largely between people who already knew one another as friends, romantic partners, colleagues or fellow prisoners.

Police believe the other 41 took drugs they had either bought from members of that group or received from them free of charge. Investigators identified cannabis and LSD as well as methamphetamine.

The inquiry covered alleged breaches of the Narcotics Control Act. Among those booked were air conditioning installers, department store sales staff, construction site managers and delivery workers. Thirty-five had no previous drug convictions, and police suspect 13 of them of supplying drugs.

The agency described face-to-face drug transactions as more common than online deals. It pledged to pursue suppliers who trade through acquaintances as well as those who sell online.

Twenty-nine suspects told investigators how they first came to take drugs. Each recalled that someone they knew had suggested it.

An industrial safety manager in his 20s took LSD offered by a woman he had met on social media. Police attributed her offer to curiosity about how he would react. After taking the drug, the man felt dizzy and experienced alternating sensations of cold and heat.

A patient offered methamphetamine to a former hospital worker in his 50s, describing it as a stimulant, according to police. The man became dependent on the drug. When he could no longer afford to buy it, he began transporting drugs in exchange for methamphetamine. He told investigators, 'To exaggerate, I felt like a slave.'

'We confirmed cases where people first encountered drugs at the suggestion of their acquaintances, and ended up cutting off ties with their families or unable to lead their everyday lives due to repeated use,' a police official stated.

excerpt: A coroner-style educational inquiry concluded that the Ballymacombs More Woman, an Iron Age bog body found near Bellaghy, was deliberately decapitated more than 2,000 years ago.
headline: 2,000-Year-Old Bog Body Reveals Chilling Evidence Of Possible Rare Female Ritual Killing In Iron Age Europe
html_content:
A coroner-style investigation in Northern Ireland has concluded that a young Iron Age woman whose remains were unearthed from a peat bog was deliberately decapitated more than 2,000 years ago.

Although chaired by Northern Ireland Coroner Joe McCrisken, the event was not a formal inquest or judicial determination. Instead, it was an educational exercise using modern coronial methods to examine the archaeological and forensic evidence.

It applied modern coronial methodology to establish who the young woman was, as well as when, where and how she died.

Researchers, forensic specialists and museum professionals presented findings from a two-year international research programme led by National Museums Northern Ireland, concluding that her death may fit a rare pattern of female ritual killing or sacrifice in Iron Age north-western Europe.

Forensic Findings of a Violent Death

Commercial peat workers from Bulrush Horticulture first uncovered the remains in bogland near Bellaghy, County Londonderry, in October 2023 alongside a woven plant-based artefact. Researchers estimated she was between 15 and 22 years old at death.

Earlier radiocarbon analysis placed the remains within the Iron Age, approximately between 343 BC and 1 BC. Researchers at the University of Glasgow subsequently dated the associated woven plant-fibre material to between 363 BC and 160 BC, a range consistent with the body's estimated age.

The acidic wetland environment preserved partial skin, fingernails, toenails, and brown hair, though her skull was never recovered. 'She died a violent death at the hands of a third party,' McCrisken said during the hearing.

Scientific analysis of the surviving neck vertebrae indicated that she had been deliberately decapitated, most likely from behind using a bladed weapon.

Theories of Iron Age Ritual Sacrifice

Archaeologists and historians participating in the inquiry noted that female bog bodies from the Iron Age are exceptionally rare, making the discovery particularly significant among the region's better-known prehistoric preserved remains, many of which belonged to men.

Niamh Baker, curator of archaeology at National Museums Northern Ireland, stated that cut marks on the neck indicate an intentional killing at the wetland site. 'It may be that she falls into a pattern of ritual and sacrifice that took place across north-west Europe in the Iron Age period,' Baker said.

Researchers also considered possible explanations for her death, although no definitive motive could be established.

Commemorating the Discovery Without Displaying Remains

The Ballymacombs More Woman represents the first authenticated prehistoric bog body discovered in Northern Ireland, prompting an international two-year research project involving experts from Ireland, England and Denmark.

Local residents in Bellaghy have named the young woman Áine after a mythical Irish goddess, and several members of the village's historical society attended the Belfast proceedings.

Hannah Crowdy, head of curatorial at National Museums NI, said the research would inform new interpretation planned for the Ulster Museum's Early Peoples gallery. Crowdy said the woman's remains would not be put on public display.

'We have all this amazing research so we can tell a really detailed story about her and we're looking at creative ways to tell that story, through illustration and poetry, for example,' Crowdy said.

excerpt: Jensen and Lori Huang gifted nearly 59 million NVIDIA shares worth over $10.5 billion to a family trust, completing a decade-long GRAT estate plan.
headline: Jensen Huang Moved $10.5B in NVIDIA Stock Into a Family Trust Months Before His Downfall, Potentially Avoiding Estate Tax
html_content:
NVIDIA former CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, transferred nearly 59 million shares of the chipmaker, worth over $10.5 billion, into an irrevocable family trust in March 2026, completing a decade-long estate-planning strategy that turned an initial $51 million investment into a multibillion-dollar fortune.

The transfer involved NVIDIA shares distributed by two grantor-retained annuity trusts established by the couple in 2016. The trusts terminated on 18th March, with each transferring 29.48 million shares to the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust.

The shares were transferred as gifts without consideration, rather than sold on the open market. Jensen Huang serves as a trustee of the receiving trust, which held around 109 million NVIDIA shares following the transaction.

Taking Estate-Planning to the Next Level

The arrangement dates back to March 2016, when Jensen and Lori Huang established four grantor-retained annuity trusts using NVIDIA shares.

Two of the trusts had four-year terms, while the other two were structured to run for 10 years. The latter arrangement was considerably more unusual because of the uncertainty involved in predicting a company's performance over such an extended period.

GRATs are estate-planning vehicles designed to transfer future asset appreciation to beneficiaries while potentially reducing federal gift and estate tax exposure.

Under the arrangement, the person establishing the trust receives annuity payments over a predetermined period. Any remaining appreciation above the applicable IRS hurdle rate can pass to beneficiaries at the end of the trust term, potentially with little or no taxable gift value when the trust is established.

The strategy can be particularly lucrative when the underlying assets appreciate substantially. However, it carries risks: insufficient investment growth can leave little or nothing for beneficiaries, while the grantor's death during the trust term can undermine the intended estate-tax benefits.

In the Huangs' case, NVIDIA's extraordinary stock-market performance transformed the original investment. NVIDIA shares surged 22,161% over the decade, turning the approximately $51 million initially committed to the two 10-year trusts into more than $10.5 billion.

Trust and estates attorney Joshua Caswell described the transaction as evidence of someone who had considerable confidence in himself and his company without knowing when a major liquidity event might occur.

Who Benefits From the $10.5 Billion NVIDIA Share Transfer

The filings identify the receiving entity as the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust but do not publicly disclose its beneficiaries. However, Barron's reported that the trust is believed to benefit the couple's children, Spencer and Madison Huang.

Both have previously worked at NVIDIA. Spencer held a director-level position in robotics products, while Madison served as a senior director of product marketing.

The March transaction was completed months before Jensen Huang's departure as NVIDIA's chief executive this month. The estate-planning filings do not establish that the transfer was connected to his subsequent departure or the allegations that emerged later.

Despite transferring a substantial number of shares into the family trust, Huang remains NVIDIA's largest individual shareholder, with a substantial remaining interest in the company.

The transaction illustrates how long-term equity ownership, particularly in companies experiencing extraordinary growth, can become a powerful component of multigenerational wealth and estate planning.

excerpt: Macaulay Culkin returns as an adult Kevin McCallister in a McDonald's advert, prompting reflection on his childhood fame, difficult upbringing and later retreat from acting.
headline: Macaulay Culkin Returns in New McDonald's 'Home Alone' Ad 36 Years Later With Pizza Fries and Socks
html_content:
The Home Alone series becomes a talking point when Christmas season comes around. In the case of Macaulay Culkin, who played DIY whiz Kevin McCallister in the series, a new McDonald's ad has thrust him back into the spotlight.

In a TV spot that came out on Tuesday, Culkin reprises his star-making role as a grown-up Kevin, who finds himself 'trapped' inside a McDonald's on a cold winter night. Realising the opportunity he has on his hands, Kevin helps himself to all the treats inside the fast food branch, munching on pizza fries and lucking out on a pair of Grimace socks.

At one point in this 'Home Alone Meal' advertisement, Kevin mockingly cries out to no one in particular: 'I'm making a McFlurry! You better come out and stop me!' This, of course, is a callback to a scene in 1990's Home Alone where Kevin revels in 'eating junk and watching rubbish' after getting left behind by his Paris-bound family.

The Highs and Lows of the 'Home Alone' Star

Thanks to the blockbuster success of this Chris Columbus flick, Culkin (who was 10 years old at the time of the film's release) became a household name. Over the next four years, he saw a dramatic uptick in his TV and film projects, including a stint as Saturday Night Live host, a Home Alone sequel in 1992, and the title role in 1994's Richie Rich.

Behind the scenes, however, Culkin was going through events that were less than comedic. The Manhattan native had a complex relationship with his father Kit, whom he once called 'the worst person' that he'd ever known. On more than one occasion, Culkin has claimed that Kit inflicted physical and mental abuse upon him as he embarked on his career as a child performer.

Weary of his acting workload, Culkin decided to step away from the spotlight in the mid-90s. In a December 2025 appearance on 'Mythical Kitchen,' he explained that he wanted to do things that his peers got to enjoy in their youth.

'What I wanted is to be with people my own age. You have to remember: A lot of the stuff I did when I was a kid...I'm not doing ensembles. It's me,' Culkin shared. 'I wanted to go out and I wanted to date girls, and I wanted to hang out with people my own age. I wanted to, you know, go to a party.'

All Grown Up

When Culkin resurfaced in the entertainment industry, he took on film and TV roles that didn't quite reach the peak of his Home Alone stardom. Still, the 46-year-old actor has found a different joy away from the cameras. In the same 'Mythical Kitchen' appearance, Culkin credited his partner Brenda Song for the resurgence of his self-confidence.

'She saw the best of me and it made me wanna be better. I try to live up to her expectations, you know. I know I disappoint her sometimes, but I've never had that before, being believed in in that way.'

For an entire generation, the sight of a nearly middle-aged Culkin is a poignant reminder of their own passage into adulthood. Still, his return as Kevin in the McDonald's ad shows that having unmitigated fun is a privilege for all ages.

excerpt: NS&I has contacted 795 of up to 15,600 estates eligible for direct contact over an error affecting deceased customers' savings. Find out who should claim and how repayments work
headline: NS&I Owes 30,300 Families £181.9M After Error, With 15,000+ Still Awaiting Contact and Payments
html_content:
NS&I has written to just 795 of the up to 15,600 estates it intends to contact about an error involving deceased customers' savings, despite estimating that nearly 30,300 estates are affected.

The holdings involved are worth up to £181.9 million, according to the state-owned savings provider. This is the estimated value of the savings, not the amount NS&I expects to pay in compensation.

As of 23 October, payment warrants had been issued to 613 estates, with total repayments and compensation exceeding £3 million. NS&I expects to complete its remediation programme in the first half of 2027.

The figures cover different stages of the process: the number of estates identified, the letters sent and the payment warrants issued. NS&I has not said how many of the warrants issued have subsequently been cashed.

Who NS&I Will Contact

Up to 15,600 estates hold £10 or more, including accrued interest, and are eligible for direct contact. Estates below that threshold will not be written to. Their personal representatives must contact NS&I to claim any money due.

The maximum estimate of 15,600 eligible estates means that, after 795 letters, up to 14,805 in this group may still be awaiting contact. This figure does not include estates below the £10 threshold, which NS&I does not plan to contact directly.

NS&I will write to executors or personal representatives rather than beneficiaries, unless a beneficiary is acting in that role. If a solicitor or professional executor handled the estate, NS&I will contact them and leave them to inform the beneficiaries.

The provider says it is working with specialist data search providers and other government departments to trace estates and obtain the information needed to make repayments. If it cannot trace an estate, NS&I says it will hold the money, with interest continuing to accrue until the appropriate person gets in touch.

MoneySavingExpert advises anyone who believes a deceased relative's NS&I savings may have been missed to call 0800 092 1286. Although the consumer website describes this as NS&I's general helpline, the provider's official website lists it as its dedicated complaints number. NS&I's general customer service number is 08085 007 007.

How Repayments and Compensation Work

Payments are made by warrant, which works similarly to a cheque. NS&I says warrants should be issued within 15 working days of the initial letter.

Estates are due the full value of the holdings that should have been returned earlier, plus compensation. This is calculated using whichever is higher: the interest accrued since the error occurred or the Bank of England base rate plus one percentage point.

Some estates may also have faced additional professional costs, such as legal or administrative fees, as a result of the error. Personal representatives can request reimbursement from NS&I, but each claim will be assessed individually.

Pensions Minister Torsten Bell told Parliament on 19 May that affected holdings returned under the scheme would receive a full Inheritance Tax exemption. The Government also confirmed that personal representatives would not be liable for Income Tax ordinarily due on qualifying interest accrued before death or during the estate administration period.

How the Error Came To Light

The issue was disclosed to Parliament in March 2026, prompting a review of historic failures in NS&I's bereavement claims process. Dax Harkins later left his post as chief executive. Sir Jim Harra, a former HMRC First Permanent Secretary, was appointed on an interim basis.

NS&I began contacting affected estates in late May. The provider has said its programme is expected to continue into the first half of 2027, while it traces estates, issues payments and considers requests for additional costs.

excerpt: Leaked files show Deutsche Bank flagged $581.9 million in Epstein-linked transactions, yet kept him as a client despite internal concerns, an international investigation found.
headline: Deutsche Bank Reported $582M in Suspicious Epstein Transactions Only After His Death, Leaked Files Reveal
html_content:
Deutsche Bank flagged approximately $581.9 million in suspicious transactions linked to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, according to leaked documents examined by an international investigation published on 17 November 2026.

The bank filed 21 suspicious activity reports (SARs) with US authorities in 2019. The filings covered approximately 3,200 transactions, according to the investigation, while an internal document from Deutsche Bank's US Financial Crimes Intelligence Unit identified around 3,000. The transactions amounted to approximately $581.9 million.

That figure is more than double the $250 million in suspicious wire transfers identified by US Senator Ron Wyden in an August 2026 investigation. The difference partly reflects Deutsche Bank's broader review, which included cheques and transactions involving other financial institutions.

Leaked Files Detail Epstein-Linked Transactions

The investigation, Inside Deutsche Bank, involved more than 200 journalists and examined over 15 million leaked files supplied by two whistleblowers to Indian journalist Josy Joseph and South African journalist Khadija Sharife.

An internal document stated that the 21 reports covered transactions between October 2013 and May 2019 involving Epstein or associated companies. Flagged activity included payments to women, shell-company transfers, suspected misuse of charitable donations, and payments from billionaire associates Leon Black and Glenn Dubin.

Bank Kept Epstein as a Client Despite Warnings

Deutsche Bank accepted Epstein as a client in August 2013, five years after his conviction for soliciting sex from a minor and after his relationship with JPMorgan Chase had ended. Senior officials, including the head of anti-financial crime and compliance and Deutsche Bank America's then-general counsel, were involved in approving his accounts. Internal documents raised concerns, but the bank continued providing financial services.

Deutsche Bank told Epstein in December 2018 that it intended to close his accounts. The bank closed his two remaining accounts three days after his arrest in July 2019, according to the leaked records. A subsequent review identified at least 112 high-risk transactions and examined possible links to sexual abuse at Epstein's Zorro Ranch in New Mexico and suspected money laundering through his charity, Gratitude America.

An internal email reportedly described Ghislaine Maxwell as an alleged co-conspirator in Epstein's illegal activities. However, an arrangement involving one of Epstein's trusts, which named her as a beneficiary, nevertheless proceeded.

Deutsche Bank Admits Onboarding Epstein Was an Error

Deutsche Bank acknowledged that accepting Epstein as a client in 2013 was an error. The bank said it had cooperated with regulators, law enforcement agencies, and the US Congress. It also highlighted improvements to its anti-financial crime controls through investment in technology, training, and specialist staff. The lender pointed to stronger controls under chief executive Christian Sewing, alongside record profits in 2025 and recent quarters.

Leaks Reveal Other Deutsche Bank Controversies

The leaked records also revealed that Deutsche Bank accidentally sent tax statements from 1,586 private banking accounts, including Donald Trump's, to an outside accountant in 2017. The recipient alerted the bank and deleted the documents, while executives discussed whether clients should be notified. Sewing, who was then head of private banking, reportedly described the incident as an awful mistake.

A separate examination of the records identified a suspicious 2014 payment to DT Marks Baku LLC, a Trump-owned company in Azerbaijan. Deutsche Bank reportedly could not establish the purpose of the transaction. Other payments were also linked through the investigation's analysis to Russian and Azerbaijani money-laundering networks.

The records further highlighted Deutsche Bank's relationships with Russian oligarchs Oleg Deripaska and Viktor Vekselberg despite internal money-laundering and sanctions warnings. Deutsche Bank shares fell 3.57% to €31.76 on Tuesday, after declining more than 6% earlier in the session. The leaked records do not establish that Trump personally participated in money laundering or other wrongdoing.

excerpt: Macaulay Culkin has returned as Kevin McCallister for McDonald's new Home Alone Christmas campaign, prompting fans to revisit childhood memories of the beloved festive film.
headline: 'Feel Like Christmas in 1992': Fans Praise Macaulay Culkin's Return in McDonald's Holiday Ad
html_content:
Macaulay Culkin has returned as Kevin McCallister in a new McDonald's Christmas advert, prompting fans to say it makes them feel like Christmas in 1992. The campaign marks his return to the role 36 years after the original film premiered, and has drawn reactions from viewers who associate the comedy with childhood Christmases.

The advert promotes McDonald's limited-edition Home Alone Meal, with food and collectibles inspired by the film. After its release, viewers shared their reactions on X. One said they would buy the meal simply to feel as though it were Christmas in 1992 again.

The response centres on the film's association with Christmas viewing. Culkin, now an adult, appears again as Kevin in a campaign based on the character and the 1990 film.

Macaulay Culkin Returns as Kevin McCallister

According to a report from Collider, Culkin is reprising his role as Kevin for McDonald's new holiday campaign, which celebrates the 1990 film.

In the commercial, the adult Kevin finds himself alone inside a McDonald's restaurant after closing time. With the premises seemingly to himself, he recreates the playful freedom associated with his childhood character, enjoying the food and getting into mischief.

🎄 Macaulay Culkin is officially back as Kevin McCallister!

36 years after Home Alone first hit theaters, Culkin is reprising his iconic role for McDonald’s new holiday campaign. The limited-time Home Alone Meal features collectible movie-inspired socks, Little Nero’s Pizza… pic.twitter.com/cqQ9aa0Grl

— Collider (@Collider) November 17, 2026

The promotional meal will be available at participating McDonald's locations across the United States from December 1, while supplies last.

The campaign gives fans an opportunity to revisit familiar details from the movie through food and merchandise, rather than simply relying on Culkin's appearance to attract attention.

Why Home Alone Still Draws Christmas Viewers

Released in 1990, Home Alone follows eight-year-old Kevin McCallister, who is accidentally left behind when his family travels to Paris for Christmas. Initially delighted by having the house to himself, Kevin soon has to defend the property from two burglars, Harry and Marv, using a series of improvised traps.

Directed by Chris Columbus and written by John Hughes, the comedy became a defining holiday film for audiences who grew up watching Kevin's adventures. Its mix of family humour, slapstick comedy, Christmas decorations and the familiar feeling of being a child during the holidays helped it become an annual viewing tradition.

According to the British Film Institute, the movie has maintained its nostalgic appeal among audiences who first watched it as children, while continuing to attract new generations of viewers.

Its central themes also remain relatable. The story combines childhood independence, family relationships and the importance of being together during the holidays. Although the original audience has grown older, those themes have not lost their appeal.

i would buy this just to feel like it is christmas in 1992 again pic.twitter.com/wp8FKmiphv

— ɴᴏᴠᴀ (@novawillii) November 17, 2026

Fans Say the Advert Brings Back Childhood Memories

The new campaign prompted enthusiastic reactions on X after Collider shared Culkin's return as Kevin.

One user wrote that they would buy the meal just to experience the feeling of Christmas in 1992 again. Another praised the advertisement, calling it a perfect Christmas campaign for fans of the movie.

Others joked about the promotional concept, with one commenter questioning whether the advertisement was AI-generated because McDonald's ice cream machines are famously associated with being out of order. Another suggested the campaign would have been even better if the burglars Harry and Marv had appeared in their iconic delivery van.

The reactions show that the film's appeal extends beyond its original release. Culkin may no longer be the young boy running around the McCallister family home, but his return as Kevin has given longtime viewers another reason to revisit a Christmas favourite.

excerpt: Australian journalist Sylvia Jeffreys has recalled tensions surrounding Prince Harry and Meghan's 2018 Fiji visit, while noting that the couple remained enormously popular with the public.
headline: 'Cracks Were Starting To Show': What a Journalist Noticed During Prince Harry and Meghan's 2018 Fiji Visit
html_content:
The 'cracks were starting to show' during Prince Harry and Meghan's 2018 visit to Fiji, Australian journalist Sylvia Jeffreys has recalled, describing tensions over security, media relations and tour arrangements. The comments, made on 9News Presents: The Backstory in November 2026, contrast with the enthusiastic public reception the couple received.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex toured Australia, Fiji, Tonga and New Zealand from 16 to 31 October 2018, five months after their wedding. Jeffreys said she had initially believed their popularity could attract a new generation of royal supporters.

Sylvia Jeffreys Reveals What She Noticed During the Fiji Visit

'Harry and Meghan fever was in full throttle at this stage,' Jeffreys told fellow Australian journalist Tom Steinfort as she revisited the assignment.

She believed the newlyweds had the potential 'to really shake things up' within the monarchy. Their reception, she said, suggested they appealed beyond traditional royal supporters.

But Jeffreys recalled a noticeable change in atmosphere as the couple continued their engagements across the Pacific. She described Harry and Meghan as 'like rockstars in town', before identifying Fiji as the point when the 'cracks were starting to show'.

According to Jeffreys, tensions developed around the media, the organisation of engagements and dissatisfaction with security arrangements.

'So things turned really quickly,' she said.

Her recollection offers a view of the tour's media and logistical challenges, alongside the crowds that greeted the couple. She did not, however, identify a specific confrontation or explain which security arrangements had caused dissatisfaction.

Nor did Jeffreys say that Harry and Meghan disagreed with one another. Her comments focused on the handling of the tour and the concerns she recalled around its official engagements.

What Happened During Meghan's 2018 Fiji Market Visit?

Security concerns were reported during the Fiji visit, particularly when Meghan attended Suva Municipal Market on Wednesday, 24 October 2018.

According to ABC News, the Duchess was escorted through the market after spending about half of her scheduled 15-minute engagement there. The visit had been arranged so she could meet women involved in UN Women's Markets for Change initiative, which supports female market vendors.

Kensington Palace attributed the shortened engagement to 'crowd management issues'. ITV News, however, reported that journalists present had not noticed anything unusual about the crowd's behaviour.

Some market vendors also expressed disappointment after missing the opportunity to speak with Meghan about their projects. The incident provides a specific example of the security and organisational concerns reported during the visit, but Jeffreys did not explicitly connect her recollections to the market engagement.

The distinction matters: the market visit is a documented event, while the precise incidents behind Jeffreys' broader comments remain unspecified in her account.

Earlier in the programme, Jeffreys described the trip as 'peak Harry and Meghan popularity'.

'Before it all went downhill,' Steinfort interjected, reflecting on the years that followed.

Harry and Meghan stepped back from their roles as senior working royals in 2020. Jeffreys did not suggest that the difficulties she recalled in Fiji directly influenced that decision.

Her account instead contrasted the couple's public popularity with reported tensions around the management of their official engagements. While the Suva market visit offers context, the available comments do not establish whether it was among the incidents she had in mind.
