excerpt: Bernie Moreno has warned Republicans face a difficult 2028 Senate cycle, with 19 seats to defend after Democrats and aligned independents secured a 56–44 majority.
headline: 'There Will Be No Patience for Bad Recruits' as Republicans Plan 2028 Senate Campaigns After Losses
html_content:
Senator Bernie Moreno has warned that Republicans face 'absolutely a savagely brutal map' in their 2028 Senate campaigns after losing control of the chamber in the 3 November midterms.

The Ohio Republican made the assessment during a Capitol Hill interview with Politico, published on Wednesday, 18 November.

The task became clearer after Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in Alaska.

The race, called on 17 November, gave Democrats and two independents who caucus with them a 56–44 majority in the next Senate. Republicans had entered the midterms controlling 53 seats.

Republicans Must Defend 19 Senate Seats in 2028

Moreno is taking over the National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC), which recruits candidates and raises funds for Senate races. His party is expected to defend 19 seats in 2028, compared with 16 held by Democrats.

Eighteen Republican seats face regularly scheduled elections. The nineteenth is an anticipated special election in Tennessee, where Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn was elected governor on 3 November.

Once she becomes governor, Blackburn is expected to appoint a Republican successor to serve until that vote.

Starting with 44 seats, Republicans would need a net gain of six to draw level at 50–50, or seven for a 51-seat majority, assuming no other changes. Which party controls a tied chamber would depend on the 2028 vice-presidential result, because the vice-president can cast deciding votes.

Republicans have possible targets in Arizona, Pennsylvania, Georgia and Nevada, where Democratic Senators Mark Kelly, John Fetterman, Raphael Warnock and Catherine Cortez Masto face voters. Ohio's Sherrod Brown must also seek a full term after winning a special election this month, two years after Moreno defeated him for the state's other Senate seat.

But the party cannot focus solely on Democratic incumbents. Republican Senators Ron Johnson in Wisconsin and Ted Budd in North Carolina hold seats that Democrats could contest aggressively. Each competitive defence would compete for funding with Republican efforts to make gains elsewhere.

Recruitment and Fundraising Put Moreno's Strategy to the Test

The first challenge is identifying nominees who can survive Republican primaries without alienating the wider electorate. Picking candidates with limited fundraising appeal or weaknesses in closely divided states could force the NRSC to redirect resources from better opportunities.

According to Politico, Moreno's team has interviewed several people for the NRSC executive director role. Chris Grant, who worked on Moreno's and President Donald Trump's campaigns, is expected to serve as a leading outside consultant.

Those staffing choices could shape how the committee recruits nominees and directs campaign spending.

Axios reported on 12 November that Moreno was also assembling an advisory team including Republican strategists Ward Baker, Jason Thielman and Scott Jennings. The group is intended to review the 2026 defeat, rebuild donor confidence and plan the next election cycle.

Moreno has avoided directly blaming Trump or Vice-President JD Vance for the losses. Before the election, he suggested public anger over high fuel prices could hurt Republicans, Politico reported.

The 2028 presidential race could bring different voters to the polls, and Vance may seek his party's nomination.

For Moreno, however, a national campaign offers no substitute for selecting credible Senate candidates and defending vulnerable seats.

excerpt: Representative Robert Garcia has asked JD Vance and other Trump administration figures to preserve documents and answer questions about the Epstein files, business ties and immigration enforcement.
headline: Trump Family and Top Aides Get Notices as House Democrats Ask Vance Who Met To Discuss the Epstein Files
html_content:
US House Democrats have formally demanded answers from Vice-President JD Vance regarding internal White House meetings and government disclosures surrounding the Jeffrey Epstein files.

On Wednesday morning, 18 November 2026, California Representative Robert Garcia, who is expected to chair the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee when Democrats assume majority control in January 2027, dispatched 12 document-preservation notices to Vance, senior administration officials, and members of President Donald Trump's family.

Central to Garcia's inquiry is a request for Vance to identify every meeting officials held concerning the investigative material relating to the late convicted sex offender, alongside demands for sworn testimony from Attorney General Todd Blanche and records from former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.

The oversight push also scrutinises the transfer of Epstein co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell to a minimum-security federal prison camp in Texas, as well as financial ties involving Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, and Jared Kushner.

What Garcia Wants From Vance on the Epstein Files

Garcia cited media coverage describing Vance's involvement in discussions about the files. He also sought details of how the administration responded to a law Congress passed the previous year requiring the public release of investigative material relating to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Lawmakers from both parties have criticised the release as incomplete.

Several of the letters request voluntary responses by December 2026, though legal observers note the notices currently carry no legal force because Democrats do not yet hold the subpoena authority required to compel answers.

Justice Department officials have maintained that they did their best to comply with the disclosure requirements and sought to correct errors or address victims' concerns.

Democrats are seeking sworn testimony from Todd Blanche, who helped oversee the release. Garcia also sought information from former White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, who was unreachable for comment.

Ghislaine Maxwell Prison Transfer Features in Epstein Inquiry

Alongside requests targeting White House deliberations, Garcia's Epstein inquiry examines the federal prison transfer of Epstein's co-conspirator, Ghislaine Maxwell.

The California lawmaker sought detailed records explaining the decision to move Maxwell to a lower-security federal prison facility where she is serving a twenty-year sentence.

Garcia sent preservation letters to Federal Bureau of Prisons Director William Marshall III and Tanisha Hall, the warden of Federal Prison Camp Bryan, the minimum-security facility in Texas that received Maxwell.

In his correspondence, Garcia wrote that both the Justice Department and the Bureau of Prisons had 'failed to meaningfully respond to any of our inquiries' regarding the transfer.

Neither the White House nor the Justice Department immediately responded to requests for comment on Wednesday, whilst Marshall and Hall likewise did not immediately return them.

Beyond the Epstein Files, Trump Family Business Ties Draw Scrutiny

Garcia plans to examine the roles of Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump as co-founders of World Liberty Financial, a Trump family cryptocurrency business.

He described the brothers as key figures in what he called 'the Trump family's pay-to-play schemes'. A company spokesperson previously stated that World Liberty Financial complies with all US laws.

The White House has repeatedly denied that the president or his family engaged in conflicts of interest. The Trump brothers did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Garcia also wrote to Jared Kushner, the president's son-in-law and a US special envoy, about his business dealings and government work.

Garcia raised concerns that management fees and other financial benefits could be disguised payments for favourable treatment or access to sensitive information and technology. Kushner has repeatedly denied using his relationship with the president for personal gain.

Finally, in a letter to White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, Garcia outlined plans to examine alleged abuses by the Department of Homeland Security under Miller's direction, stating that the committee had identified 1,165 troubling instances involving the use of force, arrests, deportations, and enforcement actions at sensitive locations.

excerpt: Christopher Nolan joked that Robert Pattinson was the "most cowardly James Bond" while discussing his brutal fate as Antinous in The Odyssey.
headline: Christopher Nolan Calls Robert Pattinson the 'Most Cowardly James Bond' in Joke About 'The Odyssey'
html_content:
Christopher Nolan poked fun at newly appointed James Bond actor Robert Pattinson during a discussion with Steven Spielberg in West Hollywood on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.

As People reported, Nolan called him the 'most cowardly James Bond' while discussing his villainous role in The Odyssey.

The joke came just one day after Amazon MGM Studios announced Pattinson, 40, as Daniel Craig's successor. Nolan previously directed him in Tenet and reunited with him for his adaptation of Homer's Greek epic, released in cinemas in July.

The Odyssey became available for digital purchase on 17 November, including through Prime Video.

Christopher Nolan's James Bond Joke Came After a Brutal Film Scene

The exchange followed a Directors Guild of America screening, where Spielberg singled out the film's climactic confrontation for praise. Matt Damon's Odysseus faces Antinous, played by Pattinson, a nobleman seeking to marry Odysseus' wife, Penelope, portrayed by Anne Hathaway.

Antinous suffers a grisly fate in the encounter. Spielberg praised stunt coordinator George Cottle for designing the sequence, and Nolan took the opportunity to contrast his actor's onscreen defeat with the formidable reputation of 007.

'Rob Pattinson is the most cowardly James Bond you've ever seen,' Nolan joked, according to People.

Robert Pattinson confessed he froze completely when Christopher Nolan called him out of nowhere, and told him the project was The Odyssey.

"Chris Nolan is obviously like king of the universe. He called to say, hey, think about doing this thing, what are you doing next year? And… pic.twitter.com/5DPx6vV4bB

— Mavo (@0xMavo) November 18, 2026

Spielberg responded with a teasing question of his own, 'I wonder if your film influenced his casting.'

Neither filmmaker was seriously questioning Pattinson's suitability for Bond. Their remarks referred to Antinous, whose fate is hardly the heroic introduction audiences might expect from the next actor entrusted with the British spy.

Nolan also credited Damon and Tom Holland, who plays Odysseus' son Telemachus, for their physical commitment to the sequence. He compared their action-film credentials to their famous roles as Jason Bourne and Spider-Man, before joking that Pattinson preferred watching from the sidelines.

The exchange reflected a familiar contrast in Pattinson's career. He has moved between blockbuster franchises and unsettling characters, including roles that make little effort to win an audience's sympathy.

Robert Pattinson's Bond Casting Brings an Old Ambition Full Circle

Pattinson will become the seventh actor to portray Bond in the official film series. Craig last played the character in 2021's No Time to Die, leaving the franchise without a leading man until Monday's announcement.

Denis Villeneuve will direct the next instalment for Amazon MGM Studios, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Villeneuve has already worked with Pattinson on Dune: Part Three, scheduled for release in December 2026. Production on the new Bond film is expected to begin in 2027.

The appointment also revisits a much earlier ambition. In a 2012 interview with ShortList, Pattinson expressed interest in playing Bond, although he imagined taking the part roughly 20 years later. He also objected to casting a fresh-faced actor as Bond.

At The Odyssey's London premiere in July, Pattinson offered a less severe reading of Antinous. He told People that the character's pursuit of Penelope could be understood as a love story, rather than simply a villain's scheme.

Following his casting announcement, Pattinson described playing 007 as the 'honour of a lifetime' in a statement released by Amazon MGM Studios.

Nolan's joke now provides an unusual footnote to that milestone, the new Bond's last role with the director ended considerably less heroically.

excerpt: Las Vegas police warn of a phone scam involving fake officials, urgent demands, and rideshare collections of cash, cards, and other valuables.
headline: Police Issue Urgent Warning Over Phone Scam That Could Wipe Out Your Life Savings
html_content:
Police in Las Vegas have warned residents about a phone scam in which fraudsters impersonate bank employees, police officers, and attorneys before arranging to collect victims' cash and valuables. Some people have reportedly lost their entire life savings, according to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department (LVMPD).

The scheme involves criminals arranging physical collections rather than simply requesting electronic payments. They may send someone to collect cash, credit cards, or other valuables. In some cases, unsuspecting rideshare drivers are allegedly used to pick up the money without knowing they are assisting a fraudulent operation. The LVMPD described the scheme as a new and devastating scam in a warning issued on 17 November 2026.

How the Phone Scam Works

According to the LVMPD, scammers contact people by telephone while pretending to represent banks, law enforcement agencies, or legal professionals. They describe an alleged emergency and pressure recipients to act immediately. Victims may be persuaded to withdraw money, surrender credit cards, or hand over valuables to resolve the supposed problem.

Criminals may then arrange for someone to collect the possessions directly or instruct victims to meet them at another location. The involvement of an unsuspecting rideshare driver can make the collection appear like an ordinary delivery arrangement.

Police Identify Warning Signs of the Scam

The LVMPD has outlined several potential indicators that could help people recognise the fraud before losing their money.

  • Unexpected phone calls: Someone claims to be a police officer, bank employee, or attorney without prior contact.
  • Pressure to act immediately: The caller insists that an alleged emergency requires an urgent response.
  • Demands for secrecy: The person discourages you from speaking with family members, friends, or others.
  • Requests for valuables: You are instructed to withdraw cash or hand over credit cards and other possessions.
  • Physical collection arrangements: Someone offers to collect your money or asks you to meet at another location.

Police have particularly warned against following instructions from callers who demand secrecy or prevent people from independently checking their claims.

Why the Physical Collection Method Is Concerning

The possible involvement of rideshare drivers adds another layer to the scheme. According to the police warning, drivers may be unaware that the money they collect is connected to fraudulent activity. This arrangement could make it harder for victims to recognise the deception because the person collecting their valuables may not appear to be directly involved in the scam.

What Should You Do if You Receive a Suspicious Call?

Police have advised residents to end suspicious calls immediately rather than continue conversations with callers demanding money or valuables. Anyone receiving such a call should independently contact the organisation the caller claims to represent. For example, if someone claims to work for your bank, use the official telephone number printed on your bank card or listed on its verified website.

Never rely on contact details supplied by the caller. Avoid withdrawing money, handing over valuables, or keeping the conversation secret without independently verifying the request. Anyone who has already surrendered money or possessions should contact the police and their financial institution as soon as possible.

Police Warn That Anyone Could Become a Victim

The LVMPD has stressed that these scams can affect anyone, regardless of their financial circumstances or background. The department has urged residents to share the warning with friends and family members to help prevent further losses. Its central advice is to hang up on suspicious callers, verify claims through independently obtained contact details, and never hand over money or valuables based solely on an unexpected telephone demand.

excerpt: Karoline Leavitt urged the White House to explain eight recent US tech outages as JD Vance reassured Americans that no crisis was approaching
headline: Trump Ally Karoline Leavitt Asks 'What's Happening?!' as She Critiques White House Over Eight Tech Outages
html_content:
Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt urged President Donald Trump's administration to address eight reported US technology disruptions on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.

Speaking on Fox & Friends, Leavitt, now a Fox News contributor, called for transparency as problems affecting aviation, banking and online services raised public questions.

The appeal followed a series of incidents between 12 and 17 November. They involved Microsoft 365, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Workday, JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Marriott International and the National Security Agency (NSA). Their proximity in time does not establish a shared cause.

Leavitt said she was now hearing concerns without access to the government briefings she received while serving in the White House.

'What's happening?! I'm checking my bank account with a little bit of worry,' she said. She did not claim that her account had been affected.

Eight US Tech Outages Put Donald Trump's Administration Under Scrutiny

The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on 13 November after communications equipment became unstable.

In its subsequent explanation, the agency said excessive data had flooded its network. Air traffic resumed that evening, although the disruption had already affected thousands of flights.

Microsoft 365 users encountered problems with services including Outlook on 12 November. Workday also reported disruption to its production services the following day. Neither incident has been shown to be connected to the FAA failure.

On 16 November, JPMorgan Chase attributed transaction delays to a software bug affecting its own hardware. The bank said it had no evidence of a cyber-related incident. Customers at other banks could encounter delays involving Chase, although US Bank said its systems were not directly affected.

United Airlines separately experienced a system problem that delayed departing flights for more than 90 minutes that Monday. On 17 November, Apple blamed service interruptions on an internal update, while Marriott said it had resolved website and Bonvoy app sign-in problems.

The NSA said some internal systems experienced temporary degradation during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday. It maintained that mission-critical capabilities remained operational. None of these explanations establishes a single incident behind the wider run of disruption.

Donald Trump's Team Responds as Leavitt Calls for Clarity

Leavitt told Fox & Friends that 'transparency is key' to helping Americans understand what officials knew. She wanted the White House to communicate Vice-President JD Vance's reassurance more clearly, rather than leave questions unanswered.

On The Ingraham Angle on 16 November, Vance said friends had asked whether they should build bunkers or stockpile supplies. 'My answer to that is no. We do not see some crisis coming down, but you have to be prepared for everything,' he said.

Leavitt suggested Trump or another official address the public when the president returned from overseas. Trump was attending a Quad leaders' summit in Manila on 17 November. She said a direct explanation could 'really calm the temperature', adding that the subject had 'really taken off on TikTok'.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio subsequently addressed the speculation in Manila on 18 November. He said officials had no evidence connecting the outages or attributing them to hackers, foreign governments or other malicious actors. His remarks offered an official assessment, though not a single explanation for every technical failure.

excerpt: A report urges major reforms to tackle the UK's rising youth inactivity, with ministers considering changes to welfare, apprenticeships and employment support for NEETs
headline: Who Are the UK's NEETs? Why More Young People Are Now Out of Work, Education and Training
html_content:
Nearly a million young people in the UK are currently not in employment, education or training, known as NEETs. The government is considering reforms to welfare and job support aimed at tackling rising youth inactivity.

A report by former Labour minister Alan Milburn said Britain needs a 'complete system reset' to address rising youth joblessness. Proposals include stronger employer incentives, expanded apprenticeships and changes to support available for younger benefit claimants.

Figures show that 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 were classified as NEET in the second quarter of 2026, accounting for around one in eight young people. The UK recorded the second-highest NEET rate in Europe last year.

NEETs Prompt Calls for a New Jobs Strategy

The latest figures have intensified concerns over how young people are moving from education into employment. The report argued that existing support systems are not working effectively for enough young people and require major reform.

'A whole-system reset is needed,' Milburn said in the report. 'These changes will not be easy to make. Nor will they be pain-free.'

Milburn said the government should aim to reduce the NEET rate to 5 per cent over a 10-year period. This could be achieved by combining better mental health support, increased apprenticeship opportunities and greater incentives for employers to recruit younger workers.

Welfare minister Pat McFadden said the government agreed that changes were needed and would introduce new legislation following a White Paper in the new year.

'The current system ... far too readily signs people off and writes people off,' he told Parliament.

However, the proposed reforms are already facing criticism over the timeline for change. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the government should move faster.

'We can't wait 10 years. This is an issue that needs to be solved now,' she said.

The report estimates that implementing the proposed changes would require an initial investment of around £500 million in 2027/28, rising to £5.8 billion annually by 2036/37. Milburn said the costs could be offset through £3.6 billion in welfare savings and £2.4 billion in additional tax revenue and reduced benefit payments.

UK Youth NEETs Face Barriers Beyond Finding a Job

The challenges the UK's NEET population faces extend beyond simply finding a job. The BBC reported on the experiences of young people who are not in employment, education or training, highlighting barriers including mental health difficulties, limited work experience and a lack of suitable opportunities.

The report highlighted how some young people struggle to re-enter education or employment after leaving the system, particularly if they lack the experience that employers demand. It also noted that mental health has become a growing factor. Department for Education data from 2025 shows that around one in five NEETs have a mental health condition, more than double the rate recorded in 2012.

The findings showed that the issue affects young people from different educational backgrounds. Graduates are also affected, with some struggling to secure employment despite qualifications and efforts to gain experience.

Young people with disabilities or additional needs who may require greater workplace support and more tailored routes into employment also face challenges, according to the report.

As ministers prepare new legislation, debate around the UK's NEET population is likely to continue, particularly over whether the proposed changes can improve pathways into work, education and training.

excerpt: The NSA says a temporary NSANet outage occurred during scheduled maintenance, as officials reject evidence of a coordinated cyberattack after US aviation and banking disruptions.
headline: NSA's Classified Communications Network Goes Down as FAA, Airline and Bank Outages Pile Up
html_content:
The US National Security Agency (NSA) has suffered a disruption to its classified internal communications network, adding to a growing list of technology failures affecting America's aviation, banking, and government infrastructure and raising fresh questions about the reliability of systems underpinning national security.

The outage affected NSANet, the highly classified network used by NSA employees to communicate and share sensitive intelligence internally, according to CNN, which first reported the incident on 17th November, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The disruption is particularly concerning because the NSA plays a central role in America's signals intelligence and cybersecurity operations. Its internal communications infrastructure supports the handling and exchange of sensitive information, making network availability important to the agency's daily work.

However, there is no evidence that the incident resulted from a cyberattack. The NSA subsequently confirmed that it experienced a temporary degradation during scheduled maintenance, stressing that its mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational.

The development does not establish that intelligence collection, national security decision-making, or operational responses were suspended. Nevertheless, the incident comes at an uncomfortable time for Washington, with several major technology failures occurring across different sectors within days.

FAA Ground Stop Disrupted Thousands of Flights

One of the most consequential incidents involved the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which issued a nationwide ground stop on 13th November following instability in its telecommunications network.

The disruption began when the FAA's legacy equipment became unstable after excessive data flooded its FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure network.

According to the agency's preliminary investigation, the system was receiving 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. Investigators identified two potential sources of the excessive traffic: a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas.

The FAA said work involving a new router at the El Dorado site was being carried out by its network service provider, L3Harris.

The FAA implemented a nationwide ground stop as a precaution, with air traffic resuming at approximately 8:15 p.m. ET after the system stabilised. The halt lasted around four and a half hours.

The agency subsequently reported approximately 12,462 flight cancellations on 13 November, although it cautioned that not all cancellations were directly attributable to the ground stop.

Banks and United Airlines Hit by Further Disruptions

The technology problems continued on 16th November, when United Airlines experienced a widespread systems outage that temporarily disrupted departing flights.

The airline said some flights were delayed, but flights already in progress and United Express operations were unaffected. An internal company alert obtained by CNN indicated that multiple applications used by flight crews were affected, including flight-planning, weather-briefing, and crew-management tools.

United subsequently confirmed that the problem had been resolved and said there was no indication that it was cybersecurity-related.

The banking sector also experienced another disruption on the same day. JPMorgan Chase acknowledged a temporary technical problem involving a software bug in its on-premise hardware systems, which slowed the processing of certain transactions.

Washington Rules Out Evidence of a Coordinated Cyberattack

The clustering of outages has inevitably raised questions about whether the disruptions could be connected or represent a broader cybersecurity threat. However, US officials have pushed back against suggestions of a coordinated attack.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was no evidence linking the incidents to hackers, criminal groups, or a foreign government. He acknowledged that the repeated technical failures were unsettling but described the incidents as distinct, with different technical causes.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton offered another possible explanation, pointing to government agencies and private companies upgrading and patching computer systems around the same time. He argued that older infrastructure could struggle when new technologies and software updates are introduced, creating temporary instability.

The banking sector also experienced another disruption on the same day. JPMorgan Chase acknowledged a temporary technical problem involving a software bug in its on-premise hardware systems, which slowed the processing of certain transactions. Washington Rules Out Evidence of a Coordinated Cyberattack The clustering of outages has inevitably raised questions about whether the disruptions could be connected or represent a broader cybersecurity threat. However, US officials have pushed back against suggestions of a coordinated attack. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was no evidence linking the incidents to hackers, criminal groups, or a foreign government. He acknowledged that the repeated technical failures were unsettling but described the incidents as distinct, with different technical causes. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton offered another possible explanation, pointing to government agencies and private companies upgrading and patching computer systems around the same time. He argued that older infrastructure could struggle when new technologies and software updates are introduced, creating temporary instability.

excerpt: Cyril Ramaphosa urged Elon Musk to remember his South African roots and questioned his understanding of apartheid during a California interview
headline: Cyril Ramaphosa Tells Elon Musk To Be 'Loyal to Your Old Country' and Questions His Grasp of Apartheid
html_content:
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa urged billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk to remain loyal to his birthplace and questioned his understanding of apartheid during a high-profile interview in California on Monday, 16 November 2026.

Speaking with ABC News Chief Washington Correspondent Jonathan Karl at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World event in Menlo Park, Ramaphosa expressed admiration for the Pretoria-born technology mogul's brilliance whilst appealing for him to support South Africa's development.

The remarks immediately reignited a bitter transatlantic dispute over post-apartheid racial redress policies and the prolonged regulatory blockade facing Musk's satellite internet network, Starlink.

After Semafor posted a video excerpt of the exchange on X, Musk hit back online, claiming 'South Africa is now super racist against Whites and Asians'.

Ramaphosa rejected Musk's earlier characterisation of South African transformation statutes as apartheid 2.0, arguing that stark apartheid-era educational disparities necessitated corrective legislation.

Meanwhile, the commercial standoff over Starlink's local operating licence remains locked in regulatory and legal limbo following a formal enforcement notice issued to SpaceX in October and a challenge in the Pretoria High Court launched earlier this month.

Cyril Ramaphosa Questions Musk's Understanding of Apartheid

Ramaphosa said he had met Musk before and was 'awed by his brilliance'. Although their schedules had not aligned on this visit, he hoped to speak with Musk about South Africa. 'You should still be loyal to your old country,' the president said.

"I have met Elon Musk in the past, and I've been awed by his brilliance. But I'd also like to chat to him about remembering his country," South African President Cyril Ramaphosa tells @jonkarl.

"What you've become today is by dint of your own origins ... It is because of the… pic.twitter.com/YJpqozgjQR

— Semafor (@semafor) November 16, 2026

Karl raised Musk's previous description of the government's policies as 'apartheid 2.0'. In May 2025, Musk alleged that 140 South African laws discriminated against people who were not Black. He later called for more than 100 laws to be repealed and urged sanctions. Those figures were Musk's allegations, not independently established findings.

Ramaphosa rejected Musk's comparison with apartheid. He said Musk 'doesn't fully understand the extent of what the apartheid policies did to black South Africans'. The president pointed to educational advantages apartheid afforded white citizens, drawing a comparison with his own upbringing.

South Africa is now super racist against Whites and Asians

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 17, 2026

Ramaphosa said the apartheid government spent 12 rand on Musk's education for every rand spent on his own. That personal comparison has not been independently substantiated. South Africa's Department of Basic Education separately says spending on white learners was about 4.5 times that for Black African learners in 1994.

Ramaphosa argued that such disparities explained why measures to redress apartheid's legacy were needed. He also urged Musk to recognise how his upbringing and early education helped shape his success.

Cyril Ramaphosa's Starlink Dispute Faces Legal Challenge

The disagreement extends to Starlink's efforts to enter the South African market. In March 2025, Musk said the service could not operate there 'because I'm not black'. Foreign ministry official Clayson Monyela rejected that explanation, saying the company could operate if it complied with local laws.

According to regulator ICASA, the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act requires individual licence holders to have at least 30% ownership by historically disadvantaged groups. In May 2026, ICASA said allowing full alignment with equity-equivalent investment arrangements would require legislative change.

The licensing dispute remains unresolved. A parliamentary reply said ICASA issued SpaceX a formal notice on 14 October, demanding that unauthorised Starlink operations cease.

On 11 November, the business group Sakeliga announced a challenge in the Pretoria High Court to ICASA's interpretation of the ownership requirement. Sakeliga argues the law allows alternative licensing conditions. The challenge concerns the regulator's interpretation, not a direct application for Starlink's operating licence. No ruling had been reported as of 18 November.

Ramaphosa maintained that businesses entering South Africa must follow its policies, just as they would elsewhere.

Asked what he wanted from Musk, he proposed a different response from the entrepreneur. 'I would like to contribute to the development of South Africa and give back to this country,' he suggested Musk should say.

excerpt: Bill O'Reilly questioned whether recent disruptions affecting Microsoft, the FAA and banks were connected, but officials said they had found no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack.
headline: 'Coincidence? Five in a Row?': Bill O'Reilly Questions Repeated US Outages and Demands Answers From Trump
html_content:
Bill O'Reilly questioned whether repeated US technology outages signalled a cyberattack on Monday, 16 November, demanding answers from President Donald Trump's administration. Officials have since reported no evidence that the disruptions were linked or malicious.

For context, Microsoft's Outlook and Teams services were disrupted on 12 November, followed by a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop on 13 November. Banking customers then reported problems on 16 November, although JPMorgan Chase traced its transaction delays to a software bug.

Speaking in Manila on Wednesday, 18 November, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials had 'zero evidence' that the incidents were connected or caused by malicious actors.

Bill O'Reilly Questions Whether US Outages Are Linked

Speaking on his No Spin News broadcast, O'Reilly said the disruptions warranted an explanation from the White House.

'We may be under cyberattack here in this country. It's possible,' he said.

The former Fox News host said a problem with Zoom had nearly prevented his own programme from going ahead. He cautioned against conspiracy theories but questioned the timing of the outages.

'Coincidence? Five in a row?' he asked.

O'Reilly called the government 'totally befuddled' and complained that no national spokesperson had explained whether the failures shared a cause. His criticism came despite transport officials having already discussed the FAA incident.

NEW: The NSA’s HIGHLY CLASSIFIED Network just GOT JAMMED. 🚨

What the HECK is GOING ON?

Apple and Charles Schwab are ALSO reporting OUTAGES.

Is this ANOTHER “COINCIDENCE”? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/HERgy2koeh

— Jesse Watters (@JesseBWatters) November 18, 2026

'I'm a little teed off about this because this is dangerous,' he said, arguing that Congress had failed to prepare for technological threats.

He proposed a department devoted to preventing cyberattacks, separate from the FBI and intelligence agencies. He also urged lawmakers to introduce tougher penalties for the misuse of technology.

Officials Offer Separate Explanations for US Outages

JPMorgan Chase said its 16 November problem involved a software bug in an internal hardware system, not a cyberattack. The bank subsequently confirmed that the problem was resolved.

Customers at other banks, including Bank of America and Wells Fargo, reported difficulties. However, those complaints did not establish independent system failures at either institution. Early Warning Services, which operates Zelle, said its payment network remained operational.

Microsoft's preliminary report linked its 12 November outage to an older software defect triggered by increased traffic and reduced server capacity. The disruption affected Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services.

For the FAA, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said contractor L3Harris was replacing ageing copper communications lines with fibre-optic connections when systems became unstable.

Officials had not determined whether faulty equipment or installation errors caused the disruption. Duffy said investigators did not believe it was a cyberattack. L3Harris said it was assisting the FAA investigation.

The differing explanations offer no basis to treat customer complaints, aviation interruptions and Microsoft failures as one incident. Reports of disruption also need to be distinguished from confirmed network outages.

Fox News host Jesse Watters also questioned the timing of the banking and aviation disruptions without presenting evidence that they were connected.

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt similarly urged greater public clarity on Tuesday, 17 November. Speaking on Fox & Friends, she said 'transparency is key' as questions continued over the reliability of essential services.

excerpt: Warren Buffett has announced a $5.5 billion Thanksgiving gift to family foundations, months after excluding the Gates Foundation from his summer donations and outlining plans to give away his fortune.
headline: Warren Buffett Gives $5.5B to Family Charities After Leaving Gates Foundation Out of Summer Gifts
html_content:
Warren Buffett announced a gift worth about $5.5 billion (£4.18 billion) to four family foundations on Monday, 16 November, months after leaving the Gates Foundation out of his summer donations.

The 96-year-old investor's latest charitable commitment comes as he accelerates plans to give away his remaining Berkshire Hathaway shares by the end of 2034. In July, Buffett announced a separate distribution worth roughly $6 billion (£4.56 billion) to the same family foundations.

How Buffett Is Directing Billions to His Family Foundations

Berkshire Hathaway said Buffett would convert 6,150 Class A shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares for the November gifts. The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named after his late wife, will receive 3.69 million shares.

The Sherwood Foundation, the Howard G. Buffett Foundation and the NoVo Foundation will each receive 1.845 million shares. They are run by Buffett's children, Susie, Howard and Peter, respectively.

The gift is worth more than four times his 2025 Thanksgiving donation, although its value depends on Berkshire's share price.

Buffett said the distribution followed his previously announced plans to transfer his remaining Berkshire shares to the four foundations by 31 December 2034. He wants to increase their annual charitable grants and has expressed confidence in his children's ability to oversee the money.

'I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity,' he wrote.

Warren Buffett Reflects on Kindness After Leadership Handover

The donation was accompanied by an unusually short Thanksgiving message. Rather than revisit Berkshire's operations, Buffett said his confidence in the company remained unchanged and returned to a theme from last year's letter: kindness.

Buffett repeated last year's observation that kindness is 'costless but also priceless'. He said it 'compounds' at a better rate than investments he and his late business partner Charlie Munger had made.

He also acknowledged mentors Ben Graham, Joe Rosenfield and Tom Murphy, recalling their generosity and the opportunities it gave him to help others.

The message followed Buffett's September departure as Berkshire chairman. His son Howard became non-executive chairman, while Greg Abel, who took over as chief executive in January, continues to run the company. Buffett remains chairman emeritus and a director.

Warren Buffett Explains Gates Foundation Omission

Buffett's July distribution was the first summer gift since 2006 to omit the Gates Foundation. In a CNBC interview on 15 July, he explained that the decision principally reflected his growing confidence in his children's readiness to manage his philanthropic wealth.

Buffett described Bill Gates' past association with Jeffrey Epstein as 'distasteful' but downplayed its role in his decision.

On 21 July, the Gates Foundation published the findings of an independent review by WilmerHale, which examined approximately 30 meetings involving Epstein and foundation personnel, including Gates, between 2011 and 2014. The law firm found no evidence that the foundation paid Epstein or that foundation personnel knew of or participated in Epstein's ongoing criminal activities. The review did not examine Gates' personal communications outside the foundation.

The foundation thanked Buffett for more than $47 billion (£35.69 billion) in support and said it remained financially strong. His November message made no further reference to the decision, ending instead with an appeal to thank those who had helped and to help someone else.

excerpt: Footage of Donald Trump's arrival in China shows apparent leg tapping and abrupt arm movements, but does not establish a medical cause
headline: Footage Shows 80-Year-Old Donald Trump Tapping His Leg Three Times Before Arm Jolts in China
html_content:
Footage of Donald Trump's arrival in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, 18 November, appears to show him repeatedly patting his right thigh. His right arm also appears to move abruptly after a military salute.

The 80-year-old US president landed in Shenzhen for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted him. The images have attracted attention online, but they do not establish the cause of the movements.

Air Force One landed at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport at 4:42pm local time, according to the White House press pool. Trump emerged shortly afterwards and raised his fist before descending the stairs with one hand on the rail. Circulating footage appears to show him touching his thigh near the aircraft doorway and again during his descent.

Xi met Trump beside the aircraft, an unusually personal welcome before the leaders' talks. China's official account said a military band played both countries' national anthems.

The press pool reported that Trump saluted during the playing of the American anthem. After lowering his salute, his right arm appeared to move abruptly upwards.

The video offers no explanation for that movement. Nor does it establish whether the gestures during his arrival were connected.

Donald Trump's China Arrival Follows Manila Visit

Trump reached Shenzhen after visiting the Philippines, where he arrived on Tuesday, 17 November.

He remained in Manila on Wednesday and met Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang Palace before leaving for China. The press pool recorded Air Force One departing Manila at 2:42pm.

A video shared by the White House's Rapid Response 47 account showed Trump walking beside Marcos at the palace. Commentator Aaron Rupar reposted it on X, writing, 'Look at Trump's legs as he walks 😬'. Other social media users speculated about Trump's gait and whether he wore leg braces.

Look at Trump’s legs as he walks 😬 https://t.co/wqNqgbb5l4

— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 18, 2026

Those posts offer no verified evidence that Trump wears braces. The Manila footage likewise cannot establish whether he has a mobility problem. A brief recording may attract conflicting interpretations, especially when viewers cannot see what happened before or after the filmed moments.

Rupar shared another clip on 16 November, showing Trump patting his right thigh as he approached Marine One at the White House. It offers an earlier example of the gesture, not an explanation for those seen in Shenzhen.

China's official statement described Xi's airport greeting as a reciprocal gesture. Trump had personally welcomed Xi during a September visit to the United States. Xi also said he hoped to discuss bilateral relations and regional cooperation during the latest visit.

What Donald Trump's Medical Report Says

Scrutiny of Trump's health has also focused on bruising visible on his hands. In a memorandum dated 29 May 2026, White House physician Capt. Sean P. Barbabella reported that Trump remained in 'excellent health'. The assessment followed an examination on 26 May.

Trump repeatedly taps his thigh as he boards Marine One. Following behind him is First Lady Natalie Harp and Stephen Miller. pic.twitter.com/gHURmPAaFb

— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) November 16, 2026

Barbabella demonstrated normal gait and balance, with slight lower-leg swelling that had improved compared with the previous year. He attributed bruising on Trump's hands to frequent handshaking while taking aspirin. The May examination, however, cannot explain movements recorded nearly six months later.

Questions about Trump's alertness during meetings have also drawn attention. At a Cabinet meeting on 29 January, he rejected suggestions that he had fallen asleep during an earlier session. 'I didn't sleep. I just closed them because I wanted to get the hell out of here,' he said.

excerpt: Housekeeping teams from 10 Las Vegas-area hotels competed in bed-making, vacuuming and other challenges at the 36th annual ISSA Housekeeping Olympics.
headline: 'Well-Deserved Spotlight': Viral Las Vegas Housekeeping Olympics Honors Overlooked Hospitality Workers
html_content:
Ten housekeeping teams from Las Vegas hotels competed in the 36th annual ISSA Housekeeping Olympics on 16 November, racing to make beds and complete other cleaning challenges. Held at Michelob ULTRA Arena inside Mandalay Bay Resort & Casino, the event showcased the skills of staff whose work helps keep hotels and other facilities running behind the scenes.

Video of the competition circulated online after TMZ shared footage of participants racing to make beds and taking part in other cleaning-related challenges. The event drew attention to the range of tasks involved in housekeeping and the workers who perform them.

Comments on X included praise for the competition's recognition of frontline workers. One commenter called it a 'well-deserved spotlight' on an often-overlooked workforce, while another joked about the difficulty of making a bed with a perfectly fitted sheet.

Inside the Housekeeping Olympics

According to information from ISSA, the 36th annual Housekeeping Olympics took place as part of ISSA Show North America, a major event for professionals in the cleaning and facility solutions industries.

Hosted by the Indoor Environmental Healthcare & Hospitality Association (IEHA), an ISSA division, the competition brings together housekeeping teams from hotels and other hospitality establishments to demonstrate their abilities through timed and skill-based activities.

The 2026 edition featured 10 participating teams representing ARIA/Vdara, Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas, Excalibur, Hotel Drover, LIV Hospitality, Luxor, Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand and Park MGM.

Rather than traditional athletic events, competitors were tested on tasks closely connected to their daily responsibilities. Challenges included bed making, a buffer pad toss, a vacuum race, a mop relay and a toilet paper toss. The programme also featured a triathlon, an executive challenge and a spirit competition.

The activities gave participants an opportunity to demonstrate the speed, coordination, precision and teamwork required in housekeeping roles. What may appear to be routine work to hotel guests can involve considerable physical effort and attention to detail.

LIV Hospitality Takes the Overall Title

LIV Hospitality emerged as the overall champion of the 2026 competition, followed by Excalibur Hotel in second place and Mandalay Bay in third.

Individual events also produced winners across several categories. Excalibur Hotel claimed the bed-making title, while Luxor Hotel won the buffer pad toss. Mandalay Bay took first place in the vacuum race, and LIV Hospitality secured victories in both the mop relay and toilet paper toss.

ARIA/Vdara won the triathlon, while The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas took home the executive challenge and spirit competition awards.

excerpt: Donald Trump reflected on his time in office at a Manila dinner with regional leaders, as a midterm defeat, domestic disruptions and planned talks in China shaped his Asian tour.
headline: Trump Says 'All of a Sudden, It Seems Like a Long Time' Weeks After Telling Reporter 'You Look Like Hell'
html_content:
Donald Trump reflected on his time in office on Tuesday at a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in Manila.

The gathering brought together leaders from Southeast Asia, Australia, India and Japan during the ASEAN Special Summit. 'All of a sudden, it seems like a long time,' the US president told the gathering.

His remarks followed an exchange during the midterm campaign in which he told a Reuters reporter, 'You look like hell,' after a question about travelling.

Trump had briefly cancelled rallies in Kansas and Iowa during the final weekend of the campaign. The Reuters reporter asked whether he was sick of travelling. Trump insisted he felt well, then turned his attention to the journalist.

'I feel perfect! You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape. You look like hell.' Trump walked away after delivering his reply.

At Dinner in Manila, Trump Reflects on His Time in Office

Trump, 80, arrived in the Philippine capital after an 18-hour flight to attend the ASEAN Special Summit. A marching band and dancers greeted him as he stepped off Air Force One. The band played YMCA, one of Trump's favourite songs.

Trump attended as the guest of honour. Among those at the table were Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

'It's an honour to be here and so many friends that I've known, for now, a long time,' Trump told the gathering. He then turned from how long he had known those in the room to how long he had been doing the job himself.

'I've been doing this for, all of a sudden, it seems like a long time. But I've gotten to know most of you, and you've done a fantastic job running your countries, your levels of popularity. And it isn't easy, but you've done a great job.'

Midterm Defeat Forms the Backdrop to Trump's Visit

Trump travelled to Asia after a midterm defeat that handed Democrats control of the House and the Senate. The result left him facing two years under Democratic control of both chambers, raising the prospect of congressional investigations and subpoenas.

Outages that disrupted air travel, banks and email services were among the problems facing the administration at home. Trump sought to play down the disruption when he spoke to reporters during a photo opportunity with leaders of the Quad.

'It's life,' he told reporters. 'When you're big and powerful, and you have all the money, things like that happen. It's fine.'

From Manila, Trump Was Set to Travel to Shenzhen

Trump's meetings in Manila extended beyond the dinner. He met leaders of the Quad, bringing him together with counterparts from Australia, India and Japan. Trump also made progress on a trade deal with Thailand during the visit.

The trip's focus was set to shift to Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. Trump was scheduled to join Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin there. The trilateral summit of nuclear powers was expected to be the centrepiece of his Asia trip.

excerpt: Tiger Woods' comeback is confirmed for the Hero World Challenge on 3 December after surgery, injury setbacks and his Florida driving case
headline: Tiger Woods Says 'I'm Feeling Better' as He Confirms Golf Comeback Following Florida DUI Arrest
html_content:
Tiger Woods' comeback to outdoor tournament golf is set for 3 December at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas.

The organisers added him to the field on 17 November. It will be his first 72-hole tournament start since the 2024 Open at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut. His entry follows injury setbacks and a Florida driving case.

Woods offered a cautious update on 10 November. Speaking to SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio, he said, 'I'm feeling better, no doubt about that,' and added, 'I've been training quite a bit.'

He said he would attend the tournament he hosts, but did not confirm he would play. 'I will be at Hero (World Challenge). I'm there either way, so I'll see you there,' he said.

Organisers later added him alongside Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland, completing the field. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler and defending champion Hideki Matsuyama are also entered. Seven of the world's top 10, based on the eligibility date following the Tour Championship, are in the field, organisers say.

Tiger Woods' Return Follows Achilles Injury and Back Surgery

Woods, 50, last made an official start on the PGA Tour at the 2024 Open. He partnered his son Charlie at the 2024 PNC Championship. He last competed in the TGL Finals for Jupiter Links Golf Club on 24 March 2026, three days before the crash.

Woods announced on 11 March 2025 that he had ruptured his left Achilles tendon and undergone surgery. On 11 October that year, he announced his seventh back operation, an L4-L5 disc replacement, after experiencing pain and limited mobility.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office report says Woods' Land Rover struck the rear of a trailer attached to a Ford F-150 on 27 March. The vehicle overturned onto its driver's side. No one was injured.

Woods was arrested on suspicion of DUI. On 2 September 2026, he pleaded no contest to willful and wanton reckless driving and refusing a lawful test. The DUI charge was dropped under the agreement, and a careless-driving citation was also resolved.

The court adjudicated him guilty of the remaining offences and suspended his licence for five years. He was not convicted of DUI.

Four Rounds Will Offer a Measure of Tiger Woods' Readiness

The Hero World Challenge is an unofficial PGA Tour event, played over 72 holes without a cut. Woods faces four rounds across four days, a different test from TGL's indoor team format. The 36-hole PNC Championship is a two-person scramble in which players can use golf carts.

Scheffler won in 2023 and 2024, while Matsuyama claimed the 2025 title. Woods has won five times and enters by tournament invitation rather than ranking. His entry confirms his intention to play, but not that he can complete four rounds.

A Reddit discussion showed differing views. One commenter called Albany 'a sensible place for a comeback'. Another noted the event does not count as an official PGA Tour victory. These were individual reactions, not a measure of wider opinion.

Woods also remains chairman of the PGA Tour's Future Competition Committee. After the Tour's boards approved its recommendations on 16 November, he said the organisation was 'in the best position it has ever been'.

Other December appearances remain uncertain. The PNC Championship is scheduled for 19-20 December, but Woods and Charlie have not confirmed they will play. Jupiter Links faces Los Angeles Golf Club on 27 December, though Woods has not committed.

excerpt: The FTC's proposed $63 million Family Dollar settlement could offer refunds to eligible shoppers who made purchases from 1 January 2023 to 1 October 2026.
headline: Family Dollar's $63 Million Settlement Could Mean Cash for Shoppers: Are You Eligible?
html_content:
Family Dollar shoppers could qualify for cash refunds under a proposed $63 million settlement over allegations that the retailer charged customers more than advertised prices.

Announced by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) on 13 November, the agreement would provide $40 million in refunds to eligible customers. Family Dollar would also offer an additional $20 million in discounts to shoppers and pay more than $3 million to the 17 states involved in the lawsuit.

Who Can Claim a Family Dollar Refund?

Customers who purchased items at Family Dollar between 1 January 2023 and 1 October 2026 could qualify for compensation under the proposed settlement. Eligible shoppers will have 180 days from the release of claim forms to submit requests through an independent third-party administrator.

However, regulators have not announced when applications will open, how much individuals could receive or when payments might arrive. According to Fox 13 News, the Arkansas Attorney General's Office said a claim form will be posted on Family Dollar's website once the settlement receives federal court approval. Customers should monitor the retail chain's website and official notices for instructions.

Shoppers Could Also Receive Discounts

Beyond refunds, Family Dollar would provide $20 million in customer discounts through a separate programme that offers 15% discounts on eligible purchases during designated two-day promotional periods. Alcohol, tobacco, gift cards, and other prepaid cards would be excluded. The agreement also requires the retail chain to pay more than $3 million to the states involved in the case.

Why Family Dollar Faces a $63 Million Settlement

According to the FTC's complaint, Family Dollar repeatedly charged customers higher prices at checkout than those displayed on shelves, promotional materials, and digital platforms. The alleged discrepancies affected household essentials, including milk, eggs, cereal, diapers, toilet paper, and laundry detergent.

Regulators said the problems were particularly concerning for shoppers in lower-income communities, where affordable alternatives may be limited. The FTC alleged that the retail chain failed to fix the problems despite thousands of failed pricing inspections, hundreds of customer complaints, and multiple previous enforcement actions.

The complaint also highlighted alleged failures involving Family Dollar's Smart Coupons app, which allegedly prevented customers from receiving advertised discounts. The FTC said internal company records documented complaints about coupon problems stretching back six years.

Undercover FTC inspections uncovered further discrepancies. In January 2026, an investigator at a Euclid, Ohio, store was overcharged on 15 of 50 purchased items. A separate investigation in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, found overcharges on eight of 50 products in March.

According to company records cited in the FTC complaint, the company failed 40% of pricing inspections in January 2026, rising to 57% in February and 59% in March. Family Dollar neither admitted nor denied the allegations.

New Rules Aim to Prevent Overcharging

The proposed settlement would require the retail chain to introduce stronger pricing controls, including two unannounced audits annually at every store. Employees and managers would also receive training to identify and correct pricing errors, while the programme would undergo independent assessment and annual certification.

Stores would also have to honour lower advertised prices when discrepancies arise and provide refunds or adjustments for overcharges. Crucially, checkout prices could not increase until corresponding shelf labels had been updated. The proposed agreement aims to prevent future pricing discrepancies while providing compensation to eligible customers.

excerpt: Jeff Bezos reveals how Robert Pattinson won the James Bond role after five finalists underwent screen tests, following Amazon MGM's official casting announcement.
headline: Amazon Founder Jeff Bezos Was 'Heavily Involved' in Choosing Robert Pattinson as James Bond: 'It Was So Obvious'
html_content:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has revealed he was 'heavily involved' in choosing Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond. Recalling the selection process, Bezos said 'it was so obvious' that Pattinson was right for the role, despite initial concerns that the actor was already too famous. Speaking at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World event on Tuesday, Bezos said Pattinson emerged as the clear favourite after five finalists underwent extensive screen tests.

Bezos Reveals How Pattinson Won the Role

Bezos offered a rare glimpse into Amazon MGM Studios' casting process, explaining that the decision followed a rigorous selection involving multiple candidates. 'We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday,' he said. 'It was interesting. Full costumes and real sets and other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all the tests and reviewing all that.'

Despite the strong competition, Pattinson quickly distinguished himself from the other contenders. 'There was something special about Rob and his performance. It was immediately undebated,' he said. Director Denis Villeneuve and other members of the casting team also favoured Pattinson, according to Bezos.

https://www.facebook.com/plugins/post.php?href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2FCBSNews%2Fposts%2Fpfbid02FQM4tkAjaDeZxSbzo1Mfci6SaFWvczpvGtMkQH5XRX9DgH6BC7ennsqdpV1Ye59Nl&show_text=true&width=500

Pattinson's Fame Initially Raised Concerns

Although Pattinson impressed during auditions, Bezos admitted the team initially questioned whether an established Hollywood star was the right fit. Bond has historically helped elevate actors' careers, prompting producers to consider whether a lesser-known performer might better suit the franchise's next chapter.

'We were slightly biased against him just because he's already so famous,' Bezos explained. However, those concerns disappeared once the team watched Pattinson's screen tests. 'It was so obvious he is James Bond,' Bezos said. The decision marks another major franchise role for Pattinson, who previously starred in The Batman and gained international recognition through the Twilight films.

Pattinson Calls 007 Role the 'Honour of a Lifetime'

Amazon MGM Studios officially announced Pattinson's casting on Monday, ending weeks of speculation surrounding Daniel Craig's successor. In a statement, Pattinson described the opportunity as a career milestone.

'James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,' he said. The actor also thanked Villeneuve and Amazon MGM's creative team for their confidence.

'To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team,' he added. Before the announcement, speculation had linked several British actors to the role, including Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden, and Nicholas Hoult.

Amazon Takes Bond Into a New Era

Amazon finalised its acquisition of MGM in 2022, gaining distribution rights to the James Bond films but not creative control of the franchise. That changed in 2025, when Amazon MGM Studios, Barbara Broccoli, and Michael G. Wilson formed a joint venture to house the Bond intellectual property rights.

Following the deal's completion in March 2025, Amazon MGM Studios assumed creative control, while all three parties remained co-owners of the franchise. Villeneuve's upcoming film, starring Pattinson, will be the first Bond instalment released under Amazon MGM's creative leadership, marking a significant transition for the decades-old franchise.

excerpt: Anthropic's proposed IPO may attract traders, but Kevin O'Leary warns its $1.4 trillion valuation and huge infrastructure commitments could mean no profits until 2030.
headline: Kevin O'Leary Warns Anthropic Investors It May Not Turn a Profit Until 2030 Despite IPO Backing
html_content:
Kevin O'Leary sees Anthropic's proposed IPO as a potential trading opportunity but warns that the artificial intelligence company may not become profitable until 2030. While he believes its Claude platform could become a major enterprise technology, its enormous valuation and infrastructure obligations present significant financial risks.

Anthropic is preparing for a highly anticipated Nasdaq listing, with an indicated valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion. O'Leary previously described the offering as a potentially hot trade, but his latest comments suggest investors should distinguish between short-term market gains and sustainable profitability.

In a post on X on Tuesday, 17 November, accompanying an interview with Brian Sozzi, O'Leary urged prospective shareholders to understand what they were buying. He warned that Anthropic might not make money until 2030, despite its enormous valuation.

If you're considering Anthropic's IPO, understand what you're betting on. It may not make money until 2030, and the valuation is enormous. But you're investing in the role AI could play across all 11 sectors of the economy. We're already seeing AI improve productivity and margins, and Claude has become a major enterprise platform. That's the long term case.

— Kevin O'Leary aka Mr. Wonderful (@kevinolearytv) November 17, 2026

Kevin O'Leary Sees Long-Term Potential in Anthropic

Despite his profitability concerns, O'Leary remains optimistic about Anthropic's commercial prospects. He sees the company as an opportunity to invest in the wider adoption of artificial intelligence across all 11 sectors of the economy. He also highlighted productivity improvements and expanding profit margins, describing Claude as a major enterprise platform.

During his interview with Sozzi, O'Leary compared the opportunity with investing in Amazon during its early years as a publicly traded company. Amazon experienced considerable volatility during its expansion before becoming one of the world's largest technology and retail businesses. However, the comparison does not guarantee a similar outcome for Anthropic. Its ability to convert AI demand into sustainable earnings will ultimately determine its long-term investment appeal.

Anthropic's $1.4 Trillion Valuation Raises Financial Concerns

Anthropic's infrastructure requirements add considerable weight to O'Leary's warning. Its indicated offering range of $70 to $78 per share implies a valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion at the upper end.

The company's regulatory filing disclosed approximately $900.9 billion in aggregate computing and infrastructure commitments, including purchase agreements and lease obligations. Around $451.6 billion is expected to fall due before 31 December 2030, with most remaining commitments scheduled between 2031 and 2045. Approximately $70.7 billion is due within the 12 months following 30 September 2026.

Anthropic also reported $6.2 billion in total indebtedness as of 30 September 2026, reflecting outstanding principal on convertible promissory notes issued to Amazon. These obligations underline the capital-intensive nature of developing and operating advanced AI systems. Investors will need to assess whether future revenues can justify the company's spending and proposed valuation.

Howard Marks and Dan Ives Disagree on Anthropic's Value

Other prominent investors and analysts have also offered contrasting assessments. Howard Marks, co-founder of Oaktree Capital Management, has questioned the reliability of forecasting Anthropic's earnings five years into the future. Rapid technological advances, competitive pressures, and changing customer demand make long-term projections difficult.

Wedbush analyst Dan Ives has taken a more optimistic position on investor demand. He anticipated stronger interest at valuations between $1.5 trillion and $1.7 trillion but cautioned against aggressive buying at $2 trillion. Their differing views highlight the challenge of determining what Anthropic is worth before its long-term earnings potential becomes clearer.

Can Anthropic Deliver Returns Before 2030?

Anthropic's proposed IPO presents investors with a difficult balance between growth potential and financial risk. O'Leary sees considerable promise in Claude's enterprise adoption but believes shareholders may have to wait years for profitability. For prospective investors, the central question is whether Anthropic can turn growing AI demand into sustainable earnings while meeting its substantial infrastructure commitments. Those expecting quick returns may need to reconsider their expectations.

excerpt: Democrats seek an independent review of nearly $7.5 billion in Big Bend border contracts, citing campaign donations and links to a Homan-associated firm.
headline: Trump Border Wall Contractor Donated $1M to Campaign as Homan's Firm Received $186K, Democrats Say
html_content:
A group of 23 Democratic members of Congress is asking for an independent review of nearly $7.5 billion (£5.7 billion) in border infrastructure contracts awarded for the Big Bend region of Texas, arguing that political connections and limited procurement oversight warrant closer scrutiny.

The lawmakers point to two separate financial links. Barnard Construction chairman Tim Barnard and his wife donated about $1 million (£760,000) to a Trump campaign fundraising committee during the 2024 election cycle. Separately, Fisher Sand & Gravel reportedly paid as much as $186,000 (£141,000) to a consulting firm formerly associated with White House border czar Tom Homan.

In a 16 November letter led by Representative Veronica Escobar, the group asked the Department of Homeland Security's inspector general to examine whether political relationships influenced contractor selection and whether the projects' costs were justified. The allegations do not establish that any contract was improperly awarded.

Billions Awarded Under Exceptional Contracting Rules

The five contracts cover barriers and related infrastructure in the Big Bend Border Patrol Sector. They comprise $1 billion (£760 million) and $960.4 million (£730 million) for Barnard Construction; $1.2 billion (£912 million) and $2.6 billion (£1.98 billion) for Fisher Sand & Gravel; and $1.7 billion (£1.29 billion) for Southwest Valley Constructors.

The lawmakers say the Department of Homeland Security waived federal contracting requirements in October 2025 to accelerate construction, followed by waivers of environmental and historic preservation laws. They want the inspector general to assess whether expedited or non-competitive procurement was justified, whether the work assigned matched the original contracts, and whether officials communicated with companies about their selection.

The letter questions the need for extensive infrastructure in a remote region. It says the Big Bend Sector accounts for 26% of the southern border but recorded less than 1% of migrant apprehensions over the five-year period DHS used to justify the measures. The lawmakers argue that the disparity warrants scrutiny of the projects' operational value and cost-effectiveness.

Changing Plans Add to Transparency Concerns

The lawmakers also question what is being built. They say Customs and Border Protection's public maps and descriptions have changed repeatedly: a wall appeared, disappeared from maps, and later reappeared. In May, the agency said there would be no wall inside Big Bend National Park. About a week later, however, a $1.7 billion contract described work associated with a border wall in the park. CBP has since referred to roads, technology, and vehicle barriers.

The waivers also affect Big Bend Ranch State Park and hundreds of miles of privately owned land. The project's potential effects on public land and private property have made it contentious among local officials, residents, and conservation groups.

Supreme Court Decision Allows Work to Resume

Construction can now proceed while a separate legal challenge continues. On 9 November, the US Supreme Court lifted a lower court injunction that had temporarily halted work in the Big Bend area. The decision did not finally resolve whether the administration's legal waivers were lawful.

The administration has defended the project on border security grounds and has said Homan does not participate in the actual awarding of contracts. The Department of Homeland Security had not immediately responded to a request for comment on the Democrats' letter.

The lawmakers asked Inspector General Joseph Cuffari to provide a written response and an investigation timetable by 27 November, and want any findings made public. Their requested review would examine whether the procurement process protected taxpayers from waste or political influence, and whether the scale of construction is supported by evidence of need.
