excerpt: New forensic scrutiny has renewed questions about the evidence surrounding Jeffrey Epstein's death, but the official suicide ruling remains unchanged, and no fresh investigation has been announced.
headline: Jeffrey Epstein's Brother Releases Graphic Autopsy Photos, Demands Homicide Probe and Wants Trump Questioned
html_content:
Mark Epstein has released graphic photographs from his brother Jeffrey Epstein's autopsy and demanded an independent homicide investigation, suggesting that Donald Trump should be questioned as part of any inquiry. He stressed that he was not accusing the president of anything while challenging the official suicide ruling.

Mark shared the images online as forensic specialist Dr Michael Freeman presented an assessment suggesting Epstein's injuries were more consistent with assault than hanging. New York City's Office of Chief Medical Examiner maintains its original suicide determination, and authorities have not announced a fresh investigation.

Epstein Autopsy Photos Renew Scrutiny

Epstein died at Manhattan's Metropolitan Correctional Center, a federal detention facility, on 10 August 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges. His brother has continued to dispute the official explanation, citing Freeman's examination of autopsy records and photographs.

Freeman also presented photographs at an event in London, outlining findings from a review that lasted approximately a year. The reports do not establish whether those images and the collection Mark released online were identical.

Mark Epstein Urges Trump Questioning, Denies Accusation

Mark suggested Trump should be questioned during a potential investigation, explicitly qualifying his request by saying: 'I am not accusing him of anything'. His remarks concerned an inquiry he wants opened, rather than an interview that investigators have requested or announced.

ABC News has reported that Trump has repeatedly denied having knowledge of Epstein's crimes. However, a 2026 report detailing an FBI interview with a former Palm Beach police chief raised questions about what he knew of Epstein's activities. Neither Mark's request nor the reporting establishes that Trump was involved in Epstein's death.

Epstein's Brother Demands Homicide Probe

Mark cited Freeman's assessment in questioning why the US Department of Justice had not pursued homicide as an explanation for his brother's death. He called for an independent body to conduct a 'true homicide investigation', challenging the authorities' handling of the case.

'Dr Freeman has conclusively shown that the injuries on Jeffrey's body could not have come from a suicide,' Mark said in an interview with Metro, as reported by Hindustan Times. 'That only leaves homicide on the table,' he added, expressing his interpretation rather than an officially established finding.

Freeman Suggests Epstein's Injuries Indicate Assault

Freeman proposed that Epstein had been strangled from behind and then most probably suspended from a bunk bed using the same ligature, citing injuries he considered inconsistent with suicidal hanging. He identified possible fingernail marks above the ligature line, bruising near the base of the neck and a deep wound in the left shoulder muscle.

Professor Michael Freeman says believes that convicted sex offender Jeffery Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.

Story here: https://t.co/H6zbBs4E5k pic.twitter.com/8jVVXpO4vD

— Tom McArthur (@TomMcArthur) November 16, 2026

Freeman's report was rejected for publication by an academic journal and has not appeared in a peer-reviewed publication, according to CBS News. Freeman said reviewers considered criticism of a medical examiner's findings inappropriate for such a publication and that he planned to resubmit it.

Epstein Suicide Ruling Stands

Dr Kristin Roman performed Epstein's autopsy on 11 August 2019, while then-chief medical examiner Dr Barbara Sampson announced the official suicide determination. Roman reportedly told federal investigators there were no indications of a struggle and described his body as 'pristine'.

In her statement to investigators, Roman said: 'This doesn't look anything like a strangulation'. Her remarks were made in the context of the original investigation, rather than in response to Freeman's latest presentation.

The medical examiner's office continues to stand by its original determination. CBS News also reported that forensic experts can interpret the same injuries differently, particularly when assessing whether neck injuries are consistent with hanging or strangulation.

Missing Body-Position Photos Questioned

Freeman highlighted the absence of photographs documenting Epstein's body in its original position when prison personnel discovered him. This concerns documentation of the body's original position, not a claim that no photographs of the cell exist.

The 2023 Justice Department Inspector General investigation documented failures at the prison without finding evidence contradicting the FBI's determination that there was no criminality connected with Epstein's death.

A July 2025 DOJ–FBI memorandum subsequently reaffirmed the suicide conclusion. The memorandum said the FBI's review of footage from the Special Housing Unit's common area found that nobody entered any of its tiers between approximately 10.40pm on 9 August 2019, when Epstein was locked in his cell, and 6.30 the following morning.

Those official findings remain distinct from Freeman's disputed interpretation and Mark's demand for another inquiry.

excerpt: PlayStation users reported sign-in failures and online service disruptions on 18 November, hours before GTA 6's scheduled release, but Sony had not confirmed an outage or identified a cause.
headline: PlayStation Network Outage Hits PS5 Players Just Hours Before GTA 6 Worldwide Launch
html_content:
PlayStation Network (PSN) users reported widespread sign-in problems on Wednesday, 18 November, with outage reports climbing just hours before Grand Theft Auto 6's scheduled release. The disruption left some PS5 players unable to access online services, raising concerns about whether Sony's network would be ready for one of gaming's biggest release days.

The reports emerged as anticipation for GTA 6 reached fever pitch. Rockstar Games' latest instalment in the Grand Theft Auto franchise is scheduled to launch on 19 November, with players across different regions preparing to enter the fictional state of Leonida. However, some PlayStation owners were already struggling to get online.

PlayStation Network Outage Leaves PS5 Players Locked Out

Players experiencing the reported PlayStation Network problems said their internet connections were working normally, but attempts to sign in to PSN continued to fail.

downdetector is already near 1,000 reports and the line is still going vertical. ten hours out, the servers picked a bad moment to wobble.

— LTes1 (@Ltes8194) November 18, 2026

The PS5 connection test reportedly showed a successful internet connection. However, the separate sign-in test failed, displaying a warning that online services could not be used at that moment. Others encountered a message stating that PlayStation services were busy.

playstation users watching everyone play GTA 6 rn: pic.twitter.com/9ECSpXFhI3

— SideEyeCentral👁️‍🗨️. (@TheeSpectat0r) November 18, 2026

According to Downdetector figures cited in the initial report, complaints climbed to 876 at approximately 6pm GMT. The figure suggested a noticeable increase in reported problems, although it did not establish how many users were actually affected.

GTA 6 Players right now pic.twitter.com/Ak2C07twZW

— CodeGlitch (@codeglitch) November 18, 2026

There was another complication. PlayStation's official network status page reportedly continued to show all services operating normally while users were reporting difficulties. That discrepancy left players facing an uncomfortable question: was PSN experiencing a wider technical problem that its status page had yet to reflect?

PlayStation subsequently acknowledged an outage affecting its online services, although the company did not immediately identify its cause.

GTA 6 Launch Timing Fuels PSN Outage Concerns

The timing was difficult to overlook. With GTA 6 approaching its 19 November release, players could potentially be attempting to access their accounts, download updates and prepare their consoles at the same time.

A sudden increase in demand could place additional pressure on online infrastructure. However, there was no confirmed evidence linking the reported PlayStation Network problems directly to Rockstar's launch.

Players were also taking their concerns to X (formerly Twitter), where the timing quickly became a running joke.

One user, @Ltes8194, pointed to Downdetector's rising reports, writing, 'the servers picked a bad moment to wobble' with GTA 6 just hours away. Another player, @sirmarcaurelius, joked that 'psn saw the countdown and called in sick before the rest of us got the chance'.

Not everyone was entirely amused. One user, @AnarchyCop, urged PlayStation to have backup options ready for distributing decryption keys if necessary.

There was some relief among players who had prepared earlier. @amorriscode wrote, 'good thing I preloaded yesterday'.

Others were less forgiving, with @GTA6lIntel expressing concern about PSN going down ahead of the UK's midnight unlock.

Speculation about hackers also surfaced, although no evidence was provided to support those suggestions. Sony had not attributed the reported disruption to a cyberattack.

For affected players, the immediate advice remained frustratingly simple: wait and attempt to sign in again later. Whether the reported problems would be resolved before GTA 6's scheduled release remained unclear.

excerpt: Natalie Harp, Donald Trump's executive assistant, attracted online attention after appearing directly behind him during a diplomatic meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr in Manila
headline: Natalie Harp Goes Viral Over 'Weird and Creepy' Stare at Trump During Meeting With Philippine President
html_content:
Donald Trump's latest appearance in the Philippines has generated an unexpected talking point, with attention shifting from the US president to his closely scrutinised executive assistant, Natalie Harp.

Harp, 35, was seated directly behind Trump during his bilateral meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr at Malacañang Palace on Wednesday, 18 November 2026. Wearing a blue evening dress, she was captured looking towards the president as he addressed officials.

The footage prompted criticism on X, where a user identified as Ethan MacDonald reportedly described the scene as 'weird and creepy'.

This behavior is just weird and creepy.

— Ethan MacDonald 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿🇺🇸 (@EthanMacD) November 18, 2026

Natalie Harp's Position Behind Trump Draws Attention

Footage released by the White House showed Harp seated directly behind Trump during the diplomatic engagement.

The Daily Beast's Zak Wheeler reported on her prominent seating position, noting that she was seated alongside senior US administration officials despite not being a Cabinet member.

The publication also highlighted how Harp remained close to Trump throughout the meeting, attracting attention as cameras captured the diplomatic proceedings.

The Times of India similarly described the incident as a 'bizarre Manila moment', reporting that Harp's presence prompted questions about her unusually close access to the president.

President Donald J. Trump and Philippine President @bongbongmarcos hold a bilateral meeting:

"I very much appreciate your welcoming me, and us, back to the Philippines as we reaffirm one of America's oldest and most important alliances in the Pacific." pic.twitter.com/amaTIYZPz4

— The White House (@WhiteHouse) November 18, 2026

'Human Printer' Aide Has Unusual Access to Trump

Harp is widely known by the nickname 'human printer', which refers to her reported responsibility for providing Trump with printed news articles, social media posts and other information.

The New York Times previously reported that Harp carried a portable printer to supply Trump with printed material, including favourable news coverage.

Her responsibilities have also reportedly included assisting with the president's communications, including taking dictation for social media posts and messages.

The Daily Beast has separately documented her frequent presence around Trump, including during international travel and official engagements.

Her responsibilities have prompted scrutiny of the extent of her access to the president and the information presented to him.

Personal Letters Fuel Questions About Their Relationship

Harp's close working relationship with Trump has also attracted attention following reports about personal letters she allegedly sent him.

According to The New York Times and The Daily Beast, one of the letters contained the declaration: 'You are all that matters to me.'

The Daily Beast published the correspondence in full in August 2026 after obtaining copies from sources within Trump's 2024 campaign through author Michael Wolff. CNN subsequently discussed the letters, while noting that it had not independently verified whether Harp wrote or sent them.

Trump has also reportedly expressed confidence in Harp's loyalty. According to The New York Times reporters Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan, Trump told others that while his staff would eventually leave to pursue other opportunities, Harp 'will never leave me'.

Harp spoke at the 2020 Republican National Convention, where she publicly praised Trump's policies and credited him with helping save her life.

She later worked as a presenter for conservative broadcaster One America News Network before joining Trump's political operation in 2022. She became a prominent supporter after publicly crediting Trump's Right to Try legislation with helping her access experimental cancer treatment.

However, medical experts have questioned whether the law was responsible for her treatment, citing the circumstances and timeline of her case.

Harp's Manila Appearance Draws Attention During Diplomatic Meeting

The footage emerged during Trump's official engagements in Manila, where he met Marcos to reaffirm relations between the Philippines and the United States.

Trump's visit to Manila followed his participation in the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits, including the ASEAN-US Special Summit. His bilateral discussions with Marcos covered the longstanding alliance between the two countries, including cooperation in defence, trade, investment and energy.

During the meeting, Trump praised the relationship between Washington and Manila, reaffirming the importance of their longstanding alliance.

Despite the diplomatic significance of the visit, Harp's prominent position behind Trump became an unexpected talking point online.

The footage has renewed scrutiny of her unusual access to the president, with critics questioning her prominent presence during a high-level diplomatic engagement.

excerpt: Stephen Hutto, a former Colorado youth pastor, received an indeterminate prison sentence with an 18-year minimum after being convicted of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl.
headline: Colorado Pastor Who Sexually Assaulted 15-Year-Old Girl and Claimed She Was 'Jealous' Gets 18 Years in Prison
html_content:
A Colorado pastor has received an indeterminate prison sentence with an 18-year minimum after being convicted of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl who told investigators he had sex with her more than 20 times. Stephen Hutto, 46, told detectives she was jealous of his family because he had been blessed, according to his arrest affidavit.

Hutto was sentenced in El Paso County on 10 November after a jury convicted him on two counts involving the teenager, whom he knew through Fountain Independent Baptist Church. He maintained his innocence after the conviction, while victims described continuing trauma and church supporters asked the judge for leniency.

Youth Pastor Convicted of Child Sexual Assault

Hutto was a youth pastor at the Fountain church when the offences occurred and was convicted of two counts of sexual assault on a child by a person in a position of trust. Both convictions concerned the teenager, although he initially faced three counts involving three girls from the church's youth programme.

All three described their experiences during the trial, according to the The Gazette. At the sentencing, the victims described continuing trauma and difficulties trusting people close to them.

Victim Described Messages Before Sexual Abuse

The teenager told investigators that she and Hutto began 'texting back and forth nonstop' when she was about 15, according to the arrest affidavit. She said he sent explicit photographs of himself before kissing her, after which the sexual contact began and continued for approximately a year.

She described several encounters and said they had sex more than 20 times, according to the affidavit. Asked by detectives why she would make such an allegation, Hutto reportedly suggested that she was jealous of his family because he had been blessed.

Earlier Police Call Was Not Forwarded

According to the arrest papers, an earlier call reporting the alleged abuse was not forwarded to the appropriate investigative unit. The incident was not reported to police until years after it allegedly occurred.

Hutto was arrested in March 2025 while serving as pastor of Highland Baptist Church in Boone, Pueblo County, after previously working at the Fountain church.

At sentencing, prosecutor Avery Stacy separately said a victim eventually confided in a therapist who was a mandatory reporter, and accused Hutto's supporters of fostering a culture that discouraged disclosure. Stacy also alleged that supporters had snickered during victim testimony, but Judge John Kane said he had not witnessed that behaviour.

Victims Describe Harm as Supporters Seek Leniency

One victim, speaking remotely at sentencing, recalled being 'an 11-year-old Christian girl who trusted a teacher', according to The Gazette's account of the hearing. She said the harm extended into the church community, 'causing fear and hesitation for people seeking faith who are now afraid of stepping inside a church'.

Supporters filled about half the courtroom, and church friend Douglass Tecklenburg described Hutto as a 'responsible citizen' while seeking leniency. Hutto's wife, Sara, requested probation because of his health, saying: 'In my heart, I genuinely fear he will die in prison.'

Judge Imposed Concurrent Prison Sentences

Kane cited Hutto's lack of remorse and abuse of spiritual authority, saying: 'You abused it, and there is abundant proof that it happened more than once.' The reports identify an 18-year sentence for the pattern-related conviction and a concurrent six-year term for the conviction involving a victim aged 15 to 18.

The 18-year term is the reported minimum, not a guaranteed release date. According to The Gazette's sentencing coverage, Hutto could potentially remain imprisoned for life if he fails to comply with the Department of Corrections' treatment requirements.

excerpt: An X user has criticised GTA 6's performance, missions and characters after an early playthrough, prompting fans to challenge his 2/10 verdict and limited gameplay time.
headline: GTA 6 Branded 'Biggest Disappointment in Gaming History' After 13-Year Wait as Fans Defend Rockstar
html_content:
GTA 6 has been branded the 'biggest disappointment in gaming history' by an X user who claims to have played Rockstar's long-awaited title, sparking a backlash from fans defending the game. In a post on X, @ItsRealAlec gave the game a score of 2/10, praising its graphics but accusing its performance and storyline of falling short after a 13-year wait.

Alec claims the game runs at 30 frames per second (fps), with no 60fps option, and struggles when the streets become crowded. He also criticises the missions, describing long drives and everyday activities as tedious distractions from the heists and mayhem traditionally associated with Grand Theft Auto.

GTA 6 Review: Why Alec Says the Wait Was Not Worth It

'I waited 13 years. I played it. I want my money back,' Alec wrote.

He called the game a '$70 screensaver', arguing that its detailed world offers little meaningful activity. He also claims Jason and Lucia lack the personality of GTA 5's cast.

GTA 6 是游戏史上最让人失望的作品。

我等了13年。我玩了。我想退钱。

下面是那些拿了赞助的人不会告诉你的真相 👇

现在是2026年，Rockstar 卖给你的是一款30帧的游戏。

没有60帧模式。一个都没有。在一台500美元的主机上，普通版 PS5… pic.twitter.com/sdURe2f5Ix

— Alec (@ItsRealAlec) November 18, 2026

His comparison with its predecessor is central to the complaint. Alec argues that GTA 5 offered three playable characters, memorable heists and a more entertaining sense of chaos. By contrast, he says GTA 6 spends too much time on routine activities, including flipping burgers, playing mini-golf and playing fetch with a dog.

没有人能收买我。

我写的，就是我玩游戏时真实的感受。

Rockstar 不行。PlayStation 商店不行。任何一个评测媒体都不行。没有人能买走我的观点。

我玩得越多，就会告诉你越多。好的坏的，全都说。

关注我，我边玩边告诉你 GTA 6 的全部真相 🔔

— Alec (@ItsRealAlec) November 18, 2026

Alec also points to the game's Metacritic score of 99, arguing that reviewers have focused on its visuals while overlooking performance concerns. The score is genuine: GTA 6 had reached a Metascore of 99 ahead of its scheduled launch on 19 November 2026. However, the suggestion that reviewers have collectively downplayed technical shortcomings is his interpretation of their coverage.

Funny，所有大媒体的评测都在夸画面，却对30帧只字不提。

所以从现在开始，我自己做评测。不拿钱，只说实话。

我也在写一篇：不靠剪辑，怎么真正用 GTA 6 赚钱。剪辑这条路已经太挤了。

想学的，关注我。

— Alec (@ItsRealAlec) November 18, 2026

There is some independent support for his frame-rate criticism. Technical analysis reported by Video Games Chronicle on 18 November found that GTA 6 targets 30fps on PlayStation 5 consoles, although performance varies between the standard PS5 and PS5 Pro.

Alec said he would continue sharing his impressions, insisting that Rockstar, the PlayStation Store and review outlets could not buy his opinion. He also encouraged other gamers not to believe the hype and telling them instead to 'Go back and replay GTA 5.'

GTA 6 Fans Push Back Over the Early Verdict

X users quickly questioned whether Alec could judge such an expansive game so soon after its release. One asked: 'You finished the game in 4 hours and you know there are no heists in it?? right??'

Another wrote: 'Bro, it's only been 4 hours since it came out and you're already criticizing an 80-hour story💀'.

You finished the game in 4 hours and you know there are no heists in it?? right??

— zommex (@ZoMmEx195531) November 18, 2026

The 80-hour figure cited by the commenter has a basis in earlier reporting, but it is not an officially confirmed story length. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson reportedly completed a playthrough in about 80 hours, including the main story and some optional objectives. This does not establish how long the average player will take to finish the game.

Bro solo han pasado 4 horas de su lanzamiento y crítica una historia de 80 horas💀 pic.twitter.com/IP2qZurh1Z

— ️ (@edsongmc) November 18, 2026

A third response was more measured, saying: 'No action in 4 hours would still be horrible (if true)'.

Guys don’t listen to these corn balls just farming for clicks… the game is very good. I’ll give you a quick random thing that just happened to me. I’m driving to the beaches in the middle of vice city. All of a sudden I see two cop cars pulled over this very nice sports car so I…

— Joe | CitiLeeks (@CitiLeeks) November 18, 2026

Other players challenged the substance of the review. One described an encounter in which a woman allegedly smashed a police car window and fled, before an officer accidentally tased his colleague. The player cited the incident as an example of the game's unpredictable moments.

Fuck you for even getting to play it before everyone then shitting on it. Games fucking great for what GTA is supposed to be. Just delete it and go back to Fortnite.

— ApeStackin (@ApeStackin) November 18, 2026

There was support for Alec, too. Some users agreed that the franchise had become overhyped, while others questioned the absence of a 60fps option on current consoles.

Finally, a real opinion. They clearly want people to believe the greatest game of all time is a visually appealing pile of poorly optimized woke slop. It’s all about selling a narrative. Indie games are truly all the West has left for real games.

— … (@CascadeTheBard) November 18, 2026

The exchange highlights the difficulty of judging an open-world game in its opening hours. Early impressions can identify technical frustrations, but cannot settle questions about a story's depth or the variety of later missions.

IBTimes UK has not independently verified Alec's individual gameplay account or the specific incidents described by other players. His assessment should therefore be treated as a personal review rather than a definitive verdict on Rockstar's latest release.

excerpt: The Gentlemen has listed NVIDIA on its extortion site, but provides no stolen files or technical evidence to support its data theft claim.
headline: NVIDIA Faces Hack Claim From the Gentlemen Ransomware Gang as 10-Day Data Leak Countdown Begins
html_content:
NVIDIA has not publicly responded after ransomware group The Gentlemen listed the chipmaker on its extortion site, displaying a countdown of about 234 hours before an alleged data release.

The 18 November listing displays NVIDIA's logo, its NVDA stock ticker, a Tox contact for negotiations and the message 'DATA INFO – SOON'. It provides no sample files, screenshots or technical evidence that company information was stolen. The group has not identified the material it claims to possess.

The Gentlemen Listing Provides Few Details About Alleged Data

The listing does not identify the information The Gentlemen claims to have obtained, specify when the alleged intrusion took place or name any affected NVIDIA systems or business units. A revenue figure of $303 billion, equivalent to about £230 billion, also appears on the page, but the group does not explain its source.

The page provides a Tox ID for contacting the operators through Tox, an encrypted peer-to-peer messaging platform. It does not identify the purported data or specify which NVIDIA department, product or service may have been affected. The listing itself does not establish that the group accessed the company's internal systems.

NVIDIA Has Not Confirmed an Intrusion

NVIDIA had not publicly confirmed an intrusion as of 18 November. The company had also not responded to requests for comment about the listing by the time of publication.

Ransomware.live, a platform that monitors extortion sites and records ransomware claims, recorded NVIDIA's listing on 18 November and marked its status as pending. The entry documents the group's claim, not a confirmed intrusion.

The Gentlemen Built Its Operation From Earlier Affiliate Activity

The Gentlemen's history predates the launch of its independent ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation in September 2025. Security research traces earlier activity to an affiliate operation known as ArmCorp, whose operators had worked with the Qilin ransomware programme. The first known sample associated with The Gentlemen was uploaded to VirusTotal on 17 July 2025, ahead of the group's independent launch.

Under the RaaS model, operators develop and maintain malware and supporting infrastructure, while affiliates use those tools to conduct attacks. The Gentlemen reportedly offers affiliates 90% of ransom proceeds, a larger share than the 80% commonly cited as an industry arrangement.

Its research profile also includes Russian-language communications and recruitment on Russian-speaking cybercrime forums. The group is reported to avoid targeting organisations in Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) countries.

In June 2026, investigative journalist Brian Krebs reported that threat-intelligence records linked the administrator aliases Zeta88 and Hastalamuerte to forum registrations originating from internet addresses in Izhevsk, Russia.

The group has claimed more than 1,000 victims. Ransomware.live recorded 1,123 claimed victims in data cited by Cybernews, but that figure does not represent an independently verified count of successful attacks.

Researchers Urge Caution Over Unverified Claims

The Gentlemen has previously faced allegations of exaggerating victim numbers, misattributing incidents and recycling stolen data. Cybernews researcher Aras Nazarovas cited those concerns when assessing the group's latest claim, urging readers to 'take each claim with a grain of salt' and verify any samples it publishes.

Without samples or details identifying the affected NVIDIA business unit, researchers cannot reliably assess the potential impact of the alleged incident.

excerpt: Wesley Dingus received probation and suspended jail sentences after pleading guilty to reduced charges over footage of him smelling a teenager's underwear.
headline: Former Ohio Mayor Wesley Dingus Avoids Jail After Video Shows Him Smelling Teen Girl's Underwear
html_content:
Former Butler, Ohio, Mayor Wesley Dingus avoided serving jail time and sex-offender registration after pleading guilty to two reduced disorderly-conduct charges stemming from footage showing him smelling a teenage girl's underwear.

Dingus entered the pleas on 13 November in Mansfield Municipal Court, replacing a scheduled trial on two original voyeurism charges. Visiting Judge James Kimbler, a retired Medina County judge, imposed a 30-day jail sentence on each count but suspended both terms. He also placed Dingus on probation for one year and ordered him to have no contact with the victim.

Video Shows Former Mayor Entering Teenager's Bedroom

The investigation began after Richland County Children's Services contacted the Richland County Sheriff's Office about footage showing an adult man entering a teenage girl's bedroom and smelling her underwear. The girl had installed a camera after suspecting Dingus, who was responsible for her care, had been entering the room.

She left home for school at about 7am on 13 January 2026. Around 15 minutes later, her phone alerted her to movement in the bedroom. The recording showed Dingus entering, picking up her underwear and smelling it.

A second alert arrived at 7.17am the following day. Dingus entered the room again, smelled her worn underwear and touched his groin area over his clothing. Sheriff's deputies and a Children's Services representative later interviewed the teenager at her high school. The investigation was forwarded to the Mansfield City Law Director's Office on 26 January.

Dingus Pleads Guilty to Reduced Charges, Avoiding Registration

Dingus originally faced two third-degree misdemeanour counts of voyeurism. Prosecutors amended them to two fourth-degree misdemeanour counts of disorderly conduct on 13 November, and he pleaded guilty to both rather than proceed with the scheduled trial.

Kimbler also ordered Dingus to pay court costs, comply with a protection order and undergo a treatment assessment as a condition of probation. The suspended sentences mean Dingus will not serve the jail terms provided he complies with his probation conditions. A violation could put the suspended sentences at risk.

A conviction for voyeurism under Section 2907.08 of the Ohio Revised Code would result in Tier I sex-offender classification and registration requirements. The disorderly-conduct convictions did not trigger that classification.

Victim Says Former Mayor Destroyed Her Senior Year

The teenager delivered a victim-impact statement at the hearing, describing the effect of the incidents on her final year of high school. She told the court she felt 'disgusted, shocked, hurt, humiliated, violated and vulnerable' and said Dingus had destroyed her senior year.

She also said she had moved away from Butler, a small village in Richland County, Ohio. By the time of the hearing, she had graduated from high school. She noted that 304 days had passed since the first recording.

Prosecutors Explain Decision to Accept Reduced Charges

Assistant Law Director Robert Sharp III said the agreement had the victim's 'full blessing and consent'. Section 2907.08(A) requires a person to trespass or otherwise surreptitiously invade another's privacy to spy or eavesdrop for the purpose of sexual arousal or gratification. Sharp questioned whether the circumstances shown in the recordings met those statutory requirements.

Defence attorney James Mayer III said the guilty pleas reflected Dingus's acceptance of responsibility. Dingus apologised to the teenager, his family and the court, saying: 'This will never happen again.'

Dingus resigned as Butler's mayor on 23 February 2026, after the allegations became public. The two voyeurism summonses had been prepared on 12 February. His November guilty pleas resolved those charges without a trial.

excerpt: An inquest heard that Alice Webb, 33, died after suffering cardiac arrests during a Brazilian butt lift, while a pathologist attributed her death to hyaluronic acid entering her bloodstream
headline: Alice Webb Died After Brazilian Butt Lift as Paramedic Recalls 'Unbothered' Response to Her Cardiac Arrest
html_content:
A mother of five died after undergoing a Brazilian butt lift at a friend's house in Gloucester, where a paramedic recalled the apparently 'unbothered' reaction of those present after she suffered a cardiac arrest.

Alice Webb, 33, collapsed during the cosmetic procedure on 23 September 2024. She was taken to hospital but died in the early hours of the following morning.

At Gloucestershire Coroner's Court, paramedic Allanah Kingston described the response of practitioner Jordan Parke and another woman, identified as Jemma Pawlyszyn, as Webb's condition deteriorated.

Paramedic Recalls 'Unbothered' Reaction

According to ITV News, Kingston, of South Western Ambulance Service, received an emergency call at around 21:00 reporting that a patient who had undergone 'bum filler' had collapsed.

She spoke to Parke, 34, who had performed the procedure. He reportedly told her Webb had gone outside for a cigarette before collapsing and was subsequently moved onto a bed inside the property.

Kingston told the inquest she informed Parke and Pawlyszyn when Webb suffered a cardiac arrest. Both appeared to lack an emotional reaction, she recalled.

'I remember Jordan talking about how much Alice smoked and that she normally smoked 80 cigarettes a day,' Kingston told the jury.

She described the pair as appearing 'unbothered by the situation', adding that they seemed unaware of the seriousness of Webb's condition.

Information Given to Paramedics

Kingston said the pair told paramedics Webb had received 10ml of lignocaine, also known as lidocaine, alongside a filler containing hyaluronic acid and another unidentified substance.

She also told the inquest that the pair did not appear to know Webb's date of birth or emergency contact details. They reportedly said they could contact her family only through Facebook.

'I found it strange they didn't come to the hospital, seeing as they were friends,' Kingston added.

Webb was taken to Gloucestershire Royal Hospital at 22:41, arriving five minutes later. She suffered further cardiac arrests despite resuscitation efforts and was pronounced dead in the early hours of 24 September 2024.

Pathologist Identifies Cause of Death

The Independent reported that Home Office forensic pathologist Dr Stephen Leadbetter identified Webb's cause of death as 'embolisation of hyaluronic acid from introduction into buttocks'.

Dr Leadbetter told the inquest that gel-like material consistent with hyaluronic acid was found in Webb's buttock tissue and blood vessels.

The substance was also identified in her lungs, brain, heart, thyroid gland and kidney.

'What had entered the circulation here was the hyaluronic acid which was a part of the cosmetic procedure,' he told the jury.

He explained that the filler could have entered her bloodstream after a blood vessel was damaged during the injections, although he could not establish a specific entry point.

Inquest Hears 1,400ml of Filler Was Injected

The Independent reported that Laura Collignon, representing Webb's family, raised evidence that approximately 1,400ml of hyaluronic acid had been injected during the procedure.

Dr Leadbetter said a greater quantity of filler meant more material could potentially enter the bloodstream.

He also confirmed that toxicology testing identified lignocaine, although he did not consider it relevant to the cause of death.

Police Investigation Into Practitioner

The coroner confirmed that Parke, who was known as the 'Lip King', had died before the inquest.

ITV News reported that he had been under investigation for gross negligence manslaughter in connection with Webb's death before he died earlier in 2026.

Detective Inspector Adam Stacey of Gloucestershire Constabulary told the inquest that investigators believed they had a case against Parke, although no charging decision had been made before his death.

'We were confident we had a case, we were confident we had a case of gross negligence manslaughter,' Stacey said.

ITV News also reported that Parke had previously received prohibition notices preventing him from performing Brazilian butt lift procedures in Dudley and Salford following concerns raised by environmental health officers.

The three-day inquest at Gloucestershire Coroner's Court began on 18 November 2026 and is scheduled to continue until 20 November.

excerpt: Donald Trump is reportedly frustrated by JD Vance's criticism of the Iran war and has increasingly praised Marco Rubio, fuelling speculation about the Republican succession in 2028.
headline: Trump Reportedly Grows Frustrated With JD Vance Over Iran War Criticism as Marco Rubio Gains Favour Ahead of 2028
html_content:
President Donald Trump has reportedly grown frustrated with Vice President JD Vance over his criticism of the Iran war, while increasingly praising Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a potential Republican presidential contender in 2028. The reported tension has emerged following the party's bruising midterm defeat, according to people familiar with Trump's private comments.

The disagreement follows Vance's post-election assessment that the conflict helped drive voters away from Republicans. Trump initially appeared to accept that argument, telling reporters: 'I think it's largely true.' However, people familiar with his conversations say he later complained that Vance had failed to make clear that the decision to attack Iran had been the right one.

Trump Wants Vance to Defend the Iran War

Trump subsequently offered a public indication of what he believed was missing from Vance's remarks.

On 8 November, he said the vice president should have 'made one other statement', adding: 'If you had it to do again, would you do it again? The answer is yes.'

The distinction matters for Vance, who must explain the political cost of the war without appearing to break with the president. In a Fox News interview this week, he rejected suggestions of a split, saying, 'I think there's no daylight between the president or any other senior member of the administration.'

The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Vance's office declined to comment, pointing to his recent interviews.

Vance's Four Reasons Republicans Lost Voters

In a lengthy post on X on 4 November, the day after the midterm elections, Vance set out four issues he believed had driven voters away from Republicans: the Iran war, the cost of living and inflation, a perceived departure from the America First approach and America's relationship with Israel.

He said those concerns accounted for nearly all the responses gathered by a Republican pollster who asked what might persuade disaffected voters to return to the party.

But Vance placed the war at the centre of his assessment, writing: 'The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so.'

His comments carried particular significance given his previous opposition to new foreign military engagements. When endorsing Trump in 2023, Vance had presented himself as an advocate of a more restrained US foreign policy.

His post-election assessment leaves him with a difficult political balancing act: how to acknowledge the unpopularity of the conflict without distancing himself from the president who authorised it.

Rubio's Iran Defence Wins Trump's Approval

Rubio has taken a markedly different public approach. Trump has repeatedly praised the secretary of state, while Rubio's defence of the administration's Iran policy has reinforced his standing within the president's inner circle.

During Trump's visit to Manila for the ASEAN summit on 17 November, the president offered another enthusiastic endorsement.

'How hot is Marco, right?' Trump asked before adding, 'He's been fantastic.'

In an interview with The New York Times, Rubio also defended Trump's decision to authorise the strikes, saying the president 'deserves a tremendous amount of credit'. He framed leadership as accepting decisions that may prove politically unpopular but are necessary for the country's long-term interests.

Vance has not decided whether to seek the presidency. 'I haven't made a decision,' he told Fox News, adding that he expected to settle the question sometime next year.

Trump has not formally endorsed a successor, while Rubio has previously indicated that he would support Vance if the vice president pursued the presidency. Nevertheless, Trump's repeated public praise has brought renewed attention to the potential rivalry.

For a vice president whose path to the Republican nomination may depend heavily on Trump's backing, that is an uncomfortable position to occupy.

excerpt: Trump's Manila reception highlights competing priorities as campaigners challenge Pax Silica plans and a rights inquiry examines earlier protest arrests.
headline: Trump Gets Red Carpet Welcome in Manila as Protesters Burn US Flags Behind Razor Wire
html_content:
Protesters burned a US flag in Manila as Donald Trump received a red-carpet welcome at Malacañang on Wednesday. Demonstrators opposed his visit and a Philippine government plan to establish a technology manufacturing hub under the US-led Pax Silica initiative.

Police blocked the march at San Sebastian Street using container vans and razor wire, preventing demonstrators from advancing towards Mendiola, near Malacañang, where Trump and Marcos were meeting.

The protest on 18 November coincided with Trump's meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, following ASEAN summit events in the capital. Campaigners say the proposed hub threatens Indigenous communities and farmers, while arrests during earlier demonstrations have drawn scrutiny from the Commission on Human Rights.

US Flag Burned as Trump Arrives

'When Trump arrived in Malacañang, we burned the US flag, and then there was protest in the street,' Bagong Alyansang Makabayan secretary general Raymond Palatino said. He added that the protest sought to hold Trump accountable for what he described as a war of aggression and opposed his visit to the Philippines.

🇵🇭 | US flags up in flames at protests in Manila against Pax Silica.

Protesters warn the US-led initiative would turn the Philippines into an "AI sweatshop." pic.twitter.com/CNSSS6zB1K

— The Specter (@specter_affairs) November 18, 2026

Palatino estimated that more than 2,000 people joined the 'Trump Out' rally. This figure was provided by the organiser and has not been independently verified. 'We condemned the barrier, the overkill security measures,' he said, criticising the use of container vans and barbed wire.

Marchers travelled from Morayta along Recto Avenue towards Mendiola, a traditional protest site near the presidential palace, before police stopped them at San Sebastian Street. Officers had installed container vans and razor wire across the road.

LOOK: Police presence in Mendiola near Malacañang has been heightened in anticipation of the arrival of protesters opposing US President Donald Trump’s Manila visit.

Trump is expected to have a bilateral meeting with President Marcos in Malacañang today. @TheManilaTimes pic.twitter.com/MSC49rv58i

— Allen Limos (@allen_limos) November 17, 2026

A separate GMA News report on security arrangements described three container vans and barbed wire blocking both lanes at the intersection. The blockade prompted a heated exchange between Bagong Alyansang Makabayan president Renato Reyes and a Manila Police District official.

Police Defend Restrictions Near Palace

Reyes maintained that protesters were not causing trouble, while labour leader Jerome Adonis said they wanted to exercise their freedom of expression at Mendiola. Police Colonel Emil Tumibay defended the deployment as necessary to maintain peace and order, saying officers would not initiate trouble.

Police described keeping demonstrators away from Mendiola as non-negotiable because it was not a designated freedom park, where rallies can be held without a permit. This distinction, as explained by Human Rights Watch, provides context for the police position but does not, in itself, establish whether the restrictions imposed on the march were lawful.

Pax Silica Hub Draws Community Opposition

Human Rights Watch says the Philippine government's proposed technology manufacturing hub in Capas, Tarlac province, under the US-led Pax Silica initiative, threatens to displace Indigenous communities and small farmers.

Orlino Lahut, an Aeta from Olongapo who joined the protest, said he feared the project would cost his community its homes and livelihoods.

Exhausted from working overtime, yet my heart is even heavier knowing that Aeta communities and fellow Filipinos still have to raise their voices, fight, and beg for justice over the very land that should rightfully be theirs. My prayers are with every one of you. I will never…

— dan | SHOCK!!! ^_–✩ (@dansahikun) November 14, 2026

A Center for Strategic and International Studies assessment said both governments had indicated that no announcement on the Pax Silica hub would accompany Trump's visit. The initiative's legal framework was not expected to be signed until the end of the year.

Earlier Arrests Draw Human Rights Scrutiny

The Commission on Human Rights reported arrests in Manila and Muntinlupa, visible injuries among detainees and concerns about detention conditions. Its investigation into alleged mistreatment remained ongoing, and the arrests during earlier demonstrations were separate from Wednesday's protest along Recto Avenue.

In its official statement, the Commission said its lawyers and investigators were initially denied access to detainees at Camp Bagong Diwa on 15 November, despite repeated requests. Access was granted later that evening after several hours of delay, and the Commission said it was continuing to gather evidence to determine whether human rights violations had occurred.

Trump Receives Honour Guard and Gun Salute

At Malacañang, Trump and Marcos inspected an honour guard, while the national anthems and a 21-gun salute accompanied the welcome. Senior US officials stood nearby on the red carpet before the leaders entered the palace.

On Recto Avenue, protesters continued their programme where police had stopped their march. They dispersed before without reaching Mendiola.

excerpt: Donald Trump announced more than $17bn in deals during his Philippines visit, including a Philippine Airlines aircraft order, defence financing and energy projects across Asia.
headline: Trump Secures Over $17 Billion in Asia Deals During Philippines Visit Across Aviation, Defence and Energy
html_content:
US President Donald Trump announced more than $17 billion (£12.9 billion) in Asia deals during a two-day visit to the Philippines that concluded on 18 November 2026. The White House said the deals included a $12 billion (£9.1 billion) aircraft agreement involving Philippine Airlines, Boeing and GE Aerospace.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr hosted Trump in Manila for a state visit that coincided with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. The announcements ranged from signed supply contracts to a proposed Philippine defence loan and an Indonesian energy project still under negotiation.

A Philippine Airlines Order Anchors Trump's Asia Deals

Philippine Airlines agreed to buy 15 Boeing 787-10 aircraft, with options for five more, powered by GE Aerospace engines. The airline first announced the plans in July and formalised the agreements on 10 November. The White House estimates that the $12 billion sale will support 47,000 American jobs.

Marcos and Trump also agreed to increase Philippine imports of American energy and farm products. Their aim, in the White House's words, is to 'eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines'.

At the summit, Trump announced that trade talks with Thailand were largely complete. If signed, the agreement would eliminate tariffs on 99% of goods and remove other barriers to selling American products in Thailand, from vehicles and medical devices to ethanol and poultry.

Separately, Thailand intends to spend up to $123 million (£93.6 million) on US artillery rocket systems. The White House estimates that the sale would support 400 American jobs if it goes ahead.

Asia Deals Link a Montana Coal Mine to Malaysia

Under a three-year agreement worth $100 million (£76.1 million), Navajo Transitional Energy Company will supply coal from its southern Montana mine to TNB Fuel Services. The buyer procures fuel for Tenaga Nasional Berhad, Malaysia's national power utility.

In Indonesia, US firm Latitude Energy and Danantara, the country's sovereign wealth fund, announced negotiations over a $2 billion (£1.5 billion) coal project. The partners want to bring in American technology to improve how Indonesia uses its coal resources.

Manila and Washington also agreed to explore a pact on civilian nuclear technology. The White House sees a potential role for American nuclear companies in expanding the Philippines' electricity supply if the two governments reach an agreement.

What the Asia Deals Could Fund for the Philippine Military

Under the US Foreign Military Financing programme, Washington and Manila will pursue a loan package worth more than $2 billion (£1.5 billion). The Philippines would borrow the money to buy defence and security equipment from American suppliers. The White House expects those orders to support more than 7,000 US jobs.

The US will direct $400 million (£304.3 million) in military financing towards extending the Philippine military's reach in the South China Sea. Priorities include drones, long-range weapons, command systems and critical infrastructure.

The Philippine Department of National Defense announced a $37 million (£28.1 million) contract with an American firm for technology to support military missions. It also pledged to work with US providers on a $63 million (£47.9 million) project to modernise its cloud infrastructure.

Subic Grain will build a $40 million (£30.4 million) fuel storage depot at Subic Bay for US military and commercial operations. Manila also plans to modernise Basco Airport to improve access for both countries in the northernmost Philippine islands.

excerpt: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended his use of a government aircraft to attend an LSU football game, saying he had reimbursed the government as lawmakers questioned his travel amid widespread flight disruption.
headline: Trump Homeland Security Chief Defends Government Plane Trip to Football Game as Americans Faced Flight Chaos
html_content:
Donald Trump's Homeland Security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, defended taking a government aircraft to a football game after a nationwide aviation disruption, telling lawmakers he had reimbursed the government. He accused Democrats of hypocrisy during Wednesday's confrontation over the trip.

Mullin attended Saturday's LSU-Texas game in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, as airlines continued recovering from Friday's Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop. Operators cancelled approximately 12,462 flights on Friday, according to the FAA, although the agency cautioned that not every cancellation was directly caused by the restriction.

HE NEEDS TO BE FIRED NOW!

The Trump administration has two sets of rules. One for the masses- and one for them. Markwayne Mullin flying off to a football game, while the nation was grounded, is the ultimate example of this let them eat cake mentality.

Your Thoughts? pic.twitter.com/qCWgbtJkWz

— Woke-Like-Jesus (@DougWahl1) November 17, 2026

Mullin Defends Government Aircraft Use

Challenged by Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, Mullin said his responsibilities required him to travel on government aircraft and remain available around the clock. A Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson separately said the arrangement was required by law to ensure secure communications and meet continuity-of-government responsibilities.

Joe Kernen: 24 hours after the skies opened up, you took a government plane to the LSU-Texas game. While people in the US were grounded and you took a private jet to a football game?

Markwayne Mullin: we also had to "deal with an issue"

I feel like they’re just laughing at… pic.twitter.com/uqYrsHiFLT

— Jamison Daniel (@AntiquarianMuse) November 18, 2026

Mullin defended the journey in a Tuesday CNBC interview, saying the airspace had been completely open for 21 hours. He said he would not have travelled had restrictions remained in place, distinguishing his Saturday journey from travel during the nationwide ground stop.

FAA Technical Failure Disrupted Thousands of Flights

The FAA's account of the disruption says a technical problem began at approximately 3.30pm Eastern Time on Friday, 13 November, affecting its telecommunications network. Instability developed at 17 of the FAA's 22 air route traffic control centres and spread to several terminal radar approach control facilities.

Air traffic resumed at 8.15pm Eastern Time, but reopening the airspace did not immediately restore airline schedules or resolve problems for passengers awaiting flights. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned during a Friday briefing that recovery depended on crew availability, with some services having to wait until Saturday.

Mullin Says Visit Was for His Great-Niece

Mullin said he attended the game for his 12-year-old great-niece, an LSU supporter who had never watched the team play in person. He described offering to take her after discovering how closely she followed its players and coaches.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended his decision to fly on a government plane to an LSU football game Saturday, one day after a nationwide FAA ground stop left travelers stranded at airports across the country.

Mullin noted the day before that DHS secretaries… pic.twitter.com/eNEmlnRQ2R

— Mosheh Oinounou (@Mosheh) November 18, 2026

Mullin told CNBC that House Majority Leader Steve Scalise helped him obtain the tickets. A source familiar with the matter told ABC News that Mullin paid full market value for them. At Wednesday's hearing, Mullin also maintained that he had paid for his own admission.

Private Box Adds Contractor Context

Mullin was reportedly seen in a private box belonging to Ben Bordelon, chief executive of Bollinger Shipyards, whose government business includes a $2.2 billion cutter contract. The deal covers four Arctic Security Cutters for the Coast Guard, which operates under DHS.

A DHS announcement says Bollinger's contract was initially awarded in December 2025, before Mullin became secretary, and finalised in July 2026. Mullin said he had never met Bordelon before and maintained that no government business was discussed during the visit. His presence in the box does not, by itself, establish an improper benefit or connection to the contract.

Mullin Accuses Democrats of Hypocrisy

During Wednesday's congressional exchange, Mullin argued that Democrats would have made a similar journey but described it as a campaign event. He also suggested they would have used campaign resources or sought complimentary tickets from a state university.

Those assertions formed part of his political rebuttal rather than documented examples of equivalent conduct by Thompson or the lawmakers questioning him. Mullin also invoked his workload, telling the committee he had gone 239 days without taking a day off since beginning the job.

Federal Rules Govern Flight Reimbursement

Federal travel regulations generally require reimbursement for personal travel on government aircraft based on the difference between the full coach fares for the flights taken and those that would have been taken without the personal activities.

For a wholly personal journey under those arrangements, the full coach fare for the entire trip applies, rather than automatic repayment of the aircraft's operating costs.

The cited reporting does not independently establish the formal travel classification or reimbursement calculation applied to Mullin's particular itinerary. His statement that he repaid the government remains attributed to him, while the precise amount and basis of that payment remain undisclosed.

excerpt: Brick Media reported 73% revenue growth in 2023, the first year of its four-day working week, with further increases in subsequent years.
headline: Company Gives Staff Fridays Off Without Cutting Pay, Reports 73% Revenue Growth After Four-Day Week
html_content:
A US-based social media agency has reported a 73% increase in revenue during the first full year of its four-day working week, allowing employees to have Fridays off without taking a pay cut.

Jake Kurtz, founder and chief executive of Tampa-based Brick Media, introduced the arrangement in January 2023 as a 90-day experiment aimed at improving work–life balance and attracting talent.

The company made the policy permanent in April 2023. Since then, its revenue has continued to grow, while voluntary employee departures have remained relatively low, according to figures provided by the company to Fortune.

Four-Day Week Introduced Without Pay Cuts

According to Fortune, Brick Media's revenue increased by 73% in 2023, followed by a further 39% in 2024 and 8% in 2025. Compounded, these increases represent approximately 160% growth over the three-year period.

The figures were supplied by Brick Media. Kurtz believes the shorter working week contributed to the company's performance, although he has not claimed it was the sole reason for the revenue growth.

Kurtz first considered the arrangement after seeing European companies experiment with shorter working weeks. He launched the pilot on 1 January 2023, initially asking employees to work four 10-hour days instead of following the traditional five-day schedule.

The company eventually found that it could operate with fewer hours. At the start of 2026, Brick Media reduced the schedule to four nine-hour days, giving employees a 36-hour working week while maintaining their salaries and benefits.

How the Company Maintains Productivity

The shorter schedule required Brick Media to change how employees organise their responsibilities and manage their time.

According to Fortune, the company introduced shorter meetings, limiting quick check-ins to approximately 15 minutes and standard discussions to 30 minutes. Longer meetings are generally reserved for strategic matters.

Brick Media also uses artificial intelligence (AI) to speed up tasks such as research, brainstorming and preparing initial drafts.

Employees work remotely for three of their four working days, with Wednesdays designated as their main office day.

Although Fridays are officially treated as non-working days, staff occasionally handle small client requests outside their regular schedules. Kurtz said these tasks usually take only a few minutes, while more serious emergencies requiring several hours of work occur approximately once or twice per quarter.

The company also avoids continuously increasing individual workloads as its client base expands. Brick Media served 56 clients throughout 2022, compared with 85 during the first six months of 2026.

Rather than overloading existing employees, Kurtz hires additional staff when workers approach their capacity.

However, he acknowledged that profit margins have remained largely unchanged because increased payroll expenses have accompanied revenue growth.

Voluntary Employee Departures Fall Overall

Figures provided by Brick Media to Fortune show that six employees voluntarily left the company in 2022, before the four-day schedule was introduced.

The number fell to two in 2023 and remained at two in 2024, before rising to three in 2025. No employees had voluntarily left by the time the report was published in November 2026.

Meanwhile, the company's workforce grew from 15 employees at the end of 2022 to 25 in 2026.

Kurtz believes the arrangement helps retain experienced workers, improving efficiency through stronger communication and established working relationships.

He also said the policy has strengthened recruitment by attracting applicants from outside Florida.

'People have a hard time leaving the four-day schedule once they experience it, because they start to realise that life is way more than just the salary,' Kurtz told Fortune.

An Employee Values Additional Day Off

Andrea Echeverry, Brick Media's director of client experience, said the arrangement has encouraged employees to become more efficient without necessarily reducing their responsibilities.

Having worked at the company before the schedule change, she said staff have found better ways to manage their time.

As a working mother whose husband also works full-time, Echeverry particularly appreciates having Fridays available to spend time with her child and manage personal commitments.

'We're sort of like redefining work-life balance,' she told Fortune.

Kurtz does not believe every business needs to adopt the same four-day schedule. Instead, he encourages employers to reconsider what they offer workers to improve recruitment and retention.
